5:1: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: O you who have believed, fulfill, O you who have acknowledged the Oneness of God, submitted to Him in servitude, surrendered to Him in divinity, and believed in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his prophethood and in what he brought to them from their Lord of the laws of His religion, fulfill your contracts, meaning: fulfill the covenants that you have made with your Lord, and the contracts that you have made with Him, and by which you have obligated rights upon yourselves, and by which you have bound yourselves to God as obligations, so complete them with fulfillment, perfection, and completeness from you to God in what He has obligated you to do with them, and to whomever you have made a covenant with from among you, in what you have obligated to him by them upon yourselves, and do not break them, so that you do not violate them after confirming them. The people of interpretation differed regarding the contracts that God Almighty commanded to be fulfilled in this verse, after they all agreed that the meaning of contracts is the covenants. Some of them said: They are the contracts that the people of ignorance made with each other to support, assist, and defend against whoever tried to oppress them or wanted to harm them, and that is the meaning of the oath that they made among themselves. It was mentioned that the meaning of contracts is covenants. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Fulfill the contracts, meaning: the covenants. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Fulfill contracts, he said: covenants. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: We sat with Mutraf ibn al-Shakheer and there was a man with him talking to them, so he said: O you who have believed, fulfill your contracts, he said: They are the covenants. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Fulfill the contracts, he said: the covenants. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: O you who have believed, fulfill contracts, he said: They are the covenants. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Fulfill the contracts, meaning the covenants. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Fulfill contracts, he said: covenants. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Fulfill the contracts, he said: They are the covenants. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, I heard Al-Thawri say: Fulfill contracts, he said: covenants. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Jaafar said: “The word ‘aqd’ contracts is the plural of ‘aqd’ contract. The root of ‘aqd’ is to tie something to something else, which is to connect it to it, just as a rope is tied to a rope, if it is connected tightly to it. It is said: ‘So-and-so tied a contract between himself and so-and-so, so he ties it’. From this comes the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbor, tighten the ties and deviate from the path of distress. This is if he entrusts him with a matter and makes a covenant with him to fulfill what he agreed upon, whether it be security and protection, or support, or marriage, or sale, or partnership, or other contracts. Mention of the meaning that we mentioned about the one who said it regarding what is meant by his saying: “Fulfill the contracts.” Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: O you who have believed, fulfill your contracts, meaning: the contracts of the Age of Ignorance. He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Fulfill the contracts of the Age of Ignorance, and do not introduce new contracts in Islam. He mentioned to us that Furat bin Hayyan Al-Ajli asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the covenant of the Age of Ignorance, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps you are asking about the covenant of Lakhm and Taym God? He said: Yes, O Prophet of God! He said: Islam only increases its severity. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Fulfill the contracts, he said: the contracts of the Age of Ignorance, the oath. Others said: Rather, it is the oath that God took from His servants to believe in Him and obey Him, in what He permitted and prohibited for them. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Fulfill contracts, meaning: what is permissible and what is forbidden, what is obligatory, and what is set in the entire Qur’an, so do not betray or break them. Then he emphasized that by saying: And those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it and sever that which God has ordered to be joined, until His statement: The worst home (al-Ra’d 13:25). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Fulfill the contracts, what God has made a contract with the servants of what He has made permissible for them and what He has forbidden for them. Others said: Rather, they are the contracts that people make among themselves, and that a person makes for himself. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin Ubaidah, he said: There are five contracts: the contract of oaths, the contract of marriage, the contract of a covenant, the contract of sale, and the contract of an oath. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, or on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin Ubaidah, something similar. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: O you who have believed, fulfill contracts, he said: The contract of a covenant, the contract of an oath, the contract of an alliance, the contract of a partnership, and the contract of marriage. He said: These contracts are five. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Utbah bin Saeed Al-Himsi told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam told us, he said, my father told us regarding the statement of God Almighty: O you who have believed, fulfill your contracts, he said: Contracts are five: the marriage contract, the partnership contract, the oath contract, the covenant contract, and the oath contract. Others said: Rather, this verse is a command from God Almighty to the People of the Book to fulfill their covenant, to act in accordance with what is in the Torah and the Gospel in believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to them from God. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Fulfill the contracts, he said: The covenants that God took from the People of the Book: that they would do what was brought to them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, he said, Muhammad bin Muslim said: I read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he wrote to Amr bin Hazm when he sent him to Najran, and the letter was with Abu Bakr bin Hazm, in it: This is a statement from God and His Messenger: O you who have believed, fulfill contracts, so he wrote the verses from it until he reached Indeed, God is swift in account (al-Ma’idah 5:4). Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in our view, is what Ibn Abbas said, and that its meaning is: Fulfill, O you who believe, the contracts of God that He has made obligatory upon you, and made in what He has made lawful for you and forbidden for you, and obligated you to fulfill its duties, and made clear to you its limits. We said that this is more correct than other statements, because God, the Exalted, the Majestic, followed that explanation with what He has permitted and forbidden for His servants, and what He has made obligatory upon them of His obligations. So it was known from that that His statement, Fulfill the contracts, is a command from Him to His servants to do what He has made obligatory upon them of His obligations and contracts after that, and a prohibition from Him from them to break what He has made obligatory upon them of it, even though His statement, Fulfill the contracts, is a command from Him to fulfill every contract that He has permitted, so it is not permissible to specify something from it until there is evidence for specifying something from it that must be accepted. So since the matter in that is as we have described, there is no meaning to the statement of those who attributed that to the meaning of the command to fulfill some of the contracts that God has commanded to be fulfilled and not others. As for his saying: Fulfill, the Arabs have two dialects for it: One of them is: Fulfill, from the saying: I fulfilled my promise to so-and-so, I fulfilled it for him. The other is from their saying: I fulfilled my promise to him. And fulfilling the covenant is completing it according to the permissible conditions stipulated in the contract. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the cattle that God Almighty mentioned in this verse that He made lawful for us. Some of them said: It is all livestock. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The livestock are camels, cows, and sheep. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the animals of grazing livestock, he said: All livestock. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ibn Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: All livestock are lawful for you. He said: All livestock. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the livestock, he said: All livestock. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: The cattle of livestock, that is, livestock. Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying: Lawful to you are the livestock, are the fetuses of livestock that are found in the wombs of their mothers - if they are slaughtered or butchered - dead. Who said that? Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Omar, regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock. He said: What is in their bellies. I said: If it comes out dead, can I eat it? He said: Yes. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Idris Al-Awdi, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Omar, something similar, and he added to it, he said: Yes, it is like her lung and her liver. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The fetus of a livestock animal, so eat it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar and Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A cow was slaughtered and a fetus was found in its belly. Ibn Abbas took hold of the tail of the fetus and said: This is from the livestock that has been made lawful for you. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is from the livestock. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim and Muammal told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, he said: We slaughtered a cow, and there was a fetus in its belly, so we asked Ibn Abbas and he said: This is a livestock animal. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: What he meant by his statement, Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, is all livestock: their fetuses, young children, and adults. Because the Arabs do not refrain from calling all of that beasts and beasts, and God did not specify one of them over another. So that is according to its generality and appearance, until a proof comes for its specificity that must be accepted. As for blessings, among the Arabs, it is a name for camels, cows, and sheep in particular, as God Almighty said: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. (al-Nahl 16:5), then He said: And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment. (al-Nahl 16:8), so He separated the genus of blessings from other genus of animals. As for its cattle, they are its children. We said that the name beast applies to the adults, just as it does to the children, because the meaning of the speaker’s saying: beast of livestock, is similar to his saying: child of livestock. So since the meaning of birth does not fall away from it after it grows old, likewise the name beast does not fall away from it after it grows old. Some people said: The cattle means the wild animals, such as gazelles, wild cows, and donkeys. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed about what God meant by His saying: Except what is recited to you. Some of them said: God meant by that: He has made lawful for you the offspring of camels, cows, and sheep, except for what God has made clear to you in what is recited to you in His saying: He has forbidden you dead animals and blood, verse (al-Ma’idah 5:3). Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The livestock, except what is recited to you, except for dead animals and what is mentioned with them. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the animals of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, meaning: of the dead animals that God has forbidden, and he mentioned them first. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Except what is recited to you, he said: Except for dead meat and that over which the name of God has not been mentioned. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Except what is recited to you, dead meat, blood, and pork. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Lawful to you are the animals of cattle, except what is recited to you, dead animals and pork. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Lawful to you are the animals of cattle, except what is recited to you, meaning dead animals, blood, pork, and that which has been dedicated to someone other than God. Others said: Rather, what God excluded in His saying: Except what is recited to you, is the pig. Who said that? Abdullah bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except what is recited to you, he said: pigs. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Except what is recited to you, meaning: the pig. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: He meant by that: except what is recited to you of God’s prohibition of what He has prohibited to you in His saying: He has forbidden you dead animals (al-Ma’idah 5:3), the verse. Because God, the Almighty, has made an exception from what He has permitted His servants of livestock, what He has forbidden them from. And what He has forbidden them from is what He has explained in His saying: He has forbidden you dead animals, blood, and the flesh of swine (al-Ma’idah 5:3). Even if God has forbidden it to us, it is not from the livestock, so it can be excepted from it. So, excluding what He has forbidden to us from what is included in the group before the exception is more similar to excluding what He has forbidden from what is not included in the group before the exception. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: O you who believe, fulfill your contracts, “except for the game you hunt while you are in a state of ihram,” lawful to you are the animals of cattle. According to them, this is from the deferred particle which means the advancement. So other is accusative - according to the saying of those who say this statement - as a state of what is in His saying: fulfill from the mention of those who believe. The interpretation of the speech according to their doctrine is: Fulfill, O believers, the contracts of God that He made with you in His Book, and do not permit hunting while you are in a state of ihram. Others said: The meaning of this is: The wild animals of grazing livestock, such as gazelles, cows, and donkeys, have been made lawful for you, except for the game that is lawful, “except for what is recited to you.” So except for what is recited to you, according to these people, is in the accusative case as a state of the kaf and mim in His statement, for you, with the interpretation: The wild animals of grazing livestock have been made lawful for you, O you who believe, but not for the hunting of them that is lawful while you are in a state of ihram. Others said: The meaning of this is: All livestock are lawful to you, except what is recited to you, except what is wild, for it is game, and it is not lawful to you while you are in a state of ihram. So it is as if the one who said this directed the speech to the meaning: All livestock are lawful to you, except what is recited to you, except what is clear to you of its wild animals, except that it is not lawful to hunt it while you are in a state of ihram. So ghair is in the accusative case, according to what they say, as a state of kaf and mim in His statement: except what is recited to you. Who said that? Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Ubayd God narrated, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: We sat with Mutraf ibn al-Shakheer, and there was a man with him, so he spoke to them and said: Lawful to you are the animals of the livestock as game, except the game that is lawful while you are in a state of ihram, so it is forbidden to you. He meant: wild cows, gazelles, and the like. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, excluding game while you are in a state of ihram, he said: All livestock is lawful, except for what is wild, for it is game, so it is not lawful if one is in a state of ihram. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter - based on the interpretation of the people of interpretation of His statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, that is, the livestock, their fetuses, and their young, and based on the apparent meaning of the revelation - is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Fulfill the contracts, except for the hunting while you are in a state of ihram, for the beasts of grazing livestock have been made lawful to you during your state of ihram or other than your state, except for what is recited to you as being forbidden, such as dead animals, blood, and what has been dedicated to someone other than God. This is because if his statement, except what is recited to you, meant except for the game, it would have been said, except for what is recited to you of the game that is not local. And in leaving out God’s connection of his statement, except for what is recited to you, to what I mentioned, and showing the mention of the game in his statement, except for the game that is local, is the clearest evidence that his statement, except for what is recited to you, is report of a finite story, and that the meaning of his statement, except for the game that is local, is separate from it. Likewise, if his statement, Lawful to you are the beasts of prey, was intended to mean wild animals, there would also be no point in repeating the mention of the game in his statement, except for the game that is lawful, and this has been mentioned before. It would have been said, Lawful to you are the beasts of prey, except for what is recited to you, except for the game that is lawful while you are in a state of ihram. And in his explicit mention of the game in his statement, except for the game that is lawful, I make clear the evidence for the correctness of what we said about the meaning of that. If someone says: The Arabs may have mentioned something by its name, even though it has been mentioned by its name? It was said: This is from her doing it out of poetic necessity, and it is not the eloquent language used in their speech. And directing the speech of God to the most eloquent of the languages of the one in whose language His speech was revealed is more appropriate - if there is a way to do so - than diverting it to something else. Abu Ja`far said: The meaning of the statement then is: O you who believe, fulfill the contracts that God has made with you of what He has forbidden and permitted, not making hunting permissible in your sanctuary. In what is permissible for you of slaughtered livestock, but not its dead meat, there is plenty for you and you do not need to hunt while you are in a state of ihram. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God decrees for His creation what He wills, of making permissible what He wills to make permissible, and forbidding what He wills to forbid, and obligating what He wills to oblige them, and other than that of His rulings and decrees. So, O believers, fulfill what He has made binding upon you of making permissible what He has made permissible for you and forbidding what He has made forbidden for you, and other than that of His contracts, and do not break them or violate them, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, God decrees what He wills, God decrees what He wills in His creation, and He made clear to His servants, and imposed His obligations, and set His limits, and commanded obedience to Him, and forbade disobedience to Him.
5:2: Abu Ja`far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of God’s statement: Do not violate the symbols of God. Some of them said that it means: Do not violate the sacred limits of God, and do not transgress His boundaries, as if they directed the symbols to landmarks, and they interpreted Do not violate the symbols of God as the landmarks of God’s boundaries, His commands, His prohibitions, and His obligations. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab Al Thaqafi told us, he said, Habib Al Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Ata’: that he was asked about the rites of God, so he said: The prohibitions of God, avoiding the wrath of God, and following His obedience, so that is the rites of God. Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not violate the sanctuary of God. It is as if they directed the meaning of his saying: the symbols of God to mean: the landmarks of God’s sanctuary in the country. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God. He said: As for the rites of God, God has forbidden. Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not violate the rituals of Hajj and waste them, and it is as if they directed the interpretation of this to: Do not violate the landmarks of the limits of God that He has set for you in your Hajj. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement: Do not violate the rites of God, he said: the rituals of Hajj. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God, he said: The polytheists used to perform Hajj to the Sacred House, and bring gifts, and venerate the sanctity of the sacred sites, and trade during their Hajj, so the Muslims wanted to attack them, so God Almighty said: Do not violate the symbols of God. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: The symbols of God, Safa and Marwa, the sacrificial animals, and the sacrificial animals, all of this is from the symbols of God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not make permissible what God has forbidden you while you are in a state of ihram. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Do not violate the rites of God, he said: The rites of God are what God has forbidden you to do while you are in a state of ihram. It is as if those who said this article intended to interpret it as: Do not violate the boundaries of God’s limits that He has forbidden you during your state of ihram. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate interpretation of his statement, Do not violate the rites of God, is the statement of Ata’ that we mentioned, from his directing the meaning of that to: Do not violate the sacred things of God and do not neglect His obligations. Because rituals is the plural of ritual, and ritual is a verbal noun from the saying: So-and-so felt this matter, if he knew about it. So rituals, landmarks, are from that. If this is the case, then the meaning of the statement is: Do not consider permissible, O you who believe, the signs of God. This includes all of God’s signs in the rituals of Hajj: from prohibiting what God has prohibited for the pilgrim to do therein, and neglecting what He has forbidden to neglect therein, and what He has prohibited of making permissible the prohibitions He has forbidden, and other than that of His limits and obligations, and what He has permitted and prohibited, because all of that is from His signs and rituals that He has made signs between truth and falsehood, by which He knows what is permissible and what is prohibited, and what He has commanded and prohibited. We said that this statement is more appropriate for the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Do not violate the symbols of God, because God forbade making His symbols and the landmarks of His boundaries permissible and making them permissible in a general prohibition, without specifying one thing over another. So it is not shameful for anyone to direct the meaning of that to the specific except with an argument that must be accepted, and there is no argument for that as well. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His saying: nor the sacred month, and do not make the sacred month permissible by fighting your enemies from among the polytheists in it. It is like His saying: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, ‘Fighting in it is a great sin.’” (al-Baqarah 2:217) Ibn Abbas and others said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: nor the sacred month, meaning: do not permit fighting in it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The polytheists at that time were not prevented from entering the House, so they were ordered not to fight in the sacred month or at the House. As for the sacred month that God meant by His saying: nor the sacred month, it is Rajab of Mudar, which is a month in which Mudar forbade fighting. It has been said: It is in this place Dhu al-Qi'dah. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It is Dhul-Qi’dah. We have already explained the evidence for the correctness of what we said about this in the past, and that was in the interpretation of His statement: They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein (al-Baqarah 2:217). Abu Jaafar said: As for the offering, it is what a person offers of a camel, cow, sheep, or other, to the House of God, drawing closer to God and seeking His reward. God Almighty says: Do not consider it permissible, so that you do not usurp it from its people by force, and do not prevent them from reaching the place that God Almighty has made its place in His Kaaba. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the gift is only a gift if it is not tied around the neck. Muhammad bin Saad told me that, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: nor the offering, he said: The offering is what has not been adorned, and he has made it his duty to offer it and adorn it. As for his saying: nor necklaces, he means: nor do you untie the necklaces. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the necklaces that God the Almighty forbade us to make permissible. Some of them said: By necklaces, He meant the necklaces of the sacrificial animals. They said: God the Almighty meant by His saying: nor the sacrificial animals nor the necklaces, and do not make permissible the gifts that are adorned or not. So His saying: nor the sacrificial animals, is the gifts that are not adorned, nor the necklaces, is the adorned ones. They said: And His saying: nor the necklaces, indicates the meaning of what He meant by the prohibition of making permissible the gifts that are adorned. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: nor necklaces, necklaces are the adornments of the sacrificial animal. And if a man adorns his sacrificial animal, then he has entered ihram. So if he does that while he is wearing his shirt, then he should take it off. Others said: What he meant by that was the necklaces that the polytheists would wear when they wanted to go on the Hajj, coming to Mecca, made of samr bark, and when they left it to their homes, returning from it, made of hair. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month. He said: When a man in the Age of Ignorance left his house intending to perform Hajj, he would wear a necklace of thorns, and no one would bother him. Then when he returned, he would wear a necklace of hair, and no one would bother him. Others said: Rather, if a man among them wanted to leave the sanctuary, or left, he would wear a necklace made of the bark of the trees of the sanctuary, thus ensuring that the rest of the Arab tribes would not harm him. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of Ata’: nor necklaces, he said: They used to wear necklaces made of the bark of the trees of the sanctuary, and they would be safe with that if they left the sanctuary, then the verse was revealed: Do not violate the rites of God, the verse, nor the offerings nor the necklaces. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: nor the necklaces, he said: The necklaces are the bark around the necks of people and animals, they are safe for them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: nor the offerings nor the necklaces, he said: The Arabs used to wear necklaces made of the bark of the trees of Mecca, and a man would stay in his place, until the sacred months had passed and he wanted to return to his family, he would wear necklaces made of the bark of the tree for himself and his camel, and he would be safe until he reached his family. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, nor necklaces, he said: The necklaces, a man would take the bark of a tree from the trees of the sanctuary, put it on a necklace, then go wherever he wanted, and he would be safe thereby. So that is the necklaces. Others said: God forbade the believers by saying: nor necklaces, from removing anything from the trees of the sanctuary and wearing it as necklaces, as the polytheists used to do in their pre-Islamic era. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: nor the offerings nor the garlands, the polytheists used to take from the trees of Mecca, from the bark of the samr tree, and wear them as garlands, so that they would be safe from the people. So God forbade uprooting its trees and wearing garlands. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: We sat with Mutraf ibn al-Shakheer, and there was a man with him, so he told them about His statement, nor necklaces. He said: The polytheists used to take from the trees of Mecca, from the bark of the samr tree, and they would wear necklaces with it to secure themselves from the people. So God, the Exalted, forbade uprooting its trees and wearing necklaces. Abu Ja`far said: What is more appropriate to interpret his statement: nor necklaces, since it was connected to the beginning of the speech, and there was nothing in the speech that indicated that it was disconnected from its beginning, nor that it meant by it the prohibition of wearing necklaces or making necklaces of anything, is that its meaning is: And do not loosen the necklaces. Since this is more appropriate in its interpretation, it is known that it is a prohibition from God, the Most High, against violating the sanctity of the imitator, whether it is a gift or a human being, but not the sanctity of the necklace. And God, the Most High, indicated by His prohibition of the sanctity of the necklace what we mentioned about the sanctity of the imitator, so He sufficed by mentioning necklaces instead of mentioning the imitator, since the meaning intended by it was understood by those addressed by that. The meaning of the verse - since the matter is as we have described - is: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the one who adorns himself with the necklaces of the sanctuary. Some poets mentioned in his poetry what we mentioned about those who interpreted necklaces as necklaces made of the bark of the trees of the sanctuary that the people of the pre-Islamic era used to wear. He said, while criticizing two men who killed two men who were wearing that necklace: Didn't you kill the two blind men when they passed by with their braided bark hands? And the two who were killed, the same. And the meaning of his saying: He made you blind, is that He gave you access to their private parts. Abu Jaafar said: What he meant by the words of God Almighty: nor those who enter the Sacred House, is that those who intend to enter the Sacred House intentionally should not be permitted to do so. You say: I intended such-and-such, if you intended it and headed towards it. Some of them say: I intended it, as the poet said: I am like that, if a country does not please me, I head with my camel to another country. And the Sacred House is the House of God in Mecca. I have previously explained why it was called the Sacred House. They seek bounty from their Lord, meaning: they seek profits from God in their trade, and Our pleasure, meaning: that God be pleased with them through their rituals. It has been said that this verse was revealed about a man from Banu Rabi’ah called Al-Hatim. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: Al-Hatim ibn Hind al-Bakri, one of the Banu Qays ibn Tha’labah, came until he reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, and his cavalry was leaving Medina. So he called him and said: What are you calling for? So he informed him - and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to his companions: A man from Rabi’ah will enter upon you today, speaking with the tongue of Satan! - So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed him, he said: Wait, and perhaps I will become Muslim, and I have someone to consult. So he left him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He entered with the face of an unbeliever, and left with the heel of a traitor! So he passed by a herd of camels from Medina and drove it away, and he went away while he was reciting: The night has enveloped her with a broken driver who is neither a camel nor a sheep herder. Nor a butcher on the back of the camel, they spent the night asleep, and Ibn Hind did not sleep A young man, with sluggish legs and a sore foot, is suffering from it. Then he came one year and met a pilgrim who had been given a necklace and a gift, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to send to him, so this verse was revealed, until he reached: nor a person who is entrusted with the Sacred House. Some of his companions said to him: O Messenger of God, leave us alone with him, for he is our companion! He said: He has been given a necklace! They said: It is only something we used to do in the pre-Islamic era! But he refused them, so this verse was revealed. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Al-Hutm, the brother of Banu Dhubay’ah ibn Tha’labah Al-Bakri, came to Madinah with a caravan of his carrying food, and he sold it. Then he entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he pledged allegiance to him and became a Muslim. When he turned away, he looked at him and said to those with him: He has entered upon me with an evil face and turned away with a treacherous back! When he arrived at Yamamah, he apostatized from Islam and went out with his caravan carrying food in Dhul-Qa’dah, heading to Makkah. When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of him, a group of the Muhajireen and Ansar prepared to go out to him to seize his caravan. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God, the verse, and the people stopped. Ibn Jurayj said: His statement: nor the one who is safe from the Sacred House, he said: He forbids the pilgrims from blocking their paths. He said: That is because Al-Hatim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to explore and see, and he said: I am a caller to a people, so tell me what you say! He said to him: I call you to God, to worship Him and not associate anything with Him, to establish prayer, to pay zakat, to fast the month of Ramadan, and to perform Hajj to the House. Al-Hatim said: In this matter of yours there is harshness, go back to my people and tell them what you have mentioned, if they accept it I will come with them, and if they turn away I will be with them. He said to him: Go back. So when he left he said: He entered upon me with the face of an unbeliever, and left me with my heels treacherously, and the man is not a Muslim! He passed by a herd of the people of Medina and set off with it. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sought him, but he escaped them. He went to Yamamah and attended the Hajj, and he prepared to go out. He was a great trader, so they asked permission to meet him and take what he had with him. Then God Almighty revealed: Do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the garlands, nor the custodians of the Sacred House. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: nor those who visit the Sacred House the verse, he said: This was on the day of the conquest, when some people from the polytheists came to the House, entering ihram for Umrah, so the Muslims said: O Messenger of God, these are polytheists like those, so we will not leave them alone unless we attack them. So the Qur’an was revealed: nor those who visit the Sacred House. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the one who is at the Sacred House, he said: the one who sets out on a pilgrimage. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: nor the one who is at the Sacred House, meaning: the pilgrim. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said: We sat with Mutraf bin al-Shakheer and there was a man with him, so he told them and said: And not the one who is safe at the Sacred House, he said: Those who want the House. Then the scholars differed about what was abrogated from this verse, after their consensus that some of it was abrogated. Some of them said: All of them were abrogated. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Amer, he said: Nothing was abrogated from Al-Ma’idah except this verse: Do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the garlands. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God, it was abrogated by, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said, nothing was abrogated from Surat al-Ma’idah except this verse: O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month 9:5, he said: It is abrogated. He said: The polytheists at that time were not prevented from entering the House, so they were commanded not to fight during the sacred months, nor at the House, so it was abrogated by his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them 9:5. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Do not violate the symbols of God until His saying: nor those who enter the Sacred House. He said: It was abrogated by Bara’ah: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, the same. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit: Do not violate the rites of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the necklaces. He said: This is something that was forbidden, so it was left as it is. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month or the offerings or the garlands or those entering the Sacred House, he said: All of this is abrogated. This abrogated His command to fight them all. Others said: What was abrogated from this verse is His statement: nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor the custodians of the Sacred House. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdah bin Sulayman told us, he said, I read to Ibn Abi Arubah and he said: This is how I heard it from Qatada: Ameen of the Sacred House was abrogated from Al-Ma’idah, it was abrogated by Bara’ah. God said: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5), and He said: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief (al-Tawbah 9:17), and He said: The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs (al-Tawbah 9:28), which is the year in which Abu Bakr performed Hajj and called out the call to prayer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God (9:5), he said: So he abrogated from it: Avoiding the Sacred House, Bara’ah abrogated it, so he said: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (9:5), and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abdah. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: The following verse was revealed regarding the destruction of the house: nor the offerings, nor the garlands, nor the guards of the Sacred House, then God abrogated it and said: And kill them wherever you find them (al-Baqarah 2:191). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: Do not violate the symbols of God until his saying: nor those who are at the House, so the believers and the polytheists would all perform Hajj to the House. So God forbade the believers from preventing anyone from performing Hajj to the House or interfering with it, whether a believer or a disbeliever. Then God revealed after this: The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs (al-Tawbah 9:28), and He said: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God (al-Tawbah 9:17), and He said: The mosques of God shall only be maintained by those who believe in God and the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9:18), so He banished the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement: Do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month the verse, he said: It is abrogated. When a man in the Age of Ignorance went out of his house intending to perform Hajj, he would put on a necklace of palm leaves and no one would interfere with him. And when he returned, he would put on a necklace of hair and no one would interfere with him. And the polytheist at that time was not prevented from entering the House. And they were commanded not to fight during the sacred months, nor near the House, so it was abrogated by the statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Others said: Nothing of that was abrogated, except the necklaces that were worn during the pre-Islamic era from tree bark. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month, the verse, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of this is from the actions of the Age of Ignorance, its doing and its establishment, so God forbade all of that in Islam, except for the barking of necklaces, so that was abandoned, nor the one who is at the Sacred House, so God forbade anyone from frightening them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: God abrogated from this verse His statement: nor the sacred month nor the offerings nor the garlands nor those at the Sacred House, because of the consensus of all that God has permitted fighting the polytheists in the sacred months and other months of the year. Likewise, they agreed that if a polytheist were to hang the bark of all the trees of the sanctuary around his neck or arms, that would not be a protection for him from being killed, if he had not received a covenant of protection from the Muslims or a protection. We have previously explained the meaning of garlands in other places. As for his statement: nor the one who is in the Sacred House, it is possible to say: And do not violate the sanctity of the one who is in the Sacred House from the people of polytheism and Islam, because it is general for all who visit the House. If that is possible, then the people of polytheism are included in their group, then there is no doubt that his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5), abrogates it. Because it is not permissible for the command to kill them and not kill them to be combined in one situation and at one time. And in the consensus of all that the ruling of God regarding the people of war from the polytheists is to kill them when they visit the Sacred House and the Holy House, during the sacred months and other than them, what is known is that the prohibition of killing them if they visit the Sacred House is abrogated. It is also possible: Nor the one who is in the Sacred House from the people of polytheism. Most of the interpreters agree on this. If he meant the polytheists among the people of war, then it is also undoubtedly abrogated. Since this is the case, and there is no apparent difference between them in this regard, and what was widespread among them was apparent as evidence, then it is obligatory, even if it could have a meaning other than what they said, to submit to what was widely reported as being correct. Abu Ja`far said: What he means by his saying: They seek, they ask and look for, and the best is the profits in trade, and the pleasure, may God be pleased with them, so that the punishment in this world will not befall them as it was inflicted upon other nations in their immediate world, because of their pilgrimage to His House. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval, he said: They are the polytheists, seeking God’s bounty and approval in what is good for them in their worldly life. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, he said, I read to Ibn Abi Arubah and he said: This is how I heard it from Qatada regarding his statement: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval. And the bounty and approval that they seek? That their livelihood in this world be improved, and that punishment not be hastened for them in it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval, meaning: they seek to please God with their Hajj. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: We sat with Mutraf ibn al-Shakheer, and there was a man with him, so he told them about His statement: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval, he said: Trade is in the Hajj, and approval is in the Hajj. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Umaimah, he said, Ibn `Umar said about a man who performs Hajj and carries provisions with him, he said: There is nothing wrong with it, and he recited this verse: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval, he said: They seek reward and trade. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt the game that I forbade you from catching while you were in a state of ihram. He says: There is no blame upon you for hunting it, and hunt if you wish then, because the meaning for which I forbade it to you while you were in a state of ihram has disappeared. And what we said about that was said by all the people of interpretation. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession, meaning his statement: And when you are released from ihram, then hunt. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: There are five things in the Book of God that are permissible, but not obligatory. Then he mentioned: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt, he said: Whoever wants to do so may do so, and whoever wants to not do so may not do so. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt. He said: When he is in a state of ihram, if he wants to hunt, he may hunt, and if he wants to, he may not hunt. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid: that he did not consider eating from the sacrificial animal of pleasure to be obligatory, and he interpreted this verse: And when you are in a state of ihram, hunt, “And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land” (al-Jumuah 62:10). Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And let not the evil of yourselves is: And let not the evil of yourselves and do not burden you, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing so, meaning: Do not let the hatred of a people cause you to do so. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing so, meaning: let it not make you bear it. As for those who know the language, they differed in its interpretation. Some of the Basrans said: The meaning of his saying: And let not the Fire be a crime against you is: It is not right for you, because his saying: It is certain that they will have the Fire (al-Nahl 16:62) means: It is true that they will have the Fire. Some of the Kufians said: Its meaning is: Do not let him burden you. He said: It is said: So-and-so made me do such-and-such, meaning: he burdened me with it. And all of them provided evidence with the poet’s verse: I stabbed Abu Uyaynah with a stab that made Fazara angry after that. Each group of them interpreted this according to the meaning they interpreted from the Qur’an. Those who said, Do not let it make you guilty said, Do not let it make you guilty, meaning the poet’s words: Fazara has committed a crime, the stab wound deserved Fazara’s anger. Those who said: Its meaning is: Do not let it make you angry. Its meaning in the verse is: Fazara committed a crime by becoming angry. Fazara committed a crime by becoming angry. Another of the Kufians said: The meaning of his saying: Do not let hatred of a people cause you to sin is: Do not let hatred of a people cause you to sin. The interpretation of the speaker of this statement is the poet’s statement in the verse: Fazara committed a crime, Fazara earned that they should be angry. He said: I heard the Arabs say: So-and-so committed the crime of his people, meaning: he earned them, and he went out to commit a crime against them, he earned them. Abu Jaafar said: These sayings that we have narrated from those we have narrated them from are close in meaning. That is because whoever makes a man hate another man has earned his hatred. And whoever earns his hatred has earned it for him. If that is the case, then what is better in clarifying the meaning of the letter is what Ibn Abbas and Qatada said, and that is their explanation of the meaning of his statement: And let not the hatred of a people incite you to aggression, and let not the hatred of a people lead you to aggression. There are different readings of this. The majority of the countries read it as: And let him not commit a crime with the opening of the ya from: jaramtuhu he committed a crime. Some of the Kufians recited this, namely Yahya bin Waththab and Al-A’mash: what: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, that he read: And let not he cause you harm, with the ya raised, from: I caused him harm, and he causes harm to me. Abu Ja`far said: What is more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it: And let him not commit a sin with the opening of the ya’, because of the prevalence of that reading in the readings of the regions, and the anomaly of what differs from it, and that it is the well-known language used by the Arabs, even though it is heard from some of them: ajram yajram according to its anomaly. And reading the Qur’an in the most eloquent languages is more appropriate and more deserving than anything else. And from the language of the one who said jarmat is the saying of the poet: O you who complain about Akl and what you have done to the tribes of killing and misery There are different readings of this. Some of them read it as shan’an by moving the sheen and the noon to the fatha, meaning: hatred of a people, directing that to the source that comes in the form of fa’laan, like flying, an-naslaan, aslaan, and ar-ramlaan. Others read it as: shan’an qawm with a sukoon on the nun and a fatha on the shin meaning: the name, directing its meaning to: do not let the hatred of a people make you bear it, so shan’an is derived on the basis of fa’laan, because fa’l is derived from fa’l, just as it is said: sakran from sakara, and ‘athan from ‘atash, and similar names. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of those who read: Hanan qawm with the fat-ha on the nun, due to the common interpretation of the people of interpretation that its meaning is: hatred of a people, and their referring that to the meaning of the source rather than the meaning of the noun. Since this was directed to the meaning of the source, the eloquent speech of the Arabs in what came from the sources is on the form of the verb fa’laan with the opening of the fa’, moving the second without making it silent, as described in their saying: darajan and ramlaan, from daraj and ramal, so also hatred from shun’atu ashuhu shanan, and some of the Arabs say: shan’an with the estimation of fa’al, and I do not know of a reader who read it in this way, and from that is the saying of the poet: Life is nothing but what you enjoy and desire, even if the one who has hatred and resentment criticizes it. This is in the language of those who omitted the hamza from hatred, so it became on the assumption of fa’al, which is originally fa’lan. It was mentioned that some of the interpreters said: Hatred of a people means hatred of a people. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing so, do not let the hatred of a people cause you to do so. Al-Muthanna told me it again with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not let the enmity of a people cause you to transgress. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing so, let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing so. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing aggression, he said: Their hatred, that you transgress. Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed. Some of the people of Medina and most of the Kufians read it as: that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of that, meaning: Do not let the hatred of a people for preventing you from entering the Sacred Mosque cause you to transgress. Some of the readers of Hijaz and Basra used to read it as: And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you if they turn you away, with a kasra on the alif of in, meaning: And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you if they create a barrier for you from the Sacred Mosque, from transgressing. They claimed that in Ibn Masoud’s reading it was: If they turn you away, so they read it like that, taking into consideration his reading. Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings that are famous in the readings of the regions, and the meaning of each one of them is correct. This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were prevented from the House on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and Surat al-Ma’idah was revealed to him after that. So whoever reads that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of that, its meaning is: Do not let the hatred of a people, O people, because they prevented you on the day of Hudaybiyyah from the Sacred Mosque, lead you to transgress against them. And whoever reads: that they prevented you with a kasra on the alif, its meaning is: Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you if they prevent you from the Sacred Mosque if you wanted to enter it. Because those who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Quraysh on the day of the conquest of Mecca, had tried to prevent them from the Sacred Mosque. So God proceeded to the believers - according to the one who read it with a kasra on that - by forbidding aggression against them, if they prevented them from the Sacred Mosque, before that happened from the preventers. However, even if the matter is as you have described, reading it with the opening of the alif is clearer in meaning. Because there is no dispute among scholars that this surah was revealed after the day of Hudaybiyyah. Since that is the case, the prevention had already occurred on the part of the polytheists, so God forbade the believers from attacking those who prevented them from entering the Sacred Mosque. As for his saying: that you transgress, he means: that you exceed the limit that God has set for you in their matter. The interpretation of the verse is: O believers, do not let the hatred of a people, because they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque, lead you to transgress God’s ruling regarding them, and go beyond it to what He has forbidden you, but adhere to obeying God in what you like and dislike. He mentioned that it was revealed to prohibit seeking the wealth of the pre-Islamic era. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: that you transgress, a believing man from among the allies of Muhammad, killed an ally of Abu Sufyan from Hudhayl on the day of the conquest at Arafat, because he used to kill the allies of Muhammad, so Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse whoever kills with the filth of the Age of Ignorance. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: This is abrogated. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from doing what is not lawful for you, he said: Their hatred, until you do what is not lawful for you. And he recited: Because they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque from transgressing and cooperating, and he said: All of this has been abrogated, abrogated by jihad. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is Mujahid’s opinion that it is not abrogated, because it is possible that you will transgress the truth in what I have commanded you to do. If that is possible, it is not permissible to say that it is abrogated, except with an argument that must be accepted. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His saying: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and let some of you, O believers, help others, in righteousness, which is doing what God has commanded us to do, and piety, which is avoiding what God has commanded us to avoid and avoid of His sins. And His statement: And do not cooperate in sin and aggression, meaning: Do not help one another, in sin, meaning: in abandoning what God has commanded you to do, and aggression, meaning: do not exceed what God has set for you in your religion, and what He has imposed on you in yourselves and in others. The meaning of the statement is: Do not let hatred of a people who prevented you from the Sacred Mosque prevent you from transgressing. Rather, let some of you help others by ordering them to desist from what God has set for you regarding the people who prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and others, and to desist from what God has forbidden you to do regarding them and others, and in all the rest of what He has forbidden you from doing. Do not help others in doing otherwise. And what we said about righteousness and piety was said by the people of interpretation. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, righteousness is what I have commanded, and piety is what I have forbidden. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abi Al-Aaliyah, regarding his statement: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, he said: Righteousness is what I have commanded, and piety is what I have forbidden. Abu Ja`far said: This is a warning from God, the Most High, and a warning to those who transgress His limits and exceed His commands. God, the Most High, says: And fear God, meaning: O believers, beware of God, lest you meet Him in your place of resurrection having transgressed His limits in what He has set for you, and disobeyed His command in what He has commanded you to do, or His prohibition in what He has prohibited you from doing, so you deserve His punishment and are deserving of His painful torment. Then He described His punishment as severe, saying: God is severe in His punishment to those of His creation who punish Him, because it is a fire whose heat cannot be extinguished, whose embers cannot be extinguished, and whose flames cannot subside. We seek refuge in God from it and from an action that brings us closer to it.
5:3: Abu Jaafar said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God has forbidden you, O believers, dead animals. Dead: is everything that has a flowing soul from the land animals and birds, which God has permitted to be eaten, whether domestic or wild, and whose soul has departed without being slaughtered. Some of them said: Dead is everything that has departed from life from the land animals and birds without being slaughtered, and which God has permitted to be eaten. We have explained the reason for the validity of what we have said in this regard in our book, A Book of Delicate Words on Rulings. As for blood, it is spilled blood, not what was not spilled, because God Almighty said: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it, unless it be a dead animal, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine.’ (al-An’am 6:145), but as for what has become like meat, such as the liver and spleen, and what was in the meat that was not spilled, then that is not forbidden, because everyone has agreed on that. As for his saying: and the meat of pigs, he means: And the meat of pigs is forbidden to you, whether domestic or wild. As for dead meat and blood, their apparent meaning is general, but what is meant by them is specific. As for pork, its appearance is like its interior, and its interior is like its appearance. It is all forbidden, and nothing has been specified. As for his saying: And what is dedicated to other than God, he means: And what is mentioned over it is not the name of God. Its origin is from the baby’s cry of ascent, when he cries when he falls from his mother’s womb. And from it is the pilgrim’s cry of ascent for Hajj, when he responds to it, and from it is the saying of Ibn Ahmar: Its riders arrive at Al-Farqad as a pilgrim arrives for Umrah What he meant by his saying: And what is dedicated to other than God is what is slaughtered for gods and idols, and is called by a name other than God’s. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation, and we mentioned the narration from those who said that in the past, so we disliked repeating it. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the strangulation that God Almighty meant by His saying: and the strangled. Some of them said: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And the strangled one he said: The one who puts her head between two branches of a tree, so she strangles and dies. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding the strangled one, he said: the one who strangles and dies. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: and the strangled, that which dies in its strangulation. Others said: It is the one who is tied up and killed by strangulation. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: and the strangled, he said: The sheep is tied up, and its strangulation kills it, so it is forbidden. Others said: Rather, it is an animal from the blessings, the polytheists used to strangle it until it died, so God forbade eating it. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the strangled one is the one who is strangled and dies. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the strangled one, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to strangle the sheep, and when it died, they would eat it. The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: It is the one that is strangled, either by its chains, or by inserting its head into a place from which it is unable to escape, so it suffocates until it dies. We said that this is more correct in interpreting it than anything else, because the one who is strangled is the one described by strangulation, without the strangulation of others. If what was meant by that was that it was the object of the action, it would have been said: and the one who is strangled, so that the meaning of the speech would be what they said. Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: and the one who is beaten to death, and the one who is killed by a sword. It is said: He struck him until he was on the verge of death. And from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: A young camel that kicks the young camel with its foot, a prey for the young camels And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the one who is struck with a stick, he said: The one who is struck with a stick is the one who is struck with wood until she is struck with it and dies. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the one who was beaten to death, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to beat it with sticks, until when it died, they would eat it. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And the one who was beaten, he said: They would beat it until they made it vomit, then they would eat it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: and the one who is struck by lightning, that which is struck and dies. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said: The one who is beaten to death is the one who is struck. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And the one who is struck with a blow, he said: It is the one who is struck and dies. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the one beaten to death, that a sheep or other livestock was beaten with wood for their gods, until they killed it and ate it. Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told us, he said, Uqbah bin Alqamah told me, Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla told me, he said, Naim bin Salamah told me, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Sanabhi, he said: The one who is killed is only in Malik, and there is no killing in hunting. Abu Jaafar said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And you are forbidden to eat dead animals that fall from a mountain or into a well, or otherwise. And to throw herself from a high, honorable place to the bottom. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the one who falls down, he said: the one who falls down from the mountain. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the one who falls into the well, she would fall into the well and die, and they would eat her. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The one who fell into the well, he said: The one who fell into the well. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: and the one who falls, he said: It is the one who falls from the mountain, or into the well, and dies. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: The one who falls is the one who falls from the mountain and dies. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the one who falls down, he said: The one who falls into a well, or from the top of a mountain, and dies. Abu Jaafar said: What he means by his saying: the gored one, is the sheep that is gored by another one and dies from the goring without being slaughtered. So God, the Most High, has forbidden that to the believers, if they do not slaughter it before its death. The root of the word natiha is mantuha, which was changed from maf’ulah to fa’ila. If someone says: How did you prove the feminine ha’ in it, while you know that the Arabs hardly prove the ha’ in similar words when they inflect them like natiha from maf’ul to fa’il, rather they say: a greasy beard, a kohl-lined eye, and a dyed hand, but they do not say: a dyed hand, nor a kohl-lined eye? It was said: The Arabists differed on this - some of the grammarians of Basra said: The ha’ was proven in it, I mean in the word natiha - because it was made like a noun, such as: al-tawila and al-tariqah.
