Others who said this statement said: There is no limit to the knowledge of dogs about that from their dog, more than if their dog did what we described as teaching him. They said: If he did that, then he became a teacher whose hunting was permissible. This is the opinion of some of the later scholars. Some of those who said this article differentiated between teaching the hawk and other birds of prey and teaching the dog and other predatory beasts of prey. He said: It is permissible to eat what the hawk has eaten from the game. They said: The hawk is only taught to fly when it is called, to respond when it is called, and not to flee from its owner if he wants to take it. They said: It is not one of the conditions of teaching it that it not eat from the game. Who said that? Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: There is nothing wrong with hunting a hawk, even if one eats some of it. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said, Abu Ishaq al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about the bird: If you release it and it kills, then eat. But if you hit the dog, it will not return. Because the bird is taught to return to its owner, and it is not hit if it eats from the hunt and plucks its feathers. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: The hawk and the falcon are not like the dog. If you send them out and they catch up and eat, and you call them and they come to you, then eat from it. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Zaid told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Hammad, Ibrahim said: All the prey of the falcon is eaten from it. Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim and Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, they said: Everyone who hunts a falcon, even if he eats it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim: If the hawk or the falcon eats from the prey, then eat, for it does not know. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim Fal: There is nothing wrong with what the falcon eats. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Hammad: that he said about the falcon when it eats from it, he said: Eat. Others among them said: It is the same as teaching birds, beasts, and wild animals. None of these types is taught except by what all other types are taught. They said: It is not permissible to eat anything from the game that a bird of prey hunted and ate from, regardless of whether that bird of prey was a beast or a bird. They said: Because one of the conditions for its training that makes its game permissible is that it holds back what it hunts for its owner, and does not eat from it. Who said that? Hanad and Abu Kuraib told us, they said, Ibn Abi Zaida told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Salim told us, on the authority of Amer Fal: Ali said: If the falcon eats from its prey, do not eat. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mujalid bin Sa`id, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi, he said: If the falcon eats from it, do not eat from it. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: If the hawk eats, do not eat. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Walid Al-Shani, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: If the hawk eats, do not eat. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Ata’ said: The dog and the hawk are all the same. Do not eat what it has eaten from the game, unless you find it slaughtered, then slaughter it. He said, I said to Ata’: The hawk plucks feathers? He said: So whatever you find and it has not eaten, then eat. He said that more than once. Others said: The training of every animal and bird is one. They said: The training that makes its prey permissible is that it stalks the prey, pulls it out and takes the prey, and its owner calls it and it responds, and does not flee from it if it takes it. They said: So if the bird of prey does that, it is a teacher included in the meaning of which God said: And what you have taught of birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you, so eat of what they catch for you. They said: It is not a condition of teaching that to someone who does not eat from the prey. They said: How can it be permissible for someone whose condition is that, and he disciplines by eating it? Those who said that mentioned: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed - or Saad - on the authority of Salman, he said: If you send your dog to hunt, and you mention the name of God, and it eats two-thirds of it and one-third remains, then eat what remains. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Humayd told us, al-Qasim ibn Rabi`ah told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Salman - and Bakr ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Salman - about the dog that takes prey and eats from it, he said: Eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it, if you send it out and mention the name of God, and it is trained. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, he said: I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Al-Musayyab, he said: Salman said: Eat, even if he eats two-thirds of it, meaning: the game if a dog eats from it. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Samad told us, on the authority of Shu’bah - H and Hannad told us, he said, Abdah told us - all of them, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said, Salman said: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God, and it eats two-thirds of it and one-third of it remains, then eat. Hanad told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Salman, something similar. Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzani and Al-Qasim: Salman said: If a dog eats, then eat, because it ate two-thirds of it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi al-Furat, on the authority of Muhammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, he said: Salman said: If you send your trained dog or your falcon, and you mention the name of God and it eats half of it or two-thirds of it, then eat the rest of it. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Mukhramah ibn Bakir told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Humayd ibn Malik ibn Khathim al-Du’ali: that he asked Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas about hunting that a dog eats from, so he said: Eat, even if nothing remains of it except a shoe - meaning: a piece. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-Samad told me, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd Rabbih ibn Sa’id, he said: I heard Bakir ibn al-Ashja narrating, on the authority of Sa’d, he said: Eat, because he ate two-thirds of it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd Rabbih bin Saeed Fal: I heard Bakir bin Al-Ashja, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab - Shu’bah said: I said: Did you hear it from Saeed? He said: No - he said: Eat, even if he ate two-thirds of it. He said: Then Shu’bah said in his hadith: On the authority of Saad, he said: Eat, even if he ate half of it. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: If you send your dog and it eats from it, if it eats two-thirds of it and there is one-third left, then eat. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yazid ibn Harun told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, something similar. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Salim bin Nuh Al-Attar told me, on the authority of Omar - meaning: Ibn Aamer - on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman, who said: If you send your dark-skinned dog and it catches and kills, then eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, he said, I heard Ubaidullah -H and Hanad told us, he said, Abdah told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Umar - on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, he said: If you send your dark-skinned dog and mention the name of God, then eat whatever it catches for you, whether it eats or not. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me: Nafi’ told them: Abdullah bin Omar did not see anything wrong with eating game, if a dog killed it he would eat from it. Yunus told me about it again, saying, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ubayd God ibn Amr, Ibn Abi Tha’lab, and more than one other told me: that Nafi’ told them, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Muhammad bin Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: He saw no harm in what a fierce wolf ate. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Bakir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashja’, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Sa’d, he said: I said to us: Are there ferocious dogs that eat and leave behind? He said: Eat, even if only a few remain. Hannad told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashja, on the authority of Hamid, who said: I asked Sa’d, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, in the interpretation of His statement: You teach them from what God has taught you is that the teaching that God mentioned in this verse for the birds of prey is that a man should teach his bird of prey to sally out when it is caught on prey, to pursue it when it is tempted, or to hold it back if it takes it without eating anything from it, and not to flee from it when it wants it, and to respond to it when it calls it. This is the teaching of all birds of prey, birds and beasts. If a hunter’s bird of prey eats from the prey, then his bird of prey is not trained. If his master finds his prey alive and slaughters it, it is permissible for him to eat it. But if he finds it dead, it is not permissible for him to eat it, because it is something that has been eaten by a wild beast, which God has forbidden by His statement: and that which a wild beast has eaten, and he has not found its slaughter. We said: This is the most appropriate statement about the trays, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are clear: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Sulayman al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim: that he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about hunting, so he said: If you send your dog, mention the name of God over it, and if you find it and it has killed and eaten some of it, then do not eat anything of it, for it has only caught it for its own sake. Abu Kuraib and Abu Hisham al-Rafa’i told us: Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Bayan ibn Bishr, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: We are people who hunt with these dogs. He said: If you send out your trained dogs and mention the name of God over them, then eat what they catch for you even if they kill, unless the dog eats. If it eats, then do not eat, for I fear that it has only kept it for itself. If someone says: What do you say about what he told you? Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i said, Abdul Aziz bin Musa told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Abu Iyas, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man sends his dog to hunt and it catches up with it and has eaten some of it, then let him eat what is left.” It was said: This is a report whose chain of transmission is questionable, because it is not known that Saeed heard it from Salman, and the trustworthy people of the hadiths stop this statement at Salman, and they narrate it from him without it being traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the trustworthy hadith masters, if they follow one another in transmitting something with a description, and a single individual who does not have their own memorization contradicts them, then the trustworthy group is more deserving of the authenticity of what they transmitted than the individual who does not have their own memorization. Abu Ja`far said: If the matter with the dog is as you mentioned: that if it eats from the game it is not trained, then the same is the ruling with every animal of prey: that whatever it eats from the game is not trained, and it is not permissible for it to eat its game unless it realizes that it was slaughtered. Abu Ja`far said: What he meant by his saying: Eat of what they catch for you, is that you eat, O people, of what your limbs catch for you. The interpreters differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: This is apparent and general, as God made it general. It is permissible to eat everything that dogs and trained birds of prey catch for us from the game that is permissible to eat, whether the birds of prey and dogs eat from it or not, whether it is slaughtered and slaughtered or not until the birds of prey kill it by wounding it or without wounding it. This is the statement of those who said: Teaching birds of prey that make it permissible to hunt them means teaching them to hunt prey, to pursue it if it is hunted, to take it, and to refrain from running away from its owner, without refraining from eating its prey if it hunts it. We have mentioned the statement of those who said this statement and the narration from them with their chains of transmission mentioned above. Others said: Rather, it is specific and not general. They said: Its meaning is: So eat of the game that they catch for you, all of it, not some of it. They said: If the birds of prey eat some of it and hold on to some of it, then what they caught is not permissible to eat, and they have eaten some of it, because they only held on to what they caught of that game after what they ate of it, for themselves, not for us. And God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, only permitted us to eat what our trained birds of prey catch for us, by His saying: So eat of what they catch for you, not what they catch for themselves. This is the saying of those who said: The training of birds of prey that makes their hunting permissible is that they pull out the game when it is untied, then they seek it out and take it, then hold it for its owner and do not eat anything of it, nor do they flee from its owner. We have mentioned many of those who said this in the past, and we will mention another group of them in this place. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And eat of that which they catch for you, meaning: Eat of that which they kill. Ali said: Ibn Abbas used to say: If it kills and eats, do not eat, but if it catches and you catch it alive, then slaughter it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If a trained dog eats from its prey before its owner comes to it and catches it alive, then it should not eat from its prey. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Then eat of that which they catch for you, if a dog hunts and catches it and kills it but does not eat from it, then it is permissible. But if it eats from it, then it is said: It only caught it for itself, so do not eat anything from it, for it is not trained. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They ask you what is lawful for them until His saying: So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it, he said: If you send your trained dog or your bird or your arrow, and you mention the name of God, and it takes or kills, then eat. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God when you send it, and it catches or kills it, then it is permissible. But if it eats from it, then do not eat from it, for it only caught it for its own sake. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi, regarding his statement: Then eat of that which they catch for you, he said: I said, O Messenger of God, is my land a hunting land? He said: If you send your dog and say Bismillah, then eat of that which your dog catches for you, even if it kills. But if it eats, then do not eat, for it only caught it for itself. We have already explained the first of the two opinions on this matter as correct, so there is no need to repeat it. If someone says: What is the reason for the inclusion of min in His statement: So eat of what they catch for you, when God has made lawful for us the hunting of our lawful birds of prey, and min only enters into the speech as part of what it entered into? It was said: The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of its inclusion in this position. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Min was used in this position for a reason other than meaning, just as the Arabs used it in their saying: Kana min tamār and Kana min ḥadīth. He said: “And from that is His statement: “And He will expiate for you some of your misdeeds” (al-Baqarah 2:271), and His statement: And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail (al-Nur 24:43), He said: And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail. He said: “And some of them said: “And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail” (al-Nur 24:43), meaning: from the sky, hail, by making the mountains of hail in the sky, and making the sending down from it.” Others among the Arab scholars denied this and said: Min was only used for an understood meaning, and speech is not permissible or valid without it. This is because it indicates partiality. He used to say: The meaning of their saying Qad kan min tammar and Kan min hadith is: Was there any rain in your country? And was there any hadith that happened in your country? And he says: The meaning of: And He will remove from you any evil (al-Baqarah 2:271), is: And He will remove from you any of your evil deeds that He wills and desires. And in His statement: And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, in which is hail (al-Nur 24:43), he allows the deletion of from from from hail, but he does not allow its deletion from mountains. And he interprets the meaning of that as: And He sends down from the sky, like mountains of hail. Then from was inserted into hail, because hail is explained by him from the examples, I mean: the examples of mountains. And mountains was established in place of the examples and mountains, and they are mountains of hail. So he does not allow the deletion of from from mountains, because it indicates that what is in the sky from which He sent down the hail is like mountains of hail. He permitted the deletion of min from al-bard, because al-bard is an explanation of al-amthal, just as you say: I have two ratls of oil and I have two ratls of oil, but you do not have the ratl, but rather you have the amount. So min enters into the explanation and leaves it. And likewise according to the one who said this: from the sky, from the likes of mountains, and it is not mountains. And he said: And if it was: He sent down from mountains in the sky mountains of cold, then the second al-jabal was deleted, and the first al-jabal is in the sky, it is permissible. You say: I ate from the food, meaning: I ate food from the food, then you delete al-ta’am and do not drop min. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard is that min does not enter into speech except for an understood meaning, and it may be permissible to omit it in some speech and in speech there is a need for it, due to the indication of what appears in the speech about it. As for it being in speech for a meaning other than that which it indicates by entering, we have explained previously that it is not permissible for it to be in what is authentic of speech. The meaning of its entering into His statement: So eat of that which they catch for you, is for partiality, since the birds of prey catch for their owners what God has made lawful for them to eat of its meat, and has forbidden them its excrement and blood, so He, the Most High, said: So eat - from that which your birds of prey catch for you - the good things that I have made lawful for you of their meat, but not what I have forbidden you of its bad things of excrement and blood and the like, which I have not made good for you. So that is the meaning of min entering into that. As for His statement: And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds (al-Baqarah 2:271), we have explained the reason for its inclusion in it previously, so there is no need to repeat it. As for its inclusion in His statement: And He sends down from the sky mountains (al-Nur 24:43), we will explain it when we come to it, God willing. Abu Ja`far said: He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: And mention the name of God over it, over whatever your birds of prey catch for you, such as: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And mention the name of God over it, meaning: If you send your limbs, say: In the name of God, and if you forget, there is no blame. Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And mention the name of God over it, he said: If you send it out, then mention the name of God over it when you send it out to hunt. Abu Ja`far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: O people, fear God in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. Beware of doing something contrary to Him, and of eating the game of untrained birds of prey, or of what they have not caught from their game and have caught for themselves, or of eating what God has not mentioned in His name from the game and the slaughtered animals, which were hunted by the idolaters and idol worshippers and those of His creation who did not make God One, or slaughtered, for God has forbidden that to you, so avoid it. Then He frightened them if they did what He forbade them from doing, including that and other things. He said: Know that God is swift in holding to account whoever among you calls Him to account for His blessings upon him, and the grateful among you will thank his Lord for what He has bestowed upon him by obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden, because He is the Guardian of all that among you, and He encompasses it, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, so He rewards the obedient among you for his obedience, and the disobedient for his disobedience, and He has made clear to you the reward of the two groups.
5:5: Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: Today, all good things have been made lawful for you, is that today, O believers, all lawful slaughtered animals and foods have been made lawful for you, but not all impure ones. And His statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and the sacrifices of the People of the Scripture from the Jews and Christians, who are those who were given the Torah and the Gospel and it was revealed to them, so they adhered to them or to one of them, are lawful for you, meaning: it is lawful for you to eat it, unlike the sacrifices of the rest of the polytheists who do not have a Scripture from the polytheists of the Arabs and the worshippers of idols and statues. For whoever among them is not one of those who acknowledge the Oneness of God, the Mighty and Sublime, and adheres to the religion of the People of the Scripture, then their sacrifices are forbidden to you. Then there is a difference of opinion about who God Almighty meant by His saying: And the food of those who were given the Scripture, from the People of the Scripture. Some of them said: God meant by that the sacrifice of every People of the Book to whom the Torah and the Gospel were revealed, or of those who entered their religion and renounced their religion, and forbade what they forbade, and permitted what they permitted, from them and from others from all the races of nations. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said, Ikrimah told us: Ibn Abbas was asked about the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, so he recited this verse: O you who believe, do not take the Jews as allies until His saying: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them, the verse (al-Ma’idah 5:51). Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us: on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Uthma told us, he said, Saeed bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah: that they saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and in marrying their women, and they would recite: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them (al-Ma’idah 5:51). Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that they saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: that he saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and he recited: And your Lord is not forgetful (Maryam 19:64). Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, they said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Ibn Shihab told me about the sacrifice of the Nasar, the Arabs, he said: It is eaten because of the people of the Book among them in religion, and they mention the name of God. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ said: They only acknowledge the religion of that book. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and they said: There is nothing wrong with it. He said: Al-Hakam recited: And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Scripture except wishful thinking (al-Baqarah 2:78). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Eat from the slaughtered animals of Banu Taghlib, and marry their women, for God said in His Book: “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you, then indeed, he is of them” (al-Ma’idah 5:51). So if they were not of them except through allegiance, then they would have been of them. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada: Al-Hasan did not see anything wrong with the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and he used to say: They adopted a religion, so that is their religion. Others said: What is meant by those who were given the Scripture in this verse are those upon whom the Torah and the Gospel were sent down from among the Children of Israel and their children. As for those who were foreigners among them from among the rest of the nations who followed their religion and were not from among the Children of Israel, then this verse does not mean them, and they are not among those whose slaughtering is permissible to eat, because they are not among those who were given the Scripture by the Muslims. This is a statement that Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi’i used to say, and al-Rabi’ told us about it - and he interprets in that the statement of those who disliked the slaughtering of the Arab Christians from among the Companions and the Followers. Mention of those who forbade the sacrifices of Arab Christians: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah, he said, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not eat the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, for they only cling to Christianity by drinking alcohol. Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Ali, who said: Do not eat the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, for they did not adhere to anything of Christianity except drinking wine. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Abdullah bin Bakr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said: I asked Ali about the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, and he said: Their sacrifices are not to be eaten, because they have not clung to anything of their religion except drinking alcohol. Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Ali bin Abis told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said: Ali forbade us from the sacrifices of the Arab Christians. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Qassab, he said: I heard Muhammad Ibn Ali narrating, on the authority of Ali: that he disliked the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said, Do not eat the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, and the sacrifices of the Armenian Christians. Abu Ja`far said: These reports from `Ali, may God be pleased with him, only indicate that he forbade the slaughtering of the Christians of Banu Taghlib because they were not Christians, for they did not permit what the Christians permitted and forbade what they forbade, except for wine. And whoever claims to follow a religion but does not adhere to anything of it, is closer to disavowing it than to joining it and its people. Therefore, `Ali forbade eating the slaughtering of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, not because they were not from the Children of Israel. If this is the case, and it is a consensus of the argument that there is nothing wrong with the sacrifice of every Christian and Jew who follows the religion of the Christian or the Jew, and makes lawful what they make lawful and makes unlawful what they make unlawful, whether from the Children of Israel or from others, then it is clear that what al-Shafi’i said about that is wrong, and his interpretation of what he interpreted in his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, that it is the sacrifices of those who were given the Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, from the Children of Israel, and the correct interpretation of what contradicts that, and the statement of the one who said: The sacrifice of every Jew and Christian is lawful, regardless of the race of the children of Adam. As for the food about which God said: And the food of those who were given the Scripture, it is the sacrifices. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: slaughtered animals. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: Their slaughtered animals. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: The slaughter of the People of the Scripture. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: Their slaughtered animals. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: their slaughtered animals. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Mualla bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, meaning: their slaughtered animals. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. As for their food, it is the slaughtered animals. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he said: God has made their food and their women lawful for us. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: As for his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, he made their food and their women lawful for us. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I asked him - meaning Ibn Zayd - about what was slaughtered for the churches and mentioned over them, so he said: God has made lawful for us the food of the People of the Book, and He did not exclude anything from it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zahriyyah Hadir ibn Kurayb, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad, on the authority of Umair ibn al-Aswad: That he asked Abu al-Darda’ about a ram that was slaughtered for a church called Girgis, which they gave as a gift to it, can we eat from it? Abu al-Darda’ said: O God, pardon us! They are only people of the Book, their food is lawful for us, and our food is lawful for them! And he ordered him to eat it. As for his saying: And your food is lawful for them, he means: Your sacrifices, O believers, are lawful for the People of the Book. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: and chaste women from among the believing women, is that it is lawful for you, O believers, to marry chaste women from among the believing women - and they are the free women from among them - and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning: and the free women from among those who were given the Scripture, and they are the Jews and Christians who believed in what is in the Torah and the Gospel before you, O believers in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Arabs and all the people, that you may marry them also, when you have given them their due compensation, meaning: if you give those whom you marry from among your chaste men and women, their due compensation, which is their dowries. The people of interpretation differed regarding the chaste women whom God Almighty meant in His saying: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. Some of them said: He meant by that free women in particular, whether they were wicked or chaste. The proponents of this statement permitted the marriage of a free woman, whether she was a believer or a woman of the Book from the Jews or Christians, from any race of people, as long as she was a woman of the Book, wicked or chaste. They forbade the female slaves of the People of the Book from marrying in any case, because God Almighty made faith a condition for the marriage of female slaves, as He said: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave girls (An-Nisa’: 25). Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawood told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture, he said: free women. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: from among the free women. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: That a man divorced his wife and his sister proposed to him, and she had become impure. So he went to Umar and mentioned that to him about her, and Umar said: What did you see from her? He said: I have seen nothing but good from her! So he said: Marry her and do not tell. Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said: Abdul Wahid told us, he said: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, he said: Amer told us, he said: A woman from among us from Hamdan committed adultery. He said: The tax collector of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, flogged her with the prescribed punishment, then she repented. So they went to Umar and said: We will marry her, and what a bad thing happened to her! Umar said: If I hear that you have mentioned anything of that, I will punish you severely. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab: A man wanted to marry his sister, but she said: I fear that I will disgrace my father, for I have been deceived! So he came to Umar and said: Hasn’t she repented? He said: Yes! He said: So he married her. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: That Nabisha, a woman from Hamdan, rebelled and wanted to slaughter herself. He said: So they caught up with her, treated her and she recovered. They mentioned that to Umar, and he said: Marry her as a chaste Muslim woman would. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer: That a man from Yemen committed an indecent act against his sister, so he ran a knife over her jugular vein, and she was caught, and her wound was treated until she recovered. Then her uncle moved with his family until he came to Madinah, and she read the Qur’an and kept quiet, until she was one of the most pious of their women. So she proposed to her uncle, and he hated to deceive her, and he hated to reveal his brother’s daughter’s secret. So he went to Umar and mentioned that to him, and Umar said: If you revealed it, I would punish you! If a righteous man comes to you whom you are pleased with, then marry her to him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer: That a girl in Yemen called Nabisha committed an immoral act, and he mentioned something similar. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated, Yazid narrated, Ismail narrated, on the authority of Aamir, who said: A man came to Umar and said: I have a daughter who was buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. I extracted her before she died, and she lived to see Islam. When she became Muslim, she committed one of the punishments set by God, so she took a knife to slaughter herself. I found her and she had cut some of her jugular vein, so I treated her until she recovered. Then she came back with a good repentance, and she is asking me for her hand in marriage, O Commander of the Faithful. Tell me about her situation and what happened? Umar said: Will you tell me about her situation? You deliberately reveal what God has concealed! By God, if you tell anyone about her situation, I will make you an example to the people of the cities. Rather, marry her as a chaste Muslim woman. Ahmad bin Mani’ told us, he said, Marwan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: A man came to Omar and mentioned something similar. Mujahid told us, Yazid told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr: A man proposed to his sister, and he told him that she had become impure. report of that reached Umar bin al-Khattab, so he struck the man and said: What do you have to do with this report? Marry and be quiet. Ibn Bashar told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I was thinking of not allowing anyone who committed an immoral act in Islam to marry a chaste woman! Ubayy ibn Ka’b said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, polytheism is greater than that, and it may be accepted from him if he repents! Others said: God meant by His statement: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, the chaste women from both groups, whether slave women or free women. So the proponents of this statement permitted marriage to slave women from among the People of the Scripture who owe their debts by this verse, and they forbade prostitutes from among the believers and the People of the Scripture. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: The chaste ones. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Amer: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: The chastity of the Jewish and Christian women: that she does not commit adultery, and that she washes herself from major ritual impurity. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Amer: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she washes herself from major ritual impurity, and that she guards her private parts. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she does not commit adultery, and that she washes herself from major ritual impurity. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: Her chastity is that she washes herself from major ritual impurity, and that she protects her private parts from adultery. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, he said, Mutraf told us, on the authority of Amer, something similar. Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture, he said: The chaste ones. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: As for chaste women, they are the chaste. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A woman took her slave and said: I have interpreted the Book of God: And those whom your right hands possess. He said: She was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have interpreted a verse of the Book of God in a way other than its meaning. He said: So the slave was exiled and his head was cut off and he said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said about the woman who commits adultery before he has consummated the marriage with her: She is not entitled to a dowry, and they should be separated. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding a virgin who commits adultery, he said: She should be lashed one hundred times, banished for a year, and she should return to her husband what she took from him. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, something similar. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:Al-Hasan used to say: If a man sees something indecent from his wife and is certain, then he should not keep her. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said: The female slaves of the People of the Book are like their free women. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the ruling of the Almighty’s saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. Is it general or specific? Some of them said: It is general for chaste women, because the chaste are chaste women. And a Muslim may marry any free woman or slave woman of the People of the Book, whether she is a combatant or a dhimmi. They based this on the apparent meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and that what is meant by them are the chaste women, whoever they may be. This is the statement of those who said: What is meant by chaste women in this context is the chaste women. Others said: Rather, those whom God Almighty meant by His saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, are the free women among them, and the verse is general in its application to all of them. So, the marriage of all free Jewish and Christian women is permissible, whether they are warlike or dhimmi, from any race of Jews and Christians. This is the opinion of a group of the early and late scholars. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan: that they saw no harm in marrying Jewish and Christian women, and they said: God permitted it with knowledge. Others of them said: Rather, he meant by that the marriage of the Children of Israel to the women of the Book among them in particular, without the rest of the nations who followed Judaism and Christianity. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and those who said the same. Others said: Rather, it refers to the women of the People of the Book who have a covenant and protection from the Muslims. As for the people of war, their women are forbidden to the Muslims. Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Uqbah narrated, he said: Al-Fazari narrated, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the women of the People of the Book are those who are permissible for us, and among them are those who are not permissible for us. Then he recited: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah.” (al-Tawbah 9:29). So whoever pays the jizyah, his women are permissible for us, and whoever does not pay the jizyah, his women are not permissible for us. Al-Hakam said: So I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and he liked it. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by His statement: and chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you is the free believers and People of the Scripture. Because God, the Most High, did not permit marriage to free slave girls in the situation in which He permitted them to do so, unless they were believers. So He, the Most High, said: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave girls (An-Nisa’: 25). So He did not permit anyone from among them except the believers. So if what was meant by His statement: and chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture was the chaste, then the chaste ones among their slave girls would be included in the permissibility, and the unchaste ones among their free women and the free women of the people of faith would be excluded. God has made lawful for us the free women of the believers, even if they have committed an immoral act, as He says: And marry those among you who are single and those of your male slaves and female slaves who are righteous (al-Tawbah 9:29). We have already demonstrated the corruption of the statement of those who said: It is not lawful for believers to marry those women of the believers and the People of the Book who have committed an immoral act, in a place other than this, so there is no need to repeat it here. Marrying free Muslim women and women from the People of the Book is permissible for believers, whether they have committed an immoral act or not, whether they are dhimmis or non-Muslims, provided that they are in a place where the man who marries does not fear that his child will be forced to disbelieve, based on the apparent words of God Almighty: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. As for the statement of the one who said: He meant by that the women of the Children of Israel, especially the women of the Book among them, it is a statement that does not require us to be preoccupied with explaining it, because of its anomaly and departure from what the scholars of the nation are upon, of permitting the women of all Jews and Christians. We have demonstrated the corruption of the statement of the one who said this statement from the aspect of analogy in other than this place sufficiently, so we disliked repeating it. As for his saying: If you give them their wages, then the wage is the compensation that the husband gives to the woman to enjoy her, which is the dowry, as: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: You have given them their due compensation, meaning: their dowries. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: It is lawful for you to take chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, while you are chaste, not fornicators or taking lovers. What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Chaste, is chaste, not fornicators, meaning: not openly committing fornication with any wicked act, which is immorality, nor taking lovers, meaning: nor alone with one prostitute, whom he has taken as his lover and she has taken as his lover, and he has taken her as a friend for himself with whom he commits fornication. We have explained the meaning of ihsan and its aspects, and the meaning of saffah and khudn in other places, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place, and it is as follows: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Chaste, not fornicators, meaning: they marry them with a dowry and evidence, not fornicators who openly commit adultery, nor take lovers, meaning: they secretly commit adultery. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: God has made two chaste women lawful for us: a chaste believing woman, and a chaste woman from among the People of the Book, nor those who take lovers: the one with a lover, the one with one close friend. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: A man asked him: Can a man marry a woman from the People of the Book? He said: What does he have to do with the People of the Book, when God has increased the number of Muslim women! If he must do so, then let him go to her in a chaste manner, not in a fornication. The man said: What is a fornication? He said: It is that which, if a man glances at her with his eyes, she follows him. Abu Ja`far said: What he means by his saying, may His praise be exalted: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, is whoever denies what God has commanded us to believe in, of the Oneness of God and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, which is the faith, about which God, may His praise be exalted, said: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless, meaning: the reward for the work he did in this world, hoping to attain a status with God, has been nullified, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers, meaning: and in the Hereafter he will be among the doomed, those who have cheated themselves of their share of God’s reward by their disbelief in Muhammad and their work in disobedience to God. It has been mentioned that his statement, And whoever disbelieves in faith, refers to the People of the Book, and that it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the sake of a people who were reluctant to marry women of the People of the Book when it was said to them, “Lawful to you are all good things. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you.” Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that some Muslims said: How can we marry their women, meaning: the women of the People of the Book - when they are not of our religion? So God Almighty revealed: And whoever disbelieves in faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers, so God permitted marrying them with knowledge. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of faith, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’: And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, he said: God, faith. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of Ata’: And whoever disbelieves in faith, he said: Faith is monotheism. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever disbelieves in faith, he said: in God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God. Muhammad told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And whoever disbelieves in faith, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God. Muhammad told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And whoever disbelieves in faith, he said: disbelief in God. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, he said: God Almighty informed us that faith is the firmest handhold, and that He does not accept any work without it, and He does not forbid Paradise except to the one who abandons it. If someone were to say to us: What is the interpretation of the meaning of his statement: And whoever disbelieves in faith, to mean: And whoever disbelieves in God? It was said: The way to interpret it is that faith is to believe in God and His messengers and what He sent them with of His religion, and disbelief is to deny that. They said: So the meaning of disbelief in faith is to deny God and deny His Oneness. So they interpreted the meaning of the word with what was intended by it, and they turned away from interpreting the word according to the reality of its words and its apparent meaning in recitation. If someone says: What is its interpretation according to its apparent meaning and the truth of its words? It was said: Its interpretation is: And whoever refuses to believe in God, and refrains from believing in His Oneness and obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden him to do, then his work has been in vain. This is because disbelief is denial in the speech of the Arabs, and faith is belief and acknowledgment. And whoever refuses to believe in the Oneness of God and acknowledge it, then he is one of the disbelievers. So this is the interpretation of the speech in its proper form.
5:6: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O you who believe, if you stand up to pray, and you are not in a state of ritual purity for prayer, then wash your faces with water and your hands up to the elbows. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding his saying: When you rise to prayer, meaning every situation in which one rises to prayer, or some of them? And what are the situations in which one rises to prayer? Some of them said something similar to what we said about it, that it refers to some of the situations in which one performs the ritual prayer, not all of the situations, and that the situation that is meant is the situation in which one performs the ritual prayer without being pure. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaidullah told us: Ikrimah was asked about the statement of God: When you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows, so does one perform ablution every hour? He said: Ibn Abbas said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, he said, I heard Mas`ud Ibn Ali Al-Shaibani say, I heard `Ikrimah say: Sa`d Ibn Abi Waqqas used to pray the prayers with one ablution. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Sufyan ibn Habib told us, on the authority of Mas`ud ibn Ali, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas used to say: Pray with your purity as long as you do not break your ablution. Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us, he said, Salim bin Akhdar told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I said to Ubaidah Al-Salmani: What necessitates ablution? He said: The state of ritual impurity. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Waqi` ibn Suhban, on the authority of Yazid ibn Tarif - or: Tarif ibn Yazid - that they were with Abu Musa on the bank of the Tigris, and they performed ablution, and prayed the noon prayer. When the call to the afternoon prayer was made, some men stood up to perform ablution from the Tigris, and he said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Tarif ibn Ziyad - or: Ziyad ibn Tarif - on the authority of Waqi’ ibn Suhban: that he witnessed Abu Musa praying the noon prayer with his companions, then they sat in circles on the banks of the Tigris, and the call to the afternoon prayer was made, so men stood up to perform ablution, and Abu Musa said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, he said: I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Waqi` Ibn Suhban, on the authority of Tarif Ibn Yazid - or: Yazid Ibn Tarif - he said: I was with Abu Musa on the banks of the Tigris, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Waqi’ Ibn Suhban, on the authority of Tarif Ibn Yazid - or: Yazid Ibn Tarif - on the authority of Abu Musa, the same. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Abu Khalid told us: I performed ablution at Abu al-`Aliyah’s house for the noon or afternoon prayer, and then I said: Should I pray with this ablution of mine, for I will not return to my family until the dark? Abu al-`Aliyah said: There is no blame. And we learned: When a person performs ablution, he is in his state of ablution until something happens. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Ibn Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, who said: Ablution without ritual impurity is an act of aggression. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed, the same. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: I saw Ibrahim praying with one ablution, the noon, afternoon, and sunset prayers. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us: I was with Yahya, and I would pray the prayers with one ablution. He said: And Ibrahim was like that. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Yazid bin Ibrahim told us: I heard al-Hasan asked about a man who performs ablution and prays all the prayers with one ablution, so he said: There is nothing wrong with it as long as he does not break his ablution. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: He prays the prayers with one ablution as long as he does not break his ablution. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Zaydah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, he said: Al-Aswad used to pray the prayers with one ablution. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, he says: you rise while you are not in a state of purity. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Al-Aswad: He had a cup the size of a man’s water, so he would perform ablution, then pray all the prayers with that ablution. Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa narrated, saying: Ziyad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka’i narrated, saying: Al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashar narrated, saying: I saw Jabir ibn Abdullah praying the prayers with one ablution. Then, if he urinated or broke his ablution, he would perform ablution and wipe his socks with the remaining water from his ablution. So I said: Abu Abdullah, is there something you should do in your opinion? He said: Rather, I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do it, so I do it as I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do. Others said: The meaning of this is: O you who believe, when you rise from your sleep for prayer. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he told me from someone who heard Malik bin Anas, narrating on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, his saying: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, he said: He means: when you rise from sleep. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us: Malik bin Anas told him on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, something similar. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his saying: When you rise to prayer, wash your faces. He said: You rose to prayer from sleep. Others said: Rather, it means that whenever a person stands up for prayer, he should renew his purity for it. Who said that? Humayd ibn Mas`adah narrated, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated, on the authority of Mas`ud ibn `Ali, who said: I asked `Ikrimah, who said: I said: O Abu `Abdullah, should I perform ablution for the dawn prayer, then go to the market and the noon prayer comes, so should I pray? He said: `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, used to say: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Mas`ud ibn Ali al-Shaibani say, I heard `Ikrimah say: `Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to perform ablution before every prayer, and he would recite this verse: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces, the verse. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us, he said, Azhar told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab performed ablution in a light, permissible manner, and he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told me, he said, Shu’bah told me, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Nazzal, he said: I saw Ali praying the noon prayer, then he sat for the people in the courtyard, then water was brought to him and he washed his face and hands, then he wiped his head and feet and said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: Ali measured a quantity of grain, then performed ablution in which he was allowed to do so, and he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. Others said: Rather, this was an order from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him: that they should perform ablution for every prayer, then that was abrogated by making it easier. Who said that? Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad Al-Qatwani told me, he said, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban Al-Ansari told me, then Al-Mazini, Mazen Bani Al-Najjar, he said to Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Omar: Tell me about Abdullah’s ablution for every prayer, whether he was pure or not, from whom? He said: Asma bint Zaid bin Al-Khattab told me: “Abdullah bin Hanzala bin Abi Amir Al-Ghasil told her: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded ablution for every prayer, and that was difficult for him, so he commanded the siwak, and ablution was lifted from him except for one who was in a state of ritual impurity. Abdullah thought that he had the strength to do it, so he would perform ablution.” Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah, he said, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban al-Ansari told me, he said: I said to Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Umar: Tell me about Abdullah’s ablution for every prayer, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer.” Then, in the year of the conquest, he performed the prayers with one ablution and wiped over his socks. Umar said: You have done something that you did not do before! He said: You did it intentionally. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. Then, on the day of the conquest of Mecca, he prayed all the prayers with one ablution.” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muharrib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was performing ablution, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed all the prayers with one ablution, and Umar said to him: O Messenger of God, did you do something that you did not do before? He said: I did it intentionally, O Umar.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. When he conquered Mecca, he prayed the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers with one ablution.” Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Dhahir told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, “On the authority of Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon, afternoon, sunset, and evening prayers with one ablution.” Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: God meant by His saying: When you rise to prayer, wash, all the states of the one who stands to pray, except that it is an obligatory command to wash what God has commanded the one who stands to pray to wash, after an impurity that invalidates his purity, and before performing ablution, and it is a recommended command for the one who was previously pure, and did not have an impurity that invalidated his purity. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to perform ablution for every prayer before the conquest of Mecca, then he prayed all the prayers on that day with one ablution, so that his nation would know that what he (peace be upon him) used to do of renewing his purity for every prayer was only from him taking advantage of the virtue, and from him giving preference to the most beloved of the two matters to God, and from him hastening to do what his Lord urged him to do, not because it was an obligatory duty for him. If someone thinks that in the hadith that we mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Hanzala, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered ablution before every prayer, is evidence of the opposite of what we said, that this was recommended for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions - and he imagines that this was obligatory - then he has thought incorrectly. This is because the statement of the speaker: God commanded his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do such and such, is possible in several ways: it is an obligation, a guidance, a recommendation, a permission, and a generalization. Since it is possible in the ways we mentioned, the more appropriate way to say it is that which the evidence is unanimously agreed upon for its authenticity, rather than that which is not proven authentically by evidence that proves the truth of its claimant. The evidence is unanimous that God Almighty did not make ablution obligatory for his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor for his servants for every prayer, and then abrogated that. In their consensus on that, there is clear evidence of the correctness of what we have said: that the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was as we have described, of his preference for doing what God Almighty urged him to do and urged his believing servants to do with His saying: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and that his leaving it in the state in which he left it was a concession for his nation, and an announcement from him to them that that was not obligatory nor binding upon him or them, except for someone who has an event that necessitates the breaking of purity. There are reports similar to what we have said about this: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Amir, “On the authority of Anas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a small bucket and he performed ablution. He said: I said to Anas: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution before every prayer? He said: Yes! I said: What about you? He said: We used to pray the prayers with one ablution.” Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqi narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi, on the authority of Abu Ghutayf, who said: I prayed the noon prayer with Ibn Umar, and he came to a gathering in his house and sat down, and I sat with him. When the call to the afternoon prayer was made, he called for water for ablution and performed ablution, then he went out to pray, then he returned to his gathering. When the call to the sunset prayer was made, he called for water for ablution and performed ablution. I said: What do I see you doing? He said: No, even though my ablution for the dawn prayer is sufficient for all the prayers as long as I do not break my ablution. But I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, ten good deeds will be recorded for him, so I only desired that. Abu Saeed Al-Baghdadi told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Harim, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Ghatif, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity will have ten good deeds recorded for him.
