Some people said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an announcement from God to him that he does not have to perform ablution unless he stands up for his prayer, and not for all other actions. This is because if he broke his ablution, he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution. So God permitted with this verse that he do whatever actions he wanted after breaking his ablution except for prayer, whether he performed ablution or not, and He commanded him to perform ablution if he stood up for prayer before entering it. Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Muawiyah bin Hisham narrated, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of Abdullah bin Alqamah bin Al-Fughawa, on the authority of his father, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urinated, we would speak to him but he would not speak to us, and we would greet him but he would not respond to us, until he came home and performed ablution as he did for prayer. So we said: O Messenger of God, we speak to you but you do not speak to us, and we greet you but you do not respond to us? He said: Until the verse of permission was revealed: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, the verse. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the definition of the face that God commanded the one who stands for prayer to wash, in His saying: When you stand for prayer, wash your faces. Some of them said: It is what is visible from the human skin, from the hair on his head, descending to the end of his chin lengthwise, and what is between the ears widthwise. They said: As for the ear and what is hidden inside the mouth, nose and eye, it is not part of the face. It is not obligatory to wash that or wash any of it in ablution. They said: As for what the hair covers from it, such as the chin that is covered by the hair of the beard, and the temples that are covered by the hair of the beard, then passing water over what is on that of the hair is sufficient for washing what is hidden from it of the skin of the face, because the face, according to them, is what is visible to the eye of the beholder and faces it, and nothing else. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Amr bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The beard is sufficient for whatever water flows from its place. Humayd bin Mas`adah told us, Yazid bin Zari` told us, Shu`bah told us, Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: What water flows from his face onto his beard is sufficient for him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah regarding combing the beard, he said: Whatever passes over your beard is sufficient for you. Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamdani told us, Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Mansur, who said: I saw Ibrahim performing ablution and he did not comb his beard. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: What flows over it is sufficient for you to clean it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Yunus, he said: When Al-Hasan performed ablution, he would wipe his beard and his face. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: He did not comb his beard. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan: He did not comb his beard when he performed ablution. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: Washing the beard is not from the Sunnah. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That when he performed ablution, the water did not reach the roots of his beard. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Abu Shaiba Saeed bin Abdul Rahman Al-Zubaidi who said: I asked Ibrahim: Should I rinse my beard with water when performing ablution? He said: No, what your hand passes over is sufficient for you. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, I asked Shu`bah about combing the beard during ablution, so he said: Al-Mughira said, Ibrahim said: What water flows from his face onto his beard is sufficient for him. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, Hajjaj bin Rushdin told us, Abdul Jabbar bin Omar told us: Ibn Shihab and Rabia performed ablution and poured water over their beards, and I did not see either of them pass water through his beard. Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I asked Saeed bin Abdul Aziz about rubbing the sides of the cheeks during ablution, and he said: That is not obligatory. I saw Makhul performing ablution and he did not do that. Abu Al-Walid Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Qurashi told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Saeed bin Bashir told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Rubbing the sides of the body during ablution is not obligatory. Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: What water passes over his beard is sufficient for him. Abu Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Zaynab, he said: I asked Al-Qasim bin Muhammad: What should I do with my beard when I perform ablution? He said: I am not one of those who wash their beards. Abu Al-Walid told us, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said: Combing the sideburns and interlacing the beard is not obligatory in ablution. Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article regarding washing what is inside the mouth and nose. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Bashir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If it were not for licking my lips during prayer, I would not have rinsed my mouth. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, I heard Abdul Malik say: Ata’ was asked about a man who prayed and did not rinse his mouth. He said: What is not mentioned in the book is sufficient for him. Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Rinsing the mouth and nose are not obligatory in ablution. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, he said: Ad-Dahhak used to forbid us from rinsing the mouth and nose during ablution in Ramadan. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, I heard Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: If he forgets to rinse his mouth and nose, he said: If he remembers and has started the prayer, then let him continue with his prayer. And if he has not started the prayer, then let him rinse his mouth and nose. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, he said: I asked Al-Hakam and Qatadah about a man who remembered while he was praying that he had not rinsed his mouth or sniffed water in his nose, so he said: He should continue with his prayer. Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article, that the ears are not part of the face: Yazid bin Mukhallad Al-Wasiti told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ghailan, he said: I heard Ibn Omar say: The ears are part of the head. Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us, Abu Matraf told us, Ghailan, a client of Banu Makhzum, told us: I heard Ibn Umar say: The ears are part of the head. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The ears are part of the head, so when you wipe the head, wipe them. Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Ghailan bin Abdullah, a client of Quraysh, told me: I heard Ibn Umar asked a questioner, saying: He performed ablution and forgot to wipe his ears. Ibn Umar said: The ears are part of the head. And he did not see anything wrong with that. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, on the authority of Saeed bin Marjana, on the authority of Ibn Omar, that he said: The ears are part of the head. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told me, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The ears are part of the head. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The ears are part of the head. Humaid bin Mas’adah told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: The ears are part of the head. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The ears are part of the head - on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed. Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Abu Amr told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: The ears are part of the head. Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The ears are part of the head. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzay’ told me, he said, Hammad bin Zayd told us, on the authority of Sinan bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah - or: on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Ibn Buzay’ was not sure - that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ma’la bin Mansur told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Sinan bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The ears are part of the head - Hammad said: I do not know if this is from Abu Umamah or: from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usama told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told me, he said, Sinan bin Rabi’ah Abu Rabi’ah told me, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head. Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj and others told me, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head. Al-Hasan bin Shabib told us, he said, Ali bin Hashim bin Al-Barid told us, he said, Ismail bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head. Humaid bin Masada told us, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:Al-Hasan said: The ears are part of the head. Others said: The face is everything below the hairline of the head to the end of the chin in length, and from ear to ear in width, what is visible to the eye of the observer and what is hidden from it from the hairline of the beard growing on the chin and on the cheekbones, and what is inside the mouth and nose, and what is in front of the ears on the face. All of that, according to them, is from the face that God commanded to be washed in His saying: So wash your faces. They said: If the one who performs ablution leaves something of that and does not wash it, his prayer with that ablution is not valid. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr and Abu Asim told me, they said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Nafi’ told me: Ibn Umar used to wet the roots of his beard’s hair, and he would put his hand into the roots of its hair until the tar was abundant. Hamid bin Mas`adah told us, he said, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Rafi`, the freed slave of Ibn `Umar, told me: Ibn `Umar used to put his hands deep in his beard until the tar was abundant. Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul Warith told us, on the authority of Saeed, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: When he performed ablution, he would comb through his beard until he reached the roots of the hair. Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Ma’la bin Jaber Al-Laqiti told us, he said, Al-Azraq bin Qais told me, he said: I saw Ibn Omar performing ablution and combing his beard. Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Layth told us, on the authority of Nafi’: Ibn Umar used to wet his beard with water until it reached the roots of the hair. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair told me: That his father Ubayd ibn Umair, when he performed ablution, would insert his fingers into the roots of the hair on his face, inserting them between the hair at its roots, rubbing the skin with his fingers - so Abdullah pointed to me as the man had told him, as he had described about him. Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that when he performed ablution, he would rub his cheeks a little, and sometimes intertwine his beard with his fingers, and sometimes leave it. Abu Al-Walid and Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said, and Abda told me, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, something similar to that. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim, he said: I saw Ibn Abi Laila performing ablution, then he washed his beard, and he said: Whoever among you can reach the roots of his hair, let him do so. Humayd bin Mas`adah told us, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said: It is his duty to wet the roots of his hair. Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said: Mujahid used to comb his beard. Hamid told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: that he used to comb his beard when he performed ablution. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Dawud al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Shabramah, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, who said: Why is the beard washed before it grows, but when it grows it is not washed? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to comb his beard when he performed ablution. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Tawus: that he used to trim his beard. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: that he used to comb his beard. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, the same. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, I asked Shu`bah about combing the beard during ablution, so he mentioned on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah: that Mujahid used to comb his beard. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Maruf, he said: I saw Ibn Sirin performing ablution and combing his beard. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Zubayr Ibn Adi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: I saw him combing his beard. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Zaid Al-Khudri, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution and running his fingers through his beard, so I said: Why did you do this, O Prophet of God? He said: My Lord commanded me to do that.” Tamim told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm, on the authority of Zaid al-Ami, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra - or: Yazid al-Raqashi - “on the authority of Anas, he said: I performed ablution for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he put his fingers under his chin and combed through his beard and said: This is what my Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, commanded me to do.” Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm Al-Madini, he said, Zaid Al-Ami told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abu Ubaidah al-Haddad told us, he said, Musa bin Tharwan told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is what my Lord commanded me! And he put his fingers in his beard and combed it. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham and Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Ilyas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, “On the authority of Umm Salamah: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and combed his beard.” Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Har told us, he said, Muhammad bin Rabia told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Sura, “on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said: We saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution and comb his beard.” Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said, Omar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, “on the authority of Abu Umamah: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and combed his beard.” Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Abu Umayya: Hassan bin Bilal Al-Muzni saw Ammar bin Yasir performing ablution and combing his beard, so he was asked: Do you do this? He said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do it. Abu al-Walid told us, al-Walid told us, Abu Amr told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi and Qatadah: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would rub his cheeks and interlock his beard with his fingers.” Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Mahdi Saeed bin Sinan told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriya, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Tanafisi Abu Abdullah told us, he said, Wasil Al-Raqashi told me, on the authority of Abu Sawda - this is how Al-Ahmasi said it - on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would rinse his mouth and wipe his beard from underneath with water. Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article regarding washing the inside of the nose and mouth: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said: I heard Mujahid say: Rinsing the nose is half of ablution. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, he said: I asked Hammad about a man who remembered while he was praying that he had not rinsed his mouth or sniffed water in his nose. Hammad said: He should turn away, rinse his mouth and sniff water in his nose. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, he said: I went to Kufa and went to Hammad and asked him about that - meaning: about someone who left rinsing the mouth and nose and prayed - and he said: I think he must repeat the prayer. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Shu`bah told us: Qatada used to say: If he leaves out rinsing his mouth, or inhaling water, or his ear, or a part of his foot, until he enters his prayer, then he should turn away, perform ablution, and repeat his prayer. Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article, that what is in front of the ears is from the face, and what is behind is from the head: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: What is in front of the ears is from the face, and what is behind it is from the head. Humayd bin Mas`adah told us, Yazid bin Zari` told us, Shu`bah told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam and Hammad, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi, regarding the ears: their inner parts are part of the face, and their outer parts are part of the head. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, he said: The front of the ears is part of the face, and the back of them is part of the head. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam and Hammad, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, similarly, except that he said: the inside of the ears. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi, similarly, except that he said: the inside of the ears. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: The inner parts of the ears are part of the face, and their outer parts are part of the head. Ibn Humayd told us, Abu Tamila told us, and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, they both said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah told me, on the authority of Ubayd God al-Khawlani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Shall I not perform ablution for you as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did? He said: We said: Yes! So he performed ablution, and when he washed his face, he put his thumbs in the front of his ears. He said: Then when he wiped his head, he wiped his ears from the backs of them. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: The face that God Almighty commanded the one who is standing for prayer to wash is everything that descends from the hairline of the head to the end of the chin in length, and between the ears in width, of what is apparent to the eye of the observer, without what is hidden of the mouth, nose, and eyes, and without what is covered by the hair of the beard, cheeks, and moustache, concealing it from the sight of observers, and without the ears. We said that this is more correct, even if what is under the hair of the beard and moustache was a face that must be washed before the growth of hair covering the eyes of onlookers, for the one who is standing for his prayer, because they all agree that the eyes are part of the face. Then, with their agreement on that, they are unanimous that washing what is above them of the eyelids without letting the water reach what is under the eyelids of them is sufficient. If this was a consensus from them, by the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, informing his nation of this, then similar to that is everything that is covered by something from the places of ablution on the body of the son of Adam from his very creation, covering it, the water does not reach it except with cost, effort, and treatment, by analogy to what we mentioned about the ruling on the eyes in this regard. If this is the case, then there is no doubt that the same as the eyes in terms of the difficulty of getting water to them when performing ablution, is what is inside of the nose, mouth, beard hair, temples, and moustache, because water cannot reach all of that except through treatment to get water to it, such as the cost of treating the pupils to get water to them or worse. If this is the case, it is clear that those of the Companions and Followers who washed what was under the hairline of the beard, the cheeks, and the moustache, and what was inside the nose and mouth, were only preferring the more difficult of two matters for him: washing that, and leaving it, just as Ibn Umar preferred washing what was under the eyelids with water by pouring water into that, not because that was an obligatory duty for him. As for the one who thought that their action was obligatory and mandatory, he has contradicted them in that by saying it is their method, and he has neglected the path of analogy, because analogy is what we have described of representing the disputed matter in that, with the agreed upon principle of the ruling on the eyes, and that there is no report from one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that obligated the one who neglected to let the water reach the roots of the hair of his beard and his cheeks in his ablution, and the one who neglected rinsing the mouth and nose, to repeat his prayer if he prayed with that purity. In that is the clearest evidence of the correctness of what we said, that their action, what they did, was a preference on their part for the better of the two actions, of neglecting and washing. If someone thinks that in the report that was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If one of you performs ablution, let him blow his nose. As evidence of the obligation of istinsar, the consensus of the argument is that it is not an obligatory duty, and that whoever leaves it must repeat the prayer that he prayed before washing, which makes it unnecessary to say much about it. As for the ears, the consensus of all of them is that leaving them out, or washing what is in front of them with the face, does not invalidate the prayer of the one who prays with the purity in which he left them out, along with their consensus that if he left out washing something that he must wash of his face in his ablution, then his prayer is not valid with that purity, which indicates that the statement in that is what the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, whose statement we mentioned: that they are not part of the face, not what Al-Sha’bi said. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding elbows. Are they part of the hand that must be washed, or not? After all of them agreed that washing the hand to them is obligatory. Malik bin Anas said, and he was asked about the statement of God: So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, do you think that the elbows should be left behind in ablution? He said: What was commanded is to reach the elbows, God the Blessed and Exalted said: So wash your faces, so this one went to wash behind him!! So it was said to him: So he should only wash up to the elbows and the ankles and not go beyond them? He said: I do not know what does not go beyond them, as for what he was commanded to reach it is this: to the elbows and the ankles - Yunus told us, on the authority of Ashhab, on his authority. Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of anyone who disagrees that the elbows are among what should be washed. It seems that he believes that its meaning is: Wash your faces and hands until you wash the elbows. Al-Rabi’ told us about that from him. Others said: God made obligatory in His statement: And your hands to the elbows, washing the hands to the elbows. The elbows are the limit of what God made obligatory to wash from the end of the hand, and the limit is not included in the definition, just as He changed the night from what God made obligatory for His servants to fast with His statement: Then complete the fast until the night (al-Baqarah 2:187). Because the night is the limit of the fast of the fasting person, if he reaches it he has fulfilled what is required of him. They said: Likewise the elbows in His statement: Then wash your faces and your hands to the elbows, are the limit of what God made obligatory to wash from the hand. This is the statement of Zafar ibn al-Hudhayl. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement regarding this matter, according to us, is that washing the hands up to the elbows is an obligation, and if one leaves it or part of it, his prayer will not be valid if he leaves it out. As for the elbows and what is beyond them, washing that is recommended, which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged his nation to do by saying: My nation will have radiant faces and white foreheads from the effects of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his radiance, let him do so. The prayer of one who neglects to wash them and what is behind them is not invalidated, because we have explained previously in what came before: that every purpose that is limited to to may in the speech of the Arabs include the purpose in the definition or its exclusion from it. If the speech includes that, then it is not permissible for anyone to rule that it is included in it, except for someone whose disagreement is not permissible in what is between him and a ruling and a ruling that the elbows are included, so what must be washed according to us is from someone whose ruling must be accepted. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the wiping that God commanded in His saying: And wipe over your heads. Some of them said: Wipe whatever you want to wipe on your heads with water when you stand up for prayer. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, Hammad bin Masada told us, on the authority of Isa bin Hafs, who said: Wiping the head was mentioned in the presence of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, so he said: O Nafi’, how did Ibn Umar wipe? He said: One wipe. And he described that he wiped the front of his head to his face, so Al-Qasim said: Ibn Umar is the most knowledgeable and most learned of us. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: Nafi’ told me: When Ibn Omar performed ablution, he would return his hands to the water and put them in it, then wipe the front of his head with his hands. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakir told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Nafi’ told me: Ibn Umar used to place the palm of his right hand on the water, then he would not shake it, then he would wipe with it the area between his horns to the forehead once, then he would not do more than that. In each of that, he would wipe once, moving from the forehead to the horn. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Al-Ansari, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that when he performed ablution, he would wipe the front of his head. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, he said: It is sufficient for you to wipe the front of your head if you are performing Umrah. And the woman should do the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abdullah Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: I saw Ibn Umar wipe his forehead once. Sufyan said: If he wiped a hair, it would suffice him, meaning one. Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abd al-Salam bin Harb told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Whichever side of your head you touch the water on, that is sufficient for you. Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ali bin Dhibyan told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Whichever side of your head you touch the water on, that is sufficient for you. Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Azraq, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, the same. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: Ibn Umar used to wipe his head like this, so Ayoub placed his palm in the middle of his head, then he passed it over the front of his head. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: If he wipes his head with one finger, that is sufficient for him. Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said: I said to Abu Amr: What is sufficient for wiping the head? He said: I prefer wiping the front of your head to the back of your head. Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me, on the authority of his father, on his authority, something similar. Others said: The meaning of this is: Wipe your entire head. They said: If he does not wipe his entire head with water, his prayer with that ablution is not valid. Who said that? Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Malik said: Whoever wipes part of his head but does not wipe it completely, must repeat the prayer, just as if he washed part of his face or part of his arm. He said: Malik was asked about wiping the head, he said: He begins from the front of his face, then moves his hands to the back of his head, then returns them to where he started. Others said: Wiping the head with less than three fingers is not sufficient. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, commanded wiping one’s head while standing for prayer, along with everything else that He commanded one to wash or wipe with it, and He did not set a limit for that which it is not permissible to fall short of or exceed. Since that is the case, then whatever the person performing ablution wipes from his head deserves to be said: He wiped his head, for he has fulfilled what God has enjoined upon him in wiping that, because it is included in what is required of him by the name of one wiping his head when he stands for prayer. If someone were to say to us: God said about dry ablution: Then wipe over your faces and your hands (An-Nisa’: 43), so is wiping part of the face and hands sufficient in dry ablution? It was said to him: Everything that is wiped with dirt, in what the scholars disputed, some of them said: It is sufficient for him as dry ablution, and some of them said: It is not sufficient for him, so it is sufficient for him, because it is included in the name of those who wipe with it. And whatever of that was agreed upon as not being sufficient, then it is accepted because of what the proof brought from its Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And no one has any proof against us in that, since it was from our saying: What came in the verses of the Book is general in meaning, so the rule is that it is general, until what must be accepted is made specific to it. So if something is made specific from it, then what was made specific from it is outside its apparent meaning and the rule for the rest of it is general. We have explained the reason for the validity of this statement in other places, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. The head that God Almighty commanded us to wipe with His saying: And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles, is the hair on the head, not including what goes beyond that to the nape of the neck, and not including what descends from that, facing the face to the forehead. Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed. A group of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: And your feet to the ankles, in the accusative case. Its interpretation is: When you stand up for prayer, wash your faces and your hands to the elbows and your feet to the ankles, and wipe your heads. If it is read like this, it is from the deferred meaning of bringing forward, and the feet would be in the accusative case in apposition to the hands. The reciters of this interpreted it like this, that God, the Most High, only commanded His servants to wash the feet, not wipe them. It was mentioned that he said: God meant by His saying: And your feet to the ankles, washing. Humayd bin Mas`adah told us, Yazid bin Zari` told us, Khalid Al-Hadha` told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, that a man prayed and there was a nail spot on the back of his foot. When he finished his prayer, Umar said to him: Repeat your ablution and your prayer. Hamid told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Israel told us, Abdullah bin Hassan told us, Hazil bin Sharhabil told us, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: Wet your fingers with water, do not wet them with fire. Abdullah bin Al-Sabah Al-Attar told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar Al-Hawdi told us, he said, Marji told us - meaning: Ibn Raja Al-Yashkari - he said, Abu Ruh Amara bin Abi Hafsa told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Hunayn: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man performing ablution while he was washing his feet, so he said: This is what I was commanded to do. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Waqid, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Khalidah, he said: I heard Mus`ab ibn Sa`d say: Umar ibn al-Khattab saw some people performing ablution, so he said: Make vinegar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: I heard Yahya say, I heard Al-Qasim say: Ibn Omar used to take off his shoes, then perform ablution, wash his feet, then interlace his toes. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn Adi, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: I said to al-Aswad: Did you see Umar washing his feet? He said: Yes. Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, he said, Muhammad bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Abdul Aziz: He said to Ibn Abi Suwaid: We have been informed of three people, all of whom saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, washing his feet, the closest of them being your cousin Al-Mughira. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Muhammad - who is Ibn Aban - on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: Wash the feet up to the ankles. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah: That Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man who had left something like a fingernail on the back of his foot, so he ordered him to repeat his ablution and prayer. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Shaiba ibn Nasah, he said: I accompanied Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad to Mecca, and I saw him, when he performed ablution for prayer, put his toes in and pour water over them. I said: O Abu Muhammad, why do you do this? He said: I saw Ibn Umar do it. Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us: I heard my father, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and wipe over your heads and your feet up to the ankles, he said: The matter returned to washing. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hafs Al-Ghadiri, on the authority of Amer bin Kulayb, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, he said: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, recited to me, and they recited: And your feet to the ankles, so Ali, may God be pleased with him, heard that - and he was judging between people - so he said: And your feet, this is from the introduction and the delay of speech. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he read it: And wipe over your heads and your feet in the accusative case, and he said: The matter returned to washing. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father: that he read it: and your feet, and he said: The matter returned to washing. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah: that he used to read: and your feet, in the accusative case. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles. As for and your feet up to the ankles, he says: Wash your faces, wash your feet, and wipe your heads. This is an example of advancing and delaying. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Shaiban, he said: It was proven to me on the authority of Ali that he read: And your feet. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father: And your feet, the matter goes back to washing. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: The companions of Abdullah used to recite it: And your feet, and they would wash them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: Wash the feet up to the ankles. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Sawda, on the authority of Ibn Abd Al-Khair, on the authority of his father, he said: I saw Ali perform ablution and wash the tops of his feet, and he said: If I had not seen the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do that, I would have thought that the bottom of the foot was more deserving than the top of it. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said: I did not see anyone wiping over the feet. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Mujahid, that he read: And your feet to the ankles, and he put it in the accusative case and said: It refers back to washing. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, I heard Al-A’mash read: And your feet, in the accusative case. Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said: Malik was asked about the statement of God, And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles, is it: your feet or: your feet? He said: It is only washing, not wiping. Do not wipe the feet, they are washed. It was said to him: What do you think of someone who wipes? Is that sufficient for him? He said: No. Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And wipe over your heads and your feet, he said: Wash them thoroughly. Others from the Hijaz and Iraq recited it as: And wipe your heads and your feet, lowering the feet. The reciters of this interpreted it as: God only commanded His servants to wipe the feet during ablution without washing them, and they made the feet in apposition to the head, so they lowered them for that reason. Mention of those who said that from the people of interpretation: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Qais Al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. Humayd ibn Mas`adah narrated, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, on the authority of Humayd, and Ya`qub ibn Ibrahim narrated, saying: Ibn `Ulayyah narrated, saying: Humayd narrated, saying: Musa ibn Anas said to Anas while we were with him: O Abu Hamza, al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon to us in Ahwaz and we were with him, and he mentioned purification and said: Wash your faces and your hands, and wipe your heads and your feet. There is nothing in the son of Adam closer to his filth than his feet, so wash their insides, their backs, and their heels. Anas said: God has spoken the truth and al-Hajjaj has lied. God said: And wipe your heads and your feet. Anas used to wet his feet when he wiped them. Ali bin Sahl told us, Muammil told us, Hammad told us, Asim al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Qur’an was revealed regarding wiping, and the Sunnah is washing. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Musa ibn Anas, he said: Al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon and said: Wash your faces, your hands, and your feet, their backs, their palms, and their heels, for that is closer to the most impure among you. Anas said: God spoke the truth and Al-Hajjaj lied. God said: And wipe over your heads and wipe over your feet to the ankles. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ubayd God al-Atki told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: There is no washing required of the feet, only wiping was revealed concerning them. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, who said: Wipe over your head and your feet. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Gabriel came down with the wiping. He said: Then Al-Sha’bi said: Do you not see that dry ablution is to wipe what was washed and nullify what was wiped? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: He was commanded to perform dry ablution as he was commanded to perform full ablution. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that he said: It is only wiping over the feet. Do you not see that what was required to be washed, was required to be wiped, and what was required to be wiped was neglected? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, that he said: He was commanded to wipe in dry ablution what he was commanded to wash in ablution, and he invalidated what he was commanded to wipe in ablution: the head and the feet. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: He was commanded to wipe with earth in dry ablution what he was commanded to wash with water, and he neglected what he was commanded to wipe with water. Ibn Abi Ziyad told us, Yazid told us, Ismail told us: I said to Amerah, some people say that Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with washing the feet! He said: Gabriel came down with wiping. Abu Bishr Al-Wasiti Ishaq bin Shahin told us, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said, someone who accompanied Ikrimah to Wasit told me: I did not see him wash his feet, he only wiped over them, until he came out of it. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles, God has made two washings and two wipings obligatory. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of Alqamah: that he read: And your feet, with the lam in the lowered position. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Al-Hussein Al-Akli told us, on the authority of Abdul-Warith, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid: that he used to recite: And your feet. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, he said, Al-Sha’bi used to recite: And your feet, in the accusative case. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saleh, on the authority of Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Jaafar: that he read: And your feet, in the accusative case. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: that he read: And your feet, with a kasra. Abu Ja`far said: The correct opinion in our view on this matter is that God, the Exalted, commanded the general wiping of the feet with water in ablution, just as He commanded the general wiping of the face with earth in dry ablution. If the person performing ablution does that to them, he deserves the name of a washer-washer, because washing them means passing water over them or touching them with water, and wiping them means passing the hand or something that takes the place of the hand over them. So if someone does that to them, then he is a washer-washer. Therefore - due to the possibility of wiping the two meanings described as general and specific, one of which is wiping with some, and the other wiping with all - the reading of the recitation differed in his saying: and your feet, so some of them put it in the accusative case, directing that to the fact that the obligation in them is washing, and denying wiping over them, with the apparent narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the generality of wiping them with water. Some of them lowered it, indicating that wiping is obligatory in both cases. And since we said in the interpretation of that - that it means the generality of wiping the feet with water - those who disliked the one performing ablution to suffice with putting his feet in the water without wiping them with his hand or with what takes the place of the hand, directed his saying: And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles, to wiping all of them in general with the hand, or with what takes the place of the hand, without some of them, with washing them with water, as: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us - Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar - on the authority of al-Ahwal, on the authority of Tawus that he was asked about a man who performs ablution and puts his feet in the water, he said: I do not consider that to be a great sin. And those who permitted it permitted it, indicating that it is meant for ablution, as: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Hisham mention, on the authority of Al-Hasan, about a man performing ablution on a ship, he said: There is nothing wrong with him immersing his feet in it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said: Abu Hura told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding a man who performs ablution on the edge of a ship, he said: He shakes his feet in the water. If the two meanings of wiping that we have described are: the generality of the feet with water, and the specificity of some of them with it, and it is correct with the indicative evidence that we will mention later, that what God intended by wiping them is generality, and their generality has the meaning of washing and wiping, then it is clear that the correctness of reading both readings, I mean the accusative for the feet and the genitive for the feet, is clear. Because in the generality of the feet by wiping them with water is washing them, and in passing the hand and what takes the place of the hand over them is wiping them. The correct reading of those who read it in the accusative case is that it is general in meaning by passing water over them. The correct reading of those who read it in the lowered form is because that involves passing the hand over them, or what takes the place of the hand, wiping them. However, even if that is the case, and both readings are good and correct, the reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with a dhammah, because of what I described of wiping combining the two meanings that I described, and because it is after His saying: And wipe your heads, so linking it to the heads, despite its proximity to it, is more appropriate than linking it to the hands, and it was prevented from it by His saying: And wipe your heads. If someone says: What is the evidence that what is meant by wiping the feet is general, without being specific, similar to what you said about wiping the head? It was said: The evidence for that is the apparent hadiths “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Woe to the heels and soles of the feet from the Fire.” If wiping part of the foot was sufficient for its generality, then there would be no woe for it for leaving what it left to wipe with water after wiping part of it. Because whoever fulfills God’s obligation upon him in what he is required to wash of it, does not deserve woe, rather he should have a great reward. In the obligation of woe for the heel of one who leaves out washing his heel in his ablution, there is the clearest evidence for the obligation of the generality of wiping the entire foot with water, and the correctness of what we said about that, and the invalidity of what contradicts it. Mentioning some of the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we mentioned: Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: Abu Hurayrah would pass by while we were performing ablution in the water-tub, and he would say: Perform ablution thoroughly, perform ablution thoroughly! Abu al-Qasim said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, except that he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, he said: “Abu Hurairah used to pass by people who were performing ablution but were not doing it properly, and he would say: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, he said, Sulayman bin Bilal told me, he said, Suhayl told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Ishaq bin Shaheen and Ismail bin Musa told me, they said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Saleh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire, and Ismail said in his hadith: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Husayn al-Mu`allim told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Salim al-Dawsi, who said: I entered with Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr upon Aisha, and he asked for water for ablution. Aisha said: O Abd al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ikrimah ibn Ammar told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, he said, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, he said, Abu Salim, the freed slave of al-Mahri told me - this is how Umar ibn Yunus said - he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr and I went out for the funeral of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas. He said: Abd al-Rahman and I passed by the room of Aisha, the sister of Abd al-Rahman, and Abd al-Rahman asked for water for ablution, and I heard Aisha calling out to him: O Abd al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Ali Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Salim, the freed slave of Dos, he said: I heard Aisha say to her brother Abd Al-Rahman: O Abd Al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Yaqub and Suwar bin Abdullah told me, they said: Yahya al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Sa`id bin Abi Sa`id, on the authority of Abu Salamah, that Aisha saw Abd al-Rahman performing ablution and she said: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Ibn Uyaynah and Yahya ibn Saeed al-Qattan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: Aisha saw Abd al-Rahman performing ablution, and she said: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid told us: Haywah ibn Shuraih told us: Abu Al-Aswad told us: Abu Abdullah, the freed slave of Shaddad ibn Al-Haad told him: He entered upon Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abd Al-Rahman was with her. Abd Al-Rahman performed ablution, then stood up and turned away. Aisha called out to him and said: O Abd Al-Rahman! So he turned to her, and she said to him: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, he said, Abu Ishaq told me, on the authority of Sa`id - or Shu`ayb - ibn Abi Karb, he said: I heard Jabir ibn `Abdullah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said, Al-Nadr told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said, I heard Ibn Abi Karb say, I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Woe to the heels - or: the heels - from the Fire.” Ismail bin Mahmoud Al-Hujairi told me, he said, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said, I heard Saeed say, I heard Jabir say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah bin Muharrib told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Aban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: I heard with my own ears from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah bin Muharib told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Aban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: I heard with my own ears from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man performing ablution and something remained from his heel, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.” Ali bin Muslim told me, he said, Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, but the water did not reach their heels, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.” Abu Sufyan al-Ghanawi Yazid bin Amr told us, he said, Khalaf bin al-Walid told us, he said, Ayoub bin Utbah told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Mu’ayqib, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, and he saw their heels shining, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform the prayer perfectly.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal Ibn Yassaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-A`raj, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution but they had not completed it, so he said: Perform the prayer perfectly, woe to the heels - or: the heels - from the Fire.” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of a man from the people of Mecca, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution but they did not complete it, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution and their heels were shining, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between Mecca and Medina, and some people preceded us and performed ablution. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and saw their feet white from the traces of ablution, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly. Ali bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Mutrah bin Yazid, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! He said: There was no noble or lowly person left in the mosque except that I looked at him turning his heels and looking at them. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah - or: Abu Umamah’s brother - “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, and on the heel of one of them - or: the heel of one of them - there was a spot the size of a dirham - or: the spot of a fingernail - that had not been touched by water, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! So he said: So if a man saw something on his heel that the water had not touched, he would repeat his ablution.” Abu Jaafar said: If someone says: What do you say about what he told you? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of Aws bin Abi Aws, he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution and wipe over his shoes, then he stood up and prayed.” What he told you: Abdullah bin Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal said, my father told me, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, he said, I heard Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s sandal and urinated on it while standing, then he called for water, performed ablution and wiped over his shoes.” What he told you: Al-Harith said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, Hisham told us, Ya`la bin Ata` told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aws bin Abi Aws, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, come to the courtyard of a people, perform ablution, and wipe over his feet. What is similar to this from the hadiths indicating that wiping part of the feet during ablution is sufficient? It was said to him: As for the hadith of Aws ibn Abi Aws, there is no evidence in it for the authenticity of that, since there was no mention in the report that was narrated from him that he saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution after an impurity that required him to perform ablution for his prayer, so he wiped over his shoes or his feet. It is possible that his wiping over his feet, which Aws mentioned, was in an ablution that he performed without an impurity that required him to renew his ablution, because the report from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if he performed ablution for something other than an impurity, he would do the same, is indicated by what: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said, Abu Malik Al-Junbi told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Habbah Al-Arni, he said: I saw Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, drinking in the courtyard while standing, then he performed ablution and wiped over his shoes. He said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. This is what I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do. This report has confirmed the correctness of what we said about the meaning of the hadith of Aws. If he said: The hadith of Aws, even if it is possible in meaning what I said, is also possible in meaning what was said by the one who said that it is meant to be wiping over the shoes or feet in an ablution that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed after a state of ritual impurity? It was said: The best cases of the report are those that carry what I said, if what was claimed of its possibility is accepted, what was mentioned about wiping the foot or the shoe after the impurity, even if that is not possible according to us, since it is not permissible for the obligations of God and the Sunnahs of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be contradictory and conflicting, and it has been authenticated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, the command to wash the feet in ablution with water in general, by the widespread transmission that conclusively excuses whoever reaches it and is informed of it. And since that is authentic from him, it is not permissible for it to be authentic from him permitting the omission of washing some of what he obligated to wash obligatorily, in one case and at one time. Because that is obligating an obligation and invalidating it in one case. And that is absent from the rulings of God and the rulings of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. However, if we accept what was claimed in the hadith of Aws, that it is possible that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped his foot while performing ablution after a major ritual impurity, out of our confidence in his argument that he has no proof for that, we say: If what you claimed is possible, is what we said possible, that it was done by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while performing ablution after a major ritual impurity? If he said no, his stubbornness is proven, because there is no statement in the hadith of Aws that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that in the ablution of someone who had become impure. And if he said: Rather, it is possible for what I said, and possible for what we said. He was asked: What is the proof that your interpretation, which you claimed, is more appropriate than our interpretation? He will not claim evidence for the validity of his claim in this regard, except that it will be countered by something similar in opposition to his claim. As for the hadith of Hudhayfah, the trustworthy preservers of hadith from the companions of Al-A’mash narrated it, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the courtyard of a people and urinated while standing, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks.” Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us that. He said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Issa bin Othman bin Issa Al-Ramli told me, he said, my uncle Yahya bin Issa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. All of these people narrate this from Al-A'mash with the chain of transmission we mentioned from Hudhayfah: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped over his socks." They are the companions of Al-A'mash. No one narrated this hadith from Al-A'mash except Jarir ibn Hazim. If no one had disagreed with him on this, it would have been necessary to verify it because of its anomaly. So how about when the trustworthy companions of Al-A'mash disagree with him in his narration of what he narrated of this!! If this was authentic from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it would have been permissible for him to have wiped over his shoes while they were worn over his socks. If this was permissible, then no one could have diverted the report to one of the possible meanings of the report except with an argument that must be accepted. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the heel. Some of them said: Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Al-Qasim bin Al-Fadl Al-Hadani told us, he said, Abu Jaafar said: Where are the ankles? The people said: Here. He said: This is the top of the leg, but the ankles are at the joint. Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Malik said: The heel towards which ablution must be performed is the heel attached to the leg, parallel to the heel, and not the one visible on the outside of the foot. Others said: Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of anyone who disagrees that the two heels that God mentioned in His Book regarding ablution are the two protruding ones, and they are the joint of the shin and foot. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement about this is that the heels are the two bones in the joint of the leg and foot, which the Arabs call the ankles. Some scholars of Arabic speech used to say: They are the two bones of the leg at its end. Scholars differed about the obligation of washing them in ablution, and the extent to which washing should reach on the feet, similar to their difference of opinion about the obligation of washing the elbows, and the extent to which washing should reach on the hands. We have mentioned that and provided evidence for the correct opinion with its reasons in what has passed before, so there is no need to repeat it. Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, is that if you are in a state of major ritual impurity before you stand up for your prayer and you stand up for it, then purify yourselves, meaning: purify yourselves by washing yourself before you enter into the prayer that you have stood up for. The word al-Janub is a noun that is used to describe all of them, because it is a noun that is used as a verb, as is said: A just man and just people, “A false man and false people,” and the like. The wording of one, all, two, male, and female is one. It is said: the man became impure, became impure, and avoided. The action is impurity and impurity. He heard in his collection of Ajnab, and this is not widespread in the speech of the Arabs, but rather the eloquent of their speech is what came in the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: If you are wounded or sick, and you are in a state of major ritual impurity. We have already explained that this is the case in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his statement: or on a journey, he is saying: And if you are travelling and you are in a state of major ritual impurity, or one of you comes from the toilet, meaning: or one of you comes from the toilet and has relieved himself in it while he is travelling. What he meant by mentioning his coming from it is relieving himself in it, or you have touched women, meaning: or you have intercourse with women while you are travelling. We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed in the past regarding touching, and we have explained the most correct of the opinions on that in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. If someone says: What is the reason for repeating his statement: or you have touched women, if the meaning of touching is sexual intercourse, and what is required of him has already been mentioned in his statement: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves? It was said: The reason for repeating this is that the meaning that the Most High obligated him to do in his statement: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourselves, is not the meaning that he obligated him to do in his statement: or have touched women. That is because he explained his ruling in his statement: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourselves, if he has access to water that purifies him, so he obligated him to perform ablution with it. Then he explained his ruling if he lacked water and could not find access to it and he was a traveler, not a sick resident, so he informed him that tayammum with earth would purify him in that case. Abu Ja`far said: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement: But if you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, is that if you do not find any, O believers, when you stand up for prayer and you are sick and resident, or on a journey and healthy, or one of you has come from relieving himself, or has had intercourse with his wife while travelling!
