Water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, meaning: then deliberately and aim to touch the surface of the earth, clean, meaning: pure and clean, not dirty or impure, permissible and lawful for you, and wipe your faces and your hands with it, meaning: then strike with your hands the earth that you performed tayammum with and deliberately struck with your hands, then wipe your faces and hands from what has stuck to your hands, from it, meaning: from the earth that you struck with your hands, from its dust and dirt. We have previously explained how to wipe the faces and hands with it, and the differences of opinion among those who differ on that, and the statement on the meaning of the ground and dry ablution, and we have provided evidence for the correct statement on all of that, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His statement, God does not want to place any difficulty on you, is that God does not want, by what He has imposed on you of ablution when you stand up for your prayer, and ritual washing after sexual impurity, and dry ablution with clean earth when you do not have water, to place any difficulty on you, to impose upon you hardship in your religion and not to make you suffer in it. And what we said about the meaning of hardship, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, and on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: from difficulty, they said: from tightness. Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: From hardship, from tightness. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: But He wants to purify you, is that God wants to purify you, by what He has imposed upon you of ablution from ritual impurity, ritual washing from major ritual impurity, and dry ablution when there is no water, so that you may clean and purify your bodies from sins, as: Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Sa`id told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, ablution expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes voluntary. I said: “Did you hear that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He said: Yes, not once, not twice, not three, not four, not five. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti told us: Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Mardanbah al-Qurashi told us: Ruqabah ibn Musaqala al-Abdi told us, on the authority of Shamr ibn Atiyah, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then stands up to pray, his sins will leave his hearing, sight, hands, and feet.’” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ka`b bin Murrah, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is no man who performs ablution, washing his hands or arms, except that his sins come out of them. So when he washes his face, his sins come out of his face. So when he wipes his head, his sins come out of his head. So when he washes his feet, his sins come out of his feet.’” Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us, he said, Hatim narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Abu Ubaid, the freed slave of Sulayman bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Amr bin Abasa, that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When a believer washes his hands, his sins fall from his hands. When he rinses his mouth and nose, his sins come out of his mouth and nostrils. When he washes his face, they come out of his face until they come out from the eyelashes. When he washes his hands, they come out of his hands. When he wipes his head and ears, they come out from his head and ears. When he washes his feet, they come out until they come out from the nails of his toes. When he has finished his ablution, that is his portion of it. If he stands and prays two rak’ahs, turning his face and heart to his Lord, his sins will be as if they were on the day his mother bore him. Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, he said, Malik ibn Anas told me, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When a Muslim servant - or a believer - performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he has looked at with his eyes will leave his face with the water - or with the last drop of water, or something like that - and when he washes his hands, every sin his hands have committed will leave his hands with the water - or with the last drop of water - until he emerges pure from sins.” Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told us, he said, Ali bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Zaid bin Aslam told us, on the authority of Hamran, the freed slave of Uthman, he said, I brought Uthman bin Affan some ablution water while he was sitting, so he performed ablution three times, three times, then he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution like this ablution of mine, then he said: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, his sins will be as if they were on the day his mother bore him, and his steps to the mosques will be voluntary. And His statement: And that He may complete His favor upon you, means that He says: And your Lord wants, along with purifying you from your sins by your obedience to Him in what He has enjoined upon you of ablution and ritual washing when you stand up for prayer, with water if you find it, and your dry ablution if you do not find it, to complete His favor upon you by permitting you to perform dry ablution and making pure earth a means of purification for you, as a concession from Him to you in that, along with all the other favors that He has bestowed upon you, O believers, that you may be grateful, meaning: so that you may thank God for the favors that He has bestowed upon you, by your obedience to Him in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you.
5:7: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And remember the blessing of God upon you, O believers, in the contracts that you made for God upon yourselves, and remember His blessing upon you in that, in that He guided you from the contracts to what is pleasing, and granted you success in what is your salvation from misguidance and ruin, in addition to many other blessings, such as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And remember the favor of God upon you, he said: The favors are the blessings of God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. As for his saying: And His covenant with which He has bound you, it means: And remember also, O believers, in the blessings of God that He has bestowed upon you, His covenant with which He has bound you, which is His promise that He has made to you. The people of interpretation differed regarding the covenant that God mentioned in this verse. Which of His covenants did He mean? Some of them said: He meant by it the covenant of God that the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were confident in, when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey him in what they liked and disliked, and to do everything that God and His Messenger commanded them to do. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you when you said, “We hear and we obey, the verse, meaning: when God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed the Book to him, and they said: We believe in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Book, and we acknowledge what is in the Torah, so God reminded them of His covenant which they acknowledged upon themselves, and He commanded them to fulfill it. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you with when you said, ‘We hear and we obey,’ for He took our covenant and we said, We hear and we obey, on the basis of faith and acknowledgment of Him and His Messenger. Others said: Rather, what He, may His praise be glorified, meant was His covenant that He took from His servants when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we testify. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And His covenant with which He bound you, he said: The covenant with which He bound the children of Adam in the back of Adam. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of Ibn `Abbas, which is that its meaning is: And remember, O believers, the favor of God upon you, which He bestowed upon you by guiding you to Islam, and His covenant by which He bound you, meaning: and His covenant by which He made a covenant with you when you pledged allegiance to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey him in ease and hardship, in difficulty and ease, when you said, ‘We hear,’ what you said to us, and you took from us the covenants, and we obeyed you in what you commanded us to do and what you forbade us from doing. And He also bestowed upon you success in accepting that from Him by saying to Him: We hear and we obey. He says: So fulfill to God, O believers, His covenant with which He has bound you, and His favor which He has bestowed upon you in that by your acknowledging upon yourselves that you will hear Him and obey what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you from doing. He will fulfill for you what He has guaranteed you to fulfill if you fulfill His covenant with Him, by completing His favor upon you, and by admitting you into His Paradise, and granting you eternal life in the abode of His honor, and saving you from His punishment and painful torment. Rather, we said that this is more correct than the statement of those who said that it meant the covenant that was taken from them in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, because God, the Most High, mentioned after reminding the believers His covenant with which He bound them, His covenant with which He bound the People of the Torah - after He revealed His Book to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, in what He commanded them and forbade them - in it, so He said: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders and the verses after that (Al-Ma’idah 5:12-13), thereby alerting the companions of the Messenger of God, Muhammad, peace be upon him, to the places where they have the opportunity to fulfill God’s covenant with them, and informing them of the evil end of the People of the Book in their neglect of what they neglected of His covenant with which He bound them in His commands and prohibitions, and strengthening His prophets and messengers, deterring them from breaking their covenants, so that what He had done to the covenant-breakers among the People of the Book before them would happen to them. So - since what he mentioned to them, admonished them with it, and forbade them from committing such an act was the covenant of a people whose covenant was taken after the Messenger was sent to them and the Book was revealed to them - it was necessary that the situation in which the covenant was taken and the admonished should be similar to the situation of those who were admonished. And if that is the case, then it is clear that what we said about that is correct, and the opposite of it is invalid. As for his saying: “And fear God. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts,” it is a threat from God, the Most High, to the believers who were among his companions in his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a warning to them that they would break the covenant of God with which he made them secure in his Messenger, and the promise they made to him in it, by harboring for him something other than what they expressed to him with their tongues. He, the Most High, says to them: And fear God, you believers, and fear Him lest you change His covenant and break His pledge with which He has bound you, or go against what you have guaranteed to Him by saying, We hear and we obey, by harboring for Him something other than fulfilling that in your souls. For God is aware of the secrets of your hearts, and knows what your souls conceal. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will bring upon you a punishment that you cannot bear, like what befell those Jews before you of transformation and various kinds of punishments, and you will become in your return to the wrath of God and His painful punishment.
5:8: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O you who believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, let your morals and characteristics be to stand up for God as witnesses to justice in your friends and enemies, and do not be unjust in your rulings and actions, so that you transgress what I have specified for you regarding your enemies because of their enmity towards you, and do not fall short in what I have specified for you of My rulings and limits regarding your friends because of their allegiance to you, but abide by My limits in all of them, and act in them according to My command. As for his saying: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just, he is saying: And let not the enmity of a people cause you to not be just in your judgment of them and your conduct among them, so that you transgress against them because of the enmity between you and them. We have mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of His statement: Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God (An-Nisa’: 135), and regarding His statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you (al-Ma’idah 5:2), and the differences of those who differed regarding the reading of that, which is more correct than the statement about it and the reading, with the evidence indicating its correctness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. It has been said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Jews intended to kill him. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir: “O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God. And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” It was revealed about the Jews of Khaybar, who wanted to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Kathir said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the Jews to ask for their help in paying blood money, and they intended to kill him. That is what His statement, And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just, is meant. Abu Ja`far said: By His saying, Be just, O believers, He means, “to treat everyone equally, whether they are your friends or enemies. So hold them to what I have commanded you to hold them to of My rulings, and do not transgress against any of them.” As for his saying: It is closer to piety, he means by his saying: It is, that justice towards them is closer to you, O believers, to piety, meaning: that you will be, with God, by using it, among the people of piety, and they are the people of fear and caution from God lest they disobey Him in any of His commands, or commit any of His sins. God Almighty described justice as closer to piety than injustice, because whoever is just is obedient to God through his justice, and whoever is obedient to God is undoubtedly one of the people of piety, and whoever is unjust is disobedient to God, and whoever is disobedient to God is far from his piety. Rather, he used the word it is closer as a metaphor for the verb. The Arabs use metaphors for verbs when you refer to them with it and that, as God, the Most High, said: It is better for you (al-Baqarah 2:271) and That is purer for you (al-Baqarah 2:232). If there was no it in the word it is closer, it would have been accusative, and it would have been said: Be just, it is closer to righteousness, as it was said: It is better for you to desist (al-Nisa’ 4:171). As for His statement: “And fear God. Indeed, God is Aware of what you do,” it means: Beware, O believers, of being unjust to His servants and transgressing His judgment and decree concerning them that He has made clear to you, lest His punishment befall you and you deserve His painful retribution. Indeed, God is Aware of what you do, meaning: God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of what you do, O believers, in what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you to do, whether you act upon it or oppose it. He has examined all of that against you, so that He may reward you with it as you are rewarded, the good-doer among you for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil, so beware of doing evil.
5:9: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, is the promise of God, O people, to those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what he brought to them from their Lord, and acted according to what God entrusted them with, and fulfilled the contracts that He made with them by saying: We will surely hear and obey God and His Messenger. So they heard God’s command and prohibition and obeyed Him, so they acted according to what God commanded them to do, and refrained from what He prohibited them from doing. What He means by His statement: For them is forgiveness, for those who fulfilled the contracts and covenant that their Lord made with them, forgiveness, which is covering and concealing their past sins, by His pardoning them for them, and leaving their punishment and disgrace for them, and a great reward, He says: And for them, along with His pardoning them for their past sins, as a reward for the deeds that they did, and their fulfillment of the contracts that they made with their Lord, is a great reward. The greatness of His goodness is unlimited in extent, and no one knows its end except Him, the Most High. If someone says: God Almighty informed in this verse that He promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, but He did not inform them of what He promised them, so where is the information about the promised? It is said: Yes, He informed about the promised, and the promised is His statement: For them is forgiveness and a great reward. If someone says: His statement: For them is forgiveness and a great reward, is the report of a subject, and if it were the promised, it would have been said: God promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward, and He did not include them in that, and in including that in it, there is evidence of the beginning of the speech and the end of the report of the promise! It was said: Even if its appearance is as you mentioned, it is one of the things that sufficed with the indication of what appeared from the speech to what was hidden from its meaning, from some that he left out mentioning in it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: God promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that He will forgive them and reward them with a great reward, because it is the nature of the Arabs to accompany the promise with an and to apply it in it, so an was left out since the promise is a statement. And it is the nature of the statement that what follows it from the sentences of report is the subject, and the sentence of report is mentioned after it to suffice with the indication of the appearance of the speech to its meaning, and to divert the promise that agrees with the statement in its meaning, even if its wording is different, to its meaning, so it is as if it was said: God said: For those who believe and do righteous deeds is forgiveness and a great reward. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was said: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward in reference to the promise that they were promised. So the meaning of the statement, according to the interpretation of the one who said this, is: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward in what He promised them.
5:10: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And those who disbelieved, and those who denied the Oneness of God and broke His covenant and contracts that they made with Him, and denied Our signs, meaning: and denied the proofs and arguments of God indicating His Oneness that were brought by the Messengers and others, those are the companions of Hellfire, meaning: those who have this description, are the people of Hellfire, meaning: the people of the Fire who will remain in it forever and will never come out of it.
5:11: Abu Ja'far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: O you who have believed, O you who have acknowledged the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to them from their Lord, Remember the favor of God upon you, remember the favor that God bestowed upon you, so thank Him for it by fulfilling His covenant with which He bound you, and the contracts that you made with your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He described His favor that He, the Most High, commanded them to thank Him for, along with all of His other favors, and said: It is His restraining from you the hands of the people who intended to attack you, so He turned them away from you, and prevented them from what they intended for you. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of this blessing that God Almighty mentioned to the companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanded them to thank Him for it. Some of them said: It is God’s rescue of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from what the Jews of Banu Nadir intended to do when they came to them demanding that they pay the blood money for the two Amris who were killed by Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri. Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, they said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu Nadir to ask for their help in paying the blood money for the two ‘Amiris whom Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed. When he came to them, some of them spoke to each other privately and said: ‘You will not find Muhammad closer than him now! Who is the man who will appear at this house and throw a rock at it and relieve us of him?’ Amr ibn Jahash ibn Ka’b said: ‘I will.’ So the report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he turned away from them, so God, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed about them and what he and his people intended: ‘O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you,’” the verse. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: When a people were about to stretch out their hands against you, he said: The Jews. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon them in their garden with his companions from behind its wall, so he sought their help in paying the blood money that he had paid, then he got up from them, and they conspired among themselves to kill him. So he went out walking backwards, looking at them, then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you, the Jews, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered their garden, and his companions were behind their garden, so he sought their help in a fine, in the blood money that he had paid, then he got up from them and they conspired among themselves to kill him, so he went out walking, crossing his arms, looking at them in fear. Then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him, God the Almighty said: So withhold their hands from you and fear God, and in God let the believers put their trust. Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, Abu Ma`shar narrated to me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Banu An-Nadir to ask for their help in a matter of insanity that he had suffered, and with him were Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali. He said: Help me in a matter of insanity that I have suffered. They said: Yes, O Abu Al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask us for something! Sit down so that we may feed you and give you what you ask of us! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions sat waiting for him, and Huyayy bin Akhtab came, and he was the head of the people, and he was the one who said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he said. Huyayy said to his companions: You do not see him closer than he is now. Throw stones at him and kill him, and you will never see any evil! So they came to a large millstone of theirs to throw them at him, but God held back their hands from it until Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and set him up from there. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed: ‘O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when they were a people who were about to They stretch out their hands against you, so restrain their hands from you and fear God, and upon God let the believers put their trust.” So God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what they intended for him. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Kathir: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you, the verse. He said: The Jews entered upon them in a garden and asked them for help in a debt he had lost, so they conspired among themselves to kill him, so he got up from them and went out, looking at them in fear, then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Ansari - one of the Banu Al-Najjar, and he was one of the leaders on the night of Al-Aqaba - and he sent him with thirty riders from the Muhajireen and Ansar, so they went out and met Amir bin Al-Tufayl bin Malik bin Ja’far at the well of Ma’unah, which is from the waters of Banu Amir, and they fought. Al-Mundhir and his companions were killed except for three men who were searching for something they had lost, and they were not startled until birds were circling in the sky, and blood clots were falling from between their trunks. One of the men said: Our companions have been killed, by the Most Merciful! Then he turned and ran until he met a man, and they exchanged two blows, and when the blow was mixed with his, he raised his head to the sky and opened his eyes and then said: God is Great, Paradise and the Lord of the Worlds!! So he was called Anqab to die, and his two companions returned and met two men from Banu Salim, and between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a truce between them and their people, so they attributed themselves to them from Banu Amir, and killed them. Their people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking for blood money. He went out with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, until they entered upon Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf and the Jews of Nadir, and he asked for their help in blood money for them. He said: The Jews gathered to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and they made an excuse by making food. Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him with what the Jews had agreed upon, which was treachery. He went out, then called Ali and said: Do not leave your place, and if any of my companions revolt against you and ask you about me, say: Go to Medina, and catch up with him. He said: So they passed by Ali, and he ordered them to do what he ordered, until the last of them came to him, then he followed them, and that is what His saying: “And you will not cease to find treachery among them” (al-Ma’idah 5:13). Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you, he said: It was revealed about Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf and his companions, when they intended to betray the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: Rather, the blessing that God mentioned in this verse, and commanded the believing companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to thank Him for it, is that the Jews intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, over a meal to which they had invited him, so God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they intended to do, so he and his companions stopped responding to him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you until his statement: and restrain their hands from you, that is because a group of Jews prepared food for the Messenger of God and his companions, in order to kill him when the food came, so God revealed to him about them, but the food did not come, and he ordered his companions, but they did not come to him. Others said: God Almighty meant by that: the blessing that He bestowed upon the believers by informing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what his enemy and their enemy, the polytheists, were up to on the day of Batn Nakhl, of their deceiving them and their attack on them, when they were distracted from them by their prayer and prostrated in it, and His informing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the need to beware of his enemy in his prayer, by teaching him the prayer of fear. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you Al-Baqarah 2:177. He mentioned to us that it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Batn Nakhl during the seventh battle. Banu Tha’labah and Banu Muharib wanted to kill him, but God informed him of that. He mentioned to us that a man volunteered to kill him, so he came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his sword was laid out. He said: Shall I take it, O Prophet of God? He said: Take it! He said: Shall I draw it? He said: Yes! Ask him. He said: Who can protect you from me? He said: God can protect me from you! So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threatened him and spoke harshly to him, so he drew his sword, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to depart, and the prayer of fear was revealed to him at that time. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he mentioned it on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Jabir: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place, and the people dispersed among the wild trees to seek shade under them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hung his weapon on a tree, and a Bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and took it and drew it, then he turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who can protect you from me? And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying: God! So the Bedouin drew the sword, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called his companions and told them what had happened to the Bedouin, while he was sitting beside him and did not punish him. Muammar said: Qatada used to mention something similar to this, and he mentioned that some Arabs wanted to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they sent this Bedouin, and he interpreted: Remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, the verse. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of those who said: God meant by the blessing mentioned in this verse, His blessing upon the believers in Him and His Messenger, which He bestowed upon them, in rescuing their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what the Jews of Banu Nadir intended to do, which was to kill him and those with him, on the day the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched to them regarding the blood money that he was carrying for the two men killed by Amr ibn Umayya. We said that this is more correct in interpreting it because God, the Most High, after mentioning that, accused the Jews of their deeds and ugly actions, and their betrayal of their Lord and their prophets, then He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pardon them and overlook their great ignorance. So it was known from this that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not commanded to pardon and overlook them immediately after His statement: When a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, and he extended his hands to others. Because if those who intended to stretch out their hands to them were not them, then it would have been more appropriate for the command to pardon and overlook them, not to those who were not mentioned about that, and the description of betrayal would have been in describing them in this place, not in describing those whose betrayal was not mentioned. So in that is what indicates the correctness of what we have decided to be correct from the interpretations in that, not what contradicts it. Abu Ja`far said: He, the Most High, means: O believers, beware of God, lest you disobey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and break the covenant with which He has bound you, so that you deserve from Him a punishment that you cannot bear. And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning: and to God let them face the reins of their affairs, and submit to His judgment, and trust in His victory and support, acknowledging the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger, acting according to His commands and prohibitions, for that is from the perfection of their religion and the completion of their faith, and that if they do that, He will protect them and watch over them, and preserve them from those who intended to harm them, just as He preserved and defended you, O believers, the Jews who intended to do what they intended to do by extending their hands to you, as a protection from Him for you, since you were from the people of faith in Him and in His Messenger, and none other, for none other than Him is able to repel the evil that your Lord intended for you, nor bring you any benefit that He did not decree for you.
5:12: Abu Ja`far said: This verse was revealed as an announcement from God, may His praise be glorified, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him, about the character of those Jews who intended to extend their hands to them, such as the one who: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, he said: The Jews are from the People of the Book. And that what they intended to do of treachery and breaking the covenant between them and him, is from their characteristics and the characteristics of their forefathers and their morals and the morals of their ancient ancestors, and as an argument for his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Jews, by informing him of what he knew of them but not of the Arabs, of the hidden matters of their affairs and the hidden knowledge of their sciences, and as a rebuke to the Jews for their persistence in error and their insistence on disbelief, despite their knowledge of the error of what they were establishing. God says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not consider the matter of those Jews who intended to extend their hands to you as too great, nor the matter of the treachery that they attempted and intended for you, for that is from the morals of their forefathers and ancestors, and they are no more than following the path of their forefathers and the way of their ancestors. Then the Almighty began the story of some of their treachery and betrayal, their audacity towards their Lord, and their breaking of the covenant that their Creator had bound them to, with His blessings that He had bestowed upon them, and His honors for which they were grateful. He said: And God had taken a covenant from those who had extended His hand to you from the Jews of the Children of Israel, O company of believers, to fulfill His covenants and obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Abu Ja`far Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, he said: God took their covenants that they would be sincere to Him and not worship anyone other than Him. And We sent from among them twelve leaders, meaning: And We sent from among them twelve guarantors, who guaranteed them the fulfillment of the covenants that We had entrusted to Him regarding what He had commanded them to do and what He had forbidden them to do. In Arabic, the naqib is like the arif chief of a people, except that he is above the arif. It is said: So-and-so dug into the Banu so-and-so, so he dug. If it is meant that he was not a naqib and became a naqib, it is said: he dug, so he dug a niqab. And from the arif: he dug into them, he is known as a fortune-teller. As for the manakib, they are like helpers who are with the arifs, one of them is mankab. Some scholars of Arabic say: He is the trustworthy guarantor of the people. As for the people of interpretation, they differed among themselves in its interpretation. Some of them said: He is a witness against his people. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel and raised up from among them twelve leaders, from each tribe a man to bear witness over his people. Others said: The captain, the trustee. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan, who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, who said: The leaders are the trustees. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, the same. God, the Almighty, commanded His Prophet Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, to send twelve leaders from his people, the Children of Israel, to the land of the giants in the Levant, to find out for Moses their report, since he wanted to destroy them, and to inherit their land and homes for Moses and his people, and to make them dwellings for the Children of Israel, after he had saved them from Pharaoh and his people, and brought them out of the land of Egypt. So Moses sent those whom God had commanded him to send to it from the leaders, as follows: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: God commanded the Children of Israel to march to Jericho, which is the land of Jerusalem, so they marched until they were close to them, then Musa sent twelve leaders from all the tribes of the Children of Israel, so they marched intending to bring him report of the giants, but a man from the giants called Aaj met them, so he took the twelve and put them in his cloak, and on his head were bearers of firewood. He went with them to his wife and said: Look at these people who claim that they want to fight us!! So he threw them in front of her, and said: Shall I not crush them with my feet! His wife said: Rather, leave them alone until they tell their people what they saw. So he did that. When the people went out, some of them said to one another: O people, if you tell the Children of Israel the report of the people, they will turn away from the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, but keep it secret and tell the Prophet of God, so that they will be the ones who make up their own minds! So some of them took a covenant from one another to keep it secret, then they returned. Ten of them went and broke the covenant, and a man began to tell his brother and his father what he had seen of the ivory, but two of them kept it secret. Then they came to Moses and Aaron and told them the story, and that is when God says: And God had taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up among them twelve leaders. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Twelve chiefs, from each tribe of the Children of Israel, a man. Moses sent them to the giants, and they found them, with two of them entering into the sleeve of each one of them, throwing them down, and no one would carry a bunch of grapes except five of them on a piece of wood, and five or four people would enter into the half of a pomegranate if its seeds were removed. So the chiefs returned, each of them forbidding his tribe from fighting them, except for Joshua ibn Nun and Kalb ibn Yafnah, who commanded the tribes to fight the giants and wage jihad against them, but they disobeyed these two and obeyed the others. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, in a similar manner - except that he said: From the Children of Israel are men - and he also said: They will meet them. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Moses was commanded to march with the Children of Israel to the Holy Land, and he said: I have written it down for you as a home, a settlement, and a place of residence. So go out to it and fight the enemy in it, for I will support you against them. And take from your people twelve leaders, from each tribe a leader who will be over his people by fulfilling what they were commanded to do, and say to them: God says to you: “I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakat” until His saying: then the right path has gone astray. And Moses took from them twelve leaders whom he chose from the tribes to be guarantors over their people in what they were in, by fulfilling his covenant and his pact. And from each tribe he took the best and most loyal of them a man - God Almighty says: And God had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders - so Moses marched with them to the Holy Land by God's command, until when he reached the desert between Egypt and Syria, a land where there was neither wine nor shade, Moses called upon his Lord when the heat harmed them, so He shaded them with clouds, and he called upon Him for provision, so God sent down upon them manna and quails. And God commanded Moses, saying: Send men to explore the land of Canaan which I gave to the Children of Israel, from each tribe a man. So Moses sent all the leaders who were among them, so God Almighty sent from the wilderness of Paran with the word of God, and they were the leaders of the Children of Israel. These are the names of the group whom God, the Most High, sent from the Children of Israel to the land of Ash-Sham, as the people of the Torah mention, to traverse it for the Children of Israel: From the tribe of Reuben: Shamon son of Zaccur, and from the tribe of Simeon: Shaphat son of Hari, and from the tribe of Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh, and from the tribe of As: Jegael son of Joseph, and from the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Ephraim: Joshua son of Nun, and from the tribe of Benjamin: Pelet son of Rephon, and from the tribe of Zebulun: Gidi son of Sodi, and from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph: Gidi son of Susa, and from the tribe of Dan: Hamlael son of Gamal, and from the tribe of Asher: Sathur son of Malkiel, and from the tribe of Naphtali: Nehi son of Povsi, and from the tribe of Gad: Golael son of Micah. These are the names of those whom Moses sent to feel out the land for him. On that day, Hoshea, son of Nun, was called Joshua, son of Nun. So he sent them and said to them, “Get up before the sun, leave the mountain, and see what is in the land, and what kind of people they have who inhabit it are: are they strong or weak, are they few or many? And see the land they inhabit: is it fat or lean? Does it have trees or not? Pass on, and bring us some of the fruit of that land!” And that was when the first fruits of the grapes were first harvested. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We sent from among them twelve leaders, they were from the Children of Israel, Moses sent them to look for the city for him, so they went and looked at the city and brought back a grain of their fruit, and a man was knocked down, so they said: Estimate the strength of a people and their might, this is their fruit!! At that point they were tempted and said: We are not able to fight, So go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here (al-Ma’idah 5:24). It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj Al-Marwazi who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid say regarding His statement: And We sent from among them twelve leaders, God commanded the Children of Israel to march to the Holy Land with their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. When they were close to Medina, Moses said to them: Enter it! But they refused and were cowardly, and sent twelve leaders to look at them. So they went and looked, and they brought a grain of their fruit the size of a man’s udder. They said: Appreciate the strength and might of a people; this is their fruit!! At that point they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight (al-Ma’idah 5:24). Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And God said to the Children of Israel: I am with you, meaning: I will support you against your enemy and My enemy whom I have commanded you to fight, if you fight them and fulfill My covenant and pledge that I took from you. There is something omitted in the speech, and what was apparent in the speech was dispensed with in what was omitted from it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: And God said to them, I am with you. So He left out mentioning them, dispensing with His saying: And God had taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, since the report had preceded about a people named specifically, so it was known that what was in the context of the speech of the report was about them, since the speech was not diverted from them to others. Then our Lord, may He be glorified, began the oath, saying: I swear that if you, the Children of Israel, establish prayer, give zakat, meaning: give it to those I have commanded you to give it, and believe in My messengers, meaning: and believe in what My messengers brought you of the laws of My religion. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas used to say: This is a speech from God to the twelve leaders. It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja`far narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas: That Moses, peace be upon him, said to the twelve leaders: Go to them - meaning: to the tyrants - and tell me their story and what they commanded, and do not fear, for God is with you as long as you establish prayer and give zakat and believe in My messengers and support them, and lend God a good loan. Abu Ja`far said: What Al-Rabi` said about this is not far from the truth, except that it is part of God’s decree for all of His creation that He supports those who obey Him, and takes care of those who follow His command, avoid disobeying Him, and avoid their sins. So since that is the case, and part of His obedience is establishing prayer, paying zakat, believing in the messengers, and all that He has urged the people to do, it is known that the expiation of sins and entering Paradise by it was not specific to the leaders and not to the rest of the Children of Israel. So it was more appropriate and fitting that it be an exhortation for all of the people and an urging for them to do what He urged them to do than it being an exhortation for some and an urging for a specific person and not a general one. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement: And you punished them. Some of them said: The interpretation of that is: And you supported them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And you supported them, he said: you aided them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And you supported them, he said: You aided them with the sword. Others said: It is obedience and support. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd say regarding His statement: And you honored them, he said: Honor and respect, obedience and support. The Arabs differed in their interpretation of it. It was mentioned on the authority of Yunus Al-Harmari that he used to say: The interpretation of that is: You praised them. I narrated this on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Ma`mar ibn al-Muthanna on his authority. Abu Ubaidah used to say: The meaning of this is: you supported them, helped them, honored them, glorified them, and supported them. And he recited in this regard: How many noble and generous are there among them, and how many lions are there who are honoured in the gathering. Al-Farra’ used to say: Al-‘azr is the response. I excused him, I responded to him, if I saw him committing injustice and I said: Fear God, or I forbade him, then that is al-‘azr. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: You supported them. That is because God, the Most High, said in Surat al-Fath 48:Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner * That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him and respect him (al-Fath 48:8-9). So respect is veneration. Since that is the case, then the saying in that is only some of what we mentioned from the sayings that we narrated from those we narrated from. If it is corrupted that its meaning is veneration, and victory may be by hand and tongue, as for the hand, it is defending it with the sword and other things, and as for the tongue, it is good praise and defending honor, then it is correct that it is victory, since victory contains the meaning of every speaker who said a saying about it from what we narrated from him. As for his statement: And you have loaned to God a good loan, he is saying: And you have spent in the way of God, and that is in the struggle against His enemy and your enemy, a good loan, he is saying: And you have spent what you have spent in His way, so you have attained the truth in your spending what you have spent in that, and you have not transgressed in it the limits of God and what He has urged you to do and urged you to do, and so on. If someone were to say to us: How did he say: And you have loaned God a good loan, and not say: a good loan, and you know that the source of I loaned is lending? It was said: If that had been said, it would have been correct, but his saying: A good loan, he extracted a source from its meaning, not from its wording. That is because in his saying: I lend, there is the meaning of I loan, as in the meaning of I gave there is I took. So the meaning of the statement is: And you have loaned God a good loan. Similar to that is: And God caused you to grow from the earth a plant (Nuh 71:17), since in I caused you to grow there is the meaning of: So you grew, and as Imru’ al-Qais said: I was satisfied and was humiliated in a difficult way Since the word raḍat means I humiliated, then humiliation is derived from its meaning, not from its wording. Abu Ja`far said: By that, He, the Most High, means the Children of Israel. He, the Most High, says to them: If you establish prayer, O people who gave Me their covenant to fulfill their obedience to Me and follow My command, and pay the zakat, and do all the rest of what I promised you, My Paradise, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds, meaning: I will cover with My pardon for you - and My forgiveness of your punishment, for your previous crimes that you committed between Me and you - your sins that you committed in the past, such as worshipping the calf and other deadly sins of yours, and I will admit you, while I cover that from you with My grace on the Day of Resurrection, into gardens beneath which rivers flow. In the gardens and orchards. I said that the meaning of his saying: I will certainly disbelieve is I will cover up, because disbelief means denial, covering up, and concealment, as Labid said: On a night when the stars are covered in clouds It means: he covered it, so takfir is the active participle of kufr. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of the letter lam in the phrase laakfarna. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The first lam has the meaning of an oath, meaning the lam in his saying: If you establish prayer. He said: The second has the meaning of another oath. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, the first lam is in the place of an oath, so it is sufficient for the oath, meaning with the first lam: If you establish prayer. He said: And the second lam, meaning his saying: I will surely expiate your sins from you, is an answer to it, meaning the lam in his saying: If you establish prayer. And he justified his saying that by saying: If you establish prayer is not complete, and does not dispense with his saying: I will surely expiate your sins from you. Since that is the case, it is not permissible for his saying: I will surely expiate your sins from you to be an introductory oath, rather it is obligatory for it to be an answer to the oath, since it does not dispense with it. And His saying: Rivers flow beneath it, means: Rivers flow beneath the trees of these gardens that I have brought you into. Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: Whoever among you, O children of Israel, denies anything that I have commanded him to do and abandons it, or commits what I have forbidden him to do and does it, after I have taken a covenant from him to fulfill my obedience and avoid disobeying me, has certainly strayed from the right path, meaning: he has missed the clear path and strayed from the straight path. And misguidance is riding without guidance, and we have explained that with evidence in other places. His saying equally means: middle, and the way means the road. We have explained the interpretation of all of this in another place, so there is no need to repeat it here.
5:13: Abu Ja`far said: The Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not be surprised by these Jews who intended to extend their hands to you and your companions, and broke the covenant between you and them, out of treachery towards you and your companions, for that is part of their customs and the customs of their ancestors, and part of that is that I took a covenant from their ancestors during the time of Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, to obey me, and I sent from them twelve leaders who were chosen from all of them to investigate the report of the tyrants, and I promised them victory over them, and that I would inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, after I showed them the lessons and signs - the destruction of Pharaoh and his people in the sea, and the splitting of the sea for them, and all the lessons - that I showed them, but they broke their covenant that they had pledged to me, and broke my covenant, so I cursed them for breaking their covenant. If this was done by their best, with their own hands, then do not find it strange that their scum did the same. There is an omission in the speech, so I sufficed with the apparent meaning of it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: So whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the right path - so they broke the covenant, so I cursed them, So because they broke their covenant We cursed them, so I sufficed with his statement: So because they broke their covenant from mentioning So they broke. What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Because they broke their covenant, is because they broke their covenant, as Qatada said. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them, meaning: So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Because they broke their covenant, he said: It is a covenant that God took from the people of the Torah, but they broke it. We have mentioned the meaning of cursing in other places. The ha and the mim in his saying: Because of their breach, refer to the mention of the Children of Israel before. Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed. The people of Medina, some of the people of Mecca, Basra and Kufa read it as Qasiyyah with an alif. On the assumption of the agent of the hardness of the heart, from the saying of the speaker: his heart hardened, so it hardens, and he is hard, and that is when it becomes thick and intense and becomes dry and hard, as the rajaz poet said: I was cruel and cruel to myself The interpretation of the statement according to this reading is: So We cursed those who broke My covenant and did not fulfill My covenant from among the Children of Israel, by breaking their covenant that they had pledged to Me, and We made their hearts hard, rough and dry from believing in Me and being guided to obey Me, stripped of compassion and mercy. The majority of Kufian readers read this as: And We made their hearts hard. Then those who read it differed in their interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of this is the meaning of cruelty, because fa’ila is more eloquent in censure than fa’ila, so we chose to read it as qasiyya instead of qasiyya, for that reason. Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of Qasiyyah is not the meaning of Qaswat, and rather Qasiyyah in this context is: the hearts whose faith in God is not sincere, but whose faith is mixed with disbelief, like Qasiyyah dirhams, which are those whose silver is mixed with adulteration of copper or lead or something else, as Abu Zubayd al-Ta’i said: She neighs in the deafening silence, as the cruel ones neigh in the hands of the money changers. This describes the impact of the surveyors who dug Uthman's grave on the rocks, which are peace. Abu Ja`far said: The reading that I like the most in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: And We made their hearts hard, with the letter fa`ilah, because it is more expressive in denouncing the people than qasiyyah. And the more correct of the two interpretations in this regard is the interpretation of the one who interprets it: fa`ilah from qaswa, as it was said: a pure soul and a pure woman, and a witness woman and a martyr, because God, may He be praised, described the people as having broken their covenant and disbelieved in Him, and He did not describe them with any faith, so their hearts are described as having faith mixed with disbelief, like hard dirhams mixed with adulteration of silver. Abu Ja`far said: God the Almighty says: And We made the hearts of those who broke Our covenants from the Children of Israel hard, from which goodness was removed, and guidance was taken away from them, so they neither believed nor were guided. So because God the Almighty removed guidance and faith from their hearts, they distorted the words of their Lord that He sent down to their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, which is the Torah, and they changed it and wrote with their own hands other than what God the Almighty sent down to their Prophet, then they said to the ignorant al-Nas 114:This is the word of God that He sent down to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, and the Torah that He revealed to him. This is from the description of the generations that came after Moses from the Jews, some of whom lived during the time of our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. However, God the Almighty included them among those about whom the story began from among those who lived during the time of Moses, since they were from their descendants, and they followed their method of lying about God, slandering Him, and breaking the covenants that He took from them in the Torah, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They distort words from their proper places, meaning: the limits of God in the Torah, and they say: If Muhammad commands you to do what you are upon, then accept it, and if he contradicts you, then beware. God Almighty means by His saying: And they forgot a portion, and they left a share, and it is like His saying: They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: they abandoned God’s command, so God abandoned them. This has been explained with evidence in other places, so there is no need to repeat it. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded, meaning: they left a portion. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded, he said: They abandoned the bonds of their religion, and the duties of God, may He be glorified, without which deeds are not accepted... Abu Ja`far said: The Blessed and Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And you, O Muhammad, will continue to see among the Jews, whose report I have informed you of, their breaking of My covenant and their breach of My agreement, despite their good deeds and My blessings upon them - despite such treachery and betrayal - ‘except a few of them’, except a few of them who did not betray.” The traitor in this context: betrayal, and it was placed - which is a noun - in the place of the source, as it was said: a sinner, for the sin, and a narrator for the nap. His saying: Except a few of them, is an exception to the ha’ and mim in his saying: On a traitor among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And you will not cease to find treachery among them, he said: treachery, lying, and immorality. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And you will not cease to find out about treachery on their part, he said: They are Jews, like what they intended to do to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the day he entered their garden. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid and Ikrimah said, his statement: And you will not cease to discover treachery among them, from the Jews, like the one who intended to harm the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the day he entered upon them. Some of the speakers said: The meaning of this is: And you will continue to find a traitor among them. He said: The Arabs add the letter ha’ to the end of the masculine, like their saying: He is a narrator of poetry, and a man of knowledge. And he recited: You told yourself to be loyal, and you were not a traitor to treachery, with your finger tied. He said: A traitor, while addressing a man. Abu Ja`far said: The correct interpretation of this is the statement we have narrated from the people of interpretation. Because God meant by this verse the people of the Jews of Banu Nadir who intended to kill the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them seeking their help in the blood money of the `Amiris, so God, the Exalted, informed him of what they intended to do. Then He, the Exalted, said after informing him of the report of their predecessors and informing him of the path of their ancestors, and that their last will follow the path of their first in treachery and betrayal, lest their action be considered too great for the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so He, the Exalted, said: And you will not cease to find out about treachery, betrayal, and breaking of covenant from the Jews, and He did not mean that He will not cease to find out about a traitor among them. This is because the report began with them about their group, so it was said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were determined to stretch out their hands against you, then it was said: And you will not cease to discover treachery among them, so since the beginning was about the group, then ending with the group is more appropriate. Abu Ja`far said: This is a command from God, the Almighty, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pardon these people who intended to extend their hands to him from the Jews. God, the Almighty, says to him: Pardon, O Muhammad, these Jews who intended to do what they intended to do, to extend their hands to you and your companions to kill you, and forgive them for their crime by refraining from exposing yourself to their harm, for I love the one who is good at pardoning and forgiving those who have wronged him. Qatada used to say: This is abrogated. He said: It was abrogated by the verse of Bara’ah: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, the verse (al-Tawbah 9:29). Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: So pardon them and overlook, he said: It was abrogated by: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful (al-Tawbah 9:29). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada: “So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.” He was not commanded that day to fight them, so God, the Exalted, commanded him to pardon them and overlook them. Then He abrogated that in Bara’ah, saying: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission while they are subdued.” (al-Tawbah 9:29), and they are the People of the Book, so God, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight them until they submit or acknowledge the jizyah. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, he said, I read on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Abu Ja`far said: What Qatada said is not possible. However, the abrogating verse that is undoubtedly in the command is that which negates all the meanings of the opposite of what came before it. As for that which does not negate all of it, there is no way to know that it is abrogating except by a report from God Almighty or from His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in His statement: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9:29), there is no indication of the command to negate the meanings of forgiveness and pardon for the Jews. And since that was the case, and it was permissible, with their acknowledgment of their humiliation and their payment of the jizya after the fighting, to order pardon for them in the treachery they intended to commit, or the breach they resolved to commit, as long as they did not set up spears without paying the jizya, and refrain from the rulings required of them, it was not necessary to rule, according to His statement: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9:29) the verse, that it abrogated His statement: “So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.”
5:14: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: And We took from the Christians a covenant to obey Me, perform My duties, follow My messengers, and believe in them. But they followed in My covenant that I took from them the path of the misguided nation of the Jews. So they changed their religion and broke it as they broke it, and they abandoned their share of My covenant that I took from them to fulfill My covenant, and they wasted My command, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And of those who said, ‘We are Christians,’ We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. They forgot the Book of God among them, and the covenant of God that He made with them, and the command of God that He commanded them with. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: The Christians said what the Jews said, and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement, So We stirred up discord among them, that We stirred up discord among them and cast discord, as one thing stirs up discord. God Almighty says: When these Christians, from whom I took a covenant to fulfill My covenant, abandoned their share of what I had entrusted to them of My commands and prohibitions, I stirred up enmity and hatred among them. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of God Almighty’s temptation of enmity and hatred among them. Some of them said: His temptation among them was due to the desires that occurred between them. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, regarding his statement: Then We stirred up among them enmity and hatred, he said: These are the different desires and hatred, so it is the temptation. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, he said: I heard Al-Nakha’i say: So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred, he said: He stirred some of them up against each other with disputes and arguments about religion. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Al-Taimi, regarding his statement: So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred, he said: I do not see the temptation in this verse except for different desires. And Mu’awiyah bin Qurra said: Disputes over religion nullify deeds. Others said: Rather, this is the enmity and hatred between them. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection the verse, because the people abandoned the Book of God, disobeyed His Messengers, neglected His obligations, and neglected His limits, He cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection, because of their evil deeds, and if the people had taken the Book of God and His command, they would not have separated nor hated one another. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the two interpretations of this, in our view, is the interpretation of the one who said: He incited them among themselves with the desires that arose among them, as Ibrahim al-Nakha`i said, because the enmity of the Christians among themselves is only due to their differences in what they said about the Messiah, and that is desires, not revelation from God. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the letters ha and mim in His statement: So We stirred up discord among them. Some of them said: He meant the Jews and Christians. So the meaning of the speech according to their statement and interpretation is: So We stirred up discord between the Jews and Christians, because they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He also said about the Christians: So they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So when they did that, God Almighty instilled enmity and hatred between them and the Jews until the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Then We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection, he said: They are the Jews and the Christians. Ibn Zayd said: Just as you cast enmity between two animals. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred, he said: The Jews and the Christians. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: They are the Jews and Christians, God has instilled enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection. Others said: Rather, God meant by that the Christians alone. They said: The meaning of that is: So We stirred up discord among the Christians, as a punishment for them forgetting a portion of what they were reminded of. They said: And upon it returned the ha and the mim in among them, not the Jews. Who said that? Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said: God, the Mighty and Sublime, said to the Children of Israel: Do not exchange the verses of God for a small price, and learn wisdom and do not take payment for it! But only a few of them did that, so they took bribes in judgment and exceeded the limits. So He said about the Jews when they ruled other than what God had commanded: And We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection (al-Ma’idah 5:64), and He said about the Christians: But they forgot a portion of that of which they had been reminded, so We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.
