Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse, in my opinion, is what Al-Rabi` bin Anas said, which is that what is meant by the temptation among them is the Christians, in this verse specifically, and that the ha and the mim refer to the Christians and not the Jews, because the mention of the temptation in God’s statement about the Christians, after He had completed His statement about the Jews, and after He had begun His statement about the Christians, so it is more appropriate for it to be meant for the Christians specifically than for it to be meant for both parties together, for what we have mentioned. If someone says: What is the enmity between Christians, so that it is specifically meant by that? It was said: This is the enmity between the Nestorians and the Jacobites, the royalists, and the royalists, the Nestorians and the Jacobites. And what was said by the one who said: (What is meant by that is: God’s temptation between the Jews and the Christians) is not far-fetched, but this is closer to me, and more similar to the interpretation of the verse, for what we mentioned. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Forgive those who intended to extend their hands to you and your companions and pardon them, for God Almighty is behind taking revenge on them. God will inform them when they come to Him in their place of resurrection, of what they did in this world, of breaking His covenant, violating His promise, altering His book, and distorting His commands and prohibitions. He will punish them for that according to what they deserved.
5:15: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says to the group of the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, who were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, Our Messenger has come to you, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: He makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book, meaning: Muhammad, our Messenger, makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal from the people and not make clear to them of what is in your Book. And among what they used to conceal from their Book, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear to the al-Nas 114:stoning married adulterers. It was said: This verse was revealed to clarify this to the people by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had hidden it from their book. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever disbelieves in stoning has disbelieved in the Qur’an without expecting it. His statement: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture, so stoning was among what they concealed. Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwaih told us, Ali bin Al-Hassan told us, Al-Hussein told us, Yazid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you, to His statement: a straight path, he said: The Jews came to the Prophet of God and asked him about stoning, and they gathered in a house. He said: Who among you is the most knowledgeable? They pointed to Ibn Suriya, so he said: Are you the most knowledgeable of them? He said: Ask whatever you wish! He said: Are you the most knowledgeable of them? He said: They claim that! He said: So he implored him by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, and the One who raised the mountain, and he implored him by the covenants that were taken from them, until he was overcome by fear. Then he said: Our women are beautiful women, and the killing among us has increased, so we shortened the hair, and we flogged a hundred, and shaved our heads, and we divided the heads among the animals - I think he said: camels - he said: So he ruled that they should be stoned, and God revealed about them: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you, the verse, and this verse: And when some of them are alone with others, they say, ‘Do you tell them what God has revealed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?’ (al-Baqarah 2:76). And His saying: And He pardons much, means by His saying: And He pardons, and He leaves you from being held accountable for much of what you were concealing from your book that God revealed to you, which is the Torah, so you do not act upon it until God commands him to take you by it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to those whom He addressed from the People of the Book: There has come to you, O People of the Torah and the Gospel, a light from God, meaning by the light Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, through whom God illuminated the truth, made Islam manifest, and destroyed polytheism. He is a light for those who are illuminated by him, clarifying the truth. And part of his illumination of the truth is his clarification to the Jews of much of what they had hidden in the Book. And His statement: And a clear Book, God Almighty says: There has come to you from God Almighty the light with which He has illuminated for you the landmarks of truth, and a clear Book, meaning a book in which there is an explanation of what they differed about among themselves: of the oneness of God, what He has permitted and forbidden, and the laws of His religion, and it is the Qur’an that He revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, explaining to the people everything they need of their religious affairs, and clarifying it for them, so that they may know its truth from its falsehood.
5:16: Abu Ja`far said: He, may His remembrance be glorified, means: He guides with this clear book that came from God, may He be glorified and exalted, and by His saying: God guides with it, He means that God guides with it and directs with it, and the ha’ in His saying: with it refers back to the book, whoever follows His pleasure, he says: whoever follows God’s pleasure. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of satisfaction from God Almighty. Some of them said: His satisfaction with something, acceptance of it, praise and commendation. They said: He accepts faith, purifies it, commends the believer for faith, and describes faith as light, guidance and separation. Others said: The meaning of satisfaction from God, the Almighty and Majestic, is an understood meaning, it is the opposite of discontent, and it is one of His attributes according to what is understood from the meanings: satisfaction which is the opposite of discontent, and that is not praise, because praise and commendation are words, and only that which is pleased is praised and commended. They said: So satisfaction is a meaning, and praise and commendation are a meaning that is not it. What he means by his saying: (paths of peace) are the ways of peace, and (peace) is God Almighty. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “Whoever follows His pleasure, the paths of peace,” the path of God that He has prescribed for His servants and called them to it, and with which He sent His messengers, which is Islam, and He does not accept any action from anyone except with it, neither Judaism, nor Christianity, nor Zoroastrianism. Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: God guides with this clear Book, whoever follows the pleasure of God to the paths of peace and the laws of His religion, and brings them out, meaning: and brings out whoever follows His pleasure, and the ha’ and meem in: and brings them out refers to whoever is mentioned, from darknesses into the light, meaning: from the darkness of disbelief and polytheism, to the light and radiance of Islam, by His permission, meaning: by the permission of God, the Almighty and Majestic. And His permission in this place: His making him love faith by removing the seal of disbelief from his heart, and the seal of polytheism from him, and enabling him to see the paths of peace. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Almighty, meant by His statement: And guides them, and directs them and directs them, to a straight path, is that He says: to a straight path, which is the upright religion of God in which there is no crookedness.
5:17: Abu Jaafar said: This is a condemnation from God Almighty for the Christians, men and women, who have strayed from the paths of peace, and an argument from Him for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their slander against him by claiming that he had a son. God Almighty says: I swear, those who said: God is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved. Their disbelief in that is their covering up the truth by abandoning the denial of a son for God Almighty, and their claim that the Messiah is God, a slander and a lie against Him. We have explained the meaning of the Messiah previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the Christians who have slandered me and have strayed from the right path by saying: God is the Messiah, son of Maryam 19:Who has control over anything from God? He says: Who is able to repel anything from the command of God Almighty, so that He may return it when He decrees it? From the saying: I have given control over so-and-so’s affairs, if he is unable to carry out an order except through it. And his saying: If He willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth, he says: Who is it that can prevent anything from God’s command, if He willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, by eliminating him from the earth, and eliminating his mother Mary, and eliminating everyone on earth from creation altogether. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these ignorant Christians: If the Messiah were as you claim - that he is God, and he is not - he would have been able to repel God’s command when it came to him to destroy him and his mother. And he destroyed his mother, but he was not able to repel His command when it came down. So in that there is a lesson for you if you consider, and an argument against you if you understand: that the Messiah was a human being like all the children of Adam, and that God the Almighty is the One who cannot be defeated or subdued and whose command cannot be repelled, rather He is the Ever-Living, the Eternal, the Self-Sustaining, who gives life and causes death, creates and destroys, and He is the Living One who does not die. Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Blessed and Exalted means: God has control over what is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them - meaning: what is between the heaven and the earth - He destroys whomever He wills of that and keeps whatever He wills of it, and creates what He wills and eliminates what He loves. Nothing prevents Him from doing what He wills of that, and nothing repels Him from it. He executes His judgment upon them, and His decree is carried out upon them - not the Messiah, who, if his Lord wanted to destroy him and destroy his mother, would not have the power to repel what his Lord wanted for him of that. God Almighty says: How can there be a god to be worshipped who is unable to repel the evil that others intended for him, and unable to avert the destruction that befell him? Rather, the god who is worshipped is the one who owns everything, and in whose hand is the control of everything in the heavens and the earth and everything in between. So He, the Most High, said: And what is between them. He mentioned the heavens in the plural form, and did not say: And what is between them, because the meaning is: And what is between these two types of things, as Al-Ra’i said: Knocks, that is my concern, I read them to you, fertile camels like bows and squints He said: Knocks, informing about two things, then he said: These are my concerns, so he returned to the meaning of the speech. And His statement: He creates what He wills, the Most High says: And He creates what He wills and brings it into existence, and brings it out from a state of nonexistence into a state of existence, and none is able to do that except God, the One, the Subduer. What He means by that is that He has the management of the heavens and the earth and everything in between and its disposition, its annihilation and its destruction, and the creation of whatever He wills of what does not exist and has no origin. He says: That is not for anyone but Me, so how did you claim, you liars, that the Messiah is a god, while he is not capable of any of that, rather he is not able to ward off harm from himself or his mother, nor bring any benefit to her except with My permission? Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God is the worshipped, He is able to do all things, and He owns all things, for whom nothing He wills is impossible, and nothing He seeks can overcome, He is able to destroy the Messiah, his mother, and everyone on earth, not the helpless one who is unable to prevent himself from the harm that has befallen him from God, nor to prevent his mother from destruction.
5:18: Abu Jaafar said: This is report from God Almighty about a group of Jews and Christians who said this statement. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas the name of the Jews who said that. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, saying, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, narrated to me, saying, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: “Nu’man bin Ada’, Bahri bin Amr, and Shas bin Adi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to them, and called them to God and warned them of His wrath. They said: What do you fear, O Muhammad? By God, we are the sons of God and His beloved!! Like the Christians say. So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed about them: ‘And the Jews and the Christians say, “We are the sons of God and His beloved,”’ until the end of the verse. Al-Saddī used to say about this: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “And the Jews and Christians said, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved.’ As for ‘the sons of God,’ they said, ‘God revealed to Israel that a child of yours will enter the Fire, and they will be in it for forty days until it purifies them and consumes their sins. Then a caller will call out, ‘Bring out every circumcised person from the children of Israel.’ So bring them out. That is what He said, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.’” (Al Imran 3:24). As for the Christians, a group of them said about the Messiah, ‘He is the son of God.’ The Arabs may present the report, if they boast, as a report about the group, even if what they boast about is the action of one of them, so they say: We are the generous and noble ones, and the generous one among them is only one of them, and the subject is not the speaker, as Jarir said: We stab Abu Mandusa, the blacksmith, with a spear, and the blood of a neighbor flows from his well He said: We infiltrated, and the infiltrator was a man from the people of Jarir other than him, so he reported the report as a report from a group of people, one of whom was one of them. Thus God Almighty informed us about the Christians that they said that, in this manner, God willing. And his saying: And his beloved ones, which is the plural of beloved. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to these liars who slander their Lord, Why has your Lord punished you? He says: Why would your Lord punish you for your sins, if the matter is as you claim, that you are His sons and beloved ones, for the Beloved does not punish His Beloved, and you admit that He will punish you? This is because the Jews said: God will punish us for forty days, the number of days in which we worshipped the calf, then He will bring us all out of it. So God said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to them: If you are, as you say, the sons of God and His beloved ones, then why has He punished you for your sins? He, the Mighty and Sublime, teaches them that they are people of slander and lies against God, the Mighty and Sublime. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: The matter is not as you claim, that you are the sons of God and His beloved, but you are human beings from among those He created. He says: He was created from the children of Adam. God created you like all the children of Adam. If you do good, you will be rewarded for your goodness, just as all the children of Adam are rewarded for their goodness. And if you do evil, you will be rewarded for your evil, just as others are rewarded for it. You have nothing with God except what others of His creation have, for He forgives whomever He wills of the people of faith in Him, so He pardons them with His grace and covers them for them with His mercy, so He does not punish them for them. We have explained the meaning of forgiveness in a place other than this with its evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And He punishes whomever He wills, meaning: He is just with whomever He wills of His creation, punishing him for his sins and disgracing him for them in front of all witnesses, so He does not conceal them from him. This is a warning from God, the Almighty, to those Jews and Christians who rely on the status of their chosen ancestors with God, whom God, the Almighty, the Almighty, preferred because of their obedience to Him, and chose them because of their hastening to please Him, and their patience in the face of what befell them. He says to them: Do not be deceived by the status of those with Me and their status with Me, for they only attained what they attained from Me through obedience to Me, and preferring My pleasure over their own desires, not through wishful thinking. So strive to obey Me, and desist from My command, and refrain from what I have forbidden them, for I only forgive the sins of whomever I wish to forgive from among the people of My obedience, and I punish whomever I wish to punish from among the people of My disobedience, not for those whose fathers were close to Me, but who are My enemies and oppose My commands and prohibitions. Al-Saddī used to say about this: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: He forgives whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills, meaning: He guides whomever He wills among you in this world and forgives him, and He causes whomever He wills among you to die in his disbelief and punishes him. Abu Ja`far said: He says: To God belongs the management and control of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them. In His hand is its command, and His is its kingdom. He disposes of it as He wills and manages it as He likes. He has no partner in anything of it, and no one has dominion over it with Him. So know, O you who say: We are the children of God and His beloved, that if He punishes you for your sins, you will have no one to prevent Him from doing so, nor will you be able to defend Him from it, because there is no kinship between anyone and Him that would favor him for that reason, and no one has dominion over anything below Him, that would stand between Him and Him if He wanted to punish him for his sins. To Him is the destination and return of everything. So fear, O slanderers, His punishment of you for your sins after you have returned to Him, and do not be deceived by hopes and the virtues of your fathers and ancestors.
5:19: Abu Ja`far said: By His saying, O People of the Book, He, the Most High, meant the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day this verse was revealed. That is because they - or: some of them, according to what was mentioned - when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to believe in him and in what he brought to them from God, they said: God did not send a prophet after Moses, nor did He send down a book after the Torah! Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, who narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, who narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Muadh bin Jabal, Saad bin Ubadah, and Uqbah bin Wahb said to the Jews: O group of Jews, fear God, for by God you know that he is the Messenger of God! You used to mention him to us before his mission, and you used to describe him to us with his characteristics! Rafi bin Huraymila and Wahb bin Yahudah said: We did not say this to you, and God did not send down any book after Moses, nor did He send a bearer of good tidings or a warner after him! So God, the Almighty, revealed regarding that from their words: “O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you [what is] clear [to the truth] after a hiatus among the messengers - lest you should say, ‘There has come to us no bearer of good tidings or a warner.’ But there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner. And God is over all things competent.” What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Our Messenger has come to you, is that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, our Messenger, has come to you, making clear to you, meaning: making the truth known to you, clarifying to you the signs of guidance, and guiding you to the approved religion of God, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: There has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you the truth after a hiatus among the messengers, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He came with the Criterion by which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. In it is God’s clarification, His light and His guidance, and protection for whoever takes it. After a period of messengers, he says: after a cessation of messengers, and the period in this place means cessation, he says: Our Messenger has come to you explaining to you the truth and guidance, after a cessation of messengers. The active period is from the saying of the speaker: This matter became calm and quiet, meaning it became still and quiet. Likewise, the period in this place means: stillness, meaning the stillness of the arrival of the messengers, which is its cessation. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the length of that period, and there was a difference in the narration of that from Qatada. Muammar narrated on his authority: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: After a period of time between the messengers, he said: There were five hundred and sixty years between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Saeed bin Abi Aruba narrated on his authority: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both, he told us was six hundred years, or whatever he wanted of that, and God knows best. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of his companions, regarding his statement: Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you the truth after a hiatus from the messengers. He said: There were five hundred and forty years between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both. Muammar said, Qatadah said: Five hundred and sixty years. Others said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: After a period of time between the messengers, he said: The period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both, was four hundred and thirty-some years. What he means by his saying: That you should say, ‘No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us,’ is that you should not say, and so that you should not say, as God Almighty said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 176), meaning: that you should not go astray, and so that you should not go astray. The meaning of the words is: Our Messenger has come to you, explaining to you after a period of messengers, so that you will not say, No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us. The Almighty informs them that He has cut off their excuse with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and has conveyed to them the argument. By Al-Bashir, he means the bearer of good tidings, the one who obeys God and believes in Him and His Messenger, and does what He has given him from God, with great reward in the Hereafter. And by Al-Nadhir, he means the one who warns, the one who disobeys Him and belies His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and does other than what God has given him of His commands and prohibitions, with what he cannot bear of painful punishment in the Hereafter, and severe torment on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to these Jews whose characteristics we have described: We have excused you, and we have argued with you through our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we have sent him to you to explain to you what is unclear to you about your religion, so that you will not say: No Messenger has come to us from you to explain to us what misguidance we are upon. A Messenger has come to you from Me, giving good tidings to whoever believes in Me and does what I have commanded him and refrains from what I have forbidden him, and warning whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command. I am the One who is capable of all things. I am the One who is capable of punishing whoever disobeys Me and rewarding whoever obeys Me. So fear My punishment for your disobedience to Me and your denial of My Messenger, and seek My reward for your obedience to Me and your belief in My good tidings and My warner, for I am the One for whom nothing I desire is impossible, and nothing I seek escapes from Him.
5:20: Abu Ja'far said: This is also from God, a definition for His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, of the long-standing persistence of these Jews in error, their distance from the truth, their poor choices for themselves, their severe opposition to their prophets, and their slowness in returning to the right path, despite the abundance of God's blessings upon them, and the succession of His favors and blessings upon them, thereby comforting His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for what befalls him in terms of their treatment, and what befalls him in terms of their suffering for the sake of God. God says to him, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not grieve over what has befallen you from them, for turning away from God, and being far from the truth, and what is in it for them is their share in this world and the hereafter, from their customs and the customs of their ancestors and their forefathers - and be comforted by what your brother Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, suffered from them - and remember when Moses said to them: O my people, remember the favor of God upon you, meaning: Remember the favors of God upon you, and His favors before you, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah: Remember the blessings of God upon you, he said: God’s favors upon you and His days. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Remember the favor of God upon you, meaning: the well-being of God Almighty. Abu Jaafar said: We chose what we said because God did not specify any of the blessings, but rather made it general by mentioning the blessings, so that applies to well-being and other things, since well-being is one of the meanings of blessings. Abu Ja`far said: By this, may His praise be glorified, He meant that Moses reminded his people, the Children of Israel, of the days of God with them, and of His blessings before them, urging them thereby to follow God’s command in fighting the tyrants. He said to them: Remember the blessing of God upon you, that He favored you, by placing among you prophets who bring you His revelation, and inform you of report of the unseen, and He did not give that to anyone other than you in your time. It was said: The prophets whom Moses mentioned that they were made among them are those whom Moses chose when he went to the mountain, and they are the seventy whom God mentioned when He said: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time (al-A’raf 7:153). And He made you kings, He made others serve you as servants. It was said: Moses said that to them because at that time there was no one other than them who served him from the sons of Adam. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when Moses said to his people, ‘O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made prophets among you and made you kings,’ he said: We used to say that they were the first of the sons of Adam to whom servants were made subservient and they became kings. Others said: Everyone who owns a house, a servant, and a woman is a king, whoever he is among the people. Who said that? Yunus bin Abdul A'la told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Hani told us: that he heard Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli say: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and a man asked him and said: Are we not among the poor emigrants? Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes! He said: Do you have a house to live in? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are among the rich! He said: I have a servant. He said: Then you are among the kings. Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar told us, he said, Abu Damrah Anas bin Ayyad told us, he said: I heard Zaid bin Aslam say: And He made you kings, so I do not know except that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a house and a servant is a king. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: that he recited this verse: And He made you kings, and he said: Is a king anything but a mount, a servant, and a house? Those who said this statement said: Moses only said that to them because they owned houses and servants, and had women and husbands. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur - he said: I think it was on the authority of Al-Hakam - And He made you kings, he said: When a man from the Children of Israel had a house, a wife, and a servant, he was considered a king. Hannad told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, H, and Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam: And He made you kings, he said: the house, the woman, and the servant. Sufyan said: Or, two of the three. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And He made you kings, he said: the house and the servant. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam or someone else, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And He made you kings, he said: the wife, the servant, and the house. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement: And He made you kings, he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Tamim, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God: And He made you kings, he said: If a man from the Children of Israel had a wife, a servant, and a house, he was called a king. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And made you kings, he said: He made servants their kings. Qatada said: They were the first to have servants as kings. Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Aban told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid: And He made you kings, he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses. Others said: What he meant by his saying: And made you kings is that they own themselves, their families, and their money. Who said that? Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And He made you kings, a man among you owns himself, his family, and his money. Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion about who was meant by this address. Some of them said: He meant the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair: And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, they said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: It refers to the people of Moses, peace be upon him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They are the people of Moses. Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Aban told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: They will be among him on that day. Then they differed about what God gave them that He did not give to anyone in the worlds. Some of them said: It is manna, quails, stones, and clouds. Who said that? Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: manna, quails, stones, and clouds. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning: the people of that time, manna, quails, stones, and clouds. Others said: It is the house, the servant, and the wife. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: A man will have a house, a servant, and a wife. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, the manna, the quails, the stones, and the clouds. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the two interpretations in this regard, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: And He gave you what He did not give to anyone in the worlds, in the context of His statement: Remember the favor of God upon you, and it is connected to it. There is no indication in the speech that his statement, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, is diverted from addressing those whom He began by addressing at the beginning of the verse. Since that is the case, then it is more appropriate for it to be addressed to them than to say that it is diverted from them to others. If someone thinks that his statement, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, cannot be addressed to them, since the nation of Muhammad had been given from the honor of God, the Almighty and Majestic, through their Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, what was not given to anyone else - and they are from the worlds - then he has thought incorrectly. That is because his statement, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, is an address from Moses, peace be upon him, to his people at that time, and he meant by that the scholars of his time, not the scholars of every time. And no one in the world had been given at that time from the blessings and honor of God what his people, peace be upon him, had been given. So the speech came from him, peace be upon him, in that regard, not to all scholars of every time.
5:21: Abu Jaafar said: This is report from God Almighty about what Moses, peace be upon him, said to his people from the Children of Israel, and his command to them - based on God’s command to him - to command them to enter the Holy Land. Then the people of interpretation differed about the land that he meant by the Holy Land. Some of them said: He meant the mountain and what is around it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The Holy Land is Al-Tur and what is around it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Enter the Holy Land, he said: Al-Tur and what is around it. Others said: It is the Levant. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: The Holy Land, he said: It is the Levant. Others said: It is the land of Jericho. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you, he said: Jericho. Yusuf bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: It is Jericho. Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It is Jericho. It was said that the Holy Land is Damascus, Palestine and some of Jordan. By his saying: the holy, he meant the purified and blessed, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The Holy Land, he said: The blessed one. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: It is the Holy Land, as the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, said, because the saying about it that it is a land apart from a land, the truth of its correctness cannot be known except by report, and no report about that can be used as a definitive testimony. However, it will not be outside of being from the land between the Euphrates and the Arish of Egypt, because of the consensus of all the people of interpretation, biography, and scholars of report on that. What he means by his saying: which God has written for you is that which He has established in the Preserved Tablet as being for you dwellings and homes, without the tyrants in it. If someone says: How could He say: which God has ordained for you, when you know that they did not enter it by His saying: It is forbidden to them? How could it be established in the Preserved Tablet that they are dwellings for them, but it is forbidden for them to inhabit them? It was said: It was written for the Children of Israel as a home and dwellings, and they inhabited it and settled in it and it became theirs, as God Almighty said. And Moses said to them: Enter the Holy Land which God has written for you, meaning by that: God wrote it for the Children of Israel, and those whom Moses commanded to enter it were from the Children of Israel, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mean that God Almighty wrote it for those whom He commanded to enter it specifically. If someone were to say: It was written for some of them and for a specific one of them, then he would make the statement general, and what is meant by it is the specific one, since Joshua and Caleb had entered, and they were among those addressed by this statement, then it would also be a correct view. Ibn Ishaq said something similar to what we said about that. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, which God has written for you, which God has given you. Al-Suddi used to say: The meaning of wrote in this context is: ordered. Musa bin Harun told us that, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Enter the Holy Land that God has written for you, which God has commanded you to do. Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty about what Moses, peace be upon him, said to his people from the Children of Israel, when he ordered them, according to the order of God Almighty to him, to enter the Holy Land, that he said to them: Go, O people, to the order of God that He ordered you to do, to enter the Holy Land, and do not turn back, he says: do not go back, turning back, on your heels, meaning: behind you, but go forward to the order of God that He ordered you to do, to enter upon the people whom God ordered you to fight and attack in their land, and God Almighty has written it for you as a dwelling and a place of settlement. What he means by his saying: Then you will return as losers, is that you will leave disappointed and destroyed. We have explained the meaning of loss in other places, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. If someone says: What was the reason for what Moses said to his people when he ordered them to enter the Holy Land: Do not turn back and become losers, or does he deserve loss if he does not enter a land that was made for him? It was said: God Almighty had commanded them to fight those in it who disbelieved in Him and imposed on them entering it, so the people deserved the loss by abandoning it when God imposed it on them for two reasons: One of them: wasting the obligation of jihad that God Almighty had imposed on them, and the second: their disobedience to God’s command in abandoning entering the land, and their saying to their prophet Moses, peace be upon him, when he said to them: Enter the Holy Land: We will not enter it until they leave it, so if they leave it, then we will enter. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O my people, enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you, they were commanded to do so, just as they were commanded to perform prayer, zakat, Hajj, and Umrah.
5:22: Abu Ja'far said: This is report from God, the Most High, about the response of the people of Moses, peace be upon him, when he ordered them to enter the Holy Land: that they refused to answer him to what he ordered them to do, and they argued with him about that by saying: In the Holy Land that you are ordering us to enter, there are a mighty people whom we have no strength to fight, nor do we have any power over. And they called them mighty because, due to the severity of their violence and the greatness of their character, as we have been told, they had subdued all other nations. The root of the word al-Jabbar is the one who reforms his own affairs and the affairs of others. Then it was used for anyone who brings benefit to himself, whether rightly or wrongly, seeking to reform it, until it was said of the one who transgresses against what is not his, out of oppression of people, and insolence towards them, and insolence towards his Lord, al-Jabbar. It is actually a verb from their saying: So-and-so repaired this fracture, if he repaired it and fixed it. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet: The religion has mended God, so mend the blindness of the Merciful, whoever turns to the blindness He means: God has reformed the religion, so it has been reformed. And among the names of God Almighty is the Compeller, because He is the one who reforms the affairs of His servants, the one who subdues them with His power. Among the greatness of their creation that I mentioned is: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said, Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a story he mentioned about the matter of Moses and the Children of Israel, he said: Then he ordered them to march to Jericho - which is the land of Jerusalem - so they marched, until they were close to them, Moses sent twelve leaders from all the tribes of the Children of Israel, so they marched intending to bring him report of the giants, but a man from the giants called Aaj met them, so he took the twelve and put them in his cloak, and on his head were loads of firewood, and he went with them to his wife and said: Look at these people who claim that they want to fight us!! So he threw them down in front of her, and said: Shall I not crush them with my feet? His wife said: No, rather leave them alone until they tell their people what they saw! So he did that. Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Saeed told us, Ikrimah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses was commanded to enter the city of the giants. Moses and those with him set out until they stopped near the city - which was Jericho - and he sent twelve spies to them, one from each tribe, to bring him report of the people. He said: So they entered the city and saw something terrible about their appearance, bodies, and size. So they entered a garden belonging to one of them. The owner of the garden came to pick the fruits from his garden, so he began to pick the fruits and look at their tracks, and followed them. Whenever he found one of them, he would take it and put it in his sleeve with the fruits, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said: You have seen our situation and our matter, go and inform your master. He said: So they returned to Moses and told him what they had seen of their situation. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, therein are a people of mighty men, he mentioned to us that they had bodies and character that no one else had. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi` who said: Moses, peace be upon him, said to his al-Nas 114:I will send men to bring me their report. He took a man from each tribe, and they were twelve chiefs. He said: Go to them and tell me their story and what they have been commanded to do, and do not fear. Indeed, God is with you as long as you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in His messengers, support them, and lend God a good loan. The people went until they attacked them, and they saw people with bodies that were amazing in size and strength. And - according to what was mentioned - one of the tyrants saw them, and they did not spare themselves from hiding themselves when they saw the wonder. So that tyrant took men from them, and he came to their leader and threw them in front of him, and they were amazed and laughed at them. Then one of them said: These people claimed that they wanted to attack you!! And that if it were not for what God had protected them from, they would have been killed, and that they returned to Moses, peace be upon him, and told him the wonder. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Twelve leaders, from each tribe of the Children of Israel, a man. Moses sent them to the giants, and they found them, two of them entering into the sleeve of one of them, throwing them down, and no one would carry their bunch of grapes except five people between them on a piece of wood, and five people, or four, would enter into half of the pomegranate when its seeds were removed. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Muhammad bin Wazir bin Qais told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: There are tyrants in it. He said: lowly people who have no morals. Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty about what the people of Moses said to Moses, in response to his saying to them: Enter the Holy Land which God has written for you. They said: We will not enter it until they leave it, meaning: until the tyrants who are in it leave the Holy Land, out of cowardice and fear of fighting them. And they said to him: If these tyrants leave it, we will enter it, otherwise we will not be able to enter it while they are in it, because we have no power over them and no ability to fight them. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Caleb bin Yufna silenced the people from Moses, peace be upon him, and said to them: We will ascend the land and inherit it, and we will have power through them! As for those who were with him, they said: We cannot reach that people, because they are bolder than us! Then those spies told the Children of Israel the report and said: We passed through a land and felt it, and behold, it devoured its inhabitants, and we saw its men as huge, and we saw giants, the sons of giants, and we were like locusts in their eyes! So the group of the Children of Israel became alarmed, and they raised their voices in weeping, and the people wept that night, and whispered to Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Oh, if only we had died in the land of Egypt! Oh, if only we had died in this wilderness, and God had not brought us into this land to fall into war, so that our women, children, and burdens would be spoils! If we had remained in the land of Egypt, it would have been better for us! The man said to his companions: Come, let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt.
5:23: Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty about the two righteous men from the people of Moses: Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana, that they were faithful to what Moses had entrusted them with, which was to leave informing his people, the Children of Israel - whom he had ordered to enter the Holy Land against the tyrants of the Canaanites - of what they had seen and witnessed of the severity of the tyrants’ brutality and the greatness of their creation, and God Almighty described them as being among those who fear God and observe Him in His commands and prohibitions, as: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, H, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, H, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed favor, said, he said: Kilab ibn Yafna and Joshua ibn Nun. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed His favor, said, he said: Joshua ibn Nun and Kilab ibn Yafna, and they were among the leaders. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid in a story he mentioned, he said: So the leaders returned, each of them forbidding his tribe from fighting them, except for Joshua bin Nun and Kalb bin Yafnah, who ordered the tribes to fight the tyrants and struggle against them, but they disobeyed them and obeyed the others, so they are the two men upon whom God bestowed His blessings. Ibn Hamid and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, like the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, except that Ibn Hamid said in his hadith: They are among the twelve leaders. Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saeed said, Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a story he mentioned. He said: So they returned - meaning the twelve leaders - to Moses and told him what they had witnessed of their situation. Moses said to them: Keep their affair secret, and do not tell anyone from the army about it, because if you tell them this report, they will fail and will not enter the city. He said: So each man of them went and told his relative and cousin, except for these two men - Joshua bin Nun and Kalb bin Yufnah - because they kept it secret and did not tell anyone about it, and they are the ones about whom God the Almighty said: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, until His saying: and among the wicked people. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed His favor, said, and they were the ones who concealed them: Joshua bin Al-Nun, the young man of Moses, and Calub bin Juphnah, the son-in-law of Moses. Sufyan told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah: “Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said: Caleb and Joshua bin al-Nun, the young man of Moses.” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Two men from among those who feared said, upon whom God bestowed favor, and the two men upon whom God bestowed favor from among the Children of Israel were: Joshua bin al-Nun, and Calub bin Yufnah. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, he told us that the two men were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`: That Moses said to the leaders when they returned and told him the wonder: Do not tell anyone what you have seen, for God will open it for you and make you prevail over it after what you have seen. And the people have spread the report among the Children of Israel, so two men from those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, stood up - one of them, as we heard, was Joshua bin Nun, who was the young man of Moses, and the other was Caleb - and they said: Enter upon them through the gate to if you are believers. Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: Two men from among those who fear said. This was read by the people of Hijaz, Iraq and Syria: Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, with the opening of the ya of they feared, according to the interpretation that we mentioned from the one we mentioned earlier, that they were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb, from the people of Moses, among those who feared God, and upon whom God had bestowed success. Qatada used to say: In some readings: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, H, and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Two men from among those who feared God’s favor upon them said, in some versions: They feared God’s favor upon them. This also indicates the correctness of the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as we mentioned about him, that he said: Joshua and Caleb. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he used to recite this: Two men from those who fear said, with the dammah on the ya’, God has bestowed His blessings upon them. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub - and we do not know that he heard it from him - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: that he used to read it with a dammah on the ya’ from yakhāfuun. It is as if Saeed went in this reading to the fact that the two men whom God told about who said to the Children of Israel: Enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious, were from the tribe of giants, and they had converted to Islam and followed Moses. So they were from the sons of giants whom the Children of Israel feared, even though they were opposed to them in religion. A similar interpretation was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you and do not turn back and become losers, he said: It is the city of the tyrants. When Moses and his people descended there, he sent twelve men from among them - they are the leaders whose mission he mentioned - to bring him report of them. So they set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, so he put them in his cloak, and carried them until he came to the city, and called out to his people, so they gathered around him, and said: Who are you? They said: We are the people of Moses, we were sent to you to bring him report of you! So they gave them a grape the size of a man’s udder, and they said to them: Go to Moses and his people and tell them: Estimate the size of their fruit! So when they came to them, they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here! Two men from among those who feared God, upon whom God had bestowed favor, and who were from the people of Medina, became Muslims and followed Moses and Aaron. They said to Moses, “Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be victorious. And upon God rely, if you should be believers.” Abu Ja`far said: According to this reading and interpretation, none of the twelve leaders concealed from the Children of Israel what Moses had ordered them to conceal from them of what they had seen and witnessed of the greatness of the giants’ bodies, the severity of their violence, and the wonders of their affairs. Rather, they disclosed all of that. The one who said to the people and to Moses, Enter upon them through the gate, were two men from the sons of those whom the Children of Israel feared and dreaded the giants entering upon them. They had converted to Islam and followed the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who reads: Of those who fear, God has bestowed His favor upon them both, due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on it, and that what is widely recited from them is an argument that cannot be contradicted, and what is recited by one person alone, error and forgetfulness are permissible in it. Then in the consensus of the argument in interpreting it that they are two men from the companions of Moses from the Children of Israel and that they are Joshua and Kalb, there is no need to cite evidence for the correctness of the reading with the opening of the ya’ in that, and the corruption of others. And it is the correct interpretation in our view, due to what we have mentioned of their consensus on it. As for his saying: God bestowed His favor upon them, it means: God bestowed His favor upon them by obeying God in obeying His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, and their adherence to his command, and their abstention from what he, peace be upon him, forbade them from, of divulging what they witnessed of the strange matter of the tyrants to the Children of Israel, which their other companions who were with them from the leaders had told about. It has been said that the meaning of this is: God bestowed fear upon them. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Khalaf bin Tamim told us, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Ali, his saying: Two men from among those who feared said, upon whom God bestowed His favor, he said: God bestowed His favor upon them with fear. Al-Dahhak and a group of others said something similar to what we said about that. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: “Two men from among those who feared said: God has bestowed His favor upon them,” with guidance, so He guided them, and they were on the religion of Moses, and they were in the city of the tyrants. Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty about the words of the two men who feared God to the Children of Israel, when they were cowardly and afraid to enter upon the tyrants, when they heard their report, and the leaders who spread what they had seen of their affair informed them, and they said: Indeed, there are tyrants in it, and we will not enter it until they leave it. So they said to them: Enter upon them, O people, through the gate of their city, for God is with you, and He is your supporter, and if you enter the gate, you will defeat them, as: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge of the first book, he said: When the children of Israel were about to return to Egypt, when the leaders informed them of what they had been told about the giants, Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in prostration before the assembly of the children of Israel, and Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana tore their clothes, and they were spies of the land, and they said to the assembly of the children of Israel: We passed through the land and found it to be good, our Lord was pleased with it for us and gave it to us, and it... flows with milk and honey, but do one thing: Do not disobey God, and do not fear the people who are in it, for they are our bread and are given into our hand. Their pride has gone from them, and God is with us, so do not fear them. So the assembly of the children of Israel wanted to stone them. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that they sent twelve men, one from each tribe, as spies for them, and to bring them report of the people. As for ten, they were cowardly towards their people and disliked them entering upon them. As for the two men, they ordered their people to enter it, and to follow the command of God, and they desired that, and they informed their people that they would be victorious if they did that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Upon them is the door, the village of the tyrants. Abu Ja`far said: This is also report from God, the Almighty, about the words of the two men who feared God, that they said to the people of Moses, encouraging them with that and encouraging them to follow God’s command to enter upon the tyrants in their city: O people, trust in God in your entry upon them. They said to them: Trust in God, for He is with you if you obey Him in what He has commanded you to do in jihad against your enemy. And what they meant by their words: If you are believers is if you believe your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he informed you about from your Lord about victory and triumph over them, and in other things of his information about his Lord, and believe that your Lord is able to fulfill what He promised you of empowering you in the lands of His enemy and your enemy.
5:24: Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God, the Most High, about the words of the leaders of Moses’ people to Moses, when they desired to fight their enemy, and promised them victory from God if they opposed them and entered upon them through the gate of their city, that they said to him: We will never enter it, meaning: We will never enter their city. The letter ha and the letter alif in his saying: We will not enter it are from the mention of the city. And by their saying: Forever, they mean as long as they are in it, meaning: as long as the tyrants were residing in that city that God had written for them and which they had been commanded to enter, “So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here,” we will not come with you, O Moses, if you go to them to fight them, but we will leave you to go alone, you and your Lord, and fight them. Some of them said about that: The meaning of the words is not: Go, you, and let your Lord go with you and fight, but rather it means: Go, you, O Moses, and let your Lord help you, and that is because God Almighty is not permitted to go. This would only require seeking a way out if the report was about a group of believers. As for a group of people who disagree with God Almighty and His Messenger, there is no reason to seek a way out for their words in what they said about God Almighty and slandered Him, except in what resembles their disbelief and misguidance. It was reported that Al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something contrary to what the people of Moses said to Moses. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq: that Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We do not say as the Children of Israel said: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, we are sitting here, but we say: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, we are with you fighting. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists prevented the sacrificial animals and they were prevented from performing their rituals: I am going with the sacrificial animals and slaughtering them near the House! Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad said to him: By God, we will not be like the leaders of the Children of Israel when they said to their prophet: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, and we are sitting here. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight, and we are fighting with you! When the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard it, they followed one another in that. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and a group of others said: They only said this to Moses, peace be upon him, when the matter of the tyrants and the severity of their violence became clear to them. Al-Husayn narrated, he said: I heard Abu Muadh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: God, the Almighty and Majestic, commanded the Children of Israel to march to the Holy Land with their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. When they were close to Medina, Moses said to them: Enter it. They refused and were cowardly. They sent twelve leaders to look at them. They went and looked and brought a piece of their fruit the size of a man’s udder. They said: Estimate the strength and might of a people; this is their fruit! Then they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will stay here. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar.
5:25: Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God, the Almighty, about what the people of Moses said to him when his people said to him what they said, of their saying: "We will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will remain right here." He said at that time, and became angry at what they said to him, supplicating: O Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother. He meant by that: I have no power over anyone to compel them to do what I love and want of obeying You and following Your commands and prohibitions, except over myself and my brother. From the saying: I do not have control over anything of the matter except such and such, meaning: I am not able to do anything other than that. What he means by his saying: So separate us from the wicked people is separate us from them by a judgment from You that You will carry out in us and in them, and distance them from us. From the saying of the poet: I separated between these two things, meaning: I separated between them, from the saying of the rajaz poet: Oh God, separate him from me as much as you separate two people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So separate us from the wicked people, he said: Judge between me and them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So separate us from the wicked people, meaning: Judge between us and them. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Moses, peace be upon him, became angry when the people said to him: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will stay here.” So he called down curses on them and said: My Lord, I have no control over anyone but myself and my brother, so separate us from the wicked people. And it was a haste on the part of Moses that he hastened. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: So separate us from the wicked people, meaning: Judge between us and them, and resolve between us and them - all of this is the man saying: Judge between us - so the judgment of God, may His praise be exalted, between him and them is that He called them wicked. By his saying: the wicked, he meant those who have departed from faith in God and in Him to disbelief in God and in Him. We have already demonstrated that the meaning of wickedness is to depart from one thing to another, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it.
5:26: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the one who opposes the forty. Some of them said: The one who made it an enemy is his saying: forbidden. God Almighty forbade the people who disobeyed Him and went against His command from the people of Moses and refused to fight the tyrants from entering their city for forty years. Then He conquered it for them and settled them in it, and He destroyed the tyrants after they fought them, after the forty years had passed and they had left the wilderness. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, he said: When the people said to them what they said, and Moses invoked God against them, God revealed to Moses: “It is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.” And they were, as he mentioned, on that day six hundred thousand fighters. So He made them defiantly disobedient because they disobeyed. So they remained for forty years in six farsakhs or less, walking every day in order to get out of it until they became tired and stopped, and behold, they were in the house from which they had departed, and that they complained to Moses about what had been done to them, so he sent down manna and quails upon them, and they were given as much clothing as was available for them, and the young one would grow up and it would be with him in his form. And Moses asked his Lord to give them drink, so He brought the Stone of Mount Tur, which is a white stone. When the people descended, he would strike it with his staff, and twelve springs would come out of it, one for each tribe, and each people would know their drinking place. Then, when forty years had passed, and they were torments because of their transgression and disobedience, it was revealed to Moses: Tell them to go to the Holy Land, for God has sufficed them against their enemy, and tell them, when they come to the mosque, to go to the gate, and prostrate themselves when they enter, and say: Forgiveness - and their saying Forgiveness means that their sins would be forgiven - but most of the people refused and disobeyed, and prostrated on their cheeks, and said: Wheat. So God, the Most High, said: But those who did wrong substituted a statement other than that which was said to them to: because they were defiantly disobedient (al-Baqarah 2:59). Others said: Rather, the object of the forty is they wander in the land. They said: The meaning of the statement is: He said, It is forbidden to them forever, they wander in the land for forty years. They said: And none of those who said, We will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here, entered the city of the tyrants. This is because God, the Exalted, forbade it to them. They said: And only Joshua and Kalb entered it from those people, who said to them, Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be victorious, and the children of those whom God forbade entering it, so God wandered them and none of them entered it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God Almighty: It is forbidden to them, he said: Forever. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God: They wander in the land, he said, forty years. Al-Muthanna told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Harun al-Nahwi told us, al-Zubayr bin al-Kharit told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: It is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander throughout the land, he said: Prohibition means wandering. Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Moses became angry with his people and supplicated against them, saying: My Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother verse. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: Then it is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander in the land. When the wilderness was imposed upon them, Moses regretted it. His people who were with him and obeyed him came to him and said to him: What have you done to us, O Moses? So they remained in the wilderness. When they came out of the wilderness, the manna and quails were taken away and they ate from the vegetables. Then Moses and Ij met, and Moses ascended ten cubits into the sky, and his staff was ten cubits long, and his height was ten cubits, so he struck Ij’s heel and killed him. None of those who refused to enter the city of the giants with Moses remained, except that he died and did not witness the conquest. Then, when the forty years had passed, God Almighty sent Joshua bin Nun as a prophet. He informed them that he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants. They pledged allegiance to him and believed him. He defeated the tyrants and they attacked them, killing them. A group of the Children of Israel would gather around a man’s neck and strike it, but they would not cut it off. Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saeed said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God the Almighty said: When Moses called, It is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander in the land. He said: So they entered the wilderness, and everyone who entered the wilderness who was over twenty years old died in the wilderness. He said: So Moses died in the wilderness, and Aaron died before him. He said: So they remained in their wandering for forty years, and Joshua and those who remained with him confronted the city of the giants, and Joshua conquered the city. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God Almighty said: It is forbidden to them for forty years, [the villages] were forbidden to them, so they would not descend into a village nor would they be able to do so, but they would follow the valleys for forty years, and it was mentioned to us that Moses, peace be upon him, died at the age of forty, and that none of them entered the Holy House except their sons and the two men who said what they said. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said, some of the people of knowledge of the first book told me: When the Children of Israel did what they did, of disobeying their prophet and their intention to attack Caleb and Joshua, when he ordered them to enter the city of giants, and they said to them what they said, the greatness of God appeared in the clouds over the door of the Tabernacle of the Cities over all the Children of Israel, and He, the Most High, said to Moses: How long will this people disobey Me?
