And how long will they not believe in all the signs that I have placed among them? I will strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make for you a people stronger and greater than them. Then Moses said, “The people of Egypt, from whom you have brought this people out by your power, will hear, and the inhabitants of this country, who have heard that you are God among this people, will say, ‘If you had slain all this people as one man, the nations who have heard of your name would have said, ‘This people was slain because they were not able to enter the land for which you created them.’ So they slew them in the wilderness. But let your hand be lifted up and your recompense be great, O LORD, as you have spoken and said to them. For your patience is long-suffering, your graciousness is abundant, and you forgive iniquities and do not repent. You reserve the iniquity of the fathers for the children and the children’s children for three generations and four years. Therefore, O LORD, forgive the iniquities of this people according to the abundance of your graciousness, as you have forgiven them since you brought them out of the land of Egypt until now.” Then God Almighty said to Moses, peace be upon him: I have forgiven them by Your word, but as I live, My praise has filled the entire earth. The people who have seen My praise and My signs that I performed in the land of Egypt and in the deserts, and who have tested Me ten times and have not obeyed Me, will not see the land that I swore to their fathers, nor will those who angered Me see it. As for My servant Caleb, whose spirit was with Me and who followed My desire, I will bring him into the land which he entered and he will see it behind him. Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites were sitting in the mountains, and they set out into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea. And the Lord spoke to Moses and Haran and said to them, How long will this evil company whisper against me? I have heard the whispering of the children of Israel. And he said, "I will do to you as I said to you, and you will cast your corpses into these wildernesses, and according to your reckoning from me, twenty years and more, because you whispered against me. You shall not enter the land to which I raised my hand, nor shall any of you dwell in it except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. And your burdens shall be, as you were, spoil. But your children this day, who did not know good from evil, they shall enter the land, and I know them; they shall have the land that I intended for them. And your corpses shall fall in these wildernesses, and you shall wander in these wildernesses according to the number of days that you counted the land for forty days, instead of each day a year, and you shall be killed for your sins for forty years, and you shall know that you whispered before me." I, God, will do this to this congregation, to this congregation of the children of Israel, who promised before me that they would wander in the wilderness and die there. As for the group that Moses had sent to probe the land, and they stirred up the congregation and spread evil report among them, they all died suddenly, but Joshua and Caleb the son of Joseph lived from the group that had gone out to probe the land. When Moses, peace be upon him, said all these words to the children of Israel, the people were very sad, and they went up to the top of the mountain and said: We will ascend the land of which God Almighty has spoken, because we have sinned. Moses said to them: Why do you transgress against the word of God? For that reason no work will be right for you, and you will not ascend, because God is not with you. Now you will be defeated by your enemies, because of the Amalekites and the Canaanites who are before you. Do not fall into battle because you have turned against God, and God was not with you. So they began to ascend the mountain, and the ark in which were the covenants of God Almighty and Moses did not leave the camp, meaning from the tent, until the Amalekites and the Canaanites descended to that wall, and burned them and chased them out and killed them. So God Almighty caused them to wander in the wilderness for forty years because of their disobedience, until those who deserved disobedience from God in that case perished. He said: When their descendants grew up and their fathers perished and the forty years in which they wandered had passed, Moses set out with them, accompanied by Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana, who was, as they claim, the wife of Mary, the daughter of Imran, the sister of Moses and Aaron, and was their son-in-law. Joshua bin Nun came to Jericho with the Children of Israel, and entered it with them, and killed the giants who were in it. Then Moses entered it with the Children of Israel, and he stayed in it as long as God willed him to stay, then God took him to Himself, and no one among creation knows his grave. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion of those who said: The forty are the object of the prohibition, and that His statement: Forbidden to them for forty years refers to all of the people of Moses, not some of them but not others. This is because God, the Exalted, mentioned that people in general and did not specify some of them but not others. God, the Exalted, fulfilled what He promised them of punishment, so He made them wander for forty years, and He forbade all of them, during the forty years in which they remained wandering, from entering the Holy Land. None of them entered it, neither young nor old, neither righteous nor wicked, until the years in which God, the Exalted, forbade them from entering it had passed. Then He permitted those who remained of them and their descendants to enter it with the Prophet of God, Moses, and the two men upon whom God had bestowed His favor. The city of the giants was conquered, God willing, by the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, and Joshua was at his head. This is due to the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the ancients that Og bin Anaq was killed by Moses, peace be upon him. If he had killed him before his fate in the wilderness, and he was one of the greatest tyrants in creation, the Children of Israel would not have been so terrified by the tyrants as they were. But that was, God willing, after the annihilation of the nation that had been terrified and disobeyed its Lord, and refused to enter the city of the tyrants. Moreover, the people of knowledge of the stories of the ancients agree that Balaam bin Ba'ur was among those who aided the tyrants by praying against Moses. It is impossible that this happened while the people of Moses were refraining from fighting and struggling against them, because aid is only needed by those who are sought after. As for those who are not seeking, there is no reason to need it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf, he said: Og’s bed was eight hundred cubits long, and Moses’ height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits, and he jumped into the sky ten cubits, and he struck Og and hit his heel, and he fell dead, and it became a bridge for people to walk over. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Moses’ staff was ten cubits long, and his jump was ten cubits long, and his height was ten cubits, so he jumped and hit the heel of Awj and killed him, and it was a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year. The meaning of: They wander in the land is that they are confused and go astray. Hence, the man who has strayed from the path of truth is called a wanderer. Their wandering was that they would spend forty years every day walking a distance of six farsakhs to get out of it, and they would end up in the place from which they had begun their journey. Al-Muthanna told me that. He said, Ishaq told us. He said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The Children of Israel wandered for forty years, going to bed where they had gone to bed in their wanderings. Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: Do not despair, do not be sad. It is said: So-and-so is sad about such-and-such, he is sad and I am saddened by such-and-such, meaning I am sad. From this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: My companions stood there on their mounts and said: Do not perish in sorrow and be patient. Meaning: Do not perish with grief. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So do not despair, he said: So do not be sad. Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: So do not grieve over the wicked people, he said: When the wilderness struck them, Musa, peace be upon him, regretted it, and when he regretted it, God revealed to him: So do not grieve over the wicked people, do not grieve over the people whom you called wicked, so he did not grieve.
5:27: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And recite to these Jews who intended to stretch out their hands against you, and to your companions with them, and make them aware of the evil consequences of injustice and deceit, and the evil consequences of treachery and breaking a covenant, and the reward of the treacherous and the faithful, the story of the two sons of Adam, Abel and Cain, and what happened to the one of them who obeyed his Lord and fulfilled his covenant, and what happened to the one of them who disobeyed his Lord and broke his covenant. So let the Jews know by this the terrible consequences of their treachery and their breaking of their covenant between you and them, and their intentions of what they intended to do of stretching out their hands against you and your companions, for you and them, in the goodness of My reward and the greatness of My recompense for fulfilling the covenant with which I rewarded the murdered one of the sons of Adam who fulfilled his covenant, and punished the murderer who broke his covenant, a beautiful consolation. Scholars differed about the reason for the two sons of Adam offering sacrifices, the reason for God Almighty accepting what He accepted from them, and who were the two who offered sacrifices. Some of them said: It was by the command of God Almighty to them to bring it near, and the reason for acceptance was that the one who was accepted brought near the best of his wealth, and the other brought near the worst of his wealth. And the two who were brought near were the two sons of Adam, one of them: Abel, and the other: Cain. Who said that? Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Ismail bin Rafi’, he said: It has reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer sacrifices, one of them was a shepherd, and a lamb had been born to him among his sheep, and he loved it so much that he would give it precedence at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love for it, until he had no wealth more beloved to him than it. So when he was commanded to offer sacrifices, he offered them to God, and God accepted them from him, and they continued to graze in Paradise until the son of Abraham, may God bless them both, was ransomed by it. Ibn Bashar narrated, Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated, Awf narrated, on the authority of Abu al-Mughira, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr, who said: The two sons of Adam who offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them and not from the other, one of them was a farmer and the other was a sheep owner. They were both commanded to offer a sacrifice, and the sheep owner offered the most noble, fattest and best of his sheep, pleased with them, while the farmer offered the worst of his crops, the darnel and the tares, but he was not pleased with them. And God accepted the sheep owner’s sacrifice, but He did not accept the sacrifice of the farmer. And of their story is what God has related in His Book. And he said: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but he was prevented from extending his hand to his brother by his shame. Others said: This was not their command, as God commanded them to do. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It was their custom that no poor person would be given charity, but rather the offering would be offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said: If we offer an offering, and if a man offered an offering and God was pleased with him, He would send fire to him and consume him. And if God was not pleased with him, the fire would go out. So they offered an offering, and one of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came and descended between them, and it consumed the sheep and left the crops. And the son of Adam said to his brother: Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you and rejected me? By God, people will not look at me and you, although you are better than me!! He said: I will kill you! His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: When they offered a sacrifice, he said: The two sons of Adam, Abel and Cain, from the loins of Adam. So one of them offered a sheep, and the other offered a vegetable, and it was accepted by the owner of the sheep, so its owner killed it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, he said: Abel and Cain. Abel offered a young goat from the best of his sheep, and Cain offered a crop from his crop. He said: The fire consumed the young goats but did not consume the crops, so he said: I will kill you! He said: God only accepts from the righteous. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man heard Mujahid tell us about his statement: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, he said: It is Abel and Cain from the loins of Adam. They offered a sacrifice. One of them offered a sheep from his flock, and the other offered green vegetables, and it was accepted from the owner of the sheep. He said to his companion, I will kill you! So he killed him. So God tied one of his legs with its shin to its thigh until the Day of Resurrection, and he made his face to the sun wherever it turned. He had a fence of snow over him in the winter, and a fence of fire over him in the summer. He had seven angels with him, and whenever one of them went away another would come. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, H, and Hannad told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said: This one offered a ram, and this one offered a heap of food, and it was accepted from one of them. He said: It was accepted from the owner of the sheep, but it was not accepted from the other. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. There were two men from the sons of Adam, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyyah: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth. He said: One of them was called Qabil, and the other Abel. One of them was a shepherd, and the other a farmer. So this one brought a lamb from the best of his sheep, and this one brought a lamb from the worst of his crops. He said: Then the fire came down and consumed the lamb, and he said to his brother: I will kill you! Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the scholars of the first book: That Adam ordered his son Cain to marry his twin sister, Abel, and ordered Abel to marry his twin sister, Cain, so he submitted to that. Abel was pleased, but Cain refused and disliked that, out of respect for Abel’s sister, and he preferred his sister over Abel, and said: We are the offspring of Paradise, and they are the offspring of Earth, and I have more right to my sister! Some of the scholars of the first book say: Cain’s sister was one of the best people, but he was stingy with her for his brother and wanted her for himself. And God knows best which of them it was. His father said to him: O my son, she is not lawful for you! But Cain refused to accept that from his father, so his father said to him: O my son, offer a sacrifice, and let your brother Abel offer a sacrifice, so whichever of you God accepts his sacrifice is more entitled to her. Cain was in charge of sowing the land, and Abel was in charge of tending the livestock. Cain offered wheat, and Abel offered the firstborn of his sheep - and some say: he offered a cow - so God Almighty sent a white fire that consumed Abel’s offering, and left Cain’s offering, and thus the offering was accepted if he accepted it. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: No child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of this other womb, and he would marry the girl of this womb to the boy of this other womb. Until two sons were born to him, they were called: Qabil and Abel. Qabil was a farmer, and Abel was a milker. Qabil was the older of them, and he had a sister who was more beautiful than Abel’s sister. Abel asked to marry Qabil’s sister, but he refused and said: She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I have more right to marry her! So his father ordered him to marry her to Abel, but he refused. They both offered a sacrifice to God, which of them had more right to the girl? Adam had gone away from them to Mecca to look at her. God, the Almighty, said to Adam: O Adam, do you know that I have a house on earth? He said: O God, no! He said: I have a house in Mecca, so go to it. Adam said to the sky: Keep my son in trust, but it refused. He said to the earth, but it refused. He said to the mountains, but it refused. He said to Cain, but it said: Yes, you can go and come back and find your family as you please. When Adam set out, they offered a sacrifice, and Cain was proud of him and said: I have more right to her than you, she is my sister, and I am older than you, and I am my father’s successor! When they offered it, Abel offered a fat young tree, and Cain offered a bundle of ears of corn. He found a large ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it. Then the fire came down and consumed Abel’s sacrifice, and left Cain’s sacrifice. He became angry and said: I will kill you so that you will not marry my sister! Abel said: God only accepts from the righteous. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth, he mentioned to us that they were Abel and Cain. As for Abel, he was a herder, so he took the best of his herd and offered it as an offering, but a fire descended upon it and consumed it - and if an offering was accepted from them, a fire descended upon it and consumed it. And if it was returned to them, the birds and wild beasts would eat it - as for Cain, he was a farmer, so he took the worst of his crops and offered it as an offering, but the fire did not descend upon him. So he became envious of his brother and said: I will kill you! He said: God only accepts from the righteous. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth, he said: They are Abel and Cain. He said: One of them was a farmer and the other a livestock owner. So one of them came with the best of his wealth and the other came with the worst of his wealth. Then the fire came and consumed the sacrifice of one of them, which was Abel, and left the sacrifice of the other. So he envied him and said: I will kill you! Sufyan told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: When they offered a sacrifice, he said: This one offered crops, and that one offered a young goat, and the fire left the crops and consumed the young goats. Others said: The two who offered a sacrifice, and God Almighty narrated their stories in this verse: two men from the Children of Israel, not from the descendants of Adam through his loins. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The two men mentioned in the Qur’an, about whom God said: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, were from the Children of Israel, and they were not the sons of Adam by his loins, but rather the sacrifice was among the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is that the two who offered the sacrifice were Adam’s two sons from his loins, not from his descendants from the Children of Israel. This is because God Almighty is too exalted to address His servants with what does not benefit them, and those addressed by this verse knew that offering the sacrifice to God was only for the children of Adam, not the angels, devils, and all other creation. So since this was known to them, it is reasonable that if what was meant by the two sons of Adam whom God mentioned in His Book were not his two sons from his loins, He would not have benefited them by mentioning them with a benefit that they did not have. Since it was not permissible for him to address them in a way that did not give them any meaning, it is known that he meant by the sons of Adam the sons of Adam by his loins, not the sons of his sons who were descended from him, despite the consensus of the people of report, biographies, and knowledge of interpretation that they were the sons of Adam by his loins, and in the time and era of Adam, and that is sufficient as evidence. We have mentioned many of those who have stated this, and we will mention many of those who have not, God willing. Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hussam bin Al-Mask told us, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained sad for a hundred years, not laughing. Then he came and it was said to him: May God give you life and happiness! He said: May God make you laugh. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ghiyath bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, he said, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam cried and said: The country and its people have changed, the color of the earth is dusty and ugly Everything changed in color and taste, and the pretty face became less cheerful. So Adam, peace be upon him, was answered: Abel's father and father were all killed, and the living became like the dead slaughtered. And Bashara came, whom he had been afraid of, so he brought her, shouting: Abu Ja`far said: As for the statement about their bringing them near as they brought them near, the correct statement is to say that God, the Mighty and Sublime, informed His servants about them that they had brought them near, and He did not inform them that bringing them near as they brought them near was by God’s command to them, nor by other than His command. It is possible that it was by God’s command to them to do that, and it is possible that it was by other than His command. However, whichever of the two it was, they did not bring that near except to seek nearness to God, God willing. As for the interpretation of his statement: He said, ‘I will kill you,’ its meaning is: The one whose offering was not accepted said to the one whose offering was accepted: I will kill you. So he omitted mentioning the one whose offering was accepted and the one whose offering was rejected, because what had already been mentioned of them sufficed without repeating it. Likewise, he omitted mentioning the one whose offering was accepted with his statement, He said, ‘God only accepts from the righteous.’ In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said, ‘I will kill you.’ His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, God only accepts from those who fear Him, he said, he says: If you feared God in your offering, it would be accepted from you. You came with an offering adulterated with the worst of what you have, and I came with a pure offering with the best of what I have. He said: And he said: God accepts from you but does not accept from me! What he means by his saying: of the righteous is those who fear God and are in awe of Him, by performing the duties He has charged them with, and avoiding the acts of disobedience He has forbidden them. A group of interpreters said: The pious in this context are those who avoid polytheism. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: God only accepts from those who fear Him, those who fear polytheism. We have previously explained the meaning of Qurban, and that it is the two verbs from the saying of the speaker: Quran as the two verbs from faraq and adwan from ‘ada. The offerings of the nations before our nation were like the alms and zakat among us. However, their offerings were known to be accepted and not accepted - as mentioned - by eating the fire of what was accepted from it, and leaving the fire of what was not accepted from it. The offerings in our nation are righteous deeds, such as prayer, fasting, charity to the poor, and paying the obligatory zakat. There is no way for them to know in the immediate future what was accepted from it and what was rejected. It was mentioned about Amer bin Abdullah Al-Anbari: When death approached him, he cried. It was said to him: What makes you cry? I was and was! He said: What makes me cry is that I hear God say: God only accepts from those who fear Him. Muhammad bin Omar Al-Muqaddami told me that. He said: Saeed bin Amer told me, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of someone who mentioned him, on the authority of Amer. Some of them said: The sacrifice of the pious is prayer. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Imran bin Sulayman, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, who said: The sacrifice of the pious was prayer.
5:28: Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty, mentioned about the one who was killed from the sons of Adam, that he said to his brother - when his brother the killer said to him: I will kill you -: By God, if you stretch out your hand against me, meaning: you stretch out your hand against me, to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you, meaning: I will not stretch out my hand against you, to kill you. There is a difference of opinion as to why the murdered man said that to his brother, and why he did not object to what was done to him. Some of them said: He said that to inform his murderous brother that he did not consider it permissible to kill him or to extend his hand to him in a way that God Almighty did not permit him to do. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that he said: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but he was prevented from extending his hand to his brother due to his embarrassment. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you, I will not be victorious, and I will withhold my hand from you. Others said: He did not prevent him from what he wanted to kill, and he said what he said to him from what God narrated in His Book: except that God Almighty imposed on them that whoever wanted to kill him should not prevent whoever wanted to kill him. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told us that he heard Mujahid say about His statement: If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Mujahid said: It was written for them, if a man wanted to kill a man, you would see him and not resist him. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is that it is said that God, the Mighty and Sublime, had forbidden them to kill a soul for another soul unjustly, and that the one killed said to his brother: I will not extend my hand to you if you extend your hand to me. Rather, it was forbidden for him to kill his brother just as it was forbidden for his brother, the killer, to kill him. As for refraining from killing him when he wanted to kill him, there is no evidence that when the killer wanted to kill him and resolved to do so, the one killed was aware of what he was determined to do and was trying to kill him, so he left it to himself. Rather, a group of scholars have stated that he killed him by treachery, he assassinated him while he was sleeping, and smashed his head with a rock. So since that is possible, and there is no evidence in the verse that he was commanded not to prevent his brother from killing him, it is permissible to claim what is not in the verse, except with proof that must be accepted. As for the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the Worlds, it is: I fear God in extending my hand to you if I extend it to kill you, Lord of the Worlds, meaning: Owner of all creation, lest He punish me for extending my hand to you.
5:29: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: I want you to bear my sin of killing me, your sin of disobeying God, and other sins of yours. Who said that? Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in his hadith, on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: the sin of killing me, in addition to your sin that is around your neck, and you will be among the companions of the Fire. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: by killing me, and your sin before that. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: the sin of killing me and your sin. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: I want your sin and my blood to be upon you, so that you bear both of them. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: for what happened from you before that. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: I want you to bear my sin and your sin. He said: As for your sin, it is the sin that he committed before killing the soul - meaning his brother - and as for his sin, it is killing his brother. The authors of this article interpreted his statement: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, as: I want you to bear the sin of killing me. So he omitted killing and was satisfied with mentioning the sin, since its meaning was understood by those addressed by it. Others said: The meaning of this is: I want you to bear my sin, so you bear its burden and your sin in killing me. This is a statement I found on the authority of Mujahid, and I fear that it may be a mistake, because the correct narration on his authority is what we mentioned before. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: I want my sin and my blood to be upon you, so you bear both of them. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement about this is to say that its interpretation is: I want you to turn away from your sin in killing me, and that is the meaning of his saying: I want you to bear my sin. As for the meaning of and your sin, it is his sin other than killing him, and that is his disobedience to God, may He be glorified, in the actions of others. We said that this is correct, because the people of interpretation have agreed upon it. Because God Almighty has informed us that every worker will be rewarded for his work or against it. If this is His ruling regarding His creation, then it is not permissible for the sins of the one killed to be taken from the killer. Rather, the killer will be taken for his sin of the forbidden killing and all the sins of his transgressions that he committed himself, not for what his victim committed. If someone says: Is not killing the murdered person from among the sons of Adam a protection for God from the murderer? It is said: Yes, and it is a greater sin! If someone says: If there is a sin against God, the Almighty and Majestic, how is it permissible for the murdered person to want that from him, and say: I want you to bear my sin, and you have mentioned that the interpretation of that is: I want you to bear the sin of killing me? It was said: Its meaning is: I want you to bear the sin of killing me if you kill me, because I will not kill you. If you kill me, then I want you to bear the sin of disobeying God in killing me. And if he kills him, then he will inevitably bear it in God’s judgment, so his desire for that does not require him to enter into error. He means by his saying: Then you will be among the people of the Fire, and that is the reward of the wrongdoers. He says: Then by killing me you will be among the inhabitants of Hell, and the fuel of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. “And that is the reward of the wrongdoers.” He says: And the Fire is the reward of those who abandon the path of truth, who deviate from the straight path, who transgress what was made for them to what was not made for them. This indicates that God Almighty had commanded and forbidden Adam after He sent him down to Earth, and had promised and warned. And were it not for that, the murdered man would not have said to the murderer: Then you will be among the people of the Fire, for killing me, nor would he have told him that this is the reward of the wrongdoers. So Mujahid used to say: One of the murderer’s legs will be suspended by its shin to its thigh from that day until the Day of Resurrection, and his face will be in the sun wherever it turns, with a fence of fire over him in the summer and a fence of snow over him in the winter. Al-Qasim told us that, he said, Al-Hussein told us that, Hajjaj told me that, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said that - he said: And Abdullah bin Amr said: And we find the son of Adam, the murderer, dividing the people of Hell in a correct division of punishment, with half of their punishment upon him. It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, a story. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, and Sufyan told us, he said, Jarir and Abu Muawiyah told us, H, and Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Waki’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no soul that is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear some responsibility for it, because he was the first to institute killing. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, H, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hasan ibn Salih, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, who said: There is no one who is killed unjustly, except that the first son of Adam and the devil have a share of it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hakim: that he told on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: that he used to say: The most wretched of people is a man, the son of Adam who killed his brother. No blood has been shed on earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection, except that some of it has been inflicted on him, and that is because he was the first to institute killing. Abu Ja`far said: This report that we have mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shows that the statement that Al-Hasan made about the two sons of Adam whom God mentioned in this place, that they are not the sons of Adam by his loins, but rather they are two men from the Children of Israel, and that the statement that was reported from him, that the first to die was Adam, and that the sacrifice that the fire consumed was only from the Children of Israel, is a mistake, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed about this murderer who killed his brother: that he was the first to establish killing. And, without a doubt, killing occurred before Israel, so how about before his descendants! So it is a mistake to say: The first to establish killing was a man from the Children of Israel. Since this is the case, it is known that the correct statement is the statement of the one who said: He is the son of Adam through his loins, because he was the first to establish killing, so God made obligatory for him the punishment that we narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
5:30: Abu Jaafar said: What He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: So I obeyed, was that I came to him and helped him with it. It is an action of obedience, from the saying of the one who says: This matter obeyed me, if he submitted to it. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said, meaning: So his soul encouraged him to kill his brother. Who said that? Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi and Muhammad bin Hamid told me, they said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: His soul was willing to do it, he said: I was encouraged. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So his soul was willing to do it, he said: So I encouraged him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, he said: It encouraged him to kill his brother. Others said: The meaning of this is: It was decorated for him. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His soul made it easy for him, he said: His soul made the killing of his brother seem attractive to him, so he killed him. Then they differed about the manner in which he killed him, how it was, and the reason for which he killed him. Some of them said: He found him sleeping and smashed his head with a rock. Who said that? Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then his soul prompted him to kill his brother. So he sought him out to kill him, and the young man finished him off on the mountaintops. One day he came to him while he was tending his sheep on a mountain, and he was asleep, so he lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, and he died, and he was left in the open. Some of them said: Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali told me, he said, I heard Ash’ath al-Sijistani say, I heard Ibn Jurayj say: The son of Adam who killed his companion did not know how to kill him, so Satan appeared to him in the form of a bird, so he took a bird and cut off its head, then put it between two stones and smashed its head, so he taught it how to kill. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: He killed him while he was tending the sheep. He came to him and did not know how to kill him, so he twisted his neck and took hold of his head. Then Satan came down and took an animal or a bird and placed his head on a rock. Then he took another rock and crushed his head with it, while the killer, the son of Adam, was watching. Then he took his brother and placed his head on a rock, and took another rock and crushed his head with it. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told us who heard Mujahid say, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the fire consumed the sacrifice of the son of Adam whom you killed! His sacrifice, the other said to his brother: Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered a sacrifice and it was accepted from you and returned to me? By God, people do not wait for me and you when you are better than me! He said: I will kill you. His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from those who fear Him. So he frightened him with the fire, but he did not stop or refrain, so his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers. Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim told me: I came with Saeed bin Jubair to throw the pebbles at the Jamarat, and he was covering his face and leaning on my hand, until we reached the place of Samurah al-Sawwaf. He stopped and told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was forbidden for a woman to marry her twin brother, and for another of her brothers to marry her. And in every pregnancy there was a man and a woman. So she gave birth to a beautiful woman, and she gave birth to an ugly, ugly woman. So the brother of the ugly woman said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they made a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the owner of the ram, but it was not accepted from the owner of the crops, so he killed him. And that ram remained with God, the Almighty, until He brought it out in ransom for Isaac, and slaughtered it on this Safa in Thabir, at the place of Samurah al-Sawwaf, and it is on your right when you throw the pebbles. Ibn Jurayj said, and others said something similar to this story. He said: The children of Adam continued to do this until four fathers passed away, and he married his cousin, and the marriage of sisters was no longer permissible. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God, the Mighty and Sublime, has informed us that the killer killed his brother, and we do not have any information that would excuse him for the manner in which he killed him. It is possible that it was as al-Suddi mentioned in his report, and it is possible that it was as Mujahid mentioned, and God knows best which of them it was. However, the killing undoubtedly took place. As for His statement: So he became one of the losers, its interpretation is: So the killer became his brother from the sons of Adam, from the party of the losers, and they are those who sold their afterlife for their worldly life, by preferring it over it - so they were deceived in their sale, were cheated in it, and were disappointed in their deal.
5:31: Abu Ja'far said: This is also one of the proofs that the statement regarding the two sons of Adam is contrary to what Amr narrated from Al-Hasan, because if the two men whose description God described in this verse had been from the Children of Israel, the killer would not have been ignorant of burying his brother and covering his brother's body, but they were from the descendants of Adam through his loins, and the killer of his brother was not one of them. He knew God's law regarding His dead servants, and he did not know what to do with his murdered brother. So he mentioned that he carried him on his shoulder for a while until his corpse was at rest, so God wanted to make him aware of the law regarding the dead of His creation, so He provided him with the two ravens whose description He described in His Book. Mentioning the report from the people of interpretation about what the killer of the two sons of Adam did to his murdered brother, after killing him. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahs bin Abi Rawq Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He continued carrying his brother in a bag on his neck for a year, until God Almighty sent the two crows. He saw them searching, so he said: Am I unable to be like this crow? So he buried his brother. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide the shame of his brother, God Almighty sent a living raven to a dead raven, and the living raven began to hide the shame of the dead raven, so the son of Adam who killed his brother said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven? The verse. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the boy died, he left him in the open, and he did not know how to bury him. Then God Almighty sent two ravens, brothers, and they fought, and one of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him and threw it over him. When he saw it, he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover my brother’s private parts? This is what God says: Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to cover his brother’s private parts. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Searching, he said, God sent a raven until it dug a hole for another dead person next to it - and the son of Adam, the killer, was looking at him - then it searched for him until it hid him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A crow digging in the ground, until it dug for another dead person next to it, and hid him, and the son of Adam, the killer, was looking at him, searching for him until he hid him, and he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow, the verse. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Then God sent a crow scratching the ground, he said: God sent a crow to a crow, and they fought, and one of them killed the other, and he began to throw dirt on him, and he said: Woe to me, am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother, so that I may become one of the regretful ones? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then God sent a crow scratching the ground, he said: A crow came to a dead crow and threw dirt on it until it covered it, so the one who killed his brother said: Woe to me! I am unable to be like this crow, the verse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah, who said: When he killed him, he regretted it, so he hugged him until he died, and the birds and beasts of prey swarmed around him, waiting for him to throw him away so they could eat him. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then God sent a crow scratching the ground to show him, that God Almighty sent him scratching the ground. He told us that they were two crows who fought, and one of them killed the other, and that - meaning the son of Adam was looking - and the living one began to throw dirt on the dead one, and then he said what he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? The verse, until His saying: among the regretful ones. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: As for his statement: Then God sent a crow, he said: A crow killed another crow, and it began to throw dirt at it. So the son of Adam who killed his brother said when he saw it: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover my brother’s shame? Then I became one of the regretful ones. Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide his brother’s private parts, he said: The raven hid the raven. He said: He carried it on his shoulder for a hundred years, not knowing what to do with it, carrying it and putting it on the ground, until he saw the raven burying the raven, so he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and hide my brother’s private parts? I have become one of those who regret it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding the statement of God: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? He said: God Almighty sent a crow, and it began searching for a dead crow in the dirt. He said: Then it said: Am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother? So I became one of the regretful ones. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Then God sent a crow, scratching the ground, God sent a living crow to a dead crow, and the living crow began to cover the dead crow’s private parts. Then the son of Adam who had killed his brother said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? The verse. Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, according to what is mentioned by some of the people of knowledge of the first book, he said: When he killed him, he was dismayed and did not know how to bury him. That is because he was, as they claim, the first of the sons of Adam to be killed and the first to die. He said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother? The verse, until His saying: Then indeed many of them after that are transgressors upon the earth. He said: The people of the Torah claim that when Cain killed his brother Abel, God Almighty said to him: O Cain, where is your brother Abel? He said: I do not know, I was not a watcher over him! Then God Almighty said to him: The sound of your brother’s blood calls to me from the earth. Now you are cursed from the earth that opened its mouth and swallowed your brother’s blood from your hand. So when you work the earth, it will no longer yield its crops to you until you are a wandering, terrified person on the earth. Cain said: My sin is too great for you to forgive it! Today you have brought me out from the face of the earth, and I will hide myself from your presence, and I will be a wanderer in fear on the earth, and everyone who meets me will kill me! God Almighty said: It is not so, and whoever kills a person will not be rewarded with seven for one, but whoever kills Cain will be rewarded with seven. And God made a sign in Cain so that everyone who finds him will not kill him, and Cain went out from before God Almighty from the east of Eden, Paradise. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Khathima, he said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth dried up his blood, so it was cursed and the earth did not dry up any blood after that. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement is: So God raised up for the killer, since he did not know what to do with his murdered brother, a crow digging in the ground, meaning: digging in the ground and stirring up its soil, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother, meaning: to show him how to hide the corpse of his brother. It may be possible that what he meant by the private parts is the vagina, but the most likely meaning is what I mentioned about the corpse, and that is how the people of interpretation interpreted it. Abu Ja`far said: There is something omitted in that which was not mentioned, as the indication of what was mentioned was sufficient, which is: “So he showed it to him by searching in the ground for another dead crow and hid it in it. Then the one who killed his brother said at that time: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow, who hid the other dead crow, “and hid the shame of my brother,” so he hid it at that time, and he became among the regretful, for what he had neglected, of disobeying God Almighty in killing his brother. And everything that God the Almighty mentioned in these verses, is an example that God the Almighty gave to the children of Adam, and with it He urged the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to use forgiveness and pardon for the Jews - who intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and kill them - from Banu Nadir, when they came to them seeking their help in the blood money for the two dead of Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri, and God the Almighty knew the bad nature of their forefathers, and their poor adherence to the path of truth, despite the many favors and blessings He bestowed upon them. And He gave an example of their treachery, and an example of the believers in their loyalty to them and their pardon for them, with the two sons of Adam, who were close relatives to them, whom God mentioned in these verses. Then that is an example for them to follow the example of the virtuous among them rather than the wicked. And with that came the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, I said to Bakr bin Abdullah, Have you not heard that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take the better of them and leave the worse of them? He said: Yes. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two sons of Adam are an example for this nation, so take the best of them. Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take from the good among them and leave the evil.
5:32: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement, Because of that, from the crime and offense he committed. He says: Whoever caused the murderer of his brother from the two sons of Adam - whose story we have related - the crime he committed and the offense he committed, We prescribed for the Children of Israel. It is said: I postponed this matter, meaning: I dragged him towards it and earned it, I postponed it for him for a period, like you say: I took it, and from that is the saying of that poet: The people of Salih’s tent fought among themselves over an urgent matter that I will postpone. By his saying: I will postpone it, he meant that I will punish them and the aggressor. The meaning of the statement: From the crime of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly, We ruled upon the Children of Israel that whoever among them killed a soul unjustly, unless it was a soul that was killed, then he was killed in retaliation, or corruption in the land, meaning: or he killed a soul among them without corruption that was on its part on the land, so it deserved to be killed. And its corruption in the land is only by war against God and His Messenger, and frightening the wayfarer. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Those who said that mentioned: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel, he said: For the sake of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land - it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. And whoever saves a life - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he killed all of humanity, and whoever supports a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he saved all of humanity. Who said that? Abu Ammar Al-Hussein bin Harith Al-Marwazi told us, he said, Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Waqid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely,” he said: Whoever strengthens the arm of a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, meaning: Whoever kills a single soul that I have made sacred, is like someone who has killed all of mankind. And whoever saves a life, he said: Whoever refrains from killing a single soul that I have made sacred out of fear of Me, and spares it from killing it, it is like sparing all of mankind, meaning by that the prophets. Others said: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, when the one killed is guilty of sin, and whoever saves a life, when rescuing it from destruction, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, when rescuing it. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, in what was mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his saying: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, in reference to the one killed, he says: in sin, and whoever saves it, so he rescues it from destruction, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, in reference to the rescuer. Others said: The meaning of this is: The one who kills a soul in a state of forbidden killing will burn in Hell just as he would burn in it if he killed all people. And whoever saves a life, whoever is saved from killing it, is saved from killing all people. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever refrains from killing it has saved it, Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, he said: And whoever destroys it. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Whoever kills a soul, it is as if he had killed all of humanity. And whoever saves a life and is saved from its oppression and does not kill it, then he has been saved from killing all of humanity. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: It is as if he had killed all of humanity, and whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of humanity. He did not kill her, and all of the people were saved from him. He did not kill anyone. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, who said, Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah told us: I asked Mujahid - or I heard him ask - about his statement: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had killed all of mankind. He said: If he had killed all of mankind, his recompense would be Hell, wherein he would abide eternally, and God would be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, reading it on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It is as if he had slain mankind entirely, he said: Whoever kills a believing soul intentionally, God will make his recompense Hell, and God will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment. He says: If he had killed all of mankind, it would not have increased the punishment like that. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: And whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever does not kill anyone, then the people are relieved of him. Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He destroyed himself. Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: In sin. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. And His statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell (An-Nisa’: 93), he said: He will go to Hell by killing a believer, just as if he had killed all of mankind, he would have gone to Hell. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. He said: It is as he said. And he said: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. So saving it means not killing a soul that God has forbidden, so that is what saves mankind entirely, meaning: whoever has forbidden killing it except for a right, saves mankind entirely from it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever revives it, he said: And whoever forbids it and does not kill it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, he said: I heard Mujahid say: Whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved all of humanity. He said: Whoever refrains from killing it has saved a life. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, he said: It is like what is in An-Nisa’: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell (An-Nisa’: 93), regarding his recompense. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, like what is in Surat An-Nisa, And whoever kills a believer intentionally in his punishment, And whoever saves a life, and did not kill anyone, then the people have been saved by him. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind, he said: He turned to his companions and said: It is this and this. Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on earth, it is as if he had killed all of mankind, because he must be subject to retaliation and retribution for his killing, just as he must be subject to retaliation and retribution if he had killed all of mankind. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, he said: He must be killed as if he had killed all of mankind. He said: My father used to say that. Others said that the meaning of his saying: And whoever saves it is whoever pardons someone from whom retaliation is due and does not kill him. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever saves a life, God, the Almighty, the Majestic, will give him a reward equal to that if he had saved mankind entirely. He saved a life, he did not kill it and pardoned it. He said: And that is because the one who was killed, and the one who was killed himself is pardoned before he dies. He said: My father used to say that. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever pardons. Sufyan told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind, he said: Whoever kills a close relative of his and pardons his blood. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind. He said: Forgiveness comes after power. Others said: The meaning of his saying: And whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind, is whoever saves one life from drowning or burning. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved all of mankind. He said: Whoever saves a life from drowning, burning, or destruction. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved all of mankind, he said: whoever drowned, burned, or demolished. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever saves it, he said: He saved it. Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Aamer, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Whoever kills a soul without a soul, he said: Whoever is pious or does not have any piousness. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: It is as if he had saved all of mankind, that he said: If he had not killed him, he would have saved all of mankind, and he would not have made permissible what is forbidden. Qatada and Al-Hasan said about this: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on earth, he said: That is a great sin! Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul the verse, whoever kills it unless for a soul or for corruption it has caused, “it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves a life it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” Great is its reward, and great is its sin! So save it, O son of Adam, with what you have, and save it with your forgiveness if you are able, and there is no power except with God. We do not know of anyone who makes the blood of a Muslim man from the people of this Qiblah permissible except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieves after his conversion to Islam, in which case he must be killed; or he who commits adultery after being married, in which case he must be stoned; or he who kills intentionally, in which case he must be subject to retaliation. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Qatada recited: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. And whoever saves a life - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” He said: By God, her reward is great, and by God, her sin is great! Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Salam bin Maskeen, he said, Sulayman bin Ali Al-Rab’i told me, he said: I said to Al-Hasan: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul the verse, is it for us, O Abu Saeed, as it was for the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, by the One besides Whom there is no god, as it was for the Children of Israel! And what made the blood of the Children of Israel more precious to God than our blood? Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Zaid, who said: I heard Khalid Abu Al-Fadl say: I heard Al-Hasan recite this verse: And his soul prompted him to kill his brother until His saying: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. Then he said: By God, the sin is great as you hear, and by God, the reward is desired as you hear! If you think, O son of Adam, that if you killed all of humanity, you would have from your deeds what would win you from the Fire!! By God, your soul has lied to you, and Satan has lied to you. Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, he said: A sin, And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind, he said: A reward. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The interpretation of that is that whoever kills a believing soul for a reason other than a soul that he killed, and did not deserve retaliation or killing in retaliation, or for corruption on earth, by war against God and His Messenger and the war of the believers in it, then it is as if he killed all of mankind in what he deserves of great punishment from God, the Most High, as his Lord has promised him for his action in His saying: And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment (An-Nisa’: 93). As for his statement: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, the most appropriate interpretation of it is the statement of the one who said: Whoever forbade killing someone whom God the Almighty has forbidden to kill for himself, and did not precede killing him, then he has saved mankind from him by their being safe from him, and that is his saving it. This is similar to the report of God the Almighty about the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord when Abraham said to him: “My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. He said: I give life and cause death” (al-Baqarah 2:258). So the meaning of the disbeliever in his saying: I give life, is that I leave whoever I am able to kill - and in his statement: and cause death, he killed whoever killed him. Likewise the meaning of revival in his statement: And whoever saves a life, is that people are safe from his killing them, except for those whom God has permitted to be killed from them, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse, because no soul whose killing in the immediate harm is equivalent to killing all souls, nor its revival is equivalent to reviving all souls in the immediate benefit. Thus it was known that the meaning of revival is the safety of all souls from it, because whoever does not advance on a single soul, all souls are safe from it - and that the one of them whose killing is equivalent to all of them is only in sin, because there is no soul of the sons of Adam whose loss is equivalent to the loss of all of them, even if the loss of some is more harmful than the loss of some. Abu Ja`far said: This is an oath from God, the Most High, by which He swore: that His messengers, may God’s prayers be upon them, came to the Children of Israel, whose stories God related and whose report He mentioned in the verses that preceded, from His saying: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you to this place, with clear proofs, meaning: with clear signs and evident arguments on the truth of what they were sent with to them, and the correctness of what they called them to of belief in them, and performing God’s obligations upon them. God Almighty says: Then many of them, after that, were transgressors upon the earth, meaning: many of the Children of Israel. The ha and the mim in his saying: Then many of them are from the mention of the Children of Israel, and likewise in his saying: And there came to them. “After that,” meaning: after the coming of God’s messengers with clear proofs. On the earth are transgressors, meaning: they are on earth committing sins against God, disobeying God’s commands and prohibitions, and defying God and His messengers, following their whims and disobeying their prophets. That was their transgression on the earth.
