5:33: Abu Ja'far said: This is a statement from God, the Exalted, about the ruling on corruption on earth, which He mentioned in His statement: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on the earth, He informed His servants: What punishment and humiliation the corrupter on earth deserves, so He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: There is no recompense for him in this world except killing, crucifixion, cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides, or exile from the land, as a disgrace for them. As for in the Hereafter, if he does not repent in this world, then there is a great punishment. Then the people of interpretation differed about who this verse was revealed to. Some of them said: It was revealed about a group of the People of the Book who had a truce with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the covenant and spread corruption on earth, so God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the ruling regarding them. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land, he said: There were people from the People of the Book who had a covenant and a pact with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the covenant and spread corruption in the land, so God gave His Messenger the choice: If He wished, he could kill them, or if He wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: There were people between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant, so they broke the covenant and cut off the way and spread corruption on the earth, so God Almighty gave His Prophet the choice regarding them, if He wished he could kill him, if He wished he could crucify him, and if He wished he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told me: I heard Al-Dahhak say: and he mentioned something similar. Others said: It was revealed about a group of polytheists. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This verse was revealed regarding the polytheists. So whoever among them repents before you are able to overpower him, there will be no punishment against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment. If he kills or spreads corruption in the land or wages war against God and His Messenger, then joins the disbelievers before he is able to overpower him, that will not prevent him from having the prescribed punishment carried out against him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, he said: It was revealed about the polytheists. Others said: Rather, it was revealed about a people from Uraynah and Ukl, who apostatized from Islam and fought God and His Messenger. Who said that? Ibn Bashar narrated, saying: Ruh ibn Ubadah narrated, saying: Saeed ibn Abi Arubah narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas: A group of people from Ukl and Uraynah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we are people of udder, and we were not people of the countryside, and we find Medina unpleasant. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered for them a flock of sheep and a shepherd, and ordered them to go out with them and drink from their milk and urine. So they killed the shepherd of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and drove away the flocks, and they disbelieved after their Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them, cut off their hands and feet, gouged out their eyes, and left them in the lava field until they died. He told us that this verse was revealed about them: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger is that they will be killed or be disgraced. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Hisham bin Abi Abdullah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a story similar to this. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq narrated, he said, I heard my father say: Abu Hamza narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, and he was asked about camel urine, so he said: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me on the authority of the warriors, he said: There were people who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We pledge allegiance to you on Islam! So they pledged allegiance to him, and they were liars, and they did not want Islam. Then they said: We are going to Medina! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These camels come to you in the morning and in the evening, so drink from their urine and milk. He said: While they were like that, the cry came, and it was cried out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: They killed the shepherd and drove the camels away! So the Prophet of God ordered that it be called out to the al-Nas 114:O horses of God, ride! He said: So they rode, and no horseman waited for another horseman. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode after them, and they kept pursuing them until they brought them to their place of safety. Then the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and had taken some of them as prisoners. They brought them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger (al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: So their exile was that they were exiled until they brought them to their place of safety and their land, and they were exiled from the land of the Muslims. The Prophet of God killed some of them, crucified them, cut off their eyes, and gouged out their eyes. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had never mutilated anyone before or after. He said: He forbade mutilation, and said: Do not mutilate anything. He said: Anas bin Malik used to say the same, except that he said: He burned them with fire after he killed them. He said: Some of them say: They are people from Bani Salim, some from Uraynah, and some from Bajila. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said, Al-Hasan bin Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Hashim, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Jarir, who said: A group of people from Uraynah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, barefoot and injured, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave orders to them. When they recovered and became strong, they killed the shepherds of the camels, then they went out with the camels, intending to go to the land of their people. Jarir said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me with a group of Muslims until we caught up with them after they had reached the land of their people, so we brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he cut off their hands and feet from opposite sides, and gouged out their eyes, and they kept saying: Water! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fire! Until they perished. He said: God, the Almighty, disliked the gouging out of eyes, so He revealed this verse: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to the end of the verse. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, H, and Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abd God ibn Salim, Sa’id ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Sam’an told me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said: Some people from ‘Uraynah raided the camels of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they drove them away and killed one of his slaves in them, so he sent after them, and they were captured, so he cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar - or: Amr, Yunus was uncertain - on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, and the verse of fighting was revealed about them. Ali bin Sahl narrated, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated, Al-Awza’i narrated, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, who said: Eight men from Ukl came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they converted to Islam. Then they settled in Madinah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink their urine and milk. So they did, and they killed their shepherds and drove away the camels. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a tracker after them, and they were brought to him. He cut off their hands and feet and left them without cauterizing them until they died. Ali told us, Al-Walid told us, Saeed told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: There were four men from Uraynah and three from Ukl. When they were brought to him, he cut off their hands and feet, put out their eyes, did not cauterize them, and left them to throw stones at Al-Harrah. Then God Almighty revealed regarding that: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger Al-Madinah 1:17. Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib: That Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Anas asking him about this verse, so Anas wrote to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those people from Arniyah, who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the travelers, and committed unlawful sexual intercourse. Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive after corruption on earth He said: It was revealed about the blacks of Uraynah. He said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had yellow water, and they complained about that to him, so he ordered them to go out to the camels of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the charity, and he said: Drink from their milk and urine! So they drank from their milk and urine, until when they recovered and were well, they killed the shepherds and drove away the camels. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate statement in this regard, in my opinion, is to say: God revealed this verse to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform him of His ruling on those who fight God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth, after what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to the two tribes of Arnayin. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings in this regard, because the stories that God Almighty told before and after this verse are stories of the Children of Israel and their report, so it is more appropriate and more appropriate for this to be in the middle, in defining the ruling on them and their peers. We said: This was revealed after what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to the two Arnayin, because the reports from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent with this. And since that was more appropriate for the verse because of what we have described, then its interpretation is: For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul, or strives to cause corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs; then indeed many of them after that were transgressors upon the earth. He says: Striving to cause corruption upon the earth, and fighting souls unless for a soul, and not striving to cause corruption upon the earth, in war against God and His Messenger. So whoever among them does that, O Muhammad, his recompense is only that they be killed, or crucified, or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides, or they be exiled from the land. If someone were to say to us: How is it possible that the verse was revealed in the situation you mentioned: the situation of a disbeliever from the Children of Israel breaking his covenant, and from your saying that the ruling of this verse is a ruling from God regarding the people of Islam, not the people of war from the polytheists? It was said: It is permissible for that to be the case, because the ruling on those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth are from among the people of our covenant and one religion. And those meant by the verse were people of a covenant and a protection, even though every dhimmi and religion is included in its ruling. And it is not invalidated by the inclusion of those who are included in the ruling of the verse from the people, that it was correct to reveal it regarding those about whom it was revealed. Scholars have differed about abrogating the Prophet’s ruling, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Arabs. Some of them said: This is an abrogated ruling, abrogated by His prohibition of mutilation in this verse, I mean His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption Al-Ma’idah 2:17. They said: This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he did to the two Arabs. Some of them said: Rather, what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did with the Arniyyin is a ruling that is always valid for their peers, it has not been abrogated or changed. And His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger 3:17, is a ruling from God regarding those who wage war and strive to spread corruption in the land through banditry. They said: The Arniyyin apostatized, killed, stole, and waged war against God and His Messenger, so their ruling is different from the ruling of the one who wages war and strives to spread corruption in the land from among the people of Islam or the covenant. Others said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not blind the eyes of the Arabs, but he wanted to blind them, so God Almighty revealed this verse to His Prophet, informing him of the ruling on them, and forbidding him from blinding their eyes. Mention of those who said what we described: Ali bin Sahl told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I mentioned to Al-Layth bin Saad what happened when the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) blinded their eyes and left them cauterized until they died, so he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ajlan say: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) as a reprimand for that, and he taught him the punishment for those like them: cutting off, killing, and banishment, and no one else was blinded after them. He said: This statement was mentioned to Abu Amr, so he denied that it was revealed as a reprimand, and he said: Yes, the punishment for those people was in their persons, then this verse was revealed regarding the punishment for others who fought after them, so the blinding was lifted from them. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent, and they were brought to him - meaning the Arabs - and he wanted to put out their eyes, but God forbade him from that and ordered him to implement the limits on them, as God had revealed them to him. Scholars differed about who deserves the title of one who fights against God and His Messenger, and who is subject to the ruling of this. Some of them said: He is the thief who cuts off the road. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Ata al-Khurasani, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption the verse, they said, this is the thief who cuts off the road, so he is a highway robber. Others said: He is the thief who openly commits his theft, who is stubborn in Egypt and elsewhere. Among those who said this is Al-Awza’i. Al-Abbas told us this, on the authority of his father, on his authority. On his authority, and on the authority of Malik, Al-Layth bin Saad, and Ibn Lahi’ah. Ali bin Sahl told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I said to Malik bin Anas: Is there a war in the city? He said: Yes, and the warlord among us is the one who carries arms against the Muslims in the city or in the open, and he does that without any conflict between them, nor any enmity or hostility, cutting off the way, the road, and the homes, frightening them with his weapon, and he kills one of them, the Imam kills him like the killers of the warlord, and the guardian of the one killed has no pardon or retaliation. Ali told me, Al-Walid told us: I asked Al-Layth bin Saad and Ibn Lahi’ah about that. I said: Will the fighting take place in the homes of cities, towns and villages? They said: Yes, if they enter upon them openly with swords, or at night with fire. I said: So they kill, or take the money and do not kill? He said: Yes, they are the combatants. If they kill, they are killed, and if they do not kill and take the money, they are cut off on opposite sides if they leave the house with it. The one who fights the Muslims in the open and on the road is not more severe in fighting than the one who fights them in their harems and homes! Ali told me, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said: And the war in the city is a month of fighting with his people with his weapon, day or night. Ali said, Al-Walid said: And Malik told me: Killing by treachery is in his view the same as fighting. I said: And what is killing by treachery? He said: It is a man who deceives a man or a boy and brings him into a house or is alone with him, and kills him, and takes his money. So the imam is the guardian of killing this one, and the guardian of the blood and the wound has no right to retaliation or retribution. This is what Al-Shafi’i said. Al-Rabi' told us about it. Others said: The warrior is a highway robber. As for the stubborn person in the cities, he is not a warrior who is subject to the same ruling as warriors. Among those who said this were Abu Hanifa and his companions. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, who said: We discussed Al-Muharib while we were with Ibn Hubayrah, among some people from Basra, and their opinion was unanimous: Al-Muharib had not left the city. Mujahid said: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption, he said: Adultery, theft, killing people, and destroying crops and offspring. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: And they strive to spread corruption in the land, he said: Corruption means murder, adultery, and theft. The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The one who fights against God and His Messenger is the one who fights against the Muslims’ paths and their protection, and raids them in their cities and wages war against them. We said: This is the most correct statement, because there is no disagreement among the proofs that whoever wages war against the Muslims due to his injustice towards them, is a combatant against them, and there is no disagreement about that. The one whose description we have described, there is no doubt about him waging war against them unjustly. Since that is the case, then whether he wages war against them in their cities and villages, or on their roads and paths, he is a combatant against God and His Messenger, by waging war against those whom God and His Messenger have forbidden from waging war against. As for his saying: And they strive to cause corruption in the land, it means: And they commit sins in the land of God: by frightening the paths of His believing servants, or the paths of their protection, and cutting off their roads, and taking their money unjustly and aggressively, and attacking their sanctuaries with immorality and wickedness. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “He who wages war against God and His Messenger, and strives to spread corruption on earth, from among the people of the religion of Islam or their protection, has nothing but some of these characteristics that God Almighty mentioned.” Then the people of interpretation differed regarding these characteristics. Is the warrior obligated to deserve the name warrior, or is he obligated to do what is obligatory for him according to the extent of his crime, varying according to the differences in his crimes? Some of them said: The combatant must be punished according to the extent of his entitlement, and he must bear what is due to him according to the extent of his crime, varying according to the severity of his crimes. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger until His statement: or be banished from the land, he said: If he wages war and kills, then he must be killed if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and takes property and kills, then he must be crucified if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and takes property and does not kill, then he must have his hand and foot cut off from opposite sides if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and frightens the wayfarer, then he must be banished. Ibn Wakee’ and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger is that if he goes out and frightens people on the road and takes money, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides. And if he frightens people on the road, but does not take money and kills, he is crucified. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim - as I see it - regarding a man who goes out to fight, he said: If he cuts off the road and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off. If he takes money and kills, he is to be killed. If he takes money and kills and mutilates, he is to be crucified. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse, he said: If he kills, takes money, and threatens the wayfarer, he is crucified. And if he killed, it was no longer that, he killed. And if he took the money, it was no longer that, he cut off. Why was he corrupting, he was banished. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger until His saying: or be banished from the land, he said: If he frightens on the road and does not kill or take money, he is banished. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, he said: It was said: Whoever fights and frightens the wayfarers and takes money but does not kill, his hand and foot will be cut off on opposite sides. And if he takes money and kills, he will be crucified. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: that he used to say regarding His statement, The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to His statement, or be banished from the land, are four limits that God has revealed: As for the one who sheds blood and property together, he is crucified. As for the one who sheds blood but refrains from property, he is killed. Whoever gains wealth and refrains from shedding blood shall have his hand cut off. Whoever does not gain any of this shall be banished. Muhammad bin Al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad bin Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: God forbade His Prophet, peace be upon him, from blinding the eyes of the Arabs who raided his camels, and He ordered him to implement the prescribed punishments on them as God had revealed them to him. So he looked at the one who took the money but did not kill, so he cut off his hand and foot from opposite sides, his right hand and his left foot. And he looked at the one who killed but did not take the money, so he killed him. And he looked at the one who took the money and killed, so he crucified him. And this is how it is appropriate for everyone who frightens the Muslims on the road and cuts off, if he took and took money, his hand was cut off for taking the money, and his foot for frightening the road. And if he killed but did not take the money, he was killed. And if he killed and took the money, he was crucified. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, he said: I heard Al-Suddi asking Atiyah Al-Awfi about a man who fights and goes out and seizes but does not seize any money or shed any blood. He said: Banishment by the sword. If he seizes money, his hand is to be cut off with the money, and his foot is to be cut off with what he feared the Muslims. If he kills but does not take any money, he is to be killed. If he kills and seizes the money, he is to be crucified. I think he said: His hand and foot are to be cut off. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani and Qatadah, regarding His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse, he said: This is the thief who robs the road, so he is a combatant. If he kills and takes money, he is crucified. If he kills and does not take money, he is killed. If he takes money without killing, his hand and foot are cut off. If he takes it before doing any of that, he is banished. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Whoever goes out in Islam fighting against God and His Messenger, and kills and seizes wealth, he is to be killed and crucified. Whoever kills but does not seize wealth, he is to be killed as he killed. Whoever seizes wealth but does not kill, his hand is to be cut off from opposite sides. If he terrifies the Muslims, he is to be banished from his country to another, because God the Almighty says: or be banished from the land. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, regarding His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, he said: There were people who were spreading corruption in the land, killing and cutting off roads, so those were crucified. Others fought and made property lawful but did not transgress that, so their hands and feet were cut off. Others fought and withdrew but did not transgress that, so those were expelled from the land. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hilak, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Muwarriq al-Ajli, regarding the warrior, he said: If he went out and killed and took the money, he is crucified. If he killed but did not take the money, he is killed. If he took the money but did not kill, his hand is cut off. If he went out to cause trouble for the Muslims, he is banished. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a warrior goes out and frightens people on the road and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off on opposite sides. If he goes out and kills and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off on opposite sides and then he is crucified. If he goes out and kills but does not take money, he is to be killed. If he frightens people on the road but does not kill or take money, he is to be banished. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive after corruption in the land, they said: If he frightens the Muslims and seizes wealth but does not shed it, he is to be cut off. If he sheds blood, he is to be killed and crucified. If he combines both and seizes wealth and sheds blood, he is to be cut off, then killed, then crucified. Crucifixion is mutilation. It is as if the cutting off is: As for the male thief, male or female, cut off their hands, and killing is: A life for a life. If he refuses, then it is the right of the leader and the Muslims to seek him out until they seize him, and implement upon him the ruling of the Book of God: or be banished from the land, from the land of Islam to the land of disbelief. Abu Ja`far said: The proponents of this statement based their argument on their statement by saying: God has made retaliation obligatory for the murderer, and amputation for the thief. They said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a man who killed and was killed, a man who committed adultery after being married and was stoned, and a man who disbelieved after becoming a Muslim. They said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of a Muslim man except in one of these three cases. As for killing for frightening people on the road without killing or taking money, this is precedence over God and His Messenger by disagreement over their ruling. They said: The meaning of the statement of those who said: The imam has the choice, if he killed and frightened people on the road and took money, then there is the choice of the imam according to their statement between killing, or killing and crucifixion, or cutting off the hand and foot from opposite sides. As for crucifixing him in the name of fighting, without doing anything like killing or taking money, this is something that no scholar has said. Others said: The imam has the choice: to do these things that God mentioned in His Book. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ata’ and on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid regarding the warrior: that the imam has a choice in it, whichever he wants he does. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibrahim: The imam has a choice regarding the combatant, he can do whatever he wants. If he wants, he can kill, if he wants, he can cut off his hand, if he wants, he can banish, or if he wants, he can crucify. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, to his statement: or be exiled from the land, he said: The imam takes whichever he prefers. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, he said: The imam has a choice in it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa`d, he said, Ata’ said: The imam can do whatever he wants in this regard. If he wants, he can kill, or cut off, or exile, based on the statement of God: that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off on alternate sides or that they be exiled from the land, so that is up to the ruling imam, and he can do whatever he wants in it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, the verse, he said: Whoever draws a weapon in the sanctuary of Islam, and frightens the wayfarer, then he is captured and overpowered, then the Imam of the Muslims has the choice regarding him: if he wants, he can kill him, if he wants, he can crucify him, and if he wants, he can cut off his hand and foot. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Usama told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that he said about the warrior: that is up to the imam, if he takes him he does with him what he wants. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding Al-Muharrib, he said: That is up to the Imam, he does with him as he wishes. Hanad told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger, he said: That is up to the Imam. Abu Ja`far said: Those who said this statement argued that we found the conjunction with or in the Qur’an to mean choice in everything that God has made obligatory from it, such as His statement regarding expiation for an oath: Then its expiation is feeding ten poor people from the average of that with which you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave (al-Ma’idah 5:89), and His statement: But if any of you is ill or has an ailment in his head, then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:96), and His statement: “Then the penalty of an animal like that which he killed, as judged by two just men among you, is an offering delivered to the Ka`bah, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting” (al-Ma’idah 5:95). They said: If the conjunction with or in the Qur’an, in everything that God has made obligatory from it in the rest of the Qur’an, means choice, then it is the same in the verse of the warriors, the imam has a choice in what he sees fit to rule on the warrior if he is able to do so before repentance. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard, in our view, is the interpretation of those who impose punishment on the combatant according to the extent to which he deserves it, and make the ruling on combatants different according to their actions. So he imposes on those who are terrifying others - if he is overpowered before repentance, and before taking money or killing - exile from the land. And if he is overpowered after taking money and killing a soul that is forbidden to be killed, he is to be crucified, for the reason I mentioned earlier for those who say this statement. As for what those who say that the imam has the choice have argued, that or in conjunction means giving a choice in the case of a supposition, this is a statement that has no meaning, because or in the speech of the Arabs may have various meanings, and if it were not for the dislike of prolonging the book by mentioning them, I would have mentioned them. I have explained many of their meanings in the past, and we will come to the rest of them in the future in their places, God willing. As for this passage, its meaning is a follow-up, and that is similar to the statement of the one who says: The reward of the believers with God on the Day of Resurrection is that He will admit them into Paradise, or raise their status in the highest place, or make them dwell with the prophets and the truthful. It is known that the one who says that does not mean by his statement that the reward of every believer who believes in God and His Messenger is in one of these ranks, and one of these stations, by his faith. Rather, what is understood from him is that its meaning is: The reward of the believer with God, the Mighty and Sublime, will not be devoid of some of these stations. The moderate one’s status is lower than the status of the one who is foremost in good deeds, and the one who is foremost in good deeds is higher than him in status, and the one who wrongs himself is lower than them both, and everyone is in Paradise as God, the Most High, said: Gardens of Eden which they will enter (Fatir 35:33). Likewise, the meaning of the conjunction with or in His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger (Fatir 35:33) is a follow-up. Its interpretation is: He who wages war against God and His Messenger and strives to spread corruption on earth will not be without deserving punishment for one of these four characteristics that God the Almighty mentioned - not that the Imam is the judge over him and has a choice in his matter - whatever his condition, whether his crime is great or small, because if that were the case, the Imam would have the right to kill and crucify whoever brandishes a weapon and frightens the wayfarer, even if he did not take money or kill anyone, and he would have the right to exile whoever kills, takes money, and frightens the wayfarer. This is a statement, if anyone says it, contrary to what is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying: The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a man who kills a man and is killed in return, or commits adultery after being married and is stoned, or apostatizes from his religion, and contrary to his saying: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more, and other than what is known of its rulings. If someone says: These rulings that I mentioned were from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding someone other than the combatant, and the combatant has a ruling other than that that is unique to him. He was asked: What is the ruling that Al-Muharrib has isolated in his Sunnah? If he claims that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, issued a ruling that is contrary to what we have mentioned, all scholars will call him a liar, because that is not found in a single transmission or group. If he claims that this is what is in the apparent meaning of the Book, it is said to him: The best way for you to do this is if we accept that the apparent meaning of the verse may include what you said and what those who disagreed with you said. So what is your proof that your interpretation is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse than his interpretation? And then, since the Imam had a choice in ruling on the combatant, in order to or in the sense of choice in this situation with you, then he could crucify him alive, and leave him crucified on the wood until he dies without killing him. If he said: That is for him, he would be contradicting the nation in that. If he claims that this is not his right, but rather he has the right to kill him and then crucify him, or crucify him and then kill him, he leaves out his reason that the imam only had the choice in ruling on the combatant because or comes with the meaning of choice. It was said to him: How did he have the choice of killing, exile, or amputation, but he did not have the choice of crucifixion alone, so that another punishment could be added to it? It was said to him: Is there a difference between you and the one who gave him the option where you refused, and he refused it where you gave it to him, based on principle or analogy? He will not say something about one of them without being obligated to say something similar about the other. It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what we said about that was correct, including that in its chain of transmission there is doubt, and that is what: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi'ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib: That Abdul Malik bin Marwan wrote to Anas bin Malik asking him about this verse, so Anas wrote back to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those people from Arniyah, who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove the camels, frightened the wayfarers, and violated the forbidden vagina. Anas said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, about the ruling on those who wage war, so he said: Whoever steals and frightens the wayfarers, cut off his hand for his theft, and his foot for frightening him. Whoever kills, kill him. Whoever kills, frightens the wayfarers, and violates the forbidden vagina, crucify him. As for his statement: Or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides, what He, may He be glorified, means by this is that their hands are cut off in a way that is different from the way their feet are cut off. That is, their right hand is cut off, and their entire foot is cut off. That is the difference between them in the cutting off. If the place of min in this position was ala or ba, then it would have been said: or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides - or: on opposite sides, and they would have conveyed the meaning conveyed by min. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the negation that God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: It is to seek until he is able to do so, or to flee from the House of Islam. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: Or they are banished from the land, he said: The imam pursues them with horses and men until he seizes them and establishes judgment over them, or they are banished from the land of the Muslims. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: His denial, is that he is asked. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or are they banished from the land? He said. Or they flee until they leave the abode of Islam for the abode of war. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of the letter of Anas bin Malik to Abdul Malik bin Marwan: that he wrote to him: And his exile, that the imam should seek him out until he takes him, and when he takes him, he should establish over him one of these positions that God Almighty mentioned with what he deemed permissible. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said: I mentioned that to Al-Layth bin Saad, so he said: His exile, his pursuit from country to country until he is captured, or his pursuit takes him out of the abode of Islam to the abode of polytheism and war, if he is a combatant who has apostatized from Islam. Al-Walid said: I asked Malik bin Anas, and he said the same. Ali told me, Al-Walid told us: I said to Malik bin Anas and Al-Layth bin Saad: And likewise, the warrior who remains a Muslim is sought after, forcing him to be sought from country to country until he reaches one of the borders of the Muslims or the furthest part of the Muslim territory. If they seek him, does he enter the land of polytheism? They said: A Muslim is not forced to do that. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: Or they are banished from the land, he said: That they seek him until they are unable to do so. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Or they are banished from the land, he said: They are banished until they cannot be controlled. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, regarding his statement: or they are banished from the land, he said: They were expelled from the land. Wherever they are found, they are taken out until they reach the enemy's land. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement: Or they are banished from the land, he said: His banishment means that he is sought after but is not able to find him, whenever he hears about him in a land he is sought after. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Saeed told me, on the authority of Qatada: Or they are banished from the land, he said: If he did not kill or take money, he is sought until he is unable to do so. Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Yazid told me, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr: or they are banished from the land, from the land of Islam to the land of disbelief. Others said: The meaning of exile in this context is that if the imam has power over him, he exiles him from his town to another town. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: or are banished from the land. He said: Whoever frightens the Muslims’ way, is banished from his country to another, because God Almighty said: or are banished from the land. Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Salih told us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid bin Abi Habib and others told me, on the authority of Hayyan bin Surayj: that he wrote to Umar bin Abdul Aziz about the thieves, and described to him their thievery and their imprisonment in prisons. He said: God said in His Book: “The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption through the land is that they shall be killed or crucified or their hands and feet shall be cut off on opposite sides,” and he left out the words: or they shall be exiled from the land. So Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to him: As for what follows, you wrote to me mentioning the words of God, the Almighty and Majestic: “The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption through the land is that they shall be killed or crucified or their hands and feet shall be cut off on opposite sides,” and you left out the words of God: or they shall be exiled from the land. So, a prophet! You, Hayyan! Do not move things from their places. You have prepared yourself for killing and crucifixion as if you were a slave of Banu Uqayl, without any resemblance to him? When this letter of mine reaches you, understand the commotion. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yazid and others, a hadith similar to this, except that Yunus said in his hadith: It is as if you are a slave of the Banu Abi Uqal, without me resembling you to him. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib: That Al-Salt, the scribe of Hayyan ibn Shurayj, told them: Hayyan wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: That some Copts were proven to have fought God and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land, and that God says: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land is that they will be disgraced. So he read until he reached: and their feet are on opposite sides, and he stopped at the denial. And he wrote to him: If the Commander of the Faithful sees fit to carry out God’s judgment concerning them, then let him write that. So when Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz read his letter, he said: Hayyan has satisfied himself! Then he wrote to him: Your letter has reached me and I have understood it, and I have been content, as if I had written according to the letter of Yazid ibn Abi Muslim, or the foreigner of Iraq, without likening you to them. So I wrote according to the beginning of the verse, then I was silent about the end of it. And God says: Or they are banished from the land. So if the evidence has been established against them as you have written, then tie iron chains around their necks, then hide them to a tumultuous and violent place. Abu Jaafar said: Shaghab and Bada are two places. Others said: The meaning of banishment from the land in this context is imprisonment. Mention of those who narrated this from him: It is the saying of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of exile from the land, in this context, is his exile from one country to another country, and his imprisonment in the prison in the country to which he was exiled, until his repentance from his immorality becomes clear, and his turning away from his disobedience to his Lord. I said that this is the most correct of the sayings, because the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that in one of the three aspects that I mentioned. Since that is the case, and it is known that God, the Most High, made the punishment of the warrior: killing, crucifixion, or cutting off the hand and foot from opposite sides, after being able to do so, not in a state of his refusal, it is known that the banishment is also his punishment after being able to do so, not before. If his fleeing from being pursued was his banishment from the land, then cutting off his hand and foot from opposite sides in a state of his refusal and his war in the form of combat, meaning carrying out the punishment on him after being able to do so. And in the consensus of all that this does not take the place of his banishment that God, the Most High, made a punishment for him after being able to do so, it is invalid that his banishment from the land was his fleeing from being pursued. Since this is the case, it is known that there are only two other options left, which are exile from one town to another, or imprisonment. Since this is the case, there is no doubt that if he is exiled from one town to another, he is not exiled from the land, but rather he is exiled from one land rather than another. Since this is the case - and God, may He be glorified, only commanded his exile from the land - it is known that there is no way to exile him from the land except by confining him to a spot in it, away from the rest of it. In that case, he would be exiled from all of it, except from that from which there is no way to exile him. As for the meaning of negation, in the speech of the Arabs, it is expulsion, and from that is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: They deny the ways of the generous as hammers deny what follows the monkey. Hence, the word nafaya refers to bad dirhams and other things. As for the source of nafaya I banished, it means banishment and waste. It is also said: The bucket banishes the water. And what is said about the water that flies from the bucket is nafaya. Hence, the saying of the rajaz poet: His back was from the banishment like the birds’ places on the pure water. And from this it is said: He banished his hair, if it fell. It is said: Your color has changed, and He banished your hair. Abu Ja`far said: By His saying, That, He, the Most High, means that this is the punishment with which I have rewarded those who fought God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption in the world, by killing, crucifixion, or cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides. For them, meaning for these fighters, is disgrace in this world. He says: It is evil, shame, humiliation, punishment, and punishment for them in this world before the Hereafter. It is said: I have disgraced so-and-so, so he was disgraced with disgrace. And His statement: And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, the Almighty says: For those who fought God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption in the land, and did not repent from their actions until they perished, in the Hereafter, along with the disgrace with which You rewarded them in this world, and the punishment with which You inflicted upon them in it, a great punishment, meaning: the punishment of Hell.
5:34: Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Except for those who repent from their polytheism and their war against God and His Messenger and their endeavor to spread corruption on earth, by Islam and entering into faith, before the believers have power over them, for there is no way for the believers to be punished by any of the punishments that God has made a recompense for those who wage war against Him and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth, such as killing, crucifixion, or cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides, or exile from the land, so no one has the right to be sold before him for what he took during his state of disbelief and war against the believers, in money, blood, or honor. They said: As for the Muslim, if he wages war against the Muslims or those with whom he has a treaty, and does some of what requires punishment, his repentance will not remove the punishment for his sin, rather his repentance is between him and God, and the Imam must implement the punishment that God has made obligatory upon him, and take the rights of the people. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said: His statement, The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon the earth until His statement, So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful, this verse was revealed regarding the polytheists. So whoever among them repents before he is overpowered, there is no punishment against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment if he kills, or spreads corruption on earth, or wages war against God and His Messenger, then joins the disbelievers before he is overpowered. The prescribed punishment that he committed will be carried out against him. Bashar told us, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: “Except for those who repent before you have them in your power. So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful.” He said: This is for the people of polytheism, if they do something in their polytheism, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, if they repent and submit. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption is adultery, theft, killing a person, and destroying crops and offspring, except for those who repent before you have them in your power, during the time of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: There were people between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant, but they broke the covenant, cut off the way, and spread corruption on the earth. So God gave His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the choice concerning them: If He wished, He could kill him, or if He wished, He could crucify him, or if He wished, He could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. Whoever repents before you are able to seize him, that will be accepted from him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse, then he mentioned something similar to what Al-Dahhak said, except that he said: If he comes repentant and enters Islam, it is accepted from him, and he is not held accountable for what came before. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Except for those who repent before you are able to seize them, he said: This is for the people of polytheism, if they did something like this in their polytheism, then repented and submitted, then God is Forgiving and Merciful. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Qatadah: As for his statement: Except those who repent before you are able to overpower them, this is for the people of polytheism. So whoever among the polytheists attacks something from the Muslims while they are at war with them, and takes property and sheds blood, then repents before you are able to overpower him, what has passed is waived for him. Others said: Rather, this verse is meant by the ruling, the warriors of God and His Messenger: the warriors of the people of Islam, whoever of them cuts off the road while he is residing in his Islam, then he seeks protection and is granted protection for the crimes he committed, and he is at war with the Muslims, and whoever of them does that while apostatizing from Islam, then he goes to the land of war, then he seeks protection and is granted protection. They said: So if the Imam grants him protection for his previous crimes, then no one has a responsibility against him in blood or money that he took before his repentance, and before the Imam grants him protection. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Osama told me, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Amer Al-Sha’bi: That Haritha bin Badr went out as a warrior, and he frightened the wayfarers, shed blood, and seized money, then he came repentant before he was overpowered, so Ali bin Abi Talib, peace be upon him, accepted his repentance, and granted him a security extended for whatever he had taken of blood or money. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: That Haritha bin Badr fought during the reign of Ali bin Abi Talib, so he went to Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, and asked him to seek protection from Ali, but he refused. Then he went to Ibn Ja’far, but he refused him. Then he went to Saeed bin Qais Al-Hamdani, and he granted him protection and took him close to him, and said to him: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, sought protection for me. He said: When Ali prayed the morning prayer, Saeed bin Qais came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the punishment for those who wage war against God and His Messenger? He said: That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. Then he said: Except for those who repent before you are able to seize them. Saeed said: Even if it was Haritha bin Badr? He said: Even if it was Haritha bin Badr! He said: So this Haritha bin Badr has come repentant, is he safe? He said: Yes! He said: So he brought him and pledged allegiance to him, and he accepted that from him, and wrote him a guarantee of safety. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said: Haritha ibn Badr had spread corruption on earth and waged war, then he repented. Ali spoke to him, but he did not grant him security. So he went to Sa’id ibn Qays and spoke to him. Sa’id ibn Qays went to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you say about one who wages war against God and His Messenger? - and he recited the entire verse - and said: What do you think of one who repents before you are able to overpower him? He said: I say as God said. He said: Then he is Haritha ibn Badr! Ali said: So he granted him security. Haritha said: Shall I not reach Hamdan? If I meet it far away, no enemy will be safe who finds fault with it. By the life of her father, Hamdan fears God and her suitor judges by the Book. Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his saying: Except for those who repent before you have them in your power, and his repentance before he is in your power is that he writes to the Imam asking him for protection from what he killed and corrupted on earth. If he does not give me protection from that, I will increase in corruption, killing, and taking of wealth more than I did before. So it is the right of the Imam to give him protection from that. So if the Imam gives him protection, he comes until he places his hand in the hand of the Imam. No one among the people has the right to follow him, nor to seize him for the blood he shed, nor for the wealth he took. And whatever wealth he had is his, so that he does not kill the believers and cause corruption as well. So if he returns to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, then He is his guardian, and He will seize him for what he did, and his repentance is between him, the Imam, and the people. So if the Imam takes him, and he has repented, as he claims, to God, the Almighty, before the Imam gives him protection, then let the prescribed punishment be carried out on him. Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, Makhul told me that he said: If the imam gives him security, then he is safe, and the punishment for what he did will not be carried out on him. Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever comes repentant from war before he is able to overpower him, seeks protection from the Imam who grants him protection or does not seek protection from him, after he comes surrendering and abandoning war. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Amir, he said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, while he was in Kufa during the reign of Uthman, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer and said: O Abu Musa, this is the place of one who seeks refuge with you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so al-Muradi. I fought against God and His Messenger, and I spread corruption in the land, but I repented before you could overpower me! So Abu Musa stood up and said: This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and he fought against God and His Messenger, and he spread corruption in the land, but he repented before you could overpower him. Whoever meets him should not treat him except with good. So the man stayed as long as God willed, then he went out and God, the Almighty and Majestic, caught up with him because of his sins and killed him. Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: A man came to Abu Musa and mentioned something similar. Ali ibn Sahl narrated that al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated: I said to Malik: What do you think of this warrior who has frightened the people and taken blood and property, and has fled to the land of war or has resisted in the lands of Islam, then has come repentant before he is overpowered? He said: His repentance is accepted. I said: Is he not to be prosecuted for any of his incidents? He said: No, unless he has specific property with him, which is returned to its owner, or the guardian of the one who was killed in his war seeks it, which is proven by evidence or confession, and he is executed for it. As for the blood that he has taken but whose guardians have not sought it, the Imam is not to be prosecuted for anything. Ali said: al-Walid said: I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: His repentance is accepted if he was a warrior against the common people and the Imams, and has harmed them in his war, so he has drawn his weapon, and taken blood and property, and has had a means of protection or a group to whom he can take refuge, or he has fled to the land of war and apostatized from Islam, or he was residing there, then he has come repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not to be prosecuted for anything of it. Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr said: I heard Ibn Shihab Al-Zuhri say that. Ali bin Sahl Tal told me, Al-Walid told us: I mentioned the statement of Abu Amr and Malik to Al-Layth bin Saad on this issue, and he said: If he declares a general war against the Imams, and seizes blood and property, and the government is prevented by his war against him, or he goes to the land of war, then he comes repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for any of his events in his war of blood, whether specific or general, because his guardian is seeking it. Ali told me, Al-Walid told us, Al-Layth said, and Musa bin Ishaq Al-Madani, who was the emir among us, also told me: Ali Al-Asadi fought and frightened the wayfarers and took blood and property, so the imams and the common people sought him out, but he refused, and they could not find him until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ (al-Zumar 39:53), so he stopped and said: O servant of God, recite it again. So he repeated it to him, then he sheathed his sword, then he came repentant. Until he arrived in Madinah at dawn, washed himself, then he came to the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and prayed the dawn prayer, then he sat with Abu Hurairah in the midst of his companions. When dawn broke, the people recognized him and stood up to him, so he said: You have no way with me, I have come repentant before you could find me! Abu Hurairah said: He has spoken the truth. Abu Hurairah took him by the hand until he came to Marwan bin Al-Hakam when he was in charge of Medina during the time of Muawiyah, and he said: This is Ali who has come repentant, and you have no way against him or killing him. He said: So he left all of that. He said: And Ali went out repentant, fighting in the way of God at sea, and they met the Romans, so they brought his ship close to one of their ships, so he attacked the Romans in their ship, and they were defeated from him to their other ship, so it capsized with them and him, and they all drowned. Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Mutraf bin Muqal told us, he said, I heard Ata’ say about a man who stole something and came back repentant without being caught, is there any punishment for him? He said: No! Then he said: Except for those who repent before you have them in your power, the verse. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, they said: If someone comes repentant and has not seized any money or shed any blood, he is left alone. This is what God said: Except for those who repent before you have them in your power, meaning that he has not shed any blood or seized any money. Others said: Rather, what is meant by the exception in that is the one who repents from his war against God and His Messenger and his striving to spread corruption on earth after joining his war in the land of disbelief. But if his war and his fighting were while he was residing in the land of Islam and entering the midst of the nation, then his repentance does not remove from him anything of the limits of God, the Exalted, the Majestic, nor of the rights of the Muslims and those with whom he has a treaty, rather he is held accountable for that. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Ismail told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah: that he told him that they asked Urwah about someone who steals in Islam and commits a crime, then comes back repentant, so he said: His repentance is not accepted, if that were accepted from them they would be emboldened against him, and it would be a great corruption. But if he flees to the enemy, then comes back repentant, I do not see any punishment for him. It was narrated on the authority of Urwa that this statement is different, which is: Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, someone who heard Hisham bin Urwa told me, on the authority of Urwa, he said: The punishment for what he fled from will be carried out on him, and no one is allowed to be safe in it - meaning, the one who commits a punishment, then flees and joins the infidels, then comes back repentant. Others said: If his fighting and warfare was in the land of Islam, and he was not protected by a group to which he could resort, then he came repenting before he was able to overpower him, then his repentance does not remove from him any of the punishment or the rights of the people. If his fighting and warfare was in the land of Islam, or he was going to the land of disbelief, but in all of that he was resorting to a group that would protect him from whoever wanted him from the authority of the Muslims, then he came repenting before he was able to overpower him, then his repentance removes from him all of the incidents that he did during those days of his fighting, unless he committed a prescribed punishment, or ordered the company to do something that included a punishment, or fined a Muslim or a covenanted person while he was not resorting to a group that would protect him, then he is held accountable for what he did of that while he was like that, and that does not remove from him his repentance. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr said: If a thief or a group of thieves cut off the road, and they took what they took of blood and money, and they had no group to turn to or protection, and they were not safe except by entering the midst of their nation and the masses of their people, then he came repentant before he was overpowered, his repentance would not be accepted, and his punishment would be carried out on him, whatever it was. Ali told me, Al-Walid told us: I mentioned to Abu Amr what Urwah said: The prescribed punishment for what he fled from shall be carried out on him, and no one shall be granted security for him. Abu Amr said: If someone fled from his incident in the land of Islam, and an imam gave him security, his security is not permissible. If he went to the land of war, then asked an imam for security for his incidents, the imam should not give him security. Because the imam gave him security even though he was unaware of his incidents, he is safe. If someone comes demanding him for blood or money, he is returned to his place of safety. If he refuses to return, he is safe and no one shall interfere with him. He said: If he gave him security for his incidents even though he was aware of them, the imam is responsible and must pay blood money for what he had taken of blood or money, and he is sinful for neglecting those prescribed punishments and blood money, and his matter is up to God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: Abu Amr said: If he does that, and he has a means of protection or a group to which he can take refuge, or he goes to the land of war and apostatizes from Islam, or he was residing there, then he comes repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not followed by any of the incidents that he committed in his war, unless something is found with him that is still there, in which case it is returned to its owner. Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Rabia, he said: His repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything he did during his war, unless someone demands that he be punished for blood that he had taken in peace before his war, then he is to be retaliated for. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Muammar Al-Raqi told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, who said: May God kill Al-Hajjaj! If he was knowledgeable! He gave a man security from fighting him, so he said: Look, did he do anything before he went out? Others said: His repentance removes the punishment imposed on him by God for fighting him, but does not remove the rights of the children of Adam. Among those who said this was Al-Shafi’i. Al-Rabi' told us about it. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements in my opinion is the statement of the one who said: The repentance of the warrior who abstains by himself or with a group with him before he is overpowered removes from him the worldly consequences that were incumbent upon him during his days of war and rebellion, from the limits of God, and the necessary fines, fuel, and retaliation, except for what was in his hand of the money of the Muslims and those with whom he had a treaty, which is returned to its people, due to the consensus of all that this is the ruling on the group that abstains and wages war against God and His Messenger, and seeks to spread corruption on earth in the manner of apostasy from Islam. So too is the ruling on every one who abstains and seeks to spread corruption on earth, whether they are a group or one. As for the one who steals in secret, or sneaks in to take advantage of the one he stole from, or brandishes a weapon in the open at some passerby, and is unable to refrain when asked, then the judgment of God upon him - whether he repents or not - is carried out, and the rights of the one whose money he stole, or whose guardian he harmed with blood or deceit are taken, and his repentance is between him and God, the Mighty and Sublime, based on the consensus of all that if he steals something of that nature while it belongs to the Muslims, he is safe, then he becomes at war with them: that his war against them will not remove from him a right of God, the Mighty and Sublime, nor of a human being. So too is his judgment if he commits that in the open or in secret, and he is not able to resist the ruler himself if he wants to, nor does he have a group to which he can resort to protect him. In His statement: Except those who repent before you have them in your power, is clear evidence for those who are guided to understand that the ruling that God, the Exalted, mentioned regarding those who are at war, applies to Muslims and those with whom we have a treaty, not to the polytheists who have waged war against the Muslims. This is because if this were a ruling regarding the polytheists who are at war, not to the Muslims and not to their protection, then their Islam would not have been removed from them - if they converted to Islam or repented after We had power over them - what they had before their conversion to Islam and repentance of being killed, and what the Muslims have regarding the polytheists at war. And in the consensus of the Muslims is that the conversion of the polytheist at war removes from him, after the Muslims have power over him, what his conversion to Islam removed from him before the power over him, which indicates that the correct statement regarding this is the statement of the one who said: What is meant by the verse about those who are at war in this place is the wars of the people of the religion or the protection, not from the polytheists other than them who are at war. As for his saying: Know that God is Forgiving and Merciful? Its meaning is: Know, O believers, that God will not hold accountable anyone who repents from among the people of war against God and His Messenger, who strive to spread corruption on earth, and others for their sins, but He pardons him and conceals them from him, and does not disgrace him for them with punishment in this world or the next, and He is Merciful to him in His pardon of him and His leaving him to be punished for them.
5:35: Abu Ja`far said: By that, He, the Most High, means: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger in what He has informed you of and promised of reward and threatened of punishment, fear God, meaning: answer God in what He has commanded you and forbidden you by obeying Him in that, and realize your faith and belief in your Lord and your offspring through your righteous deeds, and seek the means of approach to Him, meaning: seek closeness to Him by doing what pleases Him. Al-Wasila is the active participle of the saying: I sought the help of so-and-so with such-and-such, meaning: I approached him. From this comes the saying of Antarah: Men have a way to get to you. If they take you, put on kohl and dye your hair.
