It means the means, the proximity, and from it the saying of the other: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the reconciliation between us and the means will return And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, H, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il: And seek a means of approach to Him, he said: drawing near to Him in deeds. Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, H, and Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Ata’: And seek a means of approach to Him, he said: closeness. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: O you who have believed, fear God and seek the means to Him, he said: It is asking and drawing near. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And seek a means of approach to Him, meaning: draw near to Him by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And seek a means of approach to Him, drawing near to God Almighty. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And seek a means of approach to Him, he said: closeness. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, regarding his statement: And seek a means of approach to Him, he said: closeness. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And seek a means of approach to Him, he said: Love, endear yourself to God. And he recited: Those are the ones who call upon God, seeking a means of approach to their Lord (al-Isra’ 17:57). Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: And strive, O believers, against My enemies and your enemies, in My cause, meaning in His religion and law that He has legislated for His servants, which is Islam. He says: Exhaust yourselves in fighting them and compelling them to enter into the true Islamic faith, that you may succeed, meaning: so that you may succeed and attain eternal life and immortality in His Paradise. We have demonstrated the meaning of success in the past with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
5:36: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: Those who denied the Lordship of their Lord and worshipped other than Him, from among the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf, and from others who worshipped idols and statues, and were destroyed for that before repenting, if they had the kingdom of all that is on the earth and double it with it, to ransom themselves with it from the punishment of God upon them for abandoning His command and worshipping other than Him on the Day of Resurrection, and ransomed themselves with all of that, God would not accept that from them as ransom and compensation for their torment and punishment, but rather He will torment them with scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, a painful torment for them. This is an announcement from God, the Most High, to the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they and all the other polytheists are equal before Him in their painful torment and great retribution. This is because they used to say, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days (Al Imran 3:24), being deceived by God, the Most High, and lying about Him. So God, the Most High, denied them with this verse and the one after it, and put an end to their hope, so He said to them and to all the disbelievers in Him and His Messenger: “Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment. They want to get out of the Fire, but they will never get out of it, and theirs is an enduring punishment.” God, the Most High, says to them: Do not hope, O disbelievers, for the ransom to be accepted from you, nor for your exit from the Fire through the means of your fathers after you have entered it, if you die in your disbelief, but repent to God with sincere repentance.
5:37: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: They want to get out of the Fire, is that He wants those who disbelieved in their Lord on the Day of Resurrection to get out of the Fire after entering it, and they will not get out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment, meaning: for them is a permanent, fixed punishment that will never leave them or be transferred, as the poet said: For on the Day of the People, you will have from me a permanent torment that will last for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah: Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq said to Ibn Abbas, may God have mercy on him: Blind of sight and blind of heart, he claims that people will come out of the Fire, and God Almighty said: And they will not come out of it? Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you, read what is above it! This is for the disbelievers.
5:38: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And whoever drives a man or woman, then cut off, O people, his hand. That is why He raised the male and female thief, because they are not specified. If what was meant by that was a male and female thief specifically, then the correct way of speaking would have been to put it in the accusative case. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he used to recite: And the male and female thieves. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: In our reading - he said: and perhaps he said: in the reading of Abdullah - And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim: In our reading: And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands. This is evidence of the correctness of what we have said about its meaning, and the correctness of the nominative case in it, and that the male and female thief are nominative by their action as I have described, for the reasons that I have described. And God Almighty said: Then cut off their hands, meaning: their right hands, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then cut off their hands, the right one. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said: In Abdullah’s recitation: And the male thief, male or female, cut off their hands. Then they differed about the thief that God Almighty meant. Some of them said: He meant by that the one who steals three dirhams or more. This is the opinion of a group of the people of Medina, including Malik bin Anas and those who said the same. They provided evidence for their opinion by saying that: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off a shield worth three dirhams. Others said: Rather, he meant by that the one who steals a quarter of a dinar or its value. Among those who said that is Al-Awza’i and those who said the same. They supported their saying by the report that was narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more. Others said: Rather, he meant by that the one who steals ten dirhams or more. Among those who said that was Abu Hanifa and his companions. They provided evidence for that with the report narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr and Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hand of a shield worth ten dirhams. Others said: Rather, he meant by that the thief of little or much. They argued for that by saying that the verse is clear, and that no one has the right to specify anything from it, except with an argument that must be accepted. They said: There is no authentic report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this is for a specific thief. They said: The reports regarding what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off his hand are confused and different, and no one narrated from him that a thief of a dirham was brought to him and he let him go. Rather, they narrated from him that he cut off his hand for a shield worth three dirhams. They said: It is possible that if a thief of a daniq were brought to him, he would cut off his hand. They said: Ibn al-Zubayr cut off his hand for a dirham. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The verse is general. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abdul-Mumin told us, on the authority of Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement: And the male thief, male or female. Is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is the statement of those who said: The verse is specifically intended for thieves, and they are those who steal a quarter of a dinar or more or its value, due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more. I have exhaustively mentioned the statements of those who differed on this matter, along with the reasons they used for their statements, and the statement of which of them is most correct, with its supporting evidence, in our book The Book of Theft, so we disliked making the book long by repeating it in this place. His saying: A punishment for what they have earned, a punishment from God, means: a reward for their theft and their work of stealing in disobedience to God. A punishment from God, means: a punishment from God for their theft. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And as for the male thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from God. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” Do not feel sorry for them by implementing the prescribed punishments on them, for by God, God has never commanded anything except that it is good, nor has He ever forbidden anything except that it is corruption. Omar bin Al-Khattab used to say: Be harsh on thieves, and cut off their hands hand by hand and foot by foot. And His saying: And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, God Almighty says: And God is Exalted in Might, in His vengeance against this male and female thief and others who disobey Him, Wise, in His judgment and decree over them. He says: O believers, do not be excessive in implementing My judgment on thieves and other criminals for whom I have imposed punishments in this world, for I have decreed that upon them, with My wisdom, and My knowledge of what is good for them and for you.
5:39: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So whoever repents, of these thieves, meaning whoever returns from what God hates of disobeying Him, to what He is pleased with of obeying Him, after his wrongdoing, and his wrongdoing is his aggression and doing what God forbade him from doing of stealing people’s money, and reforms, meaning: and reforms himself by carrying it to what it hates in obedience to God, and repenting to Him for what he was doing of disobeying Him. Mujahid - as he told us - used to say: His repentance in this situation is the punishment that will be carried out on him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, then God forgives him, he says: the limit. Abu Kuraib narrated: Musa ibn Dawud narrated: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated: Huyayy ibn Abdullah narrated: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli narrated: Abdullah ibn Amr said: A woman stole jewelry. Those whom she had stolen from came and said: O Messenger of God, this woman stole from us! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut off her right hand. The woman said: Is there any repentance? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are today as free from your sin as the day your mother bore you! Then God, the Almighty, revealed: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends, then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. And his saying: Then God will accept his repentance, means: God Almighty will return him to what He loves and is pleased with, from what He hates and is displeased with in His disobedience. And His saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, means: Indeed, God, the Almighty, will cover the sins of whoever repents and turns from his sins to His obedience, by pardoning his punishment, making it lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection, and leaving him disgraced by it in front of all witnesses. Merciful, to him and to His servants who repent to Him for their sins.
5:40: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do these people - meaning those who say: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days, who claim that they are the sons of God and His beloved ones - not know that God is the Manager of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and its Disposer and Choker, and nothing in either of them is prevented from what He wills, because all of that is His property, and His command is to Him, and there is no relation between Him and anything in them or in either of them, so He favors him because of his kinship to Him, so He saves him from His punishment, even though he is a disbeliever in Him, and opposes His command and prohibition, or He sends him to the Fire while he is obedient to Him because of his distant kinship to Him, but He punishes whomever He wills of His creation in this world for disobeying Him by killing, swallowing up, transforming, and other types of His punishment, and He forgives whomever He wills of them in this world by repenting to Him for his disbelief and disobedience, so He saves him from destruction and rescues him from punishment, and God is over all things competent. He says: God Almighty is able to punish whomever He wants to punish from among His creation for disobeying Him, and to forgive whomever He wants to forgive from among them by rescuing them from destruction through repentance and other than that of all matters, because creation is His creation, and the kingdom is His kingdom, and the servants are His servants. His statement, Do you not know that to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? was addressed to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it are those mentioned from the groups of the Children of Israel who were in the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those around it. We have explained the Arabs’ use of something similar to that in their speech with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
5:41: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed about who was meant by this verse. Some of them said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba bin Abdul Mundhir, because of his saying to Banu Qurayzah when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them: It is only slaughter, so do not accept the judgment of Saad. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief - of those who say, “We believe with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe,” he said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar - they claimed that he was Abu Lubaba - whom Banu Qurayzah pointed to on the day of the siege, what is the matter? And why was it revealed? So he pointed to them that it was slaughter. Others said: Rather, it was revealed about a Jewish man who asked a Muslim man to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his ruling on a person he had killed. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Aamer: Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, he said: There was a Jewish man who was killed by a man from his religion, so the killer said to their Muslim allies: Ask Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for me, for if he sends the blood money, we will dispute before him, but if he orders us to kill, we will not go to him. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, something similar. Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Abdullah bin Suriya, because he apostatized after converting to Islam. Who said that? Hannad and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Az-Zuhri narrated to me, saying: I heard a man from Muzaynah narrating, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah narrated to them: The rabbis of the Jews gathered in Bayt Al-Madras when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina. A man from among them had committed adultery with a Jewish woman who had been married after his marriage. They said: Take this man and this woman to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him what the ruling is regarding them. And bring him the ruling regarding them. If he does with them what you do with regard to stoning, which is flogging with a rope of palm fiber coated with tar, then blackening their faces, then carrying them on two donkeys, and turning their faces towards the donkey’s back, then follow him, for he is a king. But if he rules that they should be stoned, then beware of him taking away from you what is in your hands. So they came to him and said: O Muhammad, this man has committed adultery with a married woman after his marriage. So rule regarding them, for we have appointed you to rule regarding them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked until he reached their rabbis at the school house, and said: O group of Jews, bring out to me your most knowledgeable one! So they brought out to him Abdullah bin Suriya the one-eyed - and some of Banu Qurayzah narrated that they brought out to him that day with Ibn Suriya, Abu Yasir bin Akhtab, and Wahb bin Yahudah - and they said: These are our scholars! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them until their matter was resolved, until they said to Ibn Suriya: This is the most knowledgeable of those remaining in the Torah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was alone with him, and he was a young boy, one of the newest of them in walking. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him the question, saying: O Ibn Suriya, I ask you by God and I remind you of His favors to the Children of Israel, do you know that God ruled in the Torah for those who commit adultery after being married that they should be stoned? He said: By God, yes! By God, O Abu al-Qasim, they know that you are a prophet sent by God, but they envy you! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and ordered them to be stoned at the door of his mosque, in the tribe of Banu Ghanim ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar. Then Ibn Suriya disbelieved after that, so God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief - those who say, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: My father narrated, H, and Hannad narrated, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, H, and Hannad narrated, he said: Ubaidah ibn Hamid narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a Jew who had been flogged and had been bathed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called one of their scholars and said: Is this how you find the punishment for adultery among you? He said: Yes! He said: I ask you by He who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery among you? He said: No, and had you not asked me about this, I would not have told you. But stoning is the punishment. However, adultery has become widespread among our nobles, so if we seized a noble person, we would leave him, and if we seized a weak person, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us meet and you can put something in place of stoning, so it can be for the noble and the lowly. So we put bathing and flogging in place of stoning! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the first to revive your matter after they killed it! So he ordered him to be stoned, and God revealed: Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, the verse. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said: I was sitting with Saeed bin al-Musayyab, and with Saeed was a man whom he respected, and he was a man from Muzaynah whose father had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, and he was one of the companions of Abu Hurayrah. He said: Abu Hurayrah said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. H, and Al-Mughni told me, he said, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: A man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and comprehends it told me, he told on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah said: While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a Jewish man came to him, and they had consulted about a friend of theirs who had committed adultery after he had become married. Some of them said to one another: This prophet has been sent, and you know that stoning has been imposed upon you in the Torah, but you concealed it and agreed among yourselves on a lesser punishment. So go and ask this prophet, and if he gives us a fatwa with what was imposed upon us in the Torah of stoning, we will leave that, for we left that in the Torah, and it is more deserving of being obeyed and believed! So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Abu Al-Qasim, a friend of ours who had become married committed adultery, so what do you think should be the punishment for him? Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) did not return to them until he had risen and we had risen with him. He set off to lead the schools of the Jews until he came to them and found them studying the Torah in the school house. He said to them: O group of Jews, I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah as punishment for one who commits adultery while he is married? They said: We find him being bathed and flogged! Their rabbi was silent in the corner of the house. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) saw his silence, he insisted on asking him. Their rabbi said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning upon them! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to him: What was the first concession you sought from God? He said: The cousin of a king committed adultery and he did not stone him. Then another man committed adultery in a family of people, and the king wanted to stone him, but his people stood up to protect him and said: By God, you will not stone him until you stone so-and-so, the cousin of the king! So they agreed among themselves on a punishment less than stoning and left off stoning. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then I will judge according to what is in the Torah! So God revealed regarding that: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Others said: Rather, he meant the hypocrites. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, regarding his statement: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you - those who say, ‘We believe’ with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe, he said: They are the hypocrites. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: We believe with their mouths, he said, he says: they are the hypocrites, listening to another people, he said: they also listen to the Jews. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is to say: What is meant by His statement, Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, of those who say, “We believe, with their mouths, but whose hearts do not believe,” are a group of hypocrites. It is possible that Ibn Suriya was among those included in this verse, or Abu Lubabah, or someone else. However, the most reliable thing that has been narrated about this is what we mentioned before from the narration on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and al-Bara’ ibn `Azib, because that was on the authority of two men from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is the case, then the correct thing to say about it is to say: What is meant by it is `Abdullah ibn Suriya. If this is true, then the interpretation of the verse is: O Messenger, do not let those who hasten to deny your prophethood and to reject that you are a prophet grieve you, from those who said: We believe in you, O Muhammad, that you are a messenger sent to God, and we know that with certainty, because of your existence and description in our book. This is because in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, which was narrated by Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: By God, O Abu Al-Qasim, they know that you are a prophet sent by God, but they envy you. This was - according to this report - from Ibn Suriya, out of faith in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his mouth, but he did not believe it in his heart. So God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, knowing the conscience of Ibn Suriya and that he did not believe in his heart, he says: And his heart did not believe that you are a messenger sent by God. Abu Ja`far said: God, the Most High, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger, do not be saddened by the haste of these hypocrites - who show with their tongues that they believe in you, but they believe in lying - to disbelieve in you, and do not let the Jews be hasty to deny your prophethood. Then God, the Most High, the Most Great, described their characteristics to him, and described them to him with their reprehensible descriptions and their vile actions, and informed him, comforting him for the sadness that befell him because of their denial of him, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, that they are people who make permissible what is forbidden and bad foods and vile meals, such as bribes and ill-gotten gains, and that they are people of slander and lies against God, and distortion of His Book. Then he informed him that he would bring them shame in this worldly life and punishment in the Hereafter. He said: They are listeners to falsehood, meaning these hypocrites from among the Jews. He said: They are listeners to falsehood, and their hearing of falsehood is their hearing of the words of their rabbis: The ruling for the married adulterer in the Torah is to be burned and flogged. They are listeners to other people who have not come to you, he said: They listen to the people of the adulterer who wanted to resort to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the other people who had not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were determined to come to him, as Mujahid said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid said: listening to other people who did not come to you, with those who came to you. The people of interpretation differed regarding the listeners of lies and the listeners of other people. Some of them said: They are listening to other people, the Jews of Fadak. The other people who did not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were the Jews of Medina. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Zakariya and Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, regarding his statement: And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood, some who listen to another people, he said: The Jews of Medina, They did not come to you altering words from their [proper] usages, he said: The Jews of Fadak, they say to the Jews of Medina: If you are given this, then take it. Others said: What is meant by this is a group of Jews who were the family of the woman who committed adultery. They sent them to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the ruling on her. And those who sent them were the other people, who were the family of the immoral woman. They had not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, his statement: And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood, some who listen to other people who have not come to you, distorting [their] truth, for God revealed to the Children of Israel: If anyone among you commits adultery, stone him. They continued to do that until one of their best committed adultery. When the Children of Israel gathered to stone him, the best and nobles stood up and prevented him. Then a man from the elite committed adultery, so they gathered to stone him. The elite gathered and said: Do not stone him until you bring your companion and stone them both! The Children of Israel said: This matter has become too much for us, so come, let us set it right! So they abandoned stoning, and replaced it with forty lashes with a strong rope, and they carried him on a donkey with his face to his tail, and they blackened his face and paraded him around. They continued to do that until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent and arrived in Madinah. A woman from the noble Jews called Busra committed adultery. Her father sent some of his companions to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Ask him about adultery and what was revealed to him about it, for we fear that he will disgrace us and tell us what we did. If he gives you flogging, take it, but if he orders you to stone, beware of him! So they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him. He said: Stoning! Then God the Almighty revealed: “And among the Jews are some who listen to falsehood, listening to other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their [proper] usages,” when they distorted stoning and made it flogging. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The listeners of lies are the listeners of other people. It may be possible that those were from the Jews of Medina, and what was heard from them was from the Jews of Fadak, or it may be possible that they were from others. However, whichever of these was, it is from the description of a group of Jews who heard the lie against God in the ruling on the woman who rebelled among them while she was married, and that her ruling in the Torah was to be burned and flogged, and they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the ruling that was required of her, and they heard what the people of the wicked woman were saying about her before they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge him about her. They only asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that for them, so that the people of the wicked woman would know what his answer would be to them. If his ruling was not stoning, they would accept it as a ruling on them. If his ruling was stoning, they would warn him and refrain from accepting it and his ruling. Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we said. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people, he said: to another people who did not come to him from the People of the Book, these are listeners to those other people who did not come to him, they say to them falsehood: Muhammad is a liar, and this is not in the Torah, so do not believe in him. Abu Ja`far said: God the Almighty says: These listeners to lies, the listeners of another people among them who have not yet come to you from the Jews, distort the words. And their distortion was that they changed the ruling of God the Almighty - which He revealed in the Torah regarding the chaste men and women who committed adultery by stoning - to flogging and blackening. So God the Almighty said: They distort the words, meaning: these Jews, and the meaning is the ruling of the words, so He was satisfied with mentioning the report of the distortion of the words instead of mentioning the ruling, so that the listeners would know its meaning. Likewise His statement: After their [proper] places, meaning: after God placed them in their proper places, so He was satisfied with mentioning the report of their places, instead of mentioning the placement of that, as God the Almighty said: But righteousness is of he who believes in God and the Last Day (Al-Baqarah 2:177), and the meaning is: But righteousness is of he who believes in God and the Last Day. It may be possible that its meaning is: they distort the words from their places, so after is placed in place of about, just as one says: I came to you after I finished work, meaning: after I finished work. What he means by his saying: If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware, is that these aggressors who listen to lies say: If Muhammad issues a fatwa to you regarding flogging and burning our companion, then take it, meaning: accept it from him, and if he does not issue a fatwa regarding that and issues a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Al-Zuhri told me, he said: I heard a man from Muzaynah telling Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: Abu Hurairah told them - in a story he mentioned - And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood, some who listen to another people who have not come to you, he said: meaning those who were sent from among them who were sent and stayed behind, and they ordered them to do what they were ordered to do of distorting words from their places, so he said: They distort words from their places, saying, ‘If you are given this, then take it,’ for the sake of collecting, And if you are not given it, then beware, meaning stoning. Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: If you are given this, if this agrees with you, then take it. The Jews say it to the hypocrites. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, If you are given this, then take it. If this suits you, then take it, and if it does not suit you, then beware of it. The Jews say this to the hypocrites. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: They distort words from their proper places, when they distorted stoning and made it flogging, They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Zakariya and Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir: They distort words from their proper places, saying, ‘If you are given this, then take it.’ The Jews of Fadak said to the Jews of Medina: If you are given this flogging, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware of stoning. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware, they are the Jews. A woman among them committed adultery, and God had ruled in the Torah that adultery should be punished by stoning. They wanted to stone her, and they said: Go to Muhammad, perhaps he has a dispensation. If he has a dispensation, then accept it! So they went to him and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a woman among us has committed adultery, so what do you say about her? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How did God rule in the Torah regarding the adulterer? They said: Leave the Torah alone, but what do you have regarding that? He said: Bring me the most knowledgeable of you about the Torah that was revealed to Moses! He said to them: By He who saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and by He who split the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh, will you not tell me what is the ruling of God in the Torah regarding the adulterer? They said: His ruling is stoning! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered it. And he stoned her to death. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: {They have not come to you, distorting words from their [proper] usages, saying, If you are given this, then take it, but if you are not given it, then beware.} It was mentioned to us that this was regarding a man killed from Banu Qurayzah, killed by Nadir. Whenever Nadir killed a man from Banu Qurayzah, they would not put him in retaliation, but would rather give them blood money because of their superiority over them. Whenever Qurayzah killed a man from Banu Qurayzah, they would not accept anything less than retaliation because of their superiority over them in their eyes, out of pride. So the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina to collect this man killed, and they wanted to report this to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). A hypocrite said to them: This man killed by you was intentionally killed, whenever you report him to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I fear for you retaliation, so if he accepts the blood money from you, then take him, otherwise be on your guard! Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, They distort the words from their [proper] usages, he said: These people who did not come to you distort the words from their [proper] usages, they do not place them as God revealed them. He said: And all of these are Jews, some of them from others. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Ubaidah bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib: “They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ They say, ‘Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding the burning and flogging, then take it, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding the stoning, then beware.’” Abu Ja`far said: This is a consolation from God, the Most High, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his grief over the haste of those whose story he told of the Jews and hypocrites in this verse. God, the Most High, says to him: Do not be saddened by their haste to deny your prophethood, for I have decreed that they will not repent from their misguidance, nor will they turn back from their disbelief, because of My previous wrath upon them. And your grief over what you see of their haste to do what I have made a cause for their destruction and their deserving of My warning will not benefit them. The meaning of fitnah in this context is: straying from the right path. God Almighty says: And whoever God, O Muhammad, wants to return due to his straying from the path of guidance, you will not be able to rescue him from God from what God wants for him of confusion and straying. So do not feel sad about what you missed of his guidance to the truth, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And whomever God wants to test, you will not possess for him anything from God. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not let those who hasten to disbelief from among the Jews, whose description I have described to you, grieve you. Because their hastening to do so is because God has willed to tempt them and has sealed their hearts, so that they will never be guided. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify, meaning: These are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify from the filth of disbelief and the dirt of polytheism, with the purity of Islam and cleanliness of faith, so that they would repent. Rather, He intended for them disgrace in this world - and that is humiliation and disgrace - and in the Hereafter the torment of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. In a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of shame, the statement was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar and others, on the authority of Ikrimah, Those are the ones whose hearts God did not want to purify - for them in this world is disgrace, he said: A city in Rome will be conquered and they will be taken captive.
5:42: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: These Jews, whose description I have described to you, O Muhammad, listen to falsehood and lies, from what some of them say to others: Muhammad is a liar, he is not a prophet, and some of them say: The punishment for the married adulterer in the Torah is flogging and burning, and other falsehoods and slander, and they accept bribes and eat them in exchange for their lies about God and their slander against Him, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Abu Aqil told us, he said, I heard Al-Hasan say regarding His statement: They are listeners to falsehood and devourers of unlawful gain, he said: That is for the rulers, they heard a lie and ate bribes. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: listeners to lies, devourers of unlawful gain, he said: This was with the Jewish rulers before you, they used to listen to lies and accept bribes. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Those who consume unlawful gain, he said: Bribery in judgment, and they are Jews. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father and Ishaq al-Azraq told us, and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah: Those who consume ill-gotten gains, he said: ill-gotten gains are bribes. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ and Wasil ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: It was said to Abdullah: What is sahh? He said: Bribery. They said: In the ruling? He said: That is disbelief. Sufyan told us, he said, Ghundar and Wahb bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Irreligious gain means bribery. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Harith, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, he said: We said to Abdullah: We did not see ill-gotten gains as anything but bribery in judgment! Abdullah said: That is disbelief. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: Is ill-gotten gain, bribery? He said: Yes. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim Ibn Abi Al-Ja`d, on the authority of Masruq, he said: I asked Abdullah about ill-gotten gains, and he said: A man seeks a need from another man, so he fulfills it, and he gives it to him, and he accepts it. Suwar told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur and Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: Irreligious gain means bribery. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah: Al-Saht, he said: Bribery in religion. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, he said, Umar said: What was from the ill-gotten gains, bribes and the dowry of the adulteress. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Al-Saht is bribery. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Those who consume what is unlawful, he said: bribes. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The dowry of a prostitute is ill-gotten, the semen of a stallion is ill-gotten, the earnings of a barber are ill-gotten, and the price of a dog is ill-gotten. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Al-Saht is a bribe in a ruling. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Masruq, he said: I asked Ibn Masoud about ill-gotten gains, he said: Bribery. I said: In the ruling? He said: That is disbelief. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: They consume ill-gotten gains, meaning bribes. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hasan narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Masruq and Alqamah: They asked Ibn Masoud about bribery, and he said: It is ill-gotten gain. They said: In the judgment? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44). Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Bakir bin Abi Bakir, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, who said: Masruq interceded for a man in need, so he gave him a slave girl. He became extremely angry and said: If I had known that you would do this, I would not have spoken to you about your need, nor will I speak to you about what remains of your need. I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: Whoever intercedes to restore a right or remove an injustice, and a gift is given to him and he accepts, then it is ill-gotten. It was said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, we did not see that as anything other than taking a judgment! He said: Taking a judgment is disbelief. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They listen to falsehood and devour what is unlawful. That is because they took bribes in judgment and ruled with lies. Hannad told us, he said, Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, he said: I asked Ibn Masoud about saht, is it bribery in judgment? He said: No, whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a disbeliever, and whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a wrongdoer, and whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a sinner. But saht is when a man seeks your help in wronging him and you help him in it, then he gives you a gift and you accept it. Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hubayrah al-Saba’i, who said: There are three types of ill-gotten gains: the dowry of a prostitute, bribery in a ruling, and what was given to soothsayers in the pre-Islamic era. Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Mut’i’ told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib: that he said about the earnings of a cupper, the dowry of a prostitute, the price of a dog, the bribe in a judgment, the fee of a soothsayer, the sperm of a stallion, the bribe in a judgment, the price of wine, and the price of a dead animal: they are from ill-gotten gains. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Those who consume what is unlawful, he said: Bribery in judgment. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawwal told me, on the authority of Umar ibn Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every flesh that is grown by ill-gotten gains, the Fire is more deserving of it. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is ill-gotten gains? He said: Bribery in judgment. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdul-Jabbar bin Omar told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abdullah, he said: Anas bin Malik said to me: If you go back to your father, say to him: Beware of bribery, for it is ill-gotten. His father was the police chief of Medina. Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Bribery is ill-gotten. Masruq said: So we said to Abdullah: Is it in the ruling? He said: No. Then he recited: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). The root of the word saht is the dog of hunger. It is said from it: So-and-so has a saht al-madah, if he is a glutton who is never found except hungry. The bribe is called saht, in imitation of that, as if the one who is being bribed is greedy for taking what is given to him, like the one who has a saht al-madah for food. It is said from it: Sahtah and Asahtah, two dialects transmitted from the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq bin Ghalib: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when nothing was left of money except what was wiped out or wasted. It means that he has eradicated it by eating it and spoiling it. Hence the Almighty’s saying: He will destroy you with a punishment (Ta-Ha 20:61). The Arabs say to the one who shaves: He has eradicated the hair, meaning: he has eradicated it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, that if these other people who have not yet come to you - and they are the people of the prostitute - come to you seeking arbitration, then judge between them if you wish with the truth that God has made His judgment for those of them who have done the act of the prostitute, or turn away from them and leave the judgment between them if you wish, and the choice in that is yours. And a group of interpreters said the same as we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Or turn away from them, the Jews. A man from among them of lowly lineage committed adultery, so they stoned him. Then a noble man from among them committed adultery, so they humiliated him and paraded him around. Then they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a fatwa to agree with them. He said: So he gave them a fatwa regarding it, stoning, but they denied it. So he ordered them to call their rabbis and monks, and he implored them by God: Do you find it in the Torah? So they concealed it, except for a man from the youngest of them who was one-eyed. So he said: They have lied to you, O Messenger of God, it is in the Torah! Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: The verse in Surat Al-Ma’idah, So if they come to you, judge between them, was about stoning. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, he said: They came to him - meaning the Jews - about a woman among them who had committed adultery, asking him about her punishment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How do you find it written in your Torah? They said: We are commanded to stone the adulteress! So the Messenger of God commanded her to be stoned. And God Almighty said: “But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, regarding his statement: But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them, he said: They used to punish for adultery, until a young man of honor among them committed adultery, and some of them said to each other: His people will not let you stone him, but flog him and mutilate him! So they flogged him, and made him ride on a saddled donkey, and made his face face to the tail of the donkey, until another lowly man of no honor committed adultery, and they said: Stone him! Then they said: How come you did not stone the one before him? But do as you did to him! So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, they said: Ask him, perhaps you will find a dispensation with him! So the following was revealed: But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them, until His saying: Indeed, God loves those who act justly. Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed about a man who was killed among the Jews, and was killed by some of them. Who said that? Hannad bin Al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq Fal, Dawud bin Al-Hussain told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the verses in Al-Ma’idah, His saying: Then judge between them or turn away from them, to His saying: those who are just, were revealed regarding the blood money in Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu Nadir, who had honor, were paid the full blood money, while Qurayzah paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them right in that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said, Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a man from Qurayzah killed a man from Nadir, he was killed in his place. And if a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, he was given one hundred wasqs of dates. When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, so they said: Give him to us! They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, “Ibn Zayd said: In the ruling of Huyy ibn Akhtab, there were two blood-moneys for the Nadirites, and one blood-money for the Quraziites, because he was from the Nadirites. He said: And God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what was in the Torah, He said: “And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), to the end of the verse. He said: When the Qurayzah saw that, they were not satisfied with the ruling of Ibn Akhtab, so they said: Let us go to Muhammad for judgment! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, so He gave him a choice, And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, the entire verse. And if the noble man committed adultery with a lowly woman, they would stone her, and they would blacken the face of the noble man, and they would carry him on a camel, and they would make his face face towards the tail of the camel. And if the lowly man committed adultery with a high-ranking woman, they would stone him, and they did that to her. So they went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for judgment, and he stoned her. He said: And The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Who is the most knowledgeable among you about the Torah? They said: So-and-so, the one-eyed man! So he sent for him and he came to him and said: Are you the most knowledgeable among them about the Torah? He said: That is what the Jews claim! The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I ask you by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, what do you find in the Torah about adulterers? He said: O Abu al-Qasim, they stone the lowly, and they carry the noble on a camel, and they blacken his face, and they make his face face towards the camel’s tail, and they stone the lowly if he commits adultery with the noble, and they do that to her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I ask you by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, what do you find in the Torah? He kept evading, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked him by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, until he said: O Abu al-Qasim, if an old man and an old woman commit adultery, stone them both. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “That is it. Go with them and stone them.” Abdullah said: I was among those who stoned them, and he continued to smite her and protect her with the stones himself until he died. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the ruling of this verse. Is it valid today? Do the rulers have the option of ruling and considering between the People of the Covenant and the People of the Covenant if they refer their case to them, like what was given to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse? Or is it abrogated? Some of them said: This is established today, nothing has abrogated it, and the rulers have the choice in every era with this verse, just as God gave to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi: If one of the polytheists brings a case before you regarding a judgment, then if you wish, then judge between them according to what God has revealed, and if you wish, then turn away from them. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim, they said: If the polytheists come to you and make you their judge, then judge between them or turn away from them. And if you judge, then judge according to the judgement of the Muslims, and do not refer it to anything else. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi: Then if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, he said: If he wishes, he may judge, and if he wishes, he may not judge. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: If he wants, he will rule, and if he wants, he will not rule. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said: If the People of the Book come to you with a matter between them, then judge between them according to the judgement of the Muslims, or leave them alone and let the people of their religion judge between them, except in the case of theft or murder. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ata’ said to me: We have a choice. If we wish, we will judge between the People of the Book, and if we wish, we will turn away and not judge between them. If we judge between them, we will judge according to our judgment between us, or we will leave them and their judgment between them. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Shu’ayb said something similar. This is His statement: So judge between them or turn away from them. Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Mughira told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, regarding His statement: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, they said: If they come to the ruler of the Muslims, then if he wishes he may judge between them, and if he wishes he may turn away from them. And if he judges between them, he judges between them according to what is in the Book of God. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: If they come to you, judge between them, meaning: If they come to you, judge between them according to what God has revealed, or turn away from them. So God gave him a concession in that, if He wills, he may judge between them, and if He wills, he may turn away from them. Hanad told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, they said: If the polytheists come to you and make you judge between them, then judge between them according to the judgment of the Muslims and do not return to anything else, or turn away from them and leave them to the people of their religion. Others said: Rather, the choice has been abrogated, and if the People of the Covenant refer the matter to the ruler, he must rule between them with justice, and he does not have the right to neglect to consider them. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri: Then if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, was abrogated by His statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: It was abrogated by: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49). Ibn Wakee’ and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, they said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: It was abrogated by: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: Nothing was abrogated from Al-Ma’idah except these two verses: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, which was abrogated by: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5:49). And His statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month or the offerings or the garlands (al-Ma’idah 5:2), which was abrogated by: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It was abrogated by: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, meaning the Jews. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge between them, and gave him permission to turn away from them if he wished. Then God, the Most High, revealed the verse that follows it: And We have revealed to you the Book until His statement: So judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5:48). So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge between them by what God has revealed, after giving him permission, if he wished, to turn away from them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari: That Omar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Adi bin Adi: If the People of the Book come to you, then judge between them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: It was abrogated by His saying: Then judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:48). Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, regarding his statement: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, he said: The Sunnah has been established that they should return their rights and inheritances to the people of their religion, unless they come desiring a punishment, in which case they should be judged according to the Book of God. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: When the verse, Then judge between them or turn away from them, was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, could judge between them if he wished, and turn away from them if he wished. Then he abrogated it and said, Then judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5:48), and he was forced to judge between them. Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Two verses were abrogated from this surah, meaning al-Ma’idah, the verse of the necklaces, and His statement: Then judge between them or turn away from them. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a choice. If he wanted to judge, he could, and if he wanted to turn away from them, he would return them to their own arbitration, that he should judge between them according to what is in our Book. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: The ruling of this verse is established and has not been abrogated, and that the rulers have the option of ruling between the people of the covenant if they come to them and seek judgment, and leaving the ruling between them and the consideration, like what God made for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse. We said that this is the more correct of the two, because those who say that the ruling of this verse is abrogated claim that it was abrogated by His statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49). We have demonstrated in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings, that abrogation is not abrogation except in what is the negation of the ruling of another in all its meanings, so that it is not permissible for the ruling to be combined with both matters in its validity in any way, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And since that was the case, and it was not impossible in speech to say: And that you judge between them by what God has revealed, and its meaning is: And that you judge between them by what God has revealed if you judge between them by your choice to judge between them, if you chose that, and did not choose to turn away from them, since the one to whom that was said had been informed by its speaker: that he has the choice to judge and to leave the judgement, it was known from that that there is no indication in his saying: And that you judge between them by what God has revealed that it abrogates his saying: “So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice,” because of what we have described of the possibility of that as we have explained. Rather, it is evidence for something similar to what his saying indicated: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Since there is no evidence in the apparent revelation that one of the two verses abrogated the other, nor that one of the two matters negated the ruling of the other, and there was no report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that one of them abrogates the other, nor is there a consensus among the Muslims on that, then what we said is correct, that each of the two matters supports the other, and its ruling agrees with its ruling, and there is no abrogation in one of them of the other. As for his saying: And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all, its meaning is: If you, O Muhammad, turn away from those who seek judgment from the People of the Book, and you refrain from looking into what they have sought judgment from you about, and do not judge between them, they will not harm you at all, he says: They will not be able to harm you in religion or in this world, so refrain from looking into what they have chosen to do. As for his saying: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, its meaning is: If you choose to judge and consider, O Muhammad, between the people of the covenant when they come to you, then judge between them with justice, which is fairness, and that is the judgment that God has made a judgment in its likeness over all of His creation from the nation of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, a group of people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. They said: If you judge between them, judge according to what is in the Book of God. Sufyan told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibrahim: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, he said: He ordered that they be judged by stoning. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, regarding his statement: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, he said: By stoning. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With justice, with fairness. Hanad told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, regarding his statement: Then judge between them with justice, he said: He ordered that judgment be passed between them by stoning. As for his saying: God loves those who are just, its meaning is: God loves those who are just in their rulings among people, who judge between them according to the ruling of God that He revealed in His Book and commanded His prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them. It is said: The judge was just in his ruling, if he was fair and ruled justly, he was just. As for qast, its meaning is: injustice, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: But as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell (al-Jinn 72:15), meaning by that? those who deviate from the truth.
5:43: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means: How can these Jews, O Muhammad, make you judge among themselves, and be satisfied with you as a judge among them, while they have the Torah, which I sent down to Moses, which they acknowledge as true, and that it is My Book which I sent down to My Prophet, and that whatever ruling is in it is from My ruling, they know that and do not deny it or dispute it, and they know that My ruling in it for the married adulterer is stoning, and despite their knowledge of that, they turn away, meaning: they abandon ruling by it, after knowing My ruling in it, out of audacity towards Me and disobedience to Me. This, even though it was from God the Most High addressing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a rebuke from Him to the Jews about whom this verse was revealed. God the Most High says to them: How do you, O Jews, acknowledge the ruling of the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while you deny his prophethood and reject him, while you abandon My ruling which you acknowledge as a right and obligation upon you that Moses brought to you from God? He says: Since you abandon My ruling that Moses brought to you, whose prophethood you acknowledge in My Book, then you are more likely to abandon My ruling that My Prophet Muhammad tells you is My ruling, while you deny his prophethood. Then the Most High said, informing about the state of these Jews whose description He described in this verse, and the state of their counterparts who transgressed against His rule and deviated from the path of truth: And those are not believers. He says: The one who did this action - that is, the one who turned away from the rule of God, which He ruled in His Book which He revealed to His Prophet, regarding His creation - is not the one who believed in God and His Messenger and acknowledged His Oneness and the Prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - because that is not the action of the people of faith. The origin of turning away from something is turning away from it, as in: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer: Then they turn away after that, he said: Their turning away is what they left of the Book of God. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, to his client: And how can they judge you while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, meaning: the limits of God, so God informed us of His judgment in the Torah. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And with them is the Torah, in which is the judgment of God, meaning: God’s explanation of what they disputed about regarding their slain man, Then they turn away after that, the verse. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said, he said - meaning the Lord, may He be exalted - taunting them: And how can they judge you while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, he says: stoning.
5:44: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is an explanation of what these Jews asked you about regarding the ruling on married adulterers, and a light, meaning: in it is the clarification of what was dark for them, and the illumination of what was unclear regarding the ruling, by which the prophets who submitted to God will judge, meaning: in what they referred to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of adulterers, the prophets who submitted to God, and they are those who submitted to God’s ruling and acknowledged it. God Almighty meant by that our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his ruling on the married Jewish adulterers by stoning, and in his equalizing the blood of those killed by Nadir and Qurayzah in retaliation and blood money.
