And before Muhammad, the prophets ruled according to what is in it from God’s ruling, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light, and the prophets who submitted to God judged by it, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when this verse was revealed: We judge the Jews and those other than them from the people of religions. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said, a man from Muzaynah told us while we were with Saeed bin al-Musayyab, “on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: A Jewish man and a woman committed adultery, and some of them said to each other: Let us go to this prophet, for he is a prophet who was sent with leniency. If he issues a fatwa to us that is less than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God and say: The fatwa of one of your prophets! He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who committed adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools, and he stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He is to be stoned, flogged, and flogged. Flogging is that the two adulterers are carried on a donkey, their backs facing each other, and they are paraded around. A young man [among them] was silent, and when he saw him, he was silent. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O God, since You have asked us, we find stoning in the Torah!” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: “A man who was a relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so He delayed stoning him. Then a man committed adultery among the people, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: ‘Do not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him!’ So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Then I will rule according to what is in the Torah!’ So he ordered them to be stoned.” Al-Zuhri said: “They were informed that this verse was revealed about them: ‘Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it,’” and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was one of them. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: The prophets who submitted to Islam will judge by it, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the prophets before him, judge by what is in it of truth. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hussein, regarding his statement: The prophets who submitted to God will judge by it, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for those who were Jews, meaning the Jews, so judge between them and do not fear them. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And he rules by the Torah and its rulings that God revealed in it in every era - according to what Muhammad passed by in ruling in it - with the prophets to whom Muhammad submitted, the rabbis and the scholars. The rabbis are the plural of rabbi, and they are the wise scholars who are insightful in the politics of people, managing their affairs, and looking after their interests, and the scholars are the rabbis. We have explained the meaning of the rabbis in the past with evidence for this and the statements of the people of interpretation regarding it. As for al-Ahbar, they are the plural of Habr, which is the expert who knows something, and from this Ka’b was called: Ka’b al-Ahbar. Al-Farra’ used to say: I have heard the Arabs say ‘ahbar’ most often when referring to a scholar! “ahbar” with a kasra on the ha’. Some of the interpreters said: What is meant by the rabbis and scholars in this place are the two sons of Suriya who acknowledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the ruling of God Almighty mentioned in the Torah regarding the married adulterers. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: There were two Jewish men, brothers, called the sons of Suriya, who followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but did not submit to Islam. They gave him a covenant that he would not ask them about anything in the Torah unless they told him about it. One of them was a rabbi and the other a rabbi. They only followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to learn from him. So he called them and asked them, and they told him how it was when the noble man committed adultery and the poor man committed adultery, and how they changed it. So God revealed: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Islam] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the rabbis and the rabbis, they were the sons of Suriya, for those who were Jews. Then he mentioned the sons of Suriya and said: And the rabbis and the rabbis, because they were entrusted with the Book of God and were witnesses thereto. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God, the Most High, has informed us that the Torah is the law by which the Muslims of the prophets judge the Jews, and the rabbis from among His creation, and the rabbis. It is possible that he meant by that Ibn Suriya and others, but the Muslims of the prophets, and every rabbi and rabbi are included in the apparent meaning of the revelation, and there is no indication in the apparent meaning of the revelation that it is meant specifically from among the rabbis and rabbis, nor is there any proof that must be accepted. So every rabbi and rabbi is included in the verse by the apparent meaning of the revelation. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said in the interpretation of the rabbis. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: The rabbis and scholars are their readers and jurists. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The rabbis and scholars, the jurists and scholars. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The rabbis are the scholars and jurists, and they are above the rabbis. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The rabbis are the jurists of the Jews, and the scholars are their rabbis. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Yazid bin Dawud told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah: The rabbis and scholars, all of them rule according to what is in it of truth. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said, the rabbis are the governors, the rabbis are the scholars. As for his saying: With what they have been entrusted with of the Book of God, its meaning is: The prophets who converted to Islam rule according to the ruling of the Torah, and the rabbis and scholars - meaning the scholars - rule according to what they have been entrusted with knowledge of, such as the Book of God, which is the Torah. The letter Baa in his saying: because of what they have preserved, is related to the scholars. As for his saying: And they were witnesses over it, it means: that the rabbis and scholars, with what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, judge by the Torah with the prophets who submitted to those who were Jews, and they were witnesses over the judgment of the prophets who submitted to those who were Jews, that they judged them by the Book of God that He revealed to His Prophet Moses and His judgment over them, as: Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: And they were witnesses over him, meaning the rabbis and scholars. They are the witnesses for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding what he said, that it is the truth that came from God, and he is the Prophet of God, Muhammad. The Jews came to him, so he judged between them with justice. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to the Jewish scholars and rabbis: Do not fear people in implementing My judgment that I have ruled upon My servants, and in carrying it out upon them as I have commanded, for they are not able to harm or benefit you except with My permission. And do not conceal the stoning that I have made a judgment in the Torah upon married adulterers, but fear Me more than any of My creation, for benefit and harm are in My hand. And fear My punishment in concealing what you have been entrusted with of My Book, as: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: So do not fear the people, but fear Me, meaning: Do not fear the people and conceal what I have revealed. As for His statement: And do not exchange My verses for a small price, he says: And do not take, O rabbis, a small price for abandoning the ruling by the verses of My Book which I revealed to Moses, and that is the small price. Rather, the Most High intended to forbid them from eating ill-gotten gains because of their distortion of the Book of God, and their changing His ruling from what He ruled regarding married adulterers, and other rulings which they changed in order to obtain bribes, such as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And do not exchange My verses for a small price, he said: Do not consume what is ill-gotten based on My Book. And he said another time, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And do not exchange My verses for a small price, he said: Do not take a bribe with it. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not exchange My verses for a small price, and do not take a small amount of hope in order to conceal what I have revealed. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And whoever conceals the judgment of God which He revealed in His Book and made it a judgment between His servants, and conceals it and judges by other than it, like the judgment of the Jews regarding married adulterers by casting off the dead body and blackening it, and their concealment of stoning, and their ruling regarding some of their dead with full blood money and in others with half the blood money, and regarding the nobles with retaliation, and regarding the lowly with blood money, and God has made all of them equal in the ruling upon them in the Torah, they are the disbelievers, meaning: These are the ones who did not rule by what God revealed in His Book, but changed and altered His judgment, and concealed the truth which He revealed in His Book, and they are the disbelievers, meaning: They are the ones who concealed the truth which they were supposed to reveal and clarify, and covered it up from the people, and showed them something other than it, and ruled by it, based on ill-gotten gain which they took from them. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of disbelief in this place. Some of them said something similar to what we said about that, that he meant the Jews who distorted the Book of God and changed its ruling. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), regarding all of the disbelievers. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: The three verses in Al-Ma’idah, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “Then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), Then it is those who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), there is nothing of it for the people of Islam, it is for the disbelievers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. He said: These verses were revealed about the People of the Book. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated that al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated that he heard Imran ibn Hudayr say: Some people from Banu Amr ibn Sadus came to Abu Majlaz and said: O Abu Majlaz, do you think that God's statement, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers is true? He said: Yes! They said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45) is true? He said: Yes! They said: O Abu Majlaz, do these people judge by what God has revealed? He said: It is their religion that they follow, and it is what they say, and to which they call. If they abandon something of it, they will know that they have committed a sin! They said: No, by God, but you are different! He said: You are more deserving of this than I! I do not see it, and you see it and do not feel embarrassed, but it was revealed about the Jews, Christians, and polytheists, or something like that. Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, who said: A group of Ibadis sat with Abu Majlaz and said to him: God says: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. “And it is those who are the wrongdoers.” (al-Ma’idah 5:45) And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient. (al-Ma’idah 5:47) Abu Majlaz said: They do what they do - meaning the rulers - and they know that it is a sin! He said: This verse was revealed about the Jews and Christians. They said: By God, you know what we know, but you fear them. He said: You are more deserving of that than we are! As for us, we do not know what you know! They said: But you know it, but fear of them prevents you from carrying out your affairs! Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Hudhayfah, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: What good brothers you have are the Children of Israel, if you have everything sweet and they have everything bitter!! And you will follow their path, the path of the traps. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. He said: These verses were revealed about the People of the Book. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said: It was said to Hudhayfah: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then it is they who are the disbelievers. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi Al-Bukhtari, he said: A man asked Hudhayfah about these verses: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “Then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), Then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). He was asked: Is that about the Children of Israel? He said: What good brothers are you, the Children of Israel, if they have every bitterness and you have every sweetness! No, by God, you will follow their path, the path of the trap. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: These verses are about the People of the Book. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He mentioned to us that these verses were revealed regarding the murder of the Jews who was one of them. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, and the wrongdoers, and the wicked, for all the People of the Book, because of what they abandoned of the Book of God. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: “A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been slapped passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he called them and said: ‘Is this how you find the punishment for adultery?’ They said: ‘Yes!’ So he called one of their scholars and said: ‘I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book?’ He said: ‘No, and had you not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find its punishment in our book as stoning, but it has become widespread among our nobles, so if we seized a noble person, we would leave him, and if we seized a lowly person, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: ‘Come, let us all gather together to flog and slap instead of stoning.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, I am the first to revive Your command when they killed it!’ So he ordered him to be stoned.” Then God revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the disbelievers. That is, The Jews: Then it is they who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45) meaning the Jews: Then it is they who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), for all the infidels. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: Whoever rules by his book that he wrote with his own hand, and abandons the Book of God, and claims that this book of his is from God, then he has disbelieved. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to the hadith of Al-Qasim on the authority of Al-Hasan, except that Hannad said in his hadith: So we said: Come, let us agree on something that we will implement on the noble and the weak, so we agreed on the blackening and flogging instead of stoning. And the rest of the hadith is similar to the hadith of Al-Qasim. Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad narrated to us, on the authority of his father, he said: We were with Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud, and a man mentioned in his presence: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the disbelievers, “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the wrongdoers,” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). Ubaidullah said: By God, many people interpret these verses in a way that they were not revealed to, and they were only revealed about two tribes of Jews. Then he said: They are Qurayzah and An-Nadir, and that is because one of the two groups had invaded the other and subdued it before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, until they agreed and agreed that for every person killed by a powerful woman from a humiliated tribe, the ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every person killed by a humiliated woman from a powerful woman, the ransom would be one hundred wasqs. So they gave them a difference and a loss. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came while they were in that state, and the two groups were humiliated by the arrival of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not prevail over them. While they were in that state, the humiliated one killed a man from the honorable one. The honorable one said: Give us a hundred wasqs! The humiliated one said: Has this ever happened in two tribes whose religion is one and whose country is one, and the blood money of some of them is double that of others? We gave you this only to separate you from us and to make Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) between us and you. So they agreed to make the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) between them. Then the honorable one discussed matters among themselves. She feared that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not give her from her companions double what she gave to her companions from it. So they sent their brothers from the hypocrites to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said to them: Tell us the opinion of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If he gives us what we want, we will rule on it, but if he does not give us, we will warn him and not rule on it! The hypocrite went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they wanted from all of that matter. Ubaidullah said: Then God Almighty revealed about them: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, all of these verses, until he reached: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein, to the wicked. Ubaidullah read that verse by verse, and explained it according to what was revealed, until he finished explaining that to them in the verses. Then he said: What I meant by that was the Jews, and this description was revealed about them. Some of them said: In the case of the infidels, the Muslims, and in the case of the oppressors, the Jews, and in the case of the immoral, the Christians. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, he said: The disbelievers were revealed regarding the Muslims, the wrongdoers regarding the Jews, and the wicked regarding the Christians. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Safar, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: The unbelievers refer to the Muslims, the oppressors refer to the Jews, and the wicked refer to the Christians. Ibn Wakee’, Abu Al-Sa’ib, and Wasil bin Abd Al-A’la told us, they said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ibn Shabrama, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: A verse concerning us, and two verses concerning the People of the Book: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, concerning us, and concerning them: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, (al-Ma’idah 5:45), and the wicked, concerning the People of the Book. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, like the hadith of Zakariya on his authority. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Safar, on the authority of al-Sha`bi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: This is regarding the Muslims. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked. (al-Ma`idah: 45) He said: The Christians. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said, regarding these verses in al-Ma’idah 5:And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said regarding us the people of Islam, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, (al-Ma’idah 5:45), he said, regarding the Jews, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked, (al-Ma’idah 5:47), he said regarding the Christians. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zakariya bin Abi Zaida, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: The first was revealed regarding the Muslims, the second regarding the Jews, and the third regarding the Christians. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, something similar. Hanad told us, he said, Ya’la told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, something similar. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: disbelief less than disbelief, injustice less than injustice, and immorality less than immorality. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47), he said: Disbelief less than disbelief, disobedience less than disobedience, and injustice less than injustice. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ata’, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Tamima, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, something similar. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, something similar. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed Al-Makki, on the authority of Tawus: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is disbelief in it, but it is not disbelief in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Hasan told me, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said: A man said to Ibn Abbas regarding these verses: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, so whoever does this has disbelieved? Ibn Abbas said: If he does that, then he has disbelieved, but he is not like someone who disbelieves in God and the Last Day, and so on and so forth. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is disbelief in it. Ibn Tawus said: It is not like the one who disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Tawus: Then those are the disbelievers, he said: Disbelief that does not remove one from the religion. He said: And Ata’ said: Disbelief less than disbelief, injustice less than injustice, and immorality less than immorality. Others said: Rather, these verses were revealed about the People of the Book, and they are intended for all people, Muslims and infidels alike. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: These verses were revealed about the Children of Israel, and He was pleased with them for this nation. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It was revealed about the Children of Israel, and He was pleased with it for you. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: It was revealed about the Children of Israel, then He was pleased with it for these people. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: It was revealed about the Jews, and it is obligatory upon us. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Alqamah and Masruq: That they asked Ibn Masoud about bribery, and he said: It is from ill-gotten gains. He said: They said: Is it in the ruling? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, he says: And whoever does not rule by what I have revealed, and abandons it intentionally and transgresses while he knows, then he is among the disbelievers. Others said: The meaning of this is: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, denying it. As for injustice and immorality, it is for the one who acknowledges it. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, he said: Whoever denies what God has revealed has disbelieved. And whoever acknowledges it but does not judge, then he is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements, in my opinion, is the statement of those who said: These verses were revealed about the infidels of the People of the Book, because the verses before and after them were revealed about them, and they are the ones meant by them. And these verses are in the context of the report about them, so it is more appropriate for them to be a report about them. If someone says: God Almighty mentioned this in the report about all those who do not rule by what God has revealed, so how did you make it specific? It was said: God Almighty made the report general about a people who denied the ruling of God that He ruled in His Book, so He informed about them that by abandoning the ruling, in the way that they abandoned it, they were disbelievers. And the same is said about everyone who did not rule by what God revealed, denying it, he is a disbeliever in God, as Ibn Abbas said, because by his denial of the ruling of God after knowing that He revealed it in His Book, it is similar to his denial of the prophethood of his prophet after knowing that he was a prophet.
5:45: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And We wrote for these Jews who rule you, O Muhammad, and they have the Torah in which is the rule of God. And what he means by his saying: And We have written, and imposed on them in it that they should judge in the case of a soul if a soul is killed, unjustly, for a soul, meaning: that the soul that kills should be killed for the soul that was killed, and an eye for an eye, meaning: And We imposed on them in it that they should put out the eye that its owner put out, like it from another soul for the gouged out eye - and the nose should be cut off for the nose - and the ear should be cut off for the ear - and the tooth should be pulled out for the tooth - and the one who wounded another should take revenge unjustly for the one who was wounded. This is a message from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Jews, and a consolation from Him to him for the disbelief of those among them who disbelieved in Him after acknowledging His prophethood, and their turning away from Him after His acceptance, and an acknowledgment from Him of their audacity, both in the past and in the present, towards their Lord and the messengers of their Lord, and their precedence over the Book of God through distortion and alteration. God the Almighty says to him: How can these Jews, O Muhammad, be satisfied with your judgment, when they come to judge you and they have the Torah, which they acknowledge as My Book and My revelation to My Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, in which is My judgment of stoning married adulterers, and My ruling between them that whoever kills a soul unjustly shall be subject to retaliation for it, and whoever puts out an eye unjustly shall have his eye put out for it as retaliation, and whoever cuts off a nose shall have his nose cut off for it, and whoever pulls out a tooth shall have his tooth pulled for it, and whoever injures another shall be subject to retaliation like the wound he inflicted? Then, with the judgment that they have in the Torah from My judgments, they turn away from it and abandon working by it. He says: They are more deserving and more worthy of abandoning Your judgment and displeasing Your judgment between them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: When Qurayzah saw that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ruled with stoning, and they had been hiding it in their letter, Qurayzah rose up and said: O Muhammad, judge between us and our brothers Banu Nadir. There had been bloodshed between them before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Nadir had been arrogant towards Banu Qurayzah, and their blood money was half that of Nadir. The blood money was from the market of dates: one hundred and forty wasqs for Banu Nadir, and seventy wasqs for Banu Qurayzah. So he said: The blood of the Qurayzi is repayment of the blood of the Nadir! Banu Nadir became angry and said: We will not obey you in the matter of stoning, but we will abide by our own limits which we were following! Then the verse was revealed: Do they then seek the judgment of the times of ignorance? (al-Ma’idah 5:50), and the verse was revealed: “And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life,” (al-Ma’idah 5:5) Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And We ordained for them therein: A life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds there is retaliation.” He said: So why do they disobey, killing two lives for a life, and gouging out two eyes for an eye? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Khallad Al-Kufi told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: There was fighting between two tribes of the Ansar, and there were deaths among them, and one of the tribes had a long way to go against the other, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and began to treat the free man with the free man, the slave with the slave, and the woman with the woman, so the verse was revealed: The free man for the free man, and the slave for the slave (Al-Baqarah 2:78). Sufyan said: It was reported to me on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It was abrogated by A life for a life. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And We ordained for them therein that a life for a life, in the Torah - and an eye for an eye, until: and for wounds, retaliation, Mujahid said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Children of Israel were required to retaliate for those killed, there was no blood money among them for a life or a wound. He said: And that is the statement of God Almighty: And We ordained for them therein, in the Torah, so God made it easier for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and made blood money for a life and wounds upon them, and that is a relief and mercy from your Lord, but whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds there is retaliation,” he said: The Children of Israel were not given blood money in what God wrote for Moses in the Torah for a life killed, or a wound, or a tooth, or an eye, or a nose. Rather, it is retaliation, or forgiveness. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We ordained for them therein, meaning in the Torah, that a life is for a life. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And We prescribed for them therein, meaning in the Torah, that a life is for a life. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life, until he reached and for wounds there is retaliation, some for some. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: A life for a life, he said, he means: A life is killed for a life, an eye is gouged out for an eye, a nose is cut off for a nose, a tooth is pulled out for a tooth, and wounds are exacted for wounds. Abu Jaafar said: This applies equally to free Muslims, men and women, if it is in the soul or less than the soul, and equally to slaves, men and women, if it is deliberate in the soul or less than the soul. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of it: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. Some of them said: He meant the wounded and the guardian of the murdered. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of al-Haitham bin al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It removes from him - meaning the wounded person - a similar amount of his sins. Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Al-Haitham bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, something similar. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, on the authority of al-Haytham ibn al-Aswad Abu al-`Aryan, he said: I saw Mu`awiyah sitting on the bed, and next to him was a red man who looked like a freedman - and he was `Abdullah ibn `Amr. So he said regarding this verse: But whoever gives it in charity, it will be an expiation for him, he said: It will wipe out from him the same amount of his sins as he gave in charity. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: for the one who was wounded. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amara bin Abi Hafsa, on the authority of Abu Uqbah, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid: Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. He said: For the wounded. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Harmi bin Amara told me, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Amara told me, on the authority of a man - Harmi said: I forgot his name - on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim: Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. He said: For the wounded. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida narrated, Ibn Fadil narrated, on the authority of Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, who said: A man from Quraysh pushed a man from the Ansar and his front tooth broke. The Ansari took him to Muawiyah. When the man insisted, Muawiyah said: What is it to you and your friend? He said: And Abu al-Darda was with Muawiyah, so Abu al-Darda said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who is afflicted with something in his body and gives it away, except that God will raise him a degree because of it, and remove a sin from him because of it. The Ansari said to him: Did you hear that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: My ears heard it and my heart remembered it! So he let the Quraysh man go. Muawiyah said: Order some money for him. Mahmoud bin Khidash told us, Hisham bin Bashir told us, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said, Ibn Al-Samit said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever is wounded in his body and gives it in charity, his sins will be expiated by the same amount he gave in charity.” Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Hussein, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It is an expiation for the one who was wounded. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, he said: I heard Amer say: It is an expiation for the one who gives charity. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: But whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, meaning: for the guardian of the murdered person who pardoned. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Shabib bin Saeed told me, on the authority of Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Haitham Abu Al-Aryan, he said: I was in Ash-Sham, and there was a man with Mu’awiyah sitting on the bed, as if he were a freed slave. He said: Whoever gives it in charity, it will be an expiation for him. He said: So whoever gives it in charity, God will remove from him an equivalent amount of his sins. And he was Abdullah bin Amr. Others said: He meant by that the one who injures. They said: The meaning of the verse: Whoever gives charity of what is due to him of retaliation or retribution to the one who is due to him, and he pardons him, then his pardon of the offender is an expiation for the sin of the criminal offender, just as the retribution from him is an expiation for it. They said: As for the reward of the one who pardons and gives charity, it is upon God. Who said that? Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. He said: It is an expiation for the one who wounded him, and the reward of the one who was wounded is with God. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Mujahid say to Abu Ishaq: Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. O Abu Ishaq, for whom? Abu Ishaq said: For the one who gives charity. Mujahid said: For the sinner who injures others. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah said, Mujahid said: for the one who wounds. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Hannad and Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. They said: For the one to whom he gave it in charity, and the reward for the one who was afflicted is with God. Hannad said in his hadith, they said: It is an expiation for the one to whom he gave it in charity. Hanad told us, he said, Abd bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Wakaba’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, he said: It is an expiation for the one who gave it in charity. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, they said: It is an expiation for the one who injures, and the reward of the one who was injured is from God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: I heard Zaid bin Aslam say: If he pardons him, or takes revenge from him, or accepts blood money from him, then it is an expiation for him. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It is an expiation for the one who hurts, and a reward for the one who pardons, because of His statement: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is due from God (al-Shura 42:40). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It is an expiation for the one to whom the charity was given. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It is an expiation for the one who hurt him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. He said: So the expiation is for the one who hurts, and the reward of the one who gives in charity is from God. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, that he used to say: Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, meaning: for the killer, and a reward for the one who pardons. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Imran bin Dhibyan told us, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, he said: “A man was orphaned during the time of Muawiyah, so he was given blood money but it was not accepted, then he was given two blood moneys but it was not accepted, then he was given three but it was not accepted. Then a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives in charity the blood of a person or less, it will be an expiation for him from the day he gave in charity until the day he was born.’” He said: So the man gave in charity. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: Wounds are subject to retaliation, but whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, meaning: Whoever wounds and gives in charity what he wounded to the one who wounded him, then there is no way, no retaliation, no blood money, and no blame upon the one who wounded him, because the one who wounded him gave him in charity, so it was an expiation for the injustice he did to him. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is that of the one who said: He meant by his statement: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, the one who is criticized. So the ha’ in his statement: for him should refer to whoever, which is more appropriate than it being from the mention of whomever was not mentioned except in meaning without explicitness, and more appropriate, since charity is what expiates the sin of its giver, not the one to whom charity is given, in all other charities other than this. So the way of this should be the way of other charities. If someone thinks that retaliation, since it expiates the sin of its companion who was being retaliated against, which he committed in killing the one he killed unjustly, according to the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he took the pledge from his companions: Do not kill, do not commit adultery, and do not steal, then he said: Whoever does any of these things and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him, it is his expiation, then it is obligatory that the forgiveness of the one who forgives the wronged person, or the guardian of the one who was killed, be similar to that in that it is an expiation for him. If that were to be the case, then it would be obligatory that the forgiveness of the one who was slandered for adultery, and his leaving him to take what is due to him of the prescribed punishment, since his slanderer slandered him while he was a chaste, Muslim, married man, would be an expiation for the slanderer for the sin he committed and the disobedience he committed. And that is something that we do not know of any scholar who says. Since it is not permissible for the slandered person - whose case we have described - to leave his slanderer to take what is due to him from the prescribed punishment, as expiation for the slanderer for the sin he committed, it is also not permissible for the wounded person to leave the injurer to take his right to retaliation, as expiation for the injurer for the sin he committed. If someone says: Doesn’t the injured person have the right, in your opinion, to receive blood money for his injury instead of retaliation? He was told: Yes! If he said: What if he chose blood money and then forgave it, would he be held accountable for it in the afterlife? It was said to him: This is an impossible statement in our view. That is because in our view no one can choose blood money unless he takes it. As for forgiveness, it is forgiveness of blood money, and we have demonstrated the validity of that in a place other than this, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place, unless what is meant by that is giving it to the one from whom it was taken after taking it. Although his forgiveness of the blood money after choosing it, if it were valid, there is nothing in the validity of that that necessitates that the one who is forgiven is innocent of the punishment of his sin before God, because God, the Most High, mentioned Him, threatened the killer of the believer with what He threatened him with if he did not repent of his sin, and the blood money is taken from him, whether he liked it or not. And the repentance of the repentant is only repentance if he chose it and wanted it and preferred it over persistence. If someone thinks that this is the case, then he must make expiation for it, just as retaliation was an expiation for him. We only made retaliation an expiation for him - with his remorse and his sacrifice of himself to take the right from her - to evade his sin, based on the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for blood money, if the injured person chooses it and then forgives it, and the punishment for his sin is not imposed on him, then he is among those who fall under the ruling of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his saying: Whoever has the punishment carried out on him, it is his expiation. Then what confirms the correctness of what we have said in this regard is the hadiths that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying: Whoever gives charity in blood, and similar hadiths that we mentioned before. It may be possible that those who said that he meant the one who wounded him meant the meaning mentioned by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who: Al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Salam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, saying: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: If a man strikes another man, and the one who was struck does not know who he struck, and the one who struck him confesses to him, then it is expiation for the one who struck him. He said: Mujahid used to say at this time: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr struck a man in the eye at the corner while they were touching it, so he said to him: O man, I am Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, so if there is something wrong with your eye, then I am the one who is harming it! If the matter was from the one who hurt him, such as what happened with Urwah, from a mistake he did unintentionally, and then he confessed to the one who hurt him what he hurt, and the one who was hurt by that forgave him for his right against him, then he has no responsibility towards the one who hurt him in this world or in the hereafter. Because what was due to him before him was money, not retaliation, and he acquitted him of it. So acquitting him of it is an expiation for the one who was acquitted of his right that he had to take it from him, so he has no claim against him because of that in this world or in the hereafter, and no punishment is required of him for what he did to the one who hurt him, because he did not intentionally hurt him with what he hurt him with, so his action is a sin for which he deserves punishment from his Lord, because God the Almighty has placed the blame on His servants for what they did wrong and did not do intentionally, as He said in His Book: And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only] for what your hearts intended (al-Ahzab 33:15). And giving charity, in this case, with blood, is forgiveness for it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And whoever does not rule according to what God has revealed in the Torah regarding the retaliation for a murderous soul, as retaliation for a soul killed unjustly, and does not put out the eye of the one who put out the eye with the eye of the one who was put out unjustly, as retaliation for what God has commanded him to do in His Book, but takes retaliation from some and does not take retaliation from others, or kills two people for one in some cases, then whoever does that is among the wrongdoers, meaning: among those who have deviated from the judgment of God, and places what he did of that in a place other than the place that God has made for it.
5:46: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: And We followed in their footsteps, that is, We followed. He says: We followed Jesus, son of Mary, in the footsteps of the prophets who submitted to Islam! Before you, O Muhammad, We sent him as a prophet confirming Our Book which We revealed to Moses, who died before him, that it is true, and that working with what the Gospel did not abrogate from it is an obligatory duty. And We gave him the Gospel, meaning: And We revealed to him Our Book called the Gospel, “in which is guidance and light,” meaning: In the Gospel guidance, which is an explanation of what the people were ignorant of of the ruling of God in his time, and light, meaning: And a radiance from the blindness of ignorance, and confirming what was before it, meaning: We revealed that to him and revealed it to him confirming what had come before it of the books of God which He had revealed to every nation, a book was revealed to its prophet to work with what was revealed to their prophet in that book, of making permissible what He made permissible, and prohibiting what He prohibited, and guidance and admonition, meaning: We revealed the Gospel to Jesus confirming the books that came before it, and an explanation of the ruling of God which He was pleased with for His righteous servants in the time of Jesus, and an admonition for them, meaning: And to deter them from doing what God hates and to doing what He loves, and to alert them to it. The righteous are those who fear God and are wary of His punishment. They fear Him by obeying what He commands them to do, and they are wary of Him by refraining from what He forbids them to do. The explanation of this with its evidence has already been given, so there is no need to repeat it.
5:47: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And let the People of the Gospel judge. The people of Hijaz, Basra and some of the Kufians read it as: Wa li-Hakam with a sukoon on the lam, as a command from God to the people of the Gospel: to judge by what God has revealed in it of His rulings. And whoever read it like that meant: And We gave him the Gospel, in it was guidance and light and confirming what was before it of the Torah, and We commanded its people to judge by what God has revealed in it, so there is something omitted in the speech, leaving out what was mentioned instead of what was omitted. A group of people from Kufa read it: And let the people of the Gospel judge with a kasra on the lam, from li-yahkam, meaning: so that the people of the Gospel judge. It seems that the meaning of those who read it like this is: And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming what was before it of the Torah, so that he might judge his people by what was in it of God’s judgment. What we say about this is that they are two famous readings with similar meanings, so whichever one a reader reads, he is correct. This is because God Almighty did not send down a book to any of His prophets except that its people, who were commanded to act upon it, would act upon it. He did not send it down to them except that He commanded them to act upon it. So He sent it down to act upon it, and He sent it down as a command to act upon it. Likewise, the Gospel, since it was one of the books of God that He sent down to His prophets, He sent it down to Jesus to act upon it, and He sent it down to him as a command to act upon it. So whether it is read as a command with the lam sukoon, or as a report with the lam kasra, their meanings are the same. As for what was mentioned about Abi bin Kaab, that he read it and that he should judge in the manner of a command, this is something that was not transmitted from him authentically. Even if it was authentic, there would not be anything in that that would require reading it in a different manner to be prohibited, since its meaning was correct, and the earlier imams of recitation had read it in this manner. And since the matter in that is as we have explained, then the interpretation of the statement, if it is read with a kasra on the lam of li-yahkam: And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirmation of what was before it of the Torah and guidance and instruction for the righteous, and in order that the People of the Gospel might judge by what We revealed in it, but they changed its judgment and opposed it, so they went astray by their opposition to it since they did not judge by what God revealed in it and opposed it, Then those are the wicked, meaning: those who went outside the command of God in it, opposing Him in what He commanded them and forbade them in His Book. If it is read with a sukoon on the lam, then its interpretation is: And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirmation of what was before him of the deviants. And We commanded his people to judge by what We revealed therein, but they did not obey Us in Our command to them with what We commanded them with therein, but they disobeyed Our command. So those who disobeyed Our command that We commanded them with therein are the wicked. Ibn Zayd used to say: The wicked ones, in this place and elsewhere, are the liars. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, "And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient," he said: And whoever among the People of the Gospel does not judge by that also, then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient, he said: The liars. This is what he said. Ibn Zayd said: Everything in the Qur'an except a little fasiq is a liar. And he recited the statement of God, O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information (al-Hujurat 49:6), he said: Here, a liar. We have explained the meaning of immorality with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
5:48: Abu Ja'far said: This is an address from God, the Most High, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God, the Most High, says: We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book, which is the Qur'an that He sent down to him. By His statement, in truth, He means with truth and no falsehood in it, and there is no doubt that it is from God. Confirming what came before it of the Scripture, meaning: We sent it down confirming what came before it of the Scriptures of God that He sent down to His prophets. And as a guardian over it, meaning: We sent down the Book that We sent down to you, O Muhammad, confirming the Scriptures that came before it, and as a witness over them that they are the truth from God, trustworthy over them and a guardian over them. The root of dominance is preservation and anticipation. It is said, if a man observes something, preserves it and witnesses it: So-and-so has dominated it, so he dominates it, and he is dominant over it. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about it, except that their expressions about it differed. Some of them said: It means: a martyr. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And a witness over him, he said: a witness. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And a witness over him, he said: a witness over him. Bishr bin Muadh told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Scripture, he says: the books that came before it, and a guardian over it, trustworthy and a witness over the books that came before it. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And a guardian over it, is a trustee of the Qur’an, a witness and a verifier. Ibn Jurayj said: And others said: The Qur’an is a trustee of the books in that if the People of the Book inform us of something in their book, if it is in the Qur’an then they are truthful, otherwise they are liars. Some of them said: It means: He is trustworthy. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, and Hannad bin al-Sarri told us, he said: Waki’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a guardian over it, he said: a trustee over it. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And a guardian over it, he said: A trustee over it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan and Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on his chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Tamim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And a guardian over it, he said: And the guardian is the trustworthy. He said: The Qur’an is trustworthy over every book before it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Scripture, which is the Qur’an, a witness to the Torah and the Gospel, confirming them, and a guardian over it, meaning: trustworthy over it, ruling over what came before it of the Scriptures. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a guardian over it, he said: a trustee over it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a guardian over him, he said: A trustee over him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yahya Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Israel, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: And a guardian over it, he said: A trustee over what came before it of the books. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I asked Al-Husayn about His statement: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. He said: Confirming these books and being trustworthy over them. And Ikrimah was asked about it while I was listening, and he said: Being trustworthy over it. Others said: The meaning of the dominant is the one who confirms. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: And a guardian over it, he said: Confirming it. Everything that God sent down of the Torah, the Gospel, or the Psalms, the Qur’an confirms that. And everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an, it confirms it and what it narrated about it that it is true. Others said: What he meant by his saying, Confirming what came before it of the Book and a guardian over it, is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And our guardian over it, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is entrusted with the Qur’an. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And a guardian over it, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is entrusted with the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement is as Mujahid interpreted it: And We sent down the Book, confirming the books before it to you, as a guardian over them. So his statement, confirming, is a state of the Book and some of it, and confirmation is an attribute of the Book, and the guardian is a state of the kaf in to you, which is a metaphor for mentioning the name of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the ha’ in his statement, upon him, refers back to the Book. This interpretation is far from the concept in the speech of the Arabs, rather it is wrong. That is because al-Muhaymin is in apposition to al-Musaddiq, so it can only be from a description of what al-Musaddiq is a description of. If the meaning of the speech was what was narrated from Mujahid, it would have been said: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Scripture and as a guardian over it, because nothing preceded the description of kaf in ilaik after it that would be a guardian over it, in apposition to it, but rather it was in apposition to al-Musaddiq, because it is from a description of the Book of which al-Musaddiq is a description. If someone thinks that the confirmer - according to Mujahid’s statement and his interpretation of this - is from the attribute of the kaf in to you, then his statement: for what was before him of the Book, invalidates that interpretation of that is like that, and that the confirmer is from the attribute of the kaf in to you. Because the ha in his statement: before him is a metaphor for a name other than the one being addressed, which is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his statement: to you. If the confirmer was from the attribute of the kaf, then the statement would be: And We have sent down to you the Book confirming what was before you of the Book, and a guardian over it, so the meaning of the statement would then be like that. Abu Jaafar said: This is a command from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge between those who seek his judgment from among the People of the Book and all other religions with His Book that He revealed to him, which is the Qur’an, which He singled out for His law. God Almighty says: Judge, O Muhammad, between the People of the Book and the polytheists by what I have revealed to you of My Book and My rulings in all that they refer to you for judgment in, from the prescribed punishments, wounds, retaliation, and lives. So stone the married adulterer, and kill the murderer for the murdered unjustly, and put out an eye for an eye, and cut off a nose for a nose, for I have revealed to you the Qur’an confirming in that what came before it of the Books, and as a watchful guardian over it, judging what came before it of all the other Books before it. And do not follow the whims of these Jews, who say: If you are given flogging for the married adulterer without stoning, and killing the lowly for the noble if he kills him, and leaving the killing of the noble for the lowly if he kills him, then take it, and if you are not given it then beware of what has come to you from God of the truth, which is the Book of God that He has revealed to you. He says to him: Work according to My Book that I revealed to you if they refer you to judgment and you choose to rule according to it, and do not abandon working according to it in order to follow their whims and prefer them over the truth that I revealed to you in My Book, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So judge between them by what God has revealed, he said: by the limits of God, and do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq: That the Jew and the Christian would swear by God, then he would read: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49), and God revealed: That you do not associate anything with Him (al-An’am 6:51). Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: For every people among you We have appointed a law. And the law is the Shari`ah itself. The plural of the law is a law, and the Shari`ah is laws. If the law were to be pluralized as laws, it would be correct, because its meaning and the meaning of the Shari`ah are one, so when pluralized, it returns it to the word of its counterpart. And everything that it legislated for is the law. And from that, the law of water was called the law, because it is legislated from it to the water. And from that, the laws of Islam were called the laws, because its people embarked on it. And from that, it was said of people if they are equal in something: They are a law, equal. As for the method, its origin is: the clear and obvious path. It is said of it: It is a clear path and method, as the rajaz poet said: Whoever has doubts, this is a clear water canal and a straight path. Then it is used in everything that is clear, obvious and easy. The meaning of the words is: For every people among you, We have made a path to the truth to follow, and a clear way to act upon. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his saying: For each of you We appointed. Some of them said: He meant by that the people of different religions, meaning: God made for each religion a law and a method. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method, meaning: a path and a way. And the ways are different: the Torah has a law, the Gospel has a law, and the Qur’an has a law. In them God permits what He wills and forbids what He wills as a test, to know who obeys Him from who disobeys Him. But the one religion that does not accept any other is monotheism and sincerity to God, which was brought by the messengers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method, he said: The religion is one, and the law is different. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, he said: Faith since God Almighty sent Adam, peace be upon him, is: the testimony that there is no god but God, and the acknowledgment of what came from God, for every people what came to them of law or method, so the one who acknowledges is not the one who abandons, but rather he is the one who obeys. Others said: Rather, he meant by that the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: The meaning of the statement is: We have made the Book that We revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, O people, for all of you - meaning for all who entered Islam and acknowledged Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as My Prophet - a law and a way. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method, he said: A Sunnah, and a method, the path, for each of you, whoever enters the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, God has prescribed for him a law and a method. He says: The Qur’an, it is a law and a method for him. Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: For every people of a religion among you, O nations, We have made a law and a method.
