Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary, meaning: They were cursed in the Gospel by the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, and they were cursed in the Psalms by the tongue of David. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. He said: They mixed with them after the prohibition in their trade, so God struck the hearts of some of them with others, so they are cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hiseen, on the authority of Mujahid: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. He said: They were cursed by the tongue of David and became monkeys, and they were cursed by the tongue of Jesus and became pigs. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said, his statement: Cursed are those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel, is by every language they were cursed in: during the time of Moses in the Torah, during the time of David in the Psalms, during the time of Jesus in the Gospel, and they were cursed by the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Qur’an. Ibn Jurayj said: Others said: Cursed are those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David, during his time, so they were cursed by his call. He said: David passed by a group of them while they were in a house and said: Who is in the house? They said: Pigs. He said: O God, make them pigs!, so they were pigs. He said: Then his curse befell them. And Jesus called down a curse upon them and said: O God, curse those who slandered me and my mother, and make them despised apes! Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel the verse, God cursed them on the tongue of David in his time, so He made them despised apes, and in the Gospel on the tongue of Jesus, so He made them pigs. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said, Abu Muhsin Husayn bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Husayn - meaning: Ibn Abd al-Rahman - on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed on the tongue of David, he said: They were transformed into monkeys on the tongue of David, and into pigs on the tongue of Jesus. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, the same. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a man from the Children of Israel saw his brother committing a sin, he would forbid him from doing so as an excuse. But the next day, what he saw of him did not prevent him from being his eater, his companion, or his drinker. When he saw that from them, he struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of their prophet David and Jesus, son of Mary, ‘That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.’ He said: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer and force him to adhere to the truth, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against others, and curse you as He cursed them.’” Ibn Humayd narrated, Al-Hakam bin Bashir bin Salman narrated, Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i narrated, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When evil spread among the Children of Israel, a man would meet another man and say: O man, fear God! But that would not prevent him from eating and drinking with him. When God saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, then He sent down a book about them: “Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors. They used not to forbid one another from the evil they were doing. Evil indeed was that which they were doing.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up and said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, until they forced the oppressor to adhere to the truth. Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, al-Mu’ammil bin Ismail told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Ali bin Badhima told us, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, I think on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When evil became apparent among the Children of Israel, a man would see his brother, neighbor, or companion committing evil, and he would forbid him, but that would not prevent him from being his eater, drinker, or companion. So God struck the hearts of some of them against others, and they were cursed on the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary, ‘That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors,’ to ‘disobedient.’ Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up straight, and became angry and said: No, by God, not until you seize the hand of the oppressor and force him to do what is right.” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Children of Israel were deficient, a man would see his brother in doubt and forbid him from it. But the next day, what he saw of him did not prevent him from being his eater, drinker, and companion. So God set the hearts of some of them against others, and the Qur’an was revealed about them, saying: ‘Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary,’ until it reached ‘but many of them are wicked.’ He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up and said: ‘No, not until you seize the hand of the oppressor and force him to follow the truth.’” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us - he said: He dictated it to me - he said, Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, he said: I heard Abu Ubaidah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar, except that they said in their hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up straight, then he said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, until you seize the hand of the oppressor and force him to adhere to the truth. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary, he said, he said: They were cursed in the Gospel and in the Psalms, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mill of faith has turned, so turn with the Qur’an wherever it turns [for... God has completed what He has enjoined in it]. [And Ibn Marah] was a nation from the Children of Israel, they were people of justice, they enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong, so their people seized them and sawed them with saws, and crucified them on wood, and a remnant of them remained, but they were not satisfied until they entered the kings and sat with them, then they were not satisfied until they ate with them, so God struck those hearts with each other and made them one. So that is the statement of God the Most High: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David to: That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing, what was their disobedience? He said: “They did not forbid one another from the evil they did. Evil was what they were doing.” So the interpretation of the words is: God cursed those who disbelieved - from the Jews - in God on the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary, and God cursed their fathers on the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary, because they disobeyed God and went against His command, and they were transgressors, meaning: and they were exceeding His limits.
5:79: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: These Jews whom God cursed, did not forbid one another, meaning: they did not forbid the evil they did, nor did they forbid one another. And by evil he means the sins with which they disobeyed God. The interpretation of the statement is: They did not desist from the evil they committed, How evil was what they were doing. This is an oath from God Almighty, saying: I swear: How evil was the deed they were doing, in their failure to desist from the sins of God Almighty, and committing His prohibitions, and killing God’s prophets and messengers, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: They did not forbid one another from the evil they did, their souls did not forbid one another after they fell into disbelief.
5:80: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: You see, O Muhammad, many of the Children of Israel, taking as allies those who disbelieve, meaning: taking as allies the polytheists who worship idols, and opposing the friends of God and His Messengers. How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them, God Almighty says: I swear: How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them before their return in the Hereafter, that the wrath of God be upon them, meaning: their souls have put forward for them the wrath of God upon them for what they have done. And that in his saying: that God’s wrath is upon them is in the nominative case, as a translation of what in his saying: what is evil. “And in the punishment they will abide eternally,” meaning: And in the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, they will abide eternally, their abode and stay in it is permanent.
5:81: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if these people who take the unbelievers from among the Children of Israel as allies, believe in God and the Prophet, meaning: they believe in God and acknowledge Him and worship Him alone, and believe in His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is a prophet sent by God and a messenger sent by Him, and what was revealed to him, meaning: and they acknowledge what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from God of the verses of the Criterion, they would not have taken them as allies, meaning: they would not have taken them as companions and supporters instead of the believers, but many of them are wicked, meaning: but many of them are people who depart from the obedience of God to His disobedience, and people who permit what God has forbidden them of saying and doing. Mujahid used to say about this: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies, he said: the hypocrites.
5:82: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You will find, O Muhammad, the people most hostile to those who believed in you and followed you and believed in what you brought them from the people of Islam, the Jews and those who associate others with God, meaning: the idol worshippers who took idols as gods that they worship instead of God, and you will find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe, meaning: and you will find the nearest of people in affection and love. And the passive participle mawadda is derived from the man’s saying: I loved so-and-so, I loved him with love, affection, and affection, if I loved him. For those who believe means: for those who believed in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who say, ‘We are Christians.’ That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant, about accepting the truth, following it, and submitting to it. It was said: This verse and the one after it were revealed about a group of Christians from Abyssinia who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they heard the Qur’an, they converted to Islam and followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It was revealed about the Negus, the king of Abyssinia, and his companions who converted to Islam with him. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Negus sent a delegation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them, and they converted to Islam. He said: Then God Almighty revealed about them: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God, to the end of the verse. He said: So they returned to the Negus and informed him, and the Negus converted to Islam, and he remained a Muslim until he died. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your brother the Negus has died, so pray over him! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him in Medina, and the Negus was there. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ he said: They are the delegation who came with Ja’far and his companions from the land of Abyssinia. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, and he feared for his companions from the polytheists, so he sent Abu Talib, Ibn Masoud, and Uthman bin Mazun, with a group of his companions to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia. When the polytheists heard about that, they sent Amr bin Al-Aas with a group of them. It is said that they preceded the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Negus, and they said: A man has emerged among us who has belittled the minds and wisdom of the Quraysh, and he claims that he is a prophet! Because he sent a group to you to corrupt your people, we wanted to come to you and tell you about them. He said: If they come to me, I will consider what they say! So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came forward and headed to the door of the Negus, and they said: Ask permission for the friends of God! He said: Give them permission, welcome to the friends of God! When they entered upon him, they greeted him. The group of polytheists said to him: Do you not see, O king, that we have believed you? They did not greet you with the greeting you greet with! He said to them: What prevented you from greeting me with my greeting? They said: We greeted you with the greeting of the people of Paradise and the greeting of the angels! He said to them: What does your master say about Jesus and his mother? He said: “He says: ‘He is a servant of God, and a word from God which He bestowed upon Mary, and a spirit from Him.’” He said about Maryam 19:She is the virgin. He said: “He took a stick from the ground and said: ‘Jesus and his mother did not add anything to what your master said, even the amount of this stick!’ The polytheists hated what he said, and their faces changed. He said to them: “Do you know anything of what has been revealed to you?” They said: Yes! He said: Read! So they read, and among them were priests, monks, and other Christians, and I knew everything they read, and their tears flowed because of what they knew of the truth. God Almighty said: “That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger” verse. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told me, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ verse. He said: The Negus sent twelve men from Abyssinia to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seven priests and five monks, to look at him and ask him questions. When they met him and he recited to them what God had revealed, they wept and believed, so God revealed to him about them: “And that they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses,’” verse. So they believed and then returned to the Negus. The Negus migrated with them and died on the way, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims prayed over him and asked forgiveness for him. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ata’ said regarding His statement: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ the verse, they are people from Abyssinia who believed when the migration of believers came to them. Others said: Rather, this is a description of a people who followed the law of Jesus and were people of faith. Then, when God Almighty sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they believed in him. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe, and he recited until he reached: Then register us among the witnesses, people from the People of the Book who were on a law of truth that which Jesus brought, they believed in it and adhered to it. Then when God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they believed in him and believed in him, and they recognized that what he brought was the truth, so what you hear praised them. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that God Almighty described the characteristics of a people who said, We are Christians, and that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, found them to be the closest people in love to the people of faith in God and His Messenger, and He did not give us their names. It may be possible that what was meant by that was the companions of the Negus, and it may be possible that what was meant by it was a people who followed the law of Jesus, and Islam overtook them and they submitted to it when they heard the Qur’an and knew that it was the truth, and they were not arrogant towards it. As for the Almighty’s saying: That is because among them are priests and monks, He is saying: He brought close the affection of those whom God described to the believers, because among them are priests and monks. Priests is the plural of priest. Priest may also be pluralized as qusus, because priest and priest have the same meaning. Ibn Zayd used to say about the priest: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: The priests, their worshippers. As for monks, it can be singular or plural. If it is a plural, then one of them is a monk, and the monk is then the subject of the saying of the speaker: God has made so-and-so fearful, meaning he feared him, he fears him with fear and awe, then the monk is made plural, monks like rider and riders and knight and knights. And the evidence that it can be plural among the Arabs is the saying of the poet: The monks of Madyan, if they saw you, they would descend, and the protection from the passion of the weak minds Monks may be one. If there is one, the plural is rabbin, like qurban and qarabin, and jardan and jaradeen. It is also permissible to pluralize it as rabbanah, if that is the case. Evidence that there may be one among the Arabs is the poet’s saying: If you saw the monks of a monastery in the valley, the monks would walk and descend The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement: That is because among them were priests and monks. Some of them said: He meant by that a people who responded to Jesus, son of Mary, when he called them, and followed him in his law. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: That is because among them were priests and monks, he said: They were sailors at sea - meaning: sailors - he said: Then Jesus, son of Mary, passed by them and called them to Islam and they responded to him. He said: That is why he said: priests and monks. Others said: Rather, he meant by that the people whom the Negus had sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salim told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: That is because among them are priests and monks, he said: Sixty-six, or sixty-seven, or sixty-eight, from Abyssinia, all of them the owners of a monastery, wearing woolen garments. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: That is because among them are priests and monks. He said: The Negus sent fifty or seventy of their best to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they began to cry, so he said: They are these! Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: That is because among them are priests and monks. He said: They are the messengers of the Negus who were sent with his Islam and the Islam of his people. They were seventy men, he chose the best of them, then the best. So they entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited to them: Ya Sin * By the Wise Qur’an (Ya Sin: 1, 2), so they wept and recognized the truth, so God revealed about them: That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant, and He revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it until His saying: They will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured (al-Qasas 28:53, 54). Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God Almighty informed us about the group of Christians whom He praised for their closeness to the people of faith in God and His Messenger, that this was only because some of them were people of diligence in worship, and were monks in monasteries and convents, and that some of them were scholars of their books and people of recitation of them. They are not far from the believers because of their humility towards the truth when they know it, and they are not arrogant about accepting it when they understand it, because they are people of religion and diligence in it, and sincere advice to themselves in the cause of God, and they are not like the Jews who were trained by killing the prophets and messengers, and opposing God in His commands and prohibitions, and distorting His revelation that He revealed in His books.
5:83: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And when those who said, We are Christians, whom I described to you, O Muhammad, whose description is that you find them the closest people in affection to those who believe, hear what has been revealed to you of the Book being recited, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears. The overflow of tears from the eye, its filling with them, then its flow from it, like the overflow of a river with water, and the overflow of a vessel, which is its flowing from its intense fullness, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: My tears flowed, and the matter remained: either in terms of how or in terms of decline. His saying: From what they knew of the truth, he says: Their tears flowed, because they knew that what was recited to them from the Book of God that He revealed to the Messenger of God was the truth, as: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Asbat bin Nasr Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Suddi, who said: The Negus sent twelve men to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him questions and bring him his report. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an to them, and they wept. Among them were seven monks and five priests - or: five monks and seven priests - so God revealed about them: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears, to the end of the verse. Amr bin Ali told us, Omar bin Ali bin Muqaddam told us, I heard Hisham bin Urwa narrating, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, who said: The following was revealed about the Negus and his companions: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears. Hanad told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement: You will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth, he said: That is about Al-Najashi. Hanad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said: They believed that this verse was revealed about the Negus: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears. Hannad told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Ibn Ishaq said: I asked Al-Zuhri about the verses: “That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears” (al-Furqan 25:63), and His statement: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace’” (al-Furqan 25:63). He said: I have not ceased to hear our scholars say: It was revealed about the Negus and his companions. As for his saying: They say, if it had been in the form of a noun, it would have been in the accusative case as a state, because the meaning of the statement is: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth, saying: Our Lord, we have believed. What is meant by the Almighty’s saying: They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed,’ is that they say: Our Lord, we have believed when we heard what You revealed to Your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Your Book, and we have acknowledged that it is from You and that it is the truth, without doubt. As for his saying: Then write us down with the two witnesses, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others in its interpretation, what: Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father and Ibn Numayr told us, all of them, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then write us down with the witnesses, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Then write us down with the witnesses, with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then write us down with the two witnesses, meaning by the two witnesses, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then write us down with the witnesses, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, they testified that he had conveyed, and they testified that the messengers had conveyed. Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Asad bin Musa told us, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, he said, Israel told me, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, like the hadith of Al-Harith bin Abdul Aziz, except that he said: And they testified for the messengers that they had conveyed. Abu Ja`far said: The one who interpreted this interpretation intended by this interpretation the meaning of the statement of God Almighty: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you (al-Baqarah 2:143). Ibn Abbas went to the view that the witnesses are the martyrs in His statement: that you will be witnesses over the people (al-Baqarah 2:143), and they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If this is the interpretation, then the meaning of the words is: They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses,’ who will testify for Your prophets on the Day of Resurrection that they conveyed Your messages to their nations. If someone were to say: The meaning of this is: Then register us among the witnesses, who testify that what You have revealed to Your Messenger of the Book is true, this would be correct. Because that is the conclusion of His statement: “And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses,’” and that is a description of God Almighty that He mentioned to them regarding their faith in what they heard from the Book of God. So their request to God would also be to make them among those whose testimony is confirmed by Him, and to include them in their stations in reward and recompense. The meaning of the book, in this context, is: making. He says: So include us among the witnesses, and include us among them.
5:84: Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God Almighty about these people whose characteristics He described in these verses, that when they heard what was revealed to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from His Book, they believed in it and confirmed the Book of God, and said: Why should we not believe in God, meaning: We do not acknowledge the Oneness of God, and what has come to us of the truth, meaning: and what has come to us from God of His Book and the verses of His revelation, and we hope by our belief in that that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people. By the righteous people, he means those who believe in God, who obey Him, and who have earned Paradise from God through their obedience to Him. The meaning of this is: We hope that our Lord will admit us with the people of His obedience into His Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and that He will join our homes with their homes, and our ranks with their ranks in His Paradise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And why should we not believe in God and what has come to us of the truth and hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people, he said: The righteous people are the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions.
5:85: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: So God rewarded them for their saying: “Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth and hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people? So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow,” meaning: orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow, abiding therein, meaning: they will remain there forever, they will not leave it nor move from it, and that is the reward of the doers of good, meaning: And this is what I rewarded those who said what I described about them from their saying for what they said, from the gardens in which they will abide eternally, the reward of every doer of good in his saying and his action. The excellence of the doer of good in this regard is to believe in the Oneness of God with a pure and unadulterated belief, without any association with Him, and to acknowledge the prophets of God and the books they brought from God, and to perform His obligations, and to avoid His disobedience. This is the perfection of the excellence of the doers of good, about whom God Almighty said: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally.
5:86: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: As for those who denied the oneness of God, rejected the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied the verses of His Book, then those are the companions of Hellfire, meaning: they are its inhabitants and those who abide therein. And hell: is the intense heat of fire, which is Al-Jahim and Al-Jahaneem.
5:87: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, and have acknowledged what their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them as the truth from God, Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful for you, meaning by the good things, the delicious things that the souls desire and the hearts incline towards, so you prevent them from them, like what the priests and monks did, for they prohibited themselves from women, good food, and delicious drinks, and some of them confined themselves to monasteries, and some of them roamed the earth. God Almighty says: So do not do, O believers, as those did, and do not transgress the limit of God which He has set for you in what He has made lawful for you and what He has forbidden you, so you transgress the limit which He has set, thus disobeying Him, for God does not love those who transgress the limit which He has set for His creation, in what He has made lawful for them and what He has forbidden for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said, Abthar Abu Zubaid told us, he said, Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you the verse, he said: Uthman bin Mazun and some of the Muslims, women were prohibited to them, and they abstained from good food, and some of them wanted to cut off their penis, so this verse was revealed. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Yazid ibn Zurai` told us, Khalid al-Hadha` told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: There were some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who intended to castrate themselves and give up meat and women, so this verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah: That some men wanted such and such, and they wanted such and such, and to be specific, so the following was revealed: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you until His saying: in which you are believers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. He said: They had prohibited good things and meat, so God Almighty revealed this about them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: Some people said: We will not marry, nor eat, nor do such and such! So God the Most High revealed: “O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, he said: Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to reject the world, abandon women, and become monks. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and spoke harshly to them, then he said: Those who came before you were destroyed because of severity. They were severe on themselves, so God was severe on them. Those are their remnants in the houses and monasteries! Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, and perform Hajj and Umrah, and be upright, and you will be upright. He said: And the verse was revealed about them: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, and the verse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, he said: It was revealed about some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who wanted to abandon the world, leave women, and become ascetics, among them Ali bin Abi Talib and Uthman bin Mazun. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not command you to be priests and monks. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, the verse, he mentioned to us that some men from among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused women and meat, and wanted to build monasteries. When this reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: It is not in my religion to abandon women and meat, or to keep monasteries. He told us that “three men agreed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one of them said: As for me, I will pray at night and not sleep! And one of them said: As for me, I will fast during the day and not break my fast! And the other said: As for me, I will not have intercourse with women! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and said: Did I not inform you that you agreed on such and such? They said: Yes! O Messenger of God, and we only wanted good! He said: But I pray and sleep, and fast and break my fast, and have intercourse with women. So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.” And in some of the readings it was: Whoever turns away from your Sunnah is not of your nation and has strayed from the right path. He told us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to some of his companions: “Those before you were harsh on themselves, so God was harsh on them. These are their brothers in the houses and monasteries! Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, perform Hajj and Umrah, and be upright and you will be upright.” Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat one day and mentioned the people, then he stood up and did not do more than frighten them. Then a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were ten, among them Ali ibn Abi Talib and Uthman ibn Maz’un, said: We are not afraid if we do not innovate any action! The Christians have forbidden themselves, so we forbid! Some of them forbade eating meat and fat, and eating during the day, and some of them forbade sleeping, and some of them forbade women. "Uthman ibn Maz'un was one of those who forbade women, and he would not come near his family nor would they come near him. His wife Aisha, who was called Al-Hawla', came to her. Aisha and the other wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: What is the matter with you, O squint-eyed woman, that your color has changed and you do not comb your hair or use perfume? She said: How can I perfume myself and comb my hair when my husband has not had intercourse with me or lifted a garment from me since such and such? They began to laugh at her words. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered while they were laughing, and he said: What makes you laugh? He said: O Messenger of God, Al-Hawla', I asked her about her situation and she said: My husband has not lifted a garment from me since such and such! So he sent for him and called him and said: What is the matter with you, O Uthman? He said: I left it for God in order to devote myself to worship! And he told him his story. Uthman wanted to answer himself, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I swear to you that you will return and have intercourse with your wife! He said: O Messenger of God, I am fasting! He said: Break your fast! So he broke his fast and came. His family. So, the squint-eyed woman returned to Aisha, having applied kohl, combed her hair, and perfumed herself. Aisha laughed and said: What is the matter with you, O squint-eyed woman? She said: He came to her yesterday! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, and sleep? I sleep and stand, break my fast and marry women. Whoever turns away from my way is not of me! Then the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. He said to Uthman: Do not force yourself, for this is transgression. He ordered them to atone for their oaths, and said: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. (al-Ma’idah
5:88: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to these believers whom He forbade from forbidding the good things that God has made lawful for them: Eat, O believers, of the provision that God has provided for you and made lawful for you, lawful and good, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah: And eat of what God has provided for you [that is] lawful and good, meaning: what God has made lawful for them of food. As for His statement: And fear God, in whom you are believers, He says: And fear, O believers, lest you transgress His limits, making permissible what He has forbidden you, and forbidding what He has made permissible for you, and beware in that lest you disobey Him, lest His wrath descend upon you, or you deserve His punishment, in whom you are believers, He says: In whose Oneness you acknowledge, and whose Lordship you believe.
5:89: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to those who had forbidden themselves good things from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had forbidden that with oaths that they had sworn, so He forbade them from forbidding it and said to them: God will not hold you accountable for what is futile in your oaths, as: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the verse: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you was revealed about the people who had forbidden women and meat to themselves, they said: O Messenger of God, what should we do with the oaths that we have sworn? So God, the Most High, revealed: God will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, the verse. This indicates what we said, that the people had forbidden themselves what they had forbidden themselves by swearing oaths, so this verse was revealed because of them. There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have made, with a shaddah on the qaf, meaning: you have made oaths and rejected them. The Kufians read: By what you have made oaths, with a light qaf, meaning: you have made them obligatory upon yourselves, and your hearts have resolved upon them. In the past of this book of ours, we disliked repeating that in this place. As for his saying: Because you have made oaths, then Hannad: He told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn, he said: for what you have done intentionally. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in deed, meaning: what you deliberately committed as a sin, for which you must make expiation. Abu Ja`far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the ha’ in His statement: his expiation, as to what it refers to, and who mentioned what? Some of them said: It refers to what is in His statement: because of what you have pledged oaths. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding this verse: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, he said: It is when you swear an oath about something and you think it is as you swore, but it is not so, so God will not hold you accountable, and there is no expiation. But the accountability and expiation are for what you swore to with knowledge. Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: There is no expiation for idle talk, But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in deed. He said: Whatever he swore in deed, he must expiate. Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: Oaths are of three types: an oath that expiates, an oath that does not expiate, and an oath for which the oath-taker will not be held accountable. As for the oath that expiates, a man swears to do something that he will not do, then he does it, so he must expiate. As for the oath that does not expiate, a man swears to do something deliberately lying, so there is no expiation for it. As for the oath for which the oath-taker will not be held accountable, a man swears to do something that he believes to be as he swore, but it is not, so there is no expiation for it. This is idle talk. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said: Aisha said: An oath is futile unless the one taking the oath has made up his mind to it. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: There is no expiation for a vain oath. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, that Urwah told him, that Aisha said: The oaths of expiation are every oath in which a man swears regarding a serious matter in anger or otherwise: Let them do it, “Let them leave it,” so that is the covenant of oaths for which God has imposed expiation. God the Most High said: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, and on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, they said: There is no expiation for a vain oath. Bishr told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in deliberate oaths, meaning: If you intentionally commit a sin, then you must make expiation for it. He said, and Qatada said: As for idle talk, there is no expiation for it. Hanad told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: There is no expiation for a false oath. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: There is no expiation for a false oath. Abu Ja`far said: The meaning of the statement according to this interpretation is: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. The expiation for what you deliberated of them is feeding ten poor people. Others said: The ha in His statement: its expiation refers to the unintentional oath, and it is a euphemism for it. They said: The meaning of the statement is: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, if you expiate it, but He will hold you accountable if you deliberated of the oaths and persist in carrying them out by not breaking the oath and not paying expiation for it. Persisting in carrying them out is not permissible for you. The expiation for what you deliberated of them, if you broke it, is feeding ten poor people. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, meaning a man swears to do something harmful but does not do it, then he sees something better than it, so God commands him to atone for his oath and do what is better. And he said another time: His statement: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, to His statement: for your deliberate oaths, he said: The unintentional oaths are those for which atonement is required, God will not hold him accountable for them. But whoever persists in forbidding what God has made lawful for him, and does not change from it, and does not atone for his oath, then that is what he will be held accountable for. Hanad told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, he said: It is the one who swears to commit a sin and does not fulfill it, so he is an unbeliever. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, he said: It is a man who swears to commit a sin, so God, the Most High, will not hold him accountable. He expiates for his oath and does what is better. But He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths, a man who swears to commit a sin and then continues to do so, so his expiation is to feed ten poor people. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said about idle oaths: It is an oath in disobedience, so he said: Do you not read and understand? He said: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. He said: He will not hold him accountable for omitting it, but He will hold him accountable for completing it. He said: And He said: And do not make God an object of your oaths (al-Baqarah 2:224). Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, he said: It is a man who swears an oath to commit a sin, but God will not hold him accountable for abandoning it if he abandons it. I said: What should he do? He said: He should expiate his oath and abandon the sin. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Idle talk is an oath for which the one who makes it will not be held accountable, and there is expiation for it. Yahya bin Jaafar told me, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, he said: The expiatory oath. Abu Ja`far said: What I think is more correct in this regard is that the ha’ in his statement: its expiation refers back to the ma in his statement: for what you have pledged oaths, because we mentioned previously: that if someone is obligated to pay his expiation in his oath and is held accountable for it, it is not permissible to say to someone who has been held accountable: God will not hold him accountable for what is unintentional. And in His Most High’s statement: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, there is clear evidence that He will not be held accountable in any way, as He, the Most High, has informed us that He will not be held accountable. If someone thinks that what God Almighty meant by His saying, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, is punishment for it in the Hereafter if you break your oath and disbelieve - except that He will not hold you accountable for it in this world by disbelief - then God Almighty’s information, commands, and prohibitions in His Book, according to the general appearance in our view - with what we have proven to be correct in other places, so there is no need to repeat it - without the general hidden meaning that there is no indication of its specificity in reason or report, nor indication from action or report that God Almighty meant by His saying, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, some of the meanings of accountability but not all of them. Since this is the case, and if someone is required to make expiation for an oath he broke, he will be held accountable for it with an immediate financial penalty, it is known that he is not the one whom God Almighty informed us that He will not hold him accountable for it. And since the correct interpretation of that is what we said with what we have proven, then the meaning of the statement is: God will not hold you accountable, O people, for what you said and swore, if you did not intentionally disobey God Almighty or oppose His command, and you did not intend sin by it, but He will hold you accountable for what you intentionally committed to sin, and imposed upon yourselves, and resolved in your hearts, and that will atone for you, and cover up the evil of what you did of lying and false speech, and erase it from you so that your Lord will not follow you with it, Feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: From the average of what you feed your families, from the most just of it, like: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: I heard Ata’ say about this verse: From the middle of what you feed your families or clothe them, Ata’ said: The middle of it, the most just of it. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement: From the average of what you feed your families. Some of them said: Its meaning is: From the average of what is fed from the types of food that the people of the country of the disbeliever feed their families. Those who said that mentioned: Hanad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hanash, on the authority of Al-Aswad, he said: I asked him about: The average of what you feed your families, he said: Bread, dates, oil, and ghee, and the best of it is meat. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hanash, he said: I asked Al-Aswad bin Yazid about that and he said: Bread and dates. Hannad added to his hadith: And oil. He said: And I think it was vinegar. Hannad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement: From the best of what you feed your families, he said: From the best of what he feeds his family: bread and dates, bread and ghee, and bread and oil. And from the best of what you feed them: bread and meat. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Umar: Among the best things you feed your families are bread and meat, bread and ghee, bread and cheese, and bread and vinegar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hanash, he said: I asked al-Aswad ibn Yazid about the average of what you feed your families, he said: Bread and dates. Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, Abdullah bin Hanash told us: I asked Al-Aswad bin Yazid, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salman: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: Bread and butter. Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: I asked Ubaidah about that, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Azhar told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah: From the average of what you feed your families, is bread and butter. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ab told us, on the authority of Yazid Ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: They used to say: The best of it is bread and meat, the middle of it is bread and ghee, and the worst of it is bread and dates. Hannad told us: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Bread and meat, or bread and ghee, or bread and milk. Hannad and Ibn Wakee’ narrated, they said: Umar ibn Harun narrated, on the authority of Abu Muslih, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement: From the best of what you feed your families, he said: Bread, meat, and broth. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd ar-Rahman narrated, he said: Zaidah narrated, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hayyan At-Ta’i, he said: I was with Shuraih when a man came to him and said: I swore an oath and I sinned. Shuraih said: What made you do that? He said: It was decreed for me, so what is the best of what I feed my family? Shuraih said to him: Bread, oil, and vinegar are good. He said: So he repeated it to him, and Shuraih said to him that three times, and Shuraih should not do more than that. So he said to him: What do you think if I feed bread and meat? He said: That is the best food for your family and the food of the people. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, he said, regarding the expiation for an oath: He feeds them breakfast and dinner with bread and oil, or bread and ghee, or vinegar and oil. Hanad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zubarqan, on the authority of Abu Razin: Among the average things you feed your families is bread, oil, and vinegar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Muhammad, he said: One meal, bread and meat. He said, It is among the average things you feed your families, and you eat khabees and fruit. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, and Hannad told us, he said: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said regarding expiation for an oath: It is sufficient for you to feed ten poor people one meal, bread and meat. If you cannot find that, then bread, ghee and milk. If you cannot find that, then bread, vinegar and oil until they are full. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Zubarqan, he said: I asked Abu Razin about the expiation for an oath, what to eat? He said: Bread, vinegar, and oil: from the average of what you feed your families, and that is the amount of their sustenance for one day. Then those who said that differed about its amount. Some of them said: The amount of that is half a sa’ of wheat, or a sa’ of other grains. Those who said that mentioned: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Marra, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Umar, he said: I swear an oath, then it changes its mind, so if you see that I have done that, then feed ten poor people, for each poor person a mudd of wheat. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Ali told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Yasar bin Numayr, he said, Umar said: I swear that I will not give to people, then it occurs to me that I should give to them. So when you see me do that, feed ten poor people on my behalf, giving for every two poor people a sa’ of wheat or a sa’ of dates. Hanad and Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali, he said: The expiation for an oath is to feed ten poor people, for each poor person half a sa’ of wheat. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: From the average of what you feed your families, half a sa’ of wheat, for each poor person. Hannad told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari, he said: I said to Saeed bin Jubair: Should I gather them? He said: No, give them two mudds of wheat, one mudd for his food, and one mudd for his condiment. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, he said: I said to Saeed, and he mentioned something similar. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Zubayd told us, on the authority of Hisayn, he said: I asked Al-Sha’bi about the expiation for an oath, and he said: Two, one for his food, and one for his condiment. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Every poor person has a debt. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Every poor person is to be given a mudd of goods as expiation for an oath. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: A mudd of food for each poor person. Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Sa’id ibn Yazid Abu Muslimah told us: I asked Jabir ibn Zayd about feeding the poor person as expiation for an oath, and he said: A meal. I said: Al-Hasan says: A handful of wheat and a handful of dates, so what do you think of a handful of wheat? He said: A handful of wheat!! Ya’qub said, Ibn Ulayyah said: Abu Muslimah gestured with his hand, as if he saw it as good, and Abu Bishr turned his hand. Hannad told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That he used to say regarding the expiation for an oath: In what is required for food, a handful of dates and a handful of wheat for each poor person. Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said, he said: If he gathered them together, he would satisfy them all once, and if he gave them something, he would give them something a little at a time. Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: It is enough for him, if he gives them in their hands, then a handful of wheat and a handful of dates. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding the expiation for an oath: half a sa’ for each poor person. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam regarding his statement: Feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families, he said: Half a sa’ of food for each poor person. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman Qali’ told us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The average of what you feed your families is half a sa’. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim say regarding His statement: Then its expiation is the feeding of ten poor people, he said: The food, for each poor person is half a sa’ of dates or wheat. Others said: Rather, the amount of that for every grain is one mudd. Who said that? Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Hisham Al-Dastawai, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, that he said regarding the expiation for an oath: a mudd of wheat for every poor person. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said regarding the expiation for an oath: A mudd of wheat for each poor person, a quarter of it as a condiment. Hanad and Abu Kuraib told us, they said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: Feeding ten poor people, one mudd for each poor person. Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Waki’ told us, he said, Al-Amri told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: A mudd of wheat for every poor person. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to expiate an oath with ten mudds, according to the smaller mudd. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Al-Qasim and Salim, regarding the expiation for an oath: What should be fed? They said: One mudd for each poor person. -Hannad narrated, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas narrated, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, he said: When one of the people disbelieved, he expiated with ten mudds, according to the smaller mudd. Hanad told us, he said, Omar bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: Feeding ten poor people, he said: Ten provisions for ten poor people. Bishr told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families. He said: It was said: wheat and dates, for each poor person a mudd of dates, and a mudd of wheat. Abu Kuraib and Hannad told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Malik Ibn Mughul, on the authority of Ata’, he said: A mudd for every poor person. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, From the average of what you feed your families, he said: From the average of what you provide for them. He said: The Muslims saw the average of that as a mudd by the mudd of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of wheat. Ibn Zayd said: It is the average of what he provides for his family, not the lowest nor the highest. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Salim told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: a mudd. Others said: Rather, it is lunch and dinner. Who said that? Hanad told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, he said, regarding the expiation for an oath: He feeds them breakfast and dinner. Hanad told us, he said, Omar bin Harun told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, regarding the expiation for an oath, he said: Lunch and dinner. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: He feeds them breakfast and dinner. Others said: What he meant by his saying: From the average of what you feed your families, is the average of what the unbeliever feeds his family. He said: If he is one of those who feed his family, he should feed the ten poor people. And if he is one of those who cannot feed them because he is unable to do so, he should feed the poor people according to what he does for his family in times of difficulty and ease. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then its expiation is to feed ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families, he said: If you feed your family, then feed the poor people, otherwise, according to the amount of what you feed your family. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The expiation for it is to feed ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families, which is to feed each poor person from what you feed your family from satiety, or half a sa’ of wheat. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: From their hardship and their ease. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said: From their hardship and their ease. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: their food. Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Absi, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: their food. Abu Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salim told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Ubayd al-Absi, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, regarding his statement: From the best of what you feed your families, he said: They used to prefer the free man over the slave, and the old over the young, so the verse was revealed: From the best of what you feed your families. Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said, they used to feed the old what they did not feed the young, and they used to feed the free man what they did not feed the slave, so he said: From the average of what you feed your families. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: If you are going to satisfy your family, then satisfy them. And if you are not going to satisfy them, then according to that. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Shaiban Al-Nahwi told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From the middle of what you feed your families, he said: from their hardship and ease. Yunus told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, he said, Ibn Abbas said: A man would feed some of his family with a poor diet, and some of them with ample diet, so God said: From the average of what you feed your families, bread and oil. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct interpretation of his statement, From the average of what you feed your families, according to us, is the statement of those who say: From the average of what you feed your families in terms of little and much. This is because the rulings of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding all expiations have been reported in this regard. This is like his ruling, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the expiation for shaving the head from harm by distributing food among six poor people, for each poor person half a sa`, and like his ruling regarding the expiation for intercourse in the month of Ramadan by distributing fifteen sa` among sixty poor people, for each poor person a quarter of a sa`. Nothing is known of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding expiations. He ordered the feeding of bread and condiments, nor lunch and dinner. If that is the case, and the expiation for an oath is one of the expiations that are required of the one who is obligated to do so, then its method is the method of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took over the ruling on: that what is required of the one who expiates it is food, estimated for the ten poor people, limited by a measure, without gathering them together for a baked and prepared lunch or dinner, since his Sunnah, may God bless him and grant him peace, was like that in all other expiations. So if what we said is correct, based on what we cited as evidence, then it is clear that the interpretation of the statement is: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in oaths. Its expiation is feeding ten poor people from the most just of what you feed your families. And that the ma in His statement: from the average of what you feed your families is in the sense of the source, not in the sense of the names. If this is the case, then the most just food for the wealthy person is two mudds, which is half a sa’ of food, and a quarter of it is a condiment. This is the highest that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled for expiation for feeding the poor. And the most just food for the poor person is one mudd, which is a quarter of a sa’, and this is the lowest that he ruled for expiation for feeding the poor. As for those who saw feeding the poor in expiation for an oath, bread and meat and what we mentioned about them before, and those who saw that they should eat or have dinner, and those who saw that they should eat in the morning and have dinner, then they went to the interpretation of his saying: from the average of what you feed your families, from the average food that you feed your families, so they made what is in his saying: from the average of what you feed your families, a noun and not a source, so they obligated the one who is expiating to feed the poor from the most equitable food that he feeds his family. And that is a doctrine, were it not for what we mentioned from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in expiations other than it, the forms of which must be attached to it, and that the expiation for an oath has a counterpart and similar that must be attached to it. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: or their clothing.
