If it is from the locust or the like, then his penalty is a handful of food. If it is from the land bird, then he must stand up and give its price in charity, and if he wishes, he may fast for each half a saa’ of food for a day. If he kills a chick or an egg of a wild bird, then its value is food or fasting, depending on what is in the bird. However, it has been mentioned regarding ostrich eggs that if a pilgrim has intercourse with them, he should carry the stallion on the number of eggs he has intercourse with the virgin camels, and whatever he has inseminated from them he should take to the House, and whatever is spoiled from them he should not pay anything. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, he said, Mujahid said: Whoever kills it - meaning the game - forgetfully, or intends to kill someone else but misses it, then that is the deliberate act that requires expiation, so he must offer a similar sacrifice to the Kaaba. If he cannot find any, he must buy food with its price. If he cannot find any, he must fast for every mudd one day. Ata’ said: If a person finds an ostrich, he will be given - even if he is wealthy - plenty, if he wishes he may offer a camel as a sacrifice, or its equivalent in food, or its equivalent in fasting, whichever he wishes, because of His saying: Then a reward, or such and such, or such and such.” He said: So everything in the Qur’an has or, “or,” so its owner can choose from it what he wishes. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, he said, al-Hasan ibn Muslim told me: Whoever kills a game animal that is a sheep or more, that is what God the Most High said: The penalty is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock. As for the expiation of feeding poor people, that is what is not enough to be an offering, a bird is killed, so there is no offering. He said: Or the equivalent of that in fasting, the equivalent of an ostrich, or the equivalent of a bird, or the equivalent of all of that. Others said: Rather, the value of the killed game is determined in dirhams, then the killer buys a similar animal with its value, then presents it to the Kaaba. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Whatever the pilgrim finds of something, the ruling on it is its value. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Hammad, he said: I heard Ibrahim say: There is a price for every kind of hunting. Abu Ja`far said: The first of the two opinions in interpreting the verse is what `Umar and Ibn `Abbas said, and those who said what they said: that the game killed is recompensed with the like of it from the livestock, as God Almighty said: Then the recompense is like that which was killed from the livestock. It is not permissible for the like of what was killed from the game to be dirhams, and God Almighty said: from the livestock, because dirhams are not from the livestock at all. If someone says: Even if the dirhams are not equivalent to the game killed, they are used to buy equivalent livestock, and the killer gives it as a gift, so by doing so he is thus punishing the game killed as equivalent livestock! It was said to him: What do you think if the game killed was small or defective, and the only way to obtain its value from the livestock is if it is large or sound, or if the game killed was large or sound, and the only way to obtain its value from the livestock is if it is small or defective, is it permissible for him to buy for its value something other than it and of a different description and give it as a gift, or is that not permissible for him, and he cannot find anything other than it? If he claims that he is not permitted to buy anything for its value except something similar, his statement on that should be abandoned. Because the people of this article claim that he is not permitted to buy something for its value and then give it as a gift, except for what is permitted in sacrificial animals. And if he permits buying something similar to what was killed from the game for its value and giving it as a gift, even though what was killed might be young and defective, he permits in the gift what is not permitted in sacrificial animals. If he claims that it is not permissible to buy it with its value and then give it as a gift except what is permissible in sacrifices, then this is clearer than his statement of disagreement with the apparent meaning of the revelation. That is because God, the Most High, mentioned it, has made it obligatory for the one who intentionally kills game from among the people in ihram to give an equivalent amount of livestock if he finds it. The author of this statement has claimed that he is not obligated to give an equivalent amount of livestock, and he has a way to do that. And it is said to the one who says this: What do you think if another speaker says: The killer of game whose value does not reach the level of what is taken from livestock that is permissible in sacrifices is not required to feed or fast? Because God Almighty only gave the killer of game from those in ihram the choice in one of the three things that He mentioned in His Book, so if he has no way to one of them, then the obligation of the others is dropped from him. Because the choice was only his, and he has a way to the three, so if he has no way to some of them, then the obligation of the penalty is invalidated from him, because he is not among those meant by the verse, similar to what you said: If the killed game is not worth the value of what is taken from livestock that is permissible in sacrifices, then the obligation of the penalty in the same amount of livestock is dropped from him, and he is only required to pay the penalty of feeding or fasting. Is there a difference between you and him in principle or similarity? He will not say something about one of them except that he will make something similar to it about the other. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: It shall be judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Kaaba. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Two just men from among you will judge with that penalty, which is like that of a killed game animal, as an offering. He means: two just men from among you - meaning: two learned scholars from among the people of religion and virtue - as an offering. He says: The penalty will be judged by two just men, meaning: it will be offered as an offering and will reach the Ka`bah. The ha in His statement: will be judged with, refers back to the reward. Abu Ja`far said: The ruling of two just men, if they want to pass a judgment against the killer, is that they look at the victim and examine him. If he mentions that he killed a young gazelle, they rule that he is a young sheep, similar in age and body to the one he killed. If the one he killed is an adult, they rule that he is an adult sheep. If the one he killed is a wild donkey, they rule that he is a cow. If the one he killed is an adult, then an adult cow. If the one he killed is a young one, then a young one. If the victim is male, then an equivalent male cow. If the victim is female, then an equivalent female cow. Then they look at the most similar animal to the victim in terms of resemblance to the animal, and they rule that he is the same, as God the Almighty said: And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that, with differences among them. Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaida narrated to us, Dawud bin Abi Hind narrated to us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzani, he said: There were two Bedouin men in ihram, one of them scared a gazelle, so the other killed it. They came to Omar, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf was with him, so Omar said to him: What do you think? He said: A sheep. He said: I see that too, go and offer a sheep as a gift. When they had left, one of them said to his companion: The Commander of the Faithful did not know what he was saying until he asked his companion!! Omar heard them, so he turned them away and said: Do you recite Surat Al-Ma'idah? They said: No! So he recited to them: Let it be judged by two just men among you, then he said: I have sought help from this companion of mine. Abu Kuraib and Ya'qub narrated, Hisham narrated, Abd al-Malik ibn Umair narrated, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Jabir, who said: My companion and I raced to hunt a gazelle on the pass, and we killed it. I went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. He turned to a man beside him and they looked at it. He said: Slaughter a ram - Ya'qub said in his hadith - and he said to me: Slaughter a sheep - so I turned and went to my companion and said: The Commander of the Faithful does not know what he is saying! My companion said: Slaughter your she-camel. Umar ibn al-Khattab heard that, so he turned to me and hit me with a whip and said: You kill game while you are in a state of ihram, and you are denying the verdict! God the Almighty says in His Book: It shall be judged by two just men among you, this is Ibn Awf, and I am Umar! Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said, Qubaysah bin Jaber told me, similar to what Abd Al-Malik told me. Hannad and Abu Hisham narrated: Waki` narrated from Al-Mas`udi from `Abd Al-Malik bin `Umair from Qubaysah bin Jabir who said: We went out as pilgrims, and after we prayed the morning prayer, we would lead our mounts, walking and talking. He said: While we were there one morning, a gazelle or a wild goat appeared to us, and one of us threw a stone at it, but did not miss its entrails, so it mounted its back dead. He said: We felt sorry for him. When we arrived in Mecca, I went out with him until we came to `Umar, and he told him the story. He said: And beside him was a man whose face was the color of silver - meaning `Abd Al-Rahman bin `Awf - so he turned to his companion and spoke to him. He said: Then he turned to the man and said: Did you kill him intentionally or by mistake? The man said: I threw him intentionally and did not mean to kill him. `Umar said: I think you have combined intentional and accidental killing. Go to a sheep, slaughter it, give its meat in charity, and give its hide as water. He said: So we got up from him, and I said: O man, honor the symbols of God! The Commander of the Faithful did not know what your fatwa was until he asked his companion! Go to your camel and slaughter it, perhaps that is it! Qubaysah said: I do not remember the verse from Surat al-Ma’idah 5:Let it be judged by two just men among you. He said: Then Umar heard what I said, and he did not surprise us with him except that he had a whip! He said: So my companion struck him with the whip, and kept saying: You killed in the sanctuary, and you made a fool of the judgment! Then he turned to me, and I said: O Commander of the Faithful, I do not permit for you today anything that is forbidden to you from me! He said: O Qubaysah bin Jabir, I see that you are young in age, broad-minded, and eloquent, and a young man may have nine good morals and one bad moral, so the bad morals spoil the good morals, so beware of the stumbling blocks of youth! Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Ibn Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq, who said: Arbad stepped on a lizard and killed it - while he was in a state of ihram. He came to Umar to pass judgment on him, and Umar said to him: Judge with me! So they ruled that it was a young goat that had gathered water and trees. Then Umar said: Let two just men among you judge it. Bishr ibn Muadh narrated, Jami’ ibn Hammad narrated, Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man had killed game, so he went to Ibn Umar and asked him about it, and Abdullah ibn Safwan was with him. Ibn Umar said to Ibn Safwan: Either I say it and you believe me, or you say it and I believe you. Ibn Safwan said: Rather you say it. Ibn Umar said, and Abdullah ibn Safwan agreed with him. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Shuraih, that he said: If I found a just judge, I would judge the fox with a young goat, and my young goat is more beloved to me than a fox. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakir told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: A man asked Ibn Umar about a man who caught game while he was in a state of ihram, and Ibn Safwan was with him. Ibn Umar said to him: Either you say it and I will believe you, or I say it and you will believe me. He said: Say it and I will believe you. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Abu Jarir al-Bajali told me: I killed a gazelle while I was in a state of ihram, so I mentioned that to Umar, and he said: Go to two of your brothers and let them judge you. So I went to Abd al-Rahman and Sa’d, and they judged me to be a black billy goat. Abu Ja’far said: Black is white. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on his chain of transmission on the authority of Umar, the same. Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ash'ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: A man was riding a camel while he was in a state of ihram, and he saw a gazelle taking refuge in a hillock, so he said, Let me see who will reach this hillock first or this gazelle? Then a female gazelle fell under the legs of his camel and killed it. He went to Umar and mentioned that to him, so he and Ibn Awf ruled that he should be given a white female goat. He said, It is the white one. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad: A man stepped on a gazelle while he was in a state of ihram, so he went to Umar and mentioned that to him, and next to him was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, so he turned to Abd al-Rahman and spoke to him, then he turned to the man and said: Give me a white goat. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he used to say: If something happens to a pilgrim in ihram and no ruling has been passed regarding it, he should face it and let two just men rule regarding it. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Wahb ibn Jarir told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la, on the authority of Amr ibn Habashi, who said: I heard a man ask Abdullah ibn Umar about a man who had a baby rabbit, and he said: There is a baby goat in it, as far as I see it. Then he said to me: Is that so? I said: You know better than me! He said: God Almighty said: Let two just men among you judge by it. Ibn Bashar narrated that Ibn Abi Uday and Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Bakr: Two men saw a gazelle while they were in a state of ihram, so they made a bet, and each of them bet on whoever would reach it first. One of them reached it first, so he shot it with his stick and killed it. When they arrived in Mecca, they came to Umar to argue with him, and Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf was with him. They mentioned that to him, and Umar said: This is gambling, and I do not permit it! Then he looked at Abdur-Rahman and said: What do you think? He said: A sheep. Umar said: I also think so. When the two men returned from Umar, one of them said to his companion: Umar did not know what to say until he asked the man! Umar turned them away and said: God, the Exalted, was not satisfied with Umar alone, so He said: Let two just men among you judge by it, and I am Umar, and this is Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf. Others said: Rather, the two just men look at the killed game, and assess its value in dirhams, then they order the killer to buy a sacrificial animal for that. So, according to what these people say, the two judges judge by the value. They are only needed to assess the value of the game in the place where it was killed. We mentioned about Ibrahim al-Nakha’i before that he used to say that whatever the pilgrim finds of something, the ruling on its value is based on it, and this is the opinion of a group of the jurists of Kufa. As for his saying: a gift, it is a verbal noun in the state of the letter ha in his saying: It is judged by it. His saying: It will reach the Kaaba is from the description of the gift and its attribute. It is permissible to describe it with it, and it is added to a definite noun, because it is in the meaning of an indefinite noun. That is because the meaning of his saying: It will reach the Kaaba is that it reaches the Kaaba. So even though it is added, its meaning is the tanween, because it means the future. It is similar to his saying: This is a cloud that will rain on us (al-Ahqaf 46:24), so he described with his saying: It will rain on us because in It will rain on us there is the meaning of the tanween, because its interpretation is the future, so its meaning is: This is a cloud that will rain on us. So it is the same in his saying: A gift that will reach the Kaaba. Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Or he must pay the expiation of feeding the poor, and the expiation is connected to the penalty in His statement: Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock. There are different readings of this: So I read it as the people of Medina generally read it, or as an expiation for feeding the poor in addition. As for the reading of the people of Iraq, most of them read it with the tanween of expiation and raising the food: or expiation of feeding the poor. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads with the tanween of expiation and the raising of the food, for the reason we mentioned in his statement: Then the recompense is like that of the livestock killed. The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of his statement: Or an expiation of feeding the poor. Some of them said: The meaning of this is that the killer who deliberately hunts while in a state of ihram is not free from the obligation of some of these three things that God the Most High mentioned: from the like of the one killed, a sacrifice to be delivered to the Kaaba, or feeding the poor as expiation for what he did, or fasting the equivalent of that, except that he has the choice of whichever of these he wants to do, and that with whichever of them he expiates, he has fulfilled what was required of him. Rather, this is an announcement from God the Most High to His servants that the killer of that is as described, and his ruling will not be outside of one of the three conditions. They said: So his ruling, if he is able to do the same, is that he should be judged with the like of the one killed from the livestock, and nothing else will suffice him as long as he has the like. They said: If he does not have the like, or the one killed does not have the like of the livestock, then his expiation in that case is feeding the poor. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And whoever among you kills him intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from sacrificial animals, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Kaaba, or an expiation by feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the evil of his deed.” He said: If a person in ihram kills any game, he is to be judged for it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, he must slaughter a sheep in Mecca. If he cannot find one, he must feed six poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for three days. If he kills a deer or the like, he must give a cow. If he cannot find one, he must feed twenty poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a wild donkey or the like, he must give a camel. If he cannot find one, he must feed thirty poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for thirty days. The food is a mudd, it will satiate them. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram, to his statement: It should be judged by two just men among you, so the expiation: for killing something less than a rabbit, is feeding. Hannad told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a pilgrim in ihram hunts game, he is required to pay its penalty in livestock. If he finds its penalty, he slaughters it and gives it in charity. If he does not find its penalty, the penalty is evaluated in dirhams, then the dirhams are evaluated in wheat, then he fasts a day in place of each saa. He said: What is meant by food is fasting, so if he finds food, he finds the penalty. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hameed bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’, Mujahid and Amer: Or the equivalent of that in fasting. He said: The food is only for the one who cannot find the sacrificial animal. Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim that he used to say: If a pilgrim hunts something, he must pay its compensation in livestock. If no people can find dirhams to pay, then the dirhams are valued as food, and he fasts for every half saa’ for a day. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated from Mughirah from Hammad who said: If a pilgrim hunts game and is judged to be guilty of it, and there is more than half a sa` left over, he must fast for it one day. Fasting is only for someone who cannot find the price of a sacrificial animal, in which case he must feed it. If he does not have food to give in charity, he must fast, so he must fast for every half sa` a day, as expiation for feeding the poor, he said: for something that does not amount to the price of a sacrificial animal. Or the equivalent of that in fasting, as a penalty, if he cannot find what to buy a sacrificial animal with, or what to give in charity, which does not amount to the price of a sacrificial animal, he must fast. The place of every half a saa is one day. Hannad told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Mujahid said: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, he said: He must offer an equivalent of the livestock as an offering to the Kaaba. And whoever cannot find any, he should buy food with its value, and feed each poor person one mudd. And if he cannot find any, he should fast one day for each mudd. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And whoever among you kills him intentionally to His saying: And whoever returns [to killing], God will take vengeance on him, he said: If he kills game, then he must pay the equivalent of the livestock he killed. If he cannot find any, then he is judged, then the ransom is assessed, how many dirhams it is, then the price of that is estimated in food for the poor person, so he fasts for each poor person one day, and the food of the poor person is not permissible, because whoever finds food for the poor person has found the ransom. Amr ibn Ali narrated that Abu Asim narrated that Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim said to me: Whoever hunts game for which the penalty is a sheep, that is what God the Most High said: The penalty is an equivalent of that which he killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you. And whatever expiation is by feeding poor people, such as a bird that is killed but is not considered a sacrificial animal, or its equivalent in fasting, he said: The equivalent of an ostrich or a bird, or the equivalent of all of that. So I mentioned that to Ata’ and he said: Everything in the Qur’an is or “or,” so the person who hunts it can choose what he wants. Amr bin Ali told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sufyan bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock.” If he does not find a penalty, then the penalty is food, then he should fast for each saa’ for two days. Others said: The meaning of this is that the one who kills game intentionally while in a state of ihram has the choice between one of the three expiations, which are: the recompense of an equivalent amount of livestock, food, and fasting. They said: The interpretation of his statement: “Then the recompense of an equivalent amount of livestock for what he killed, as judged by two just men among you, is an offering delivered to the Kaaba, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent amount of that in fasting,” He must repay the same favor, or atone by feeding the poor, or by fasting with food equal to the amount of food. Who said that? Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaidah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding the words of God, the Most High: “Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Ka’bah, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or its equivalent in fasting.” He said: If a person in a state of ihram kills an ostrich, then he has the right - even if he is well-off - to offer as an offering whatever he wants, a camel, or its equivalent in fasting. He said: Everything in the Qur’an has or “or,” so let its owner choose whatever he wants. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: Then the recompense is the like of what he killed from livestock, he said: Whatever is in the Qur’an: or such and such, then its companion has the choice in it, whichever of those things he wants to do. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Asbat and Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Whatever is in the Qur’an, or or or, then there is a choice in it. And whatever is: and whoever does not find, then the one that follows it, then the one that follows it. Yaqub told me: Hisham told us, Laith told us on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid: They said regarding His statement: Then the recompense is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, they said: Whatever is in the Qur’an or such and such, then its owner has the choice in it, whichever he wants to do. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Whatever is in the Qur’an: or such and such, then its companion has the choice, whichever he wants he may do. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said, and Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Everything in the Qur’an that has or or or is up to him to choose, he does whatever he wants. Hannad told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Everything in the Qur’an that has or or or has a choice in it. And everything that has but he who does not find has a choice in it, so the first, then the next. Those who say that the one who kills game in a state of ihram has a choice between the three things differed regarding the nature of what is required of him in terms of expiation by feeding and fasting, if he chooses to expiate with one of them without offering a sacrifice. Some of them said: If he chooses to atone for that, then he must provide the equivalent amount of food from the blessings, then fast one day in place of each mudd. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: I said to Ata’: What is or the equivalent of that in fasting? He said: If he gets what is equivalent to a sheep, the sheep is set aside as food, then he makes a day of fasting in place of each mudd. Others said: Rather, what is obligatory upon him, if he wants to atone by feeding or fasting, is to provide the killed game for food, then give the food in charity if he chooses charity. And if he chooses fasting, he should fast. Then they also differed about fasting. Some of them said: He fasts one day for each mudd. Others said: He fasts one day for every half a sa`. Others said: He fasts one day for each sa`. It was mentioned that the basis for feeding is the killed game. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada: O you who believe! Do not kill game, the verse. He said: Qatada used to say: They judge regarding livestock, and if he does not have what is sufficient for that, they look at its price and estimate it as food, then he fasts two days in place of each sa’. Others said: There is no meaning to atonement by feeding, because whoever finds a way to atone by feeding, he also finds a way to repay the sin with the same blessings. And whoever finds a way to repay the sin with the same blessings, atonement by anything else is not permissible for him. They said: God Almighty mentioned atonement by feeding in this place to indicate the nature of atonement by fasting, not that He made atonement by feeding one of the atonements by which killing game is atonement. We have already mentioned the interpretation of that previously. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct opinion in my opinion regarding the statement of God the Most High: Then the recompense is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock, is that what is meant by it is: then the one who intentionally kills him must pay an equivalent of what he killed of livestock, not its value, if he chooses to recompense him with an equivalent of livestock. This is because the value is in dinars or dirhams. And dirhams or dinars are not equivalent to hunting, and God the Most High only made the recompense obligatory in the form of an equivalent of livestock. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct opinion in my opinion regarding his statement: Or an expiation of feeding poor people or the equivalent of that in fasting, is that it is a choice, and that the killer has the choice of expiating for killing the game while he is in a state of ihram with any of these three expiations he wishes. Because God, the Most High, mentioned that what He has made obligatory in killing the game, both the penalty and the expiation, is a punishment for his action, and an expiation for his sin in destroying what he destroyed of the game that it was forbidden for him to destroy while he was in a state of ihram, and it was permissible for him before his state of ihram, just as He made the ransom of fasting, charity, or ritual for shaving the hair that the person in a state of ihram shaved while he was in a state of ihram, and it was permissible for him before his state of ihram, a punishment for his action, and an expiation for his sin in shaving the hair that the person in a state of ihram shaved while he was in a state of ihram, and he was allowed to shave it before his state of ihram, then he was forbidden to shave it while he was in a state of ihram, similar to hunting. Then he made it a penalty for shaving it. All agreed that if he shaved it because of its harm, he has the choice to expiate it by doing so with any of the three expiations he wishes. The same applies to the one who killed the game from the people in ihram, and he has the choice to expiate his killing of the game with any of the three expiations he wishes. There is no difference between that. And whoever rejects what we said about it, it is said to him: God, the Most High, has ruled on the killer of the game with the like of the livestock, or the expiation of feeding the poor, or its equivalent in fasting, just as He ruled on the shaver with a ransom of fasting, charity, or sacrifice. So you claimed that one of them has the choice to expiate what he made a compensation for with any of the three he wishes, and you denied that this is for the other. So is there a difference between you and the one who reversed the matter to you in that, and made the choice in it where you refused, and he refused where you made it for him, of origin or similarity? So he will not say a statement about one of them except that he will make the same statement about the other. Then they differed about the method of evaluation if he wanted to atone by feeding. Some of them said: The value of the hunted animal is determined by the place where it was hunted. This is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Hammad, Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. The narration from Ibrahim and Hammad has been mentioned previously, indicating this, and this is the text of the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Others said: Rather, it is based on the price of the land in which he is performing the atonement. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said, regarding a person in ihram who hunted game in Khorasan, he said: He should atone in Mecca or in Mina. And he said: The food is based on the price of the land in which he atones. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Yaman told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding a man who caught game in Khorasan, he said: He is to be judged in Mecca. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that if the killer of the game rewards it with an equivalent of the animal, then he rewards it with its equivalent in creation and size in its body, from the things that most closely resemble it from the animals. If he rewards it with food, then he should assess its value in the place where he struck it, because there he must atone by feeding. Then if he wishes, he may feed it in the place where he struck it, or in Mecca, or in any other place wherever he wishes, because God, the Most High, mentioned, only stipulated that the killing of the game be brought to the Ka`bah with the sacrificial animal, not any other form of its reward. So the one who rewards with something other than the sacrificial animal may reward it with feeding and fasting wherever he wishes on earth. A group of scholars said the same thing as we said about this. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Arubah told us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Whatever is of blood, then it is in Mecca. And whatever is of charity or fasting, then it is wherever he wishes. Some people disagreed with this and said: The sacrifice and feeding are not valid except in Mecca. As for fasting, if it is not disbelief, then he may fast it wherever he wants in the land. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Ata’, he said: The blood and food are in Mecca, and fasting is wherever one wants. Hanad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Malik bin Mughul, on the authority of Ata’, he said: The expiation for Hajj is in Mecca. Amr ibn Ali told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: Where should he give food in charity if he so wishes? He said: In Mecca, because it is like an offering. He said: Then the recompense for the like of what he killed of the livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Ka’bah, because he killed it in the sanctuary - meaning the House - so his recompense is at the House. As for the sacrificial animal, if he is rewarded with what he killed from the game, it will not suffice him as an expiation for what he killed from that unless he takes it to the Kaaba as God Almighty said, and slaughters it or slaughters it and gives it in charity to the poor of the Haram, and what is meant by the Kaaba in this place is the entire Haram. Whoever offers his obligatory sacrifice as a reward for hunting, may slaughter it at any time he wishes, before or after the Day of Sacrifice, and feed it. Likewise, if he expiates by feeding it, he may expiate by it whenever and wherever he likes. If he expiates by fasting, then the same applies. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, except for what we mentioned about their differences regarding expiation by feeding, as we explained previously. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, I said to Ata’: Or the equivalent of that in fasting. Is there a time for fasting it? He said: No, if he wants and wherever he wants, and hastening it is more preferable to me. Hannad told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: I said to Ata’: A man hunts game during Hajj or Umrah, and sends its reward to the Sacred Sanctuary in Muharram or any other month, is it acceptable for him? He said: Yes. Then he recited: A gift delivered to the Ka’bah. Hannad said: Yahya said: And this is what we take. Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said: If you come to Mecca with a reward for hunting, then slaughter it, for God Almighty says: A sacrifice to be brought to the Kaaba, unless he comes in the ten days, then he delays it until the Day of Sacrifice. Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said: The one who hunts game in Mecca should give charity, for God Almighty says: A gift delivered to the Kaaba. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by that: Or for the one who kills the game while in a state of ihram, the equivalent of fasting for the game killed. That is, the game, alive and not killed, is worth its value in food in the place where the person in a state of ihram killed it, then he fasts a day in place of each mudd. That is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, equaled a mudd of food to a day’s fast in expiation for sexual intercourse during the month of Ramadan. If someone were to say: Why didn’t you make the place of each sa’ in the penalty for hunting a day’s fast, based on the ruling of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in its equivalent, which is his ruling on Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, when he ordered him to feed, if he atones by feeding, a group of food, which is three sa’s, between six poor people - if he atones by fasting, he should fast for three days, so he made the three days of fasting equal to feeding three sa’s, because that is like the atonement in the penalty for hunting, more similar than the atonement for killing game is to the atonement for having intercourse with one’s wife in the month of Ramadan? It was said: Analogy is referring the disputed branches to their counterparts from the agreed-upon principles. There is no disagreement among all of them regarding the argument that fasting does not suffice as an expiation for killing game by fasting, if one equates a day’s fast with a sa’ of food. Since that is the case, and it is not permissible to contradict it in what it has brought about from the religion that is agreed upon, it is thus correct that the ruling on equating fasting with food in killing game is contrary to the ruling on equating it with it in the expiation for shaving, since it is not permissible to return a principle to a principle by analogy. Rather, it is permissible to compare the branch to the principle. Whether someone says: Why don’t you return the ruling on fasting in expiation for killing game to its ruling on shaving the harmful thing in what is equivalent to food? Or another says: Why don’t you return the ruling on fasting in shaving to its ruling on expiation for killing game in what is equivalent to food, so that instead of every mudd or instead of every half sa’, he is required to fast a day? We have previously explained that justice in the speech of the Arabs with the fat-ha is the amount of something other than its kind, and that justice is its amount of its kind. Some scholars of Arabic language used to say: Justice is a noun derived from the saying: I have balanced this with that in a good balance. He said: Justice is also with the fat-ha, the proverb. But they differentiated between justice in this and justice of goods, by breaking the ‘ayn in justice of goods, and opening it from the saying of God Almighty: And no compensation will be accepted from her (al-Baqarah 2:23), and the saying of God Almighty: Or the equivalent of that in fasting just as they said: a sensible woman and a sensible stone. Some of them said: Justice is fairness in right, and justice in the broken form is the proverb, and we have explained that with its evidence in the past. As for the accusative of fasting, it is an interpretation, as it is said: I have a wineskin full of ghee, and the equivalent of a pound of honey. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, Abu Asim narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, I said to Ata’: What is the equivalent of fasting for that? He said: The equivalent of food for fasting. He said: For each mudd, one day, he takes what he claimed by fasting Ramadan and by zihar. He claimed that this was his opinion, but he did not hear it from anyone, and it was not a Sunnah. He said: Then I returned to him after a while, I said: What is the equivalent of fasting for that? He said: If he gets what is equivalent to a sheep, I should give him food, then he should fast one day in place of each mudd. He said: And I did not ask him: Is this an opinion or a recommended Sunnah? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding the words of God Almighty: or the equivalent of that in fasting, he said: He fasts three days to ten days. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Hammad: Or the equivalent of that in fasting, as a penalty if he does not find what to buy a sacrificial animal with, or what to give in charity that does not reach the price of a sacrificial animal, he is required to fast one day in place of every half sa’. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or the equivalent of that in fasting. He said: If a pilgrim kills a game animal, he is to be judged for it. If he kills a gazelle or something similar, he must slaughter a sheep in Mecca. If he cannot find one, he must feed six poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for three days. If he kills a deer or something similar, he must give a cow. If he cannot find one, he must feed twenty poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a wild donkey or something similar, he must give a camel. If he cannot find one, he must feed thirty poor people. If he cannot find one, he must fast for thirty days. Food: a measure of measure, to satisfy them. Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Sa`id: I asked him about a pilgrim who hunts game and must pay a ransom, a sheep, a cow, or a camel, but he cannot find one. What is the equivalent of that in terms of fasting or charity? He said: The price of that. If he cannot find the price of it, he should estimate its price in the form of food and give it in charity to every poor person, one mudd, then he should fast for each mudd one day. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: That he may taste the consequences of his deed. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: I have made obligatory upon the one who kills game in a state of ihram what I have made obligatory of the penalty and expiation mentioned in this verse, so that he may taste the consequences of his action and its punishment. Meaning by his command his sin and the action he did of killing what God Almighty forbade him from killing while he was in a state of ihram. He says: So I obligated him to pay the expiation that I obligated him to do, to make him taste the punishment for his sin, by obligating him to pay a fine and to do physical work that would tire him out and be difficult for him. The root of the word wabal is severity in something unpleasant. From this comes the saying of God Almighty: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible seizure (al-Muzzammil 73:16). God Almighty has made clear in His saying: That he may taste the evil consequences of his deed, that the expiations required in terms of money and bodies are punishments from Him for His creation, even though they are a test for them and an expiation for the sins that they have atoned for. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: As for and the punishment of his affair, it means the punishment of his affair. The statement in the interpretation of his saying: God has pardoned what is past, and whoever returns [to the past], God will take vengeance on him. Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says to His believing servants in Him and in His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has pardoned, O believers, what happened to you in your ignorance, such as hunting game while you were in a state of ihram, and killing it. He will not hold you accountable for what you did before He made it forbidden to you, nor will you be required to pay expiation for it in terms of wealth or life. But whoever among you returns to killing it while in a state of ihram, after it was forbidden in the sense that he used to kill it when he was a disbeliever, and before it was forbidden to him, by considering it permissible to kill it, God will take revenge on him. It may be possible that its meaning is: Whoever returns to killing him after it was forbidden in Islam, God will take revenge on him in the Hereafter. As for in this world, he will have to pay the punishment and expiation that I have explained. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, I said to Ata’: What is God has pardoned what is past? He said: What was during the pre-Islamic era. I said: What is And whoever returns [to sin], God will take vengeance on him? He said: Whoever returns [to sin] in Islam, God will take vengeance on him. And he must also pay expiation. Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, I said to Ata’, and he mentioned something similar, and added to it, and said: If he returns and kills, he must pay expiation. I said: Is there a known punishment for returning? He said: No. I said: Do you think it is right for the imam to punish him? He said: It is a sin that he committed between himself and God, but he must pay expiation. Sufyan told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’: And whoever returns, God will take vengeance on him, he said: In Islam, and he must also pay expiation. I said: Is there a punishment for him from the Imam? He said: No. Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’: God has pardoned what is past, what was in the pre-Islamic era, and whoever returns, he said: in Islam, God will take vengeance on him, and he must pay expiation. He said, I said to Ata’: Is there a punishment for him from the Imam? He said: No. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ who said: He is judged in the case of error, intent, and forgetfulness, and whenever he is right, God the Almighty says: God has pardoned what is past, meaning what was in the days of ignorance, but whoever returns [to sin], God will take vengeance on him, with expiation. Sufyan said, Ibn Jurayj said: So I said: Will the ruler punish him? He said: No. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, I said to Ata’: God has pardoned what came before? He said: What was in the pre-Islamic era. Yaqoub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, that he said: He is judged every time he returns. Hanad told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Whenever a pilgrim kills game by mistake, he is judged. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Whenever a forbidden game is hunted, it is judged. Amr bin Ali told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, who said: Whoever kills game and then returns, he is to be punished. Amr told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: He is to be sentenced, should he be deposed? Should he be left alone? Amr told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: What about someone who hunts game while in a state of ihram, is he to be punished and then returns? He said: He is to be punished. Amr told us, Katheer bin Hisham told us, Al-Furat bin Salman told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ata’, who said: He is judged every time he returns. Others said: The meaning of this is: God has forgiven what you did in the past in this regard during the pre-Islamic era, and whoever returns to Islam, God will take revenge on him by obligating him to pay expiation. Who said that? Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’, regarding the statement of God Almighty: But whoever returns [to sin], God will take vengeance on him, they said: God will take vengeance, meaning the retribution, God has pardoned what is past, in the pre-Islamic era. Others said about this: God has pardoned what has passed of killing whoever among you killed game unlawfully the first time. And whoever returns to killing it a second time after the first unlawful killing, God is the Guardian of vengeance against him, without any expiation required of him for killing it. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever kills a game by mistake while in a state of ihram, he will be judged for it once. If he returns, it will be said to him: May God take revenge on you, as God the Almighty said. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If a person in a state of ihram kills a game, he will be judged for it. If he returns, he will not be judged for it, and that is up to God the Almighty: If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him. Then he recited this verse: “But if he returns, God will take vengeance on him. And God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.” Hannad narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Zaida narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, on the authority of Aamer, who said: A man came to Shuraih and said: I killed game while I was in a state of ihram! He said: Did you kill anything before that? He said: No. He said: If you say yes, I will entrust you to God, and He will take revenge on you, for He is Exalted in Might and Avenge! Dawud said: So I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair, and he said: Rather, he will be sentenced to death. Should he be divorced?! Abu Al-Sa'ib and Amr bin Ali told me, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: If a man hunts game while in a state of ihram, he is asked: Did you hunt game before this? If he says: Yes, he is told: Go, and God will take revenge on you! If he says: No, he is judged. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding the one who kills game and then returns, he said: They used to say: Whoever returns, no judgment is passed on him, his matter is up to God Almighty. Amr told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: That a man came to Shuraih and said: I caught game. He said: Did you catch game before him? He said: No. He said: If you had said yes, I would not have ruled against you. Amr told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shuraih, the same. Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Shuraih, regarding the one who kills game, he said: He is judged, and if he returns, God will take revenge on him. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, as judged by two just men among you. He said: He is judged for the intentional killing once, but if he repeats it, he is not judged, and it is said to him: Go, God will take revenge on you, and he is judged for the unintentional killing forever. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: He permitted killing game once, but whoever returns, God Almighty will not leave him alone until He takes revenge on him. Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya bin Saeed and Ibn Abi Uday told us, all on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding someone who hunts game and rules against it, then returns, he said: He does not rule against it, God will take revenge on him. Amr told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: God Almighty said: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, meaning: intentionally killing him, forgetting his state of ihram, then that is the one who is judged. But if he returns, then he is not judged, and it is said to him: God will take revenge on you. Amr told us, Katheer bin Hisham told us, Al-Furat bin Salman told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid: If he returns, he will not be judged, and it will be said to him: May God take revenge on you. Amr told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Al-Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the one who hunts game and is judged against, then returns, he said: He is not judged against. Others said: The meaning of this is: God has pardoned what happened in the past when you killed game before God Almighty forbade it to you. And whoever returns to killing it after God forbade it to him, knowing that He forbade it to him, intentionally killing it, remembering his state of ihram, then God is the one who will take revenge on him, and there is no expiation for his sin, nor is there any punishment required of him in this world. Who said that? Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, But whoever returns, God will take vengeance on him, he said: Whoever returns after God's prohibition - after knowing that it is forbidden and that he remembers its prohibition - no one should pass judgment on him, and they will leave him to the vengeance of God, the Almighty and Majestic. As for the one who intentionally kills game while forgetting its prohibition, or is ignorant that killing it is forbidden, these are the ones who will be judged. As for the one who kills it intentionally after God's prohibition, and he knows that it is forbidden and that it is forbidden, he is left to the vengeance of God, and this is the one upon whom God has placed the vengeance. This is similar to what Mujahid said that we mentioned before. Others said: A specific person is rich in that. Who said that? Amr bin Ali told us, Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, Zaid Abu Al-Mu'alla told us: A man killed game while he was in a state of ihram, and it was permissible for him to do so. Then he returned, so God sent a fire upon him and burned him. This is what He said: But whoever returns, God will take vengeance upon him. He said: In Islam. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: And whoever returns to killing it in Islam after God Almighty forbade it, then God will take revenge on him, and he must also pay expiation, because God Almighty, when He informed us that He will take revenge on him, did not inform us, and He has made it obligatory for him to kill game intentionally what He has made obligatory of punishment or expiation by His saying: And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is like that which he killed from livestock, that He has removed the expiation from him the second and third time, rather He informed His servants of what He has made obligatory of the ruling on the one who kills game intentionally from those in ihram, then He informed that He will take revenge on whoever returns, and He did not say: And there is no expiation upon him in this world. If someone thinks that expiation removes punishment, and if expiation was required of him in this world, the punishment in the Hereafter would be nullified, then he has thought wrong. This is because God, the Almighty, can vary the punishments for His disobedience as He wills and loves, so He increases His punishment for some of His disobediences by what He detracts from others, and He decreases from some by what He removes from others, as He did in His variation between His punishment for the unmarried adulterer and the married adulterer, and between the thief of a quarter of a dinar and the thief of less than that. Likewise, He varied between His punishment for the one who intentionally kills game from among those in ihram, initially, and his punishment if he repeats it after beginning. So He made it obligatory for the one who begins to give him an equivalent amount of livestock, or expiation by feeding or fasting justly, and He made that the punishment for his crime by saying: That he may taste the evil of his deed, and He made it obligatory for the one who repeats after beginning, and He increased his punishment for him what He informed His servants that He would do of vengeance, as a severe punishment from Him, the Almighty, for repeating after beginning. If His punishments for things were consistent, then there would be no punishment for one thing that would differ from a punishment for another, nor would there be a punishment in the Hereafter that would be more severe than another punishment. This is contrary to what the decisive Qur’an states. Some claimants have claimed that the meaning of this is: Whoever returns to Islam after God has forbidden killing him, to kill him in the sense in which the people used to kill him in their pre-Islamic era, then He pardons them when it was forbidden for them to kill him, and that is killing him because it was permissible to kill him. He said: But if he kills him in a way other than that, and that is killing him in a way that is immoral and not in a way that it was permissible, then he must pay the penalty and expiation every time he returns. This is a statement that we do not know of anyone who has said it from the people of interpretation. It is enough that his statement is wrong, as it departs from the statements of the people of knowledge, even if there is no evidence for his error other than himself. So how is it when the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates its corruption? This is because God, the Almighty, included in His statement, But whoever returns, God will take vengeance on him, every one who returns to killing game in the sense that was previously prohibited from him at the beginning of the verse, and He did not specify one of them who returns to killing it over another. So whoever claims in the revelation something that is not in its apparent meaning, is required to provide proof for his claim in a manner that must be accepted. As for the one who claims that the meaning of this is: And whoever returns to killing it deliberately after he had begun killing it while he was in a state of ihram, then God will take revenge on him, the meaning of his statement, God has pardoned what is past, is: God has pardoned what is past of his sin of killing the game initially, because in the statement of God, the Most High, That he may taste the consequences of his deed, there is clear evidence that the statement in this regard is not what he said, because pardoning a crime means leaving it to be held accountable for. And whoever tastes the consequences of his crime has been punished for it. And it is not permissible to say to someone who has been punished: He has been pardoned. And the report of God, the Most High, is more truthful than for there to be contradiction in it. If someone says: Why do you find it objectionable that the one who killed the game was one of the people in ihram the first time, and that he tasted the consequences of his action with the penalty and expiation that was required, and that he was pardoned from the punishment with more than that which God Almighty could have punished him with? It was said to him: If that is permissible for you to interpret the verse - even if it is contrary to the saying of the people of interpretation - then why do you deny that the vengeance that God Almighty promised him for returning after the beginning is that increase that He pardoned him for the first time, from what he had to do to him with the one who made him taste the consequences of his affair, so He makes him taste in his return after the beginning the consequences of his affair that he made him taste the first time, and leaves His pardon for what He pardoned in the beginning, so He holds him accountable for it? So he will not say anything about that except that he will make the same thing obligatory in the end. The statement in the interpretation of His statement: And God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God is impregnable in His dominion, no one can subdue Him, and no one can prevent Him from taking revenge on whomever He takes revenge on, nor from punishing whomever He wants to punish. This is because creation is His creation and the command is His command. He has glory and power. As for His saying: Possessor of Retribution, He means by this His punishment of whoever disobeys Him for his disobedience to Him.
5:96: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: Lawful for you, O believers, is sea game, which is what is caught fresh, such as: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab told you about his statement: Lawful to you is the game of the sea, he said: Its game, whatever is caught from it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, he said, I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: It is permissible for you to hunt in the sea. He said: So hunting is what is taken. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is the game of the sea, he said: Its game, whatever is caught from it. Sulayman bin Umar bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is the game of the sea, he said: Its game, fresh. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hudhayl bin Bilal told us, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is game from the sea, he said: Its game, whatever is hunted. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: Lawful to you is the game of the sea, he said: The sea urchin. Ibn Wakee` told us, he said, Al-Hasan ibn `Ali Al-Hanafi told us - or: Al-Husayn, Abu Ja`far was not sure - on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of `Ikrimah, he said: Ibn `Abbas used to say: The game of the sea is what is caught. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Permissible for you is the game of the sea. He said: Fresh. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Badr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: Sea game means what is caught. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Permissible for you is the game of the sea. He said: Fresh. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: It is permissible for you to catch fish from the sea, he said: fresh fish. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Permissible for you is sea fishing. As for sea fishing, it is the fish, which are whales. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: His prey, what you hunt fresh - Muammar said, and Qatada said: His prey, what you hunt. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Lawful to you is the game of the sea, he said: its whales. Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said: Saeed was asked about sea hunting, so he said, Makhul said, Zaid bin Thabit said: Its hunting, what you hunt. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and for the travelers, he said: The pilgrim and the non-pilgrim may hunt from the sea and eat from their catch. Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Abu Bakr said: The food of the sea is everything in it. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: Whatever is uncovered, eat. And he said: Everything in it, meaning everything that is caught. Saeed ibn al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, he heard Ikrimah say: Abu Bakr said: And its food is provision for you and for the travelers, he said: It is everything in it. In this context, the word sea refers to all rivers. The Arabs call rivers seas, as God Almighty said: Corruption has appeared on land and sea (al-Rum 30:41). Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement is: It is permissible for you, O believers, to eat fresh river fish that you caught during your time of pilgrimage and your sanctuary, and what you did not catch of its food that it killed and then threw on its shore. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: and his food. Some of them said: What he meant by that is: what was thrown to its shore dead, similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, he said, I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: Lawful for you is the hunting of the sea and its food as provision for you, and its food is what is thrown up. Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I was in Bahrain, and they asked me about what the sea casts up. He said: I gave them a fatwa that they should eat it. When I came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, I mentioned that to him, and he said to me: What did you give them a fatwa on? I said: Did you give them a fatwa that they should eat it? He said: If I had given them a fatwa other than that, I would have beaten you with a whip! He said: Then he said: God Almighty said in His Book: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you. So its game is what is caught from it, and its food is what is cast up. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food as provision for you, he said: Its food is what is thrown up. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food, he said: Its food is what is thrown up. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hussain bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His food is everything that the sea throws up. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Ali told us - or: Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Hanafi, Abu Jaafar was not sure - on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His food is what he expels from his dead body. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hudhayl bin Bilal told us, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, he said: Its food is what is found dead on the shore. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: His food is what he threw away. Saeed bin al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, he heard Ikrimah say: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: And his food is provision for you, he said: His food is everything in it. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Amr ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr said: And his food is a provision for you, he said: His food is his dead body. Amr said: I heard Abu al-Sha’tha’ say: I did not think his food was anything but his salt. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar bin Saad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And its food is provision for you, he said: Its food is its dead body. Humaid bin Mas`adah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari` told us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Ikrimah: And his food is provision for you. He said: His food is what he threw up. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muammar ibn Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi', he said: Abd al-Rahman came to Abdullah and said: The sea has thrown up many whales? He said: So he forbade him from eating them, then he said: O Nafi', bring me the Qur'an! So I brought it to him, and he recited this verse: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you. I said: Its food is what it has thrown up. He said: So catch up with it and order it to eat it. Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has thrown up many dead whales, so can we eat them? He said: Do not eat them! So when Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Qur’an and read Surat al-Ma’idah, and he came to this verse: And its food is provision for you and for the travelers. He said: Go and tell him to eat it, for it is his food. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Amr bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said, Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, said: And its food is provision for you, he said: its dead body. Amr said: I heard Abu Al-Shatha’ say: I did not think its food was anything but its saltiness. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Nafi’ told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah asked Ibn Umar about many whales that the sea had thrown up, Are they dead? He said, Yes! So he forbade him from doing so, then he entered the house and called for the Qur’an and recited the following verse: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you. He said, “Its food, everything taken out of it, so eat it, there is no harm in it. And everything in it may be eaten, dead or on its shores.” Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, Qatada said: (His food is what he ejaculates from it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said: Whatever the sea throws up is its food, even if it is dead. Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr, he said: Abu Ayoub was asked about the statement of God Almighty: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision, he said: It is what the sea throws up. Others said: What he meant by his saying: and its food is the salty fish, so the interpretation of the speech according to that is their interpretation: The fish of the sea and its salty fish are permissible for you in every case, in the case of your being in ihram and in the state of your being in ihram. Who said that? Sulayman bin Omar bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And his food, he said: his food, the salty part of it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And its food is a provision for you, meaning: with its food, its saltiness, and what the sea throws up of it, its saltiness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And its food is a provision for you, and it is salty. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Majma’ al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: For your enjoyment, he said: The beautiful. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas and Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: The handsome man Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And his food is a provision for you, he said: The good, and what is the wording. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you, he said: A man comes to the people of the sea and says: Feed me! If he says: A fish, they cast their net and catch it for him. And if he says: Feed me from your food, they feed him from their salted fish. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed: Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food. He said: The abandoned fish, the salted fish. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And his food, he said: salty. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And his food, he said: It is his food. Then he said: What he slandered. Ibn Muadh told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And his food, he said: salted fish. Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Al-Thawri told me, on the authority of Mansur, he said: Ibrahim used to say: His food is good fish. Then he said after that: What he threw away. Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: His food is good. Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: His food is good fish.
